Kahoot: 'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi (5-dars).
WRITING Ex (savol + namuna kirish/Body 1) — proyektor.
Reading matni — uyga; listening transcript — faqat ustozda.
Rubrikalar: W-4.0 (E bo'lim jadvali) + W-CHECK-4.0 — class_ex dagi jadval (proyektor); TEST-4.0.
timeline: Salomlashish
Telefonlar yig'iladi. Kirish savoli: "Is your school strict? Name one rule." — 2 o'quvchi javob beradi.
TAKROR: Kahoot — 5-dars (Adverbial phrases)
'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi → 5-dars savollari (20 ta). Bugungi darsning Kahooti bu yerda EMAS — u 7-darsda o'ynaladi. Oxirgi 1 daqiqa: eng ko'p xato qilingan 2 savol izohi.
TAKROR: Yozma normativ — Essential Words 5 (Health and lifestyle)

Normativ — belgilangan vaqtda bajariladigan qisqa o'lchov; natijasiga qarab coin beriladi. 5-dars CORE 20: ustoz o'zbekchasini aytadi, o'quvchi inglizchasini yozadi — 4 daq; 1 daq sherik bilan almashib tekshirish. 18–20 = 2 coin; 15–17 = bajarildi; 14 va kam = 7-darsda qayta topshiradi.
PROGRESS TEST 1 (pt1) — 1–5-darslar

Test: tests/pt1 (tizim). A Grammatika 15 (10 daq) · B Lug'at 10 (5 daq) · C Reading 8 (10 daq) · D Listening 5 (5 daq) · E Writing paragraf 12 (10 daq, W-4.0) = 50 ball. Telefonlar yig'iladi; javoblar test paytida ko'rsatilmaydi; natija tahlili 7-darsda.
YANGI GRAMMATIKA — Be allowed to / be permitted to / be supposed to + CCQ

Lead-in (2 daq): "You are allowed to use a dictionary. Phones are not permitted. You are supposed to be here at 9." → formula proyektorda (5 daq) → 2–3 misol → CCQ (4 daq) → can/could va be allowed to (3 daq) → 2 daq tez og'zaki tekshiruv.
LUG'AT — Essential Words 6 CORE 20
20 so'z proyektorda talaffuz + tarjima (2 daq); qiyin so'zlarga CCQ/misol — legislation, law-abiding, apartheid (2 daq); juftlikda A o'zbekchasini, B inglizchasini aytadi (2 daq). Flashcard — uyga.
Kombinatsiya — S + be + allowed / permitted / supposed to + V1

Kombinatsiya — juftlikda formula → gap → tarjima zanjiri: A formulani yoki o'zbekcha gapni aytadi, B shu formula bilan inglizcha gap tuzib tarjima qiladi, keyin almashadi. Formula proyektorda qoladi; 3 daq juftlikda (me'yor normativ[1]); ustoz 2 juftlikni tinglaydi.
SINF MASHQLARI — Ex1–Ex3 (MAJBURIY) + ZAXIRA
Ex1 4 daq yakka · Ex2 5 daq juftlik · Ex3 5 daq yakka · 2 daq kalit proyektorda. ZAXIRA — vaqt qolsa: Xatoni toping.
WRITING — School rules and freedom

Task 2 (discuss both views + opinion), test darsi taqsimoti: 2' savol tahlili (savol turi, kalit so'zlar: strict rules / uniforms / phones / more freedom, pozitsiya, 2 body: Body 1 — qat'iy qoidalar, Body 2 — erkinlik) · 4' NAMUNA kirish + Body 1 tahlili (box, proyektorda: topic sentence, bog'lovchilar, be supposed to / be allowed to, EW6 so'zlari: obey the law, ban, law-abiding) · 4' Body 2 va xulosa REJASI (g'oya / izoh / misol jadvali, daftarda), insho uyda 40 daqiqa taymer bilan.
LISTENING — IELTS Part 2
Library rules (monolog, 8 bo'shliq, yakka): 1 daq — savollarni o'qish; 1-tinglash (3 daq); 2-tinglash (3 daq); 1 daq — javoblar proyektorda.
Xatolar ustida ishlash + uyga vazifa

2 daq — darsdagi 3 ta xato doskada tuzatiladi; 3 daq — uyga vazifa (1–4 majburiy, jumladan 4 — WRITING: to'liq insho; 5–7 qo'shimcha). Vaqt yetmasa: ZAXIRA mashqlar va reading'ning 'find' topshirig'i uyga o'tadi.

intro: BE ALLOWED TO + V1 — ruxsat berilgan (og'zaki, umumiy): "He is allowed to stay out late." Inkor: isn't allowed to (taqiq).
BE PERMITTED TO + V1 — rasmiy ruxsat (qoida, hujjat): "They were permitted to enter." Rasmiy e'lonlarda: "Smoking is not permitted."
BE SUPPOSED TO + V1 — kutilgan, qoida bo'yicha shunday bo'lishi kerak: "You are supposed to wear a uniform." O'tganda — bo'lmagan: "I was supposed to call you (lekin qilmadim)."

can (ruxsat) kelajak haqida ham ishlatiladi, agar ruxsat hozirdan bor bo'lsa: "You can leave early tomorrow." Kelajakda YANGI paydo bo'ladigan ruxsat uchun — will be allowed to: "Next year you'll be allowed to vote." Present Perfect va infinitivda faqat be allowed to: "have been allowed to". *will can — xato.
formulas: Be allowed to
S + am/is/are/was/were + allowed to + V1
He is allowed to stay out late.
Unga kechgacha qolishga ruxsat berilgan.
Be permitted to
S + be + permitted to + V1 (rasmiy)
They were permitted to enter.
Ularga kirishga ruxsat berilgan edi.
Be supposed to
S + be + supposed to + V1
You are supposed to wear a uniform.
Sen forma kiyishing kerak (qoida).
Inkor
S + be + not + allowed/permitted/supposed to + V1
Prisoners weren't allowed to read newspapers.
Mahbuslarga gazeta o'qishga ruxsat berilmagan.
Savol
Be + S + allowed/supposed to + V1?
Are we allowed to leave early? / What am I supposed to do?
Erta ketishga ruxsat bormi? / Men nima qilishim kerak?
Zamonlar
will be allowed to / has been permitted to / was supposed to
Mandela was supposed to stay in prison for life.
Mandela umrbod qamoqda qolishi kerak edi.
presentation: Are students allowed to use phones in the exam?
No, they aren't allowed to — it's against the rules.
Was Mandela permitted to have visitors?
Only one visitor every six months was permitted.
Were black South Africans allowed to vote before 1994?
No, they weren't allowed to vote in national elections.
CCQ: You were supposed to arrive at 9.
Was there a rule/plan? (Yes) Did you arrive at 9? (No)
CCQ: I was supposed to call you, but I forgot.
Did I call? (No) Was it planned? (Yes)
CCQ: Smoking is not permitted in the building.
Can you smoke inside? (No) Is it formal — a sign or a law? (Yes)
CCQ: Next year you'll be allowed to vote.
Can you vote now? (No) Will you have permission next year? (Yes)
notes: allowed — og'zaki; permitted — rasmiy (belgi, qonun, e'lon); supposed — qoida, reja yoki kutish bo'yicha (amalda doim bajarilmaydi).
"be supposed to" hozirgi zamonda ham "deyishadi" ma'nosi: "This film is supposed to be good."
let + odam + V1 = allow + odam + to V1: "They let him go" = "He was allowed to go".
O'quvchi so'raydi: Nega "Smoking is not allowed" da to yo'q? — Javob: to faqat undan keyin fe'l kelganda qo'yiladi; bu yerda keyin fe'l yo'q. Solishtiring: Students are not allowed to smoke.
O'quvchi so'raydi: "I can help you tomorrow" xatomi? — Javob: yo'q, ruxsat/imkoniyat hozirdan bor. Yangi ruxsat: Next year you'll be allowed to drive.
O'quvchi so'raydi: could ham o'tgan ruxsatmi? — Javob: umumiy ruxsat uchun ha (When I was ten, I could stay up late); bitta aniq holat uchun — was allowed to.
mistakes: He is allowed to stay late.
Students are supposed to wear uniforms.
I was allowed to go out yesterday.
You suppose to be here at 9.
You are supposed to be here at 9.
to faqat undan keyin fe'l kelganda qo'yiladi; harakatning o'zi ega bo'lsa, keyin fe'l ham, to ham yo'q.

how: CORE 20 — qonun va jamiyat asoslari; STRONG — sud va jinoyat-jazo; SUPER — Task 2 kollokatsiyalari (enforce the law, commit a crime). STRONG/SUPER — ixtiyoriy.
Misolda so'zning o'zi albatta bo'ladi, gap tabiiy va faktik to'g'ri; bugungi grammatika qolipi — ixtiyoriy, faqat tabiiy tushsa.
core: New legislation is supposed to protect workers.
Yangi qonunchilik ishchilarni himoya qilishi kerak.
Most people in our town are law-abiding citizens.
He was not permitted to apply for citizenship.
Unga fuqarolik uchun ariza berishga ruxsat berilmadi.
Everyone is supposed to enjoy civil rights.
Har kim fuqarolik huquqlaridan foydalanishi kerak.
Employers aren't allowed to practise discrimination.
Under apartheid, black people weren't permitted to vote in national elections.
Aparteid davrida qora tanlilarga umummilliy saylovlarda ovoz berishga ruxsat berilmagan.
Citizens are supposed to have freedom of speech.
Fuqarolar so'z erkinligiga ega bo'lishi kerak.
A court is supposed to deliver justice.
Equality before the law means everyone is treated the same.
Qonun oldida tenglik — hamma bir xil munosabat ko'radi.
Prisoners still have basic human rights.
Mahbuslar ham asosiy inson huquqlariga ega.
The constitution says what the state is allowed to do.
Konstitutsiya davlatga nima qilishga ruxsat berilganini belgilaydi.
In a democracy, people are allowed to choose their leaders.
Demokratiyada odamlarga rahbarlarini tanlashga ruxsat beriladi.

Fuqarolik itoatsizligi — adolatsiz qonunlarni tinch yo'l bilan buzish.

normativ: Og'zaki: CORE 20 + tarjima + 1 gap, 2 daqiqa — 1 coin.

class_ex.title: Progress Test 1 (1–5-darslar): ustoz uchun o'tkazish tartibi va ball jadvali
class_ex.instr: Test 6-darsda, Salomlashish (3), Kahoot — 5-dars (8) va Yozma normativ — Essential Words 5 (5) dan keyin yoziladi: 16-daqiqadan 56-daqiqagacha, 40 daqiqa, yakka, qog'ozda. Jami 50 ball: A Grammatika 15 · B Lug'at 10 · C Reading 8 · D Listening 5 · E Writing 12. Natija tahlili — 7-darsda (PT1 NATIJA TAHLILI, 8 daqiqa).
items: 1. Darsdan oldin (1 kun oldin): o'quvchi varag'ini har o'quvchiga bittadan chop eting — unda faqat A, B, C (matn va savollar), D (bo'sh forma) va E (savol va reja) bor. Listening skripti, kalit, W-4.0 rubrikasi, ball varag'i va QAYTA TOPSHIRISH varianti (fayl oxiridagi 6 ta blok) faqat ustozda, alohida varaqda — 6-darsda tarqatilmaydi. Tahlil uchun har o'quvchiga 1 toza qoralama varaq.

2. Proyektor: test davomida faqat taymer (40:00) va bo'lim vaqtlari chiqariladi. Savollar, listening skripti va kalit proyektorga CHIQARILMAYDI. Telefonlar yig'iladi (qutiga), lug'at va daftarlar sumkaga.
3. Tarqatish (Kahoot va normativdan keyin, 1 daqiqa ichida): varaq yuzini pastga qilib tarqating; o'quvchi ism-familiya, guruh va sanani yozadi. 'Start' deganda hamma varaqni ochadi.

4. 0–5-daqiqa — D. LISTENING (hamma birga, BIRINCHI bo'lib): 30 soniya — o'quvchilar D formasini o'qiydi; keyin ustoz 'Listening skripti' ni ikki ovozda (RECEPTIONIST — oddiy, STUDENT — sal balandroq) o'rtacha tezlikda o'qiydi; 10 soniya pauza; ikkinchi marta o'qiydi; 20 soniya — javoblarni tekshirish. Skript o'quvchiga ko'rsatilmaydi, so'zlar alohida takrorlanmaydi va harf-harf aytilmaydi (faqat skriptdagi T-O-S-H-E-V dan tashqari).

5. 5–40-daqiqa — qolgan bo'limlar o'z tezligida. Tavsiya: A Grammatika 10 · B Lug'at 5 · C Reading 10 · E Writing 10 daqiqa. 15-, 20-, 30-daqiqalarda keyingi bo'limni eslating; 35-daqiqada '5 minutes left' deng. Savollarga javob tushuntirilmaydi — faqat topshiriq shartini qayta o'qib berasiz.
6. 40-daqiqada varaqlar yig'iladi. Shu darsning o'zida kalit KO'RSATILMAYDI (dars 16 daqiqalik yangi grammatika bilan davom etadi).

7. Tekshirish (7-darsgacha): A — har savol 1 ball (13–15: xato topilib, to'g'ri tuzatilsa 1; faqat topilib, tuzatish noto'g'ri — 0.5). B — 1 ball; bitta harf imlo xatosi — 0.5. C — har javob 1 ball; 5–8 da ikki so'zdan ortiq yoki matndagi so'z xato yozilgan — 0. D — 1 ball; bitta harf xatosi (ismdan tashqari) — 0.5; 1-savolda imlo aniq bo'lishi shart. E — W-4.0 rubrikasi (4 mezon × 0–3 = 12). Kalitdagi muqobil javoblar ham to'liq ball.
8. Natija tizimga bo'limlar kesimida kiritiladi: A, B, C, D, E alohida + jami; foizni jamidan hisoblang (ball × 2 = %). Keyingi qadam quyidagi jadval bo'yicha belgilanadi.

9. 7-dars — PT1 NATIJA TAHLILI (8 daqiqa): tekshirilgan varaqlar qaytariladi; eng ko'p uchragan 5 xato doskada — o'quvchilar juftlikda tuzatadi (5 daq); 6-dars uy reading kaliti (1 daq); < 70% olganlar ro'yxati va qayta topshirish sanasi (2 daq). Tahlildan keyin varaqlar ustozga qaytariladi (qayta topshirish uchun savollar yangi bo'ladi — 10-band).

10. Qayta topshirish (SHARTLI — keyingi 2 dars ichida, dars vaqtidan tashqari, 15 daqiqa; O'TMADI — remedial mashg'ulotdan keyin): faqat qayta topshiriladigan bo'lim(lar). Savollar testdagidan boshqa — fayl oxiridagi 'QAYTA TOPSHIRISH varianti' bloklari: A (15 savol), B (10 savol), C (yangi matn, 8 savol), D (yangi skript, 5 savol), E (yangi savol). 15 daqiqaga 1–2 bo'lim sig'adi: A — 7 daq, B — 4 daq, C — 8 daq, D — 4 daq, E — 10 daq. Qayta topshirilmagan bo'limlarning birinchi bali saqlanadi; yangi jami = eski ballar + qayta topshirilgan bo'lim(lar)ning yangi bali.
answers: O'TDI + 5 coin: jami 45–50 ball (90–100%) va har bo'lim ≥ 50% (A ≥ 7.5, B ≥ 5, C ≥ 4, D ≥ 2.5, E ≥ 6) → 7-darsdan davom etadi.
O'TDI + 3 coin: jami 40–44.5 ball (80–89%) va har bo'lim ≥ 50% → davom etadi.
O'TDI: jami 35–39.5 ball (70–79%) va har bo'lim ≥ 50% → davom etadi; eng past bo'lim bo'yicha uyga 1 ta qo'shimcha mashq.

SHARTLI: jami ≥ 30 ball (≥ 60%), lekin O'TDI sharti bajarilmagan — jami 30–34.5 (60–69%) YOKI bir yoki bir necha bo'lim < 50% → < 50% bo'lim(lar) (jami 60–69% bo'lsa — eng past 1–2 bo'lim) bo'yicha 15 daqiqalik qayta topshirish keyingi 2 dars ichida (dars vaqtidan tashqari). Qayta topshirilgan bo'lim(lar) bali eski bali o'rniga qo'yilib, jami qayta hisoblanadi: jami ≥ 35 (70%) VA har bo'lim ≥ 50% → O'TDI (coin berilmaydi). Yetmasa — natija rahbarga, O'TMADI dagi kabi ota-onaga xabar va 1 remedial mashg'ulot. Misol: A 9 · B 4 · C 6 · D 4 · E 9 = 32 (64%) → SHARTLI (B < 5); B qayta topshirildi — 7 → 9+7+6+4+9 = 35 (70%), hamma bo'lim ≥ 50% → O'TDI.

O'TMADI: jami 0–29.5 ball (< 60%) → ota-onaga xabar (shu hafta), 1 qo'shimcha (remedial) mashg'ulot eng past bo'limlar bo'yicha, keyin qayta topshirish (10-banddagi yangi savollar bilan, to'liq test yoki < 50% bo'limlar).
Coin faqat birinchi topshirishda beriladi (90%+ — 5 coin, 80–89% — 3 coin). Natija va qaror 7-dars tahlilida o'quvchiga yakka aytiladi, guruh oldida ball e'lon qilinmaydi.
class_ex.note: Test_after (5-dars): PROGRESS TEST 1 (pt1) — 6-dars boshida, 40 daqiqa; qamrov 1–5-darslar (prefixes, suffixes, ought to / be able to, future forms, adverbial phrases; Essential Words 1–5 CORE). ZAXIRA mashqlari va STRONG/SUPER lug'at testga kirmaydi.

class_ex.title: A. Grammatika, 1-qism: 1–8 — Multiple choice (8 × 1 = 8 ball)
class_ex.instr: Choose the correct answer: A, B, C or D. (To'g'ri javobni tanlang va harfini aylantiring.)
items: 1. It is ___ to learn a new language in one week — nobody can do it. A) unpossible B) impossible C) inpossible D) dispossible
2. I ___ the teacher's question, so my answer was completely wrong. A) misunderstood B) disunderstood C) ununderstood D) reunderstood
3. ___ from old factories is a serious problem in our city. A) Pollute B) Polluted C) Pollution D) Pollutely
4. Sorry, I ___ come to your party tomorrow — I have an exam. A) won't can B) won't be able to C) not able to D) am not can
5. Yesterday the lift stopped between two floors, but the firefighters ___ open the door and help everyone out. A) could B) were able to C) can D) ought
6. According to the timetable, the next train to Samarkand ___ at 9.15. A) leaves B) is about to leave C) leaving D) is leave
7. Look at those black clouds! It ___ rain. A) is going to B) is due to C) rains D) is to
8. ___ the heavy rain, the football match started on time. A) Because of B) Despite C) In order to D) Although
why: 1-dars: p oldida im- → impossible (unpossible, inpossible — xato).
1-dars: 'noto'g'ri' ma'nosi → mis- (misunderstand).
2-dars: gap egasi — OT kerak → -tion (pollution).
3-dars: can'ning kelajagi yo'q → will be able to (won't be able to).
3-dars: bitta aniq holatda uddaladi → was/were able to (could — umumiy qobiliyat).
4-dars: jadval (timetable) → Present Simple.
4-dars: dalilli bashorat (black clouds) → be going to.
5-dars: yon berish + OT (the heavy rain) → despite; although + gap; because of — ma'no teskari.
class_ex.note: Qamrov: 1–2 — 1-dars, 3 — 2-dars, 4–5 — 3-dars, 6–7 — 4-dars, 8 — 5-dars. Har to'g'ri javob — 1 ball.

class_ex.title: A. Grammatika, 2-qism: 9–12 — Bo'shliqni to'ldiring (4 × 1 = 4 ball)
class_ex.instr: 9–10: Write the word in brackets in the correct form. 11–12: Write ONE word. (9–10: qavsdagi so'zni to'g'ri shaklda yozing. 11–12: bitta so'z yozing.)
items: 9. Recycling paper and plastic is an ______ friendly habit. (ENVIRONMENT)
10. Plastic bags are very ______ to sea animals — they kill thousands of them every year. (DANGER)
11. You ought ______ drink more water when you do sport.
12. He stayed at home ______ of his illness and missed the exam.
why: 2-dars: sifat (friendly) oldida RAVISH → environmental + -ly = environmentally (bitta l emas: -ally).
2-dars: sifat kerak (are very ___) → danger + -ous = dangerous. danger (ot) yoki dangerously (ravish) — 0.
3-dars: ought dan keyin doim to + V1.
5-dars: sabab + OT → because of (his illness). 'instead of' — ma'noga mos emas.
class_ex.note: 9–10: imlo aniq bo'lishi shart (environmentaly, dangerus — 0.5). 11–12 da faqat bitta so'z to'liq ball oladi.

class_ex.title: A. Grammatika, 3-qism: 13–15 — Xatoni toping va tuzating (3 × 1 = 3 ball)
class_ex.instr: Each sentence has ONE mistake. Find it and write the correct sentence. (Har gapda bitta xato bor — toping va to'g'ri gapni yozing.)
items: 13. Driving without a licence is inlegal in Uzbekistan.
14. The meeting is due start at 10 a.m., so please don't be late.
15. Despite he was very tired, he finished the marathon.
answers: 13. Driving without a licence is illegal in Uzbekistan. (inlegal → illegal)
14. The meeting is due to start at 10 a.m., so please don't be late. (due start → due to start)
15. Despite being very tired, he finished the marathon. / Although he was very tired, he finished the marathon. / In spite of being very tired, …
why: 1-dars: l oldida il- (illegal).
4-dars: be due TO + V1.
5-dars: despite + OT yoki V-ing; to'liq gap bilan — although.
class_ex.note: Xato topilib, to'g'ri tuzatilgan — 1 ball; xato to'g'ri topilgan, lekin tuzatish noto'g'ri — 0.5. Qamrov: 13 — 1-dars, 14 — 4-dars, 15 — 5-dars.

class_ex.title: B. Lug'at, 1-qism: 1–5 — Ta'rif → so'z (5 × 1 = 5 ball)
class_ex.instr: Read the definitions and write the correct word from the box. There are THREE extra words. (Ta'rifni o'qing va ramkadan mos so'zni yozing. Uchta so'z ortiqcha.)
box: undergraduate · scholarship · deforestation · emission · obsolete · burnout · salary · life expectancy
items: 1. a university student who is studying for his or her first degree
2. the cutting down of large areas of trees
3. no longer used, because something newer and better exists
4. a state of extreme tiredness caused by working too hard for too long
5. the number of years that a person is expected to live, on average
class_ex.note: Qamrov (hammasi CORE): 1 — EW1 Education, 2 — EW2 Environment, 3 — EW3 Technology, 4 — EW4 Work, 5 — EW5 Health. Ortiqcha so'zlar: scholarship (EW1), emission (EW2), salary (EW4). Bitta harf imlo xatosi — 0.5.

class_ex.title: B. Lug'at, 2-qism: 6–10 — Gapga so'z (5 × 1 = 5 ball)
class_ex.instr: Complete the sentences with a word from the box. There are TWO extra words. (Gapni ramkadagi so'z bilan to'ldiring. Ikkita so'z ortiqcha.)
box: compulsory · vocational · renewable · extinction · cyberbullying · promotion · sedentary
items: 6. Maths and English are ______ subjects in our school — every student must study them.
7. Solar and wind power are ______ sources of energy because they never run out.
8. Many parents worry about ______: online bullies can send cruel messages to children at any time.
9. After eight years at the bank, she got a ______ and became the manager of her department.
10. A ______ lifestyle, with many hours of sitting and little exercise, can lead to obesity.
class_ex.note: Qamrov (hammasi CORE): 6 — EW1, 7 — EW2, 8 — EW3, 9 — EW4, 10 — EW5. Ortiqcha so'zlar: vocational (EW1), extinction (EW2). Bitta harf imlo xatosi — 0.5.

class_ex.title: C. Reading, 1–4: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN (4 × 1 = 4 ball)
class_ex.instr: Read the text "The Ten-Minute Walk". Do the statements agree with the information in the text? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN. (Matnni o'qing. TRUE — matnda shunday; FALSE — matnda aksi; NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqida ma'lumot yo'q.)
box: A. Two years ago, a technical college in Namangan noticed a problem. Many of its 600 students spent almost the whole day sitting: in lectures, on the bus and in front of screens at home. The college nurse, Dilfuza Karimova, was worried because they hardly moved at all. "Young people think that chronic illness is a problem only for the elderly," she says, "but bad habits start at sixteen."

B. In September 2024, the college started a simple experiment. After every second lesson, teachers stopped the class for ten minutes, and everyone walked around the building or across the sports field. Phones stayed in the classroom. All first-year students had to join the walks; for everyone else they were optional.

C. At first, most students were unhappy. Some said the breaks were a waste of time, and a few teachers complained that they were not able to finish their lessons. However, after one term the results were surprising. First-year students walked, on average, 4,000 more steps a day, and 70 percent of them said they felt less tired in the afternoon. Their test results did not fall, and attendance rose by 8 percent.

D. Despite this success, the project is not perfect. In winter, the walks move indoors because of the cold, and the corridors become crowded and noisy. Mrs Karimova believes the college ought to build a covered path next to the sports field. The regional health department is likely to pay for part of it.

E. Next year the project is going to spread to three more colleges in the region. "Physical activity is not a lesson on the timetable," Mrs Karimova says. "It is a habit, and habits are built every day, not once in a while."
items: 1. The nurse believes that unhealthy habits can begin when people are young.
2. All students at the college had to take part in the walks.
3. Students who walked more also started eating healthier food.
4. Most students liked the walking breaks from the beginning.
why: A: "bad habits start at sixteen".
B: "All first-year students had to join the walks; for everyone else they were optional" — faqat 1-kurslar majbur edi.
Matnda ovqatlanish haqida hech narsa yo'q (faqat qadam, charchoq, test natijalari, davomat).
C: "At first, most students were unhappy".
class_ex.note: Original matn (Jony Academy), 285 so'z; kollej va hamshira to'qima. Mavzu 5-darsga (Health and lifestyle) oid, dars matni emas. T/F/NG qisqartmasi (T, F, NG) — to'liq ball; YES/NO — 0.

class_ex.title: C. Reading, 5–8: Sentence completion (4 × 1 = 4 ball)
class_ex.instr: Complete the sentences. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the text for each answer. (Gapni to'ldiring: matndan ko'pi bilan IKKI so'z.)
items: 5. During the walks, the students' phones stayed in the ______.
6. A few teachers said they could not finish their ______.
7. In winter, the walks take place indoors because of the ______.
8. Mrs Karimova thinks the college should build a ______ next to the sports field.
why: B: "Phones stayed in the classroom."
C: "not able to finish their lessons" (could not = were not able to).
D: "move indoors because of the cold".
D: "ought to build a covered path" (should = ought to).
class_ex.note: Qavsdagi 'the' ixtiyoriy. Ikki so'zdan ortiq (masalan 'a covered path next') yoki imlo xatosi — 0 ball.

class_ex.title: Listening skripti (faqat ustozga, o'qib beriladi)
class_ex.instr: Ustoz ikki rolni ovozini o'zgartirib o'qiydi (o'rtacha tezlik, ~1 daqiqa). 2 marta o'qiladi: oldin 30 soniya — o'quvchilar formani o'qiydi; o'qishlar orasida 10 soniya pauza. Skript o'quvchiga ko'rsatilmaydi va proyektorga chiqarilmaydi. Original skript, 183 so'z.
items: 1. RECEPTIONIST: Good afternoon, Jony Career Centre. How can I help you?
2. STUDENT: Hello. I'd like to book a place on one of your free workshops, please.
3. RECEPTIONIST: Of course. Can I have your name?
4. STUDENT: Sardor Toshev. That's T-O-S-H-E-V.
5. RECEPTIONIST: Thank you. Which workshop are you interested in? We have Interview Skills and Writing a CV.
6. STUDENT: I was going to take Interview Skills, but my friend says it's full.
7. RECEPTIONIST: Yes, I'm afraid it is. But there are still places on the CV workshop.
8. STUDENT: Great, the CV one, then. Is it on the twelfth of March?
9. RECEPTIONIST: It was due to start on the twelfth, but the trainer is ill, so now it's on Thursday, the fourteenth.
10. STUDENT: No problem. What time does it start? Four o'clock?
11. RECEPTIONIST: Usually, yes, but this time it starts at half past four and finishes at six.
12. STUDENT: And which room is it in?
13. RECEPTIONIST: Room two-one-five... sorry, let me check. No, it's two-five-one, on the second floor.
14. STUDENT: Two-five-one. Should I bring anything?
15. RECEPTIONIST: You ought to bring your student card and a copy of your old CV, if you have one.

items: 1. Question: Some people believe that university education should be free for all students. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
2. Plan: Topic sentence (your opinion + main reason) → Explain (why?) → Example (a real or typical situation) → Link (back to the question).
3. Use: at least 2 linking words (because, however, as a result, for example) and 2 words from Essential Words 1 (tuition fees, degree, qualification, academic, literacy…).

answers: NAMUNA (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6, 96 so'z): In my view, university education ought to be free because it gives equal chances to talented young people. At the moment, many families in Uzbekistan are unable to pay high tuition fees, so clever students from villages often choose a low-paid job instead of a degree. As a result, the country loses future doctors and engineers. For example, my cousin had excellent grades at school, but he was not able to study in Tashkent due to the cost. Free education is likely to help more young people get a good qualification and build a successful career.

Namunada: pozitsiya (ought to be free) → izoh (unable to pay tuition fees) → natija (As a result) → misol (For example, my cousin…) → xulosa (is likely to help…); Essential Words 1: tuition fees, degree, qualification; EW4: career; 1–5-darslar grammatikasi: ought to, unable (prefiks), not able to, due to, is likely to.

box: A. Last spring, a school in Bukhara asked its 450 pupils to try a small challenge: one evening a week without any screens. The idea came from the school psychologist, Nodira Rashidova. She had noticed that many pupils looked tired in the morning and found it hard to concentrate in class. "Most of them go to bed with a phone in their hand," she explains.

B. The rules were simple. Every Wednesday, from six o'clock until bedtime, pupils switched off their phones, tablets and computers. Parents were asked to join in, but this was not required. Each family received a list of ideas, such as board games, cooking together and reading aloud.

C. After two months, the school asked pupils and parents about the challenge. More than half of the families said they talked more at dinner, and many pupils reported that they fell asleep faster on Wednesdays. However, some older pupils said that the evening was difficult because they had to do their homework online.

D. Because of this problem, the school is going to change one rule next term: pupils will be able to use a computer for homework, but not for games or social media. Mrs Rashidova thinks other schools ought to try the idea. "Technology is useful," she says, "but we should control it, not the other way round."

E. Other schools in the city are likely to follow. Two of them have already asked Mrs Rashidova to explain how the challenge works. She is due to give a talk to their teachers in October, and she is going to bring some of her pupils with her, so that they can describe the evenings in their own words.

box: Question: Some people think that schools should have strict rules, for example about uniforms and mobile phones. Others believe students should be allowed more freedom. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

MODEL — Introduction: Every school has rules, but people disagree about how strict they should be. Some argue that pupils need firm rules on things like uniforms and phones, while others feel that teenagers deserve more freedom. In my opinion, schools need clear rules, but students should be allowed to take part in making them.

MODEL — Body 1: On the one hand, supporters of strict rules believe that they prepare young people for adult life. At school, children learn to follow rules in the same way that adults have to obey the law. For example, in many schools in Uzbekistan, students are supposed to wear a uniform and arrive before eight o'clock, and this teaches them discipline. In addition, a ban on phones during lessons helps students concentrate, because they are not distracted by social media. As a result, strict schools often produce organised and law-abiding young people.
items: 1) Savol turi qanday? Insho nechta body paragrafdan iborat bo'ladi va har birida nima yoziladi?
2) Kirishda yozuvchining pozitsiyasi qaysi gapda? Savoldagi qaysi so'zlar boshqacha aytilgan (parafraz)?
3) Body 1 da bugungi grammatika (be allowed to / be permitted to / be supposed to) qayerda?
4) Body 1 da qaysi EW6 (Law, rules and society) so'zlari bor? Qaysi bog'lovchilar ishlatilgan?
5) Body 1 ning tuzilishi: topic sentence -> explain -> example -> link — har birini toping.

TASK (4 min, plan only): Body 2 (the 'more freedom' view) — Idea: … | Explain: … | Example (Uzbekistan / your school): … | Link: … ; Conclusion — restate your opinion in new words (1–2 sentences): … Use 1 structure: be allowed to / be permitted to / be supposed to.
answers: Tahlil kaliti: 1) Discuss both views + opinion: 2 body — Body 1 qat'iy qoidalar tarafdorlari fikri, Body 2 erkinlik tarafdorlari fikri; o'z fikr kirishda va xulosada.

2) Pozitsiya — kirishning oxirgi gapi: 'In my opinion, schools need clear rules, but students should be allowed to take part in making them.' Parafraz: strict rules -> firm rules; students -> pupils / teenagers; be allowed more freedom -> deserve more freedom.
3) Body 1: 'students are supposed to wear a uniform' (qoida bo'yicha kutilgan). Kirishda: 'should be allowed to take part' (ruxsat).
4) EW6: obey the law, ban, law-abiding. Bog'lovchilar: On the one hand, For example, In addition, because, As a result.

5) Topic: 'supporters of strict rules believe that they prepare young people for adult life' -> Explain: adults have to obey the law -> Example: uniform, arrive before eight o'clock, ban on phones -> Link: 'As a result, strict schools often produce organised and law-abiding young people.'

NAMUNA REJA (faqat ustoz uchun): Body 2 — Idea: too many rules make students passive | Explain: never permitted to choose -> no responsibility | Example: school council, vote on the length of breaks -> democracy, civil rights | Link: without freedom, students break rules when nobody watches. Conclusion: both views true; rules + a real voice for students = balance.

NAMUNA Body 2 + Conclusion (faqat ustoz uchun): On the other hand, too many rules can make students passive. Teenagers who are never permitted to make their own choices may not learn how to take responsibility. For instance, when pupils elect a school council and vote on small changes, such as the length of breaks, they practise democracy and learn about their civil rights and duties. However, when adults decide every detail, young people may simply break the rules when nobody is watching. || In conclusion, both views have some truth. Rules about safety, uniforms and phones are necessary, but schools should also give students a real voice. I believe that a balance between rules and freedom creates responsible citizens.
To'liq namuna: 253 so'z (box dagi kirish va Body 1 + yuqoridagi Body 2 va xulosa).
Baholash: W-4.0 — shu darsdagi E bo'lim jadvali (insho uchun 'Qoidalar' qatori global W-4.0 da); tekshiruv — quyidagi W-CHECK-4.0.
why: Bugungi grammatika namunada 3 marta: 'should be allowed to take part' (kirish — ruxsat berilishi kerak), 'are supposed to wear a uniform' (Body 1 — qoida bo'yicha kutilgan), 'are never permitted to make their own choices' (Body 2 — rasmiy ruxsat, inkor).

EW6 so'zlari: obey the law (qonunga bo'ysunmoq), ban (taqiq), law-abiding (qonunga itoatkor), vote (ovoz bermoq), democracy (demokratiya), civil rights (fuqarolik huquqlari); break the rules — 'break the law' qolipi.
O'zbek hayotidan misol: forma va soat sakkizgacha kelish qoidasi (Body 1), maktab kengashini saylash (Body 2) — umumiy emas, aniq misol TR uchun muhim.
Discuss both views inshosida o'z fikr faqat xulosada emas, kirishda ham aniq aytiladi — W-CHECK 1-band.
class_ex.note: Jony Academy savoli (kitob uslubida): Kitob IELTS 4.0, SAMPLE ESSAYS uslubida tuzilgan; savol va namuna insho Jony Academy original matni. Baholash: W-4.0 — shu darsdagi E bo'lim jadvali (insho uchun 'Qoidalar' qatori global W-4.0 da). Namuna Band 5.5–6.

homework.title: WRITING — School rules and freedom: to'liq insho (yozma, uyga)
homework.instr: MAJBURIY. Telefonda 40 daqiqalik taymer qo'ying va inshoni daftar yoki ilovada yozing (220–260 so'z, 4 abzats). Sinfda tuzgan Body 2 va xulosa rejangizni ishlating; namunaga qaramang. Vaqt tugaganda chiziq torting. Oxirida so'z sonini yozing va W-CHECK-4.0 bilan tekshiring.
items: Question: Some people think that schools should have strict rules, for example about uniforms and mobile phones. Others believe students should be allowed more freedom. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Paragraph 1 — Introduction: paraphrase the question + your clear opinion (1 sentence).
Paragraph 2 — Body 1: the 'strict rules' view: topic sentence -> explain -> example -> link.
Paragraph 3 — Body 2: the 'more freedom' view: topic sentence -> explain -> example (Uzbekistan / your school) -> link.
Paragraph 4 — Conclusion: both views in 1 sentence + your opinion again in new words.
Use: be allowed to / be permitted to / be supposed to (1–3 times) and 4+ Essential Words 6 (ban, obey the law, law-abiding, vote, democracy, civil rights, freedom of speech…).
answers: NAMUNA (faqat ustoz uchun; o'quvchiga baholangandan keyin ko'rsatiladi; Band 5.5–6, 253 so'z): Every school has rules, but people disagree about how strict they should be. Some argue that pupils need firm rules on things like uniforms and phones, while others feel that teenagers deserve more freedom. In my opinion, schools need clear rules, but students should be allowed to take part in making them. || On the one hand, supporters of strict rules believe that they prepare young people for adult life. At school, children learn to follow rules in the same way that adults have to obey the law. For example, in many schools in Uzbekistan, students are supposed to wear a uniform and arrive before eight o'clock, and this teaches them discipline. In addition, a ban on phones during lessons helps students concentrate, because they are not distracted by social media. As a result, strict schools often produce organised and law-abiding young people. || On the other hand, too many rules can make students passive. Teenagers who are never permitted to make their own choices may not learn how to take responsibility. For instance, when pupils elect a school council and vote on small changes, such as the length of breaks, they practise democracy and learn about their civil rights and duties. However, when adults decide every detail, young people may simply break the rules when nobody is watching. || In conclusion, both views have some truth. Rules about safety, uniforms and phones are necessary, but schools should also give students a real voice. I believe that a balance between rules and freedom creates responsible citizens.

Baholash: W-4.0 / S-4.0 (class_ex dagi jadval), NORM-4.0 — insho W-4.0 bilan (shu darsdagi E bo'lim jadvali, 12 ball): 10–12 — 2 coin; 7–9 — bajarildi; ≤6 — feedback bilan keyingi darsgacha qayta yozadi. 180 so'zdan kam — TR ko'pi bilan 1.

homework.title: QO'SHIMCHA: Speaking yozuvi — bugungi Part 2 kartochkasi, 2 daqiqa (og'zaki, ovozli)
homework.instr: Bugun test darsi bo'lgani uchun Speaking sinfda o'tkazilmadi — kartochka uyga. Kartochka A yoki B ni tanlang: 1 daq tayyorgarlik (5–6 kalit so'z), 1.5–2 daq gapirib, ovozli yozib ilovaga yuboring. Bugungi strukturadan 1–2 marta (be allowed to / be permitted to / be supposed to) va CORE dan 2+ so'z ishlating. Xohlasangiz Part 3 savollaridan biriga ham 3 gapda javob yozib yuboring.
answers: NAMUNA A (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6, 120–160 so'z): I'd like to talk about a rule at my school that I really agree with. Students are not allowed to use their phones during lessons. The rule was made by our head teacher a few years ago. At the start of the day, we are supposed to put our phones in our bags, on silent. We are allowed to use them only at break or when a teacher asks us to look something up. At first, many students didn't like it, and some people broke the rule. But now I think it is fair. Without phones, I concentrate better, and I actually talk to my classmates at break. In my opinion, phones are useful, but in class they are a distraction, so this rule helps us to learn more.

NAMUNA B: A rule I would like to change is at home. I'm not allowed to go out with friends after eight, even at the weekend. My parents worry about me, and I agree that school comes first. But on Saturdays there is no school the next day, so I would change the time to ten. If I finish my homework and tell them where I am, I think I should be allowed to stay out later.

Part 3 namuna javoblari: 1) Phones are useful in an emergency, but students shouldn't be allowed to use them in lessons. 2) Not always — children who are never allowed to decide may not become independent. 3) Some think the rules are unfair; others believe nobody will catch them.
Baholash: S-4.0 rubrikasi (FC / LR / GRA / P, 4 mezon x 0–3 = 12 ball): 10–12 — 1 coin; ≤6 — qayta yozib yuborishi mumkin.
items: KARTOCHKA A: Describe a rule at your school that you agree with. You should say: what the rule is ; who made it ; what students are (not) allowed to do because of it ; and explain why you agree with it.

KARTOCHKA B: Describe a rule you would like to change. You should say: what the rule is ; where it exists (school, home or your town) ; what people are supposed to do ; and explain how you would change it and why.
Part 3: Should teenagers be allowed to use phones at school?
Part 3: Are strict parents better than relaxed parents?
Part 3: Why do some people break rules?

reading.title: Nelson Mandela — the prisoner who was supposed to die in jail
text: A  Nelson Mandela was born in 1918 in a small village in South Africa. At that time, the country had a system called apartheid. Black South Africans were not allowed to vote in national elections, they were not permitted to live in white areas, and they were supposed to carry a pass at all times. Mandela became a lawyer in Johannesburg, joined the African National Congress (ANC) and organised protests against these laws. After the ANC was banned in 1960, he went underground. He was arrested in 1962, and in 1964 he was sentenced to life imprisonment.

B  On Robben Island, life was hard. Prisoners were permitted only one letter and one visitor every six months. They were supposed to break rocks all day, and they were not allowed to talk while they worked. Many people thought the world would forget him. Instead, Mandela studied law by correspondence and helped other prisoners with their education. In the late 1980s, while he was still a prisoner, he was allowed to hold secret talks with the government.

C  In 1990, after 27 years in prison, Mandela was released. Many people feared a civil war, because they expected him to want revenge. Instead, he chose reconciliation and asked all South Africans to build the country together.

D  In 1994, in the first election in which all adult citizens were allowed to vote, Mandela became president. He even invited one of his former prison guards to his inauguration. Later, a truth commission allowed victims and people who had committed crimes to tell their stories in public.

E  Mandela could have stood for a second term, but he chose to serve only one, and he left office in 1999. He died in 2013. Near the end of his autobiography, Long Walk to Freedom, he writes that being free is more than breaking your own chains: it also means living in a way that respects the freedom of other people.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; raqamlar va tuzatishlarni aniq ayting.
Librarian: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Riverside City Library. Before you start using your new cards, I'm going to explain a few rules.
Librarian: First, borrowing. Members are allowed to take out six books at a time — not eight, as it says on our old website. You can keep them for three weeks.
Librarian: Now, the reading room. Laptops are permitted there, and so are tablets. Phones must be switched to silent and left in your bag.
Librarian: Children under twelve are supposed to stay with an adult at all times.
Librarian: Food is not permitted anywhere in the building, except in the café. It used to be on the first floor, but the new café is on the ground floor, next to the entrance.
Librarian: Books are supposed to come back by the date on your receipt. If they're late, you pay 2,000 soums a day. We used to charge 1,000, but the price went up in January.
Librarian: Finally, opening hours. On weekdays we open at half past eight. On Saturdays we open at nine — sorry, at ten — and we close at four. Any questions?

kahoot.q: He ___ stay out late on Fridays.
kahoot.explain: be + allowed TO + V1: He is allowed to stay.

kahoot.q: Students ___ wear uniforms at this school.
kahoot.explain: be + supposed TO + V1 = qoida bo'yicha shunday bo'lishi kerak.

kahoot.q: I ___ go to the cinema yesterday because I'd done my homework.
kahoot.explain: O'tgan zamondagi ruxsat → was allowed to + V1.

kahoot.q: Sign in a hospital: "Smoking is not ___."
kahoot.explain: to faqat undan keyin fe'l kelganda qo'yiladi; bu yerda keyin fe'l yo'q: Smoking is not permitted.

kahoot.q: I ___ call you yesterday, but I forgot. Sorry!
kahoot.explain: was supposed to = qilishim kerak edi (lekin qilmadim).

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: You suppose to be here at 9.
You are supposed to be here at 9.
kahoot.explain: be yordamchisi shart: You ARE supposed to...

kahoot.q: ___ we allowed to leave early today?
kahoot.explain: Savol: Be + S + allowed to + V1? → Are we allowed to leave?

kahoot.q: Next year you ___ drive — you'll be 18.
kahoot.explain: Kelajakda YANGI paydo bo'ladigan ruxsat → will be allowed to. *will can — xato.

kahoot.q: "This film is supposed to be good." — ma'nosi?
kahoot.explain: be supposed to be = "deyishadi, aytishlaricha".

kahoot.q: "They let him go." = "He ___ go."
kahoot.explain: let + odam + V1 = odam + was allowed TO + V1.

kahoot.q: Rasmiy RUXSAT (qonun, e'lon, belgi) uchun eng mos shakl qaysi?
kahoot.explain: permitted — rasmiy ruxsat; allowed — og'zaki; supposed to — ruxsat emas, kutilgan majburiyat.

kahoot.q: Tarjima: "Mahbuslarga gazeta o'qishga ruxsat berilmagan edi."
options: Prisoners weren't allowed to read newspapers.
Prisoners didn't allowed to read newspapers.
Prisoners weren't allow to read newspapers.
kahoot.explain: Inkor: weren't + allowed (V3) + TO + V1.

kahoot.q: Treating people unfairly because of their race or gender is ___.
kahoot.explain: discrimination = kamsitish.

kahoot.q: People who always follow the law are ___.
kahoot.explain: law-abiding = qonunga bo'ysunuvchi.

kahoot.q: The right to say what you think in public is freedom of ___.
kahoot.explain: freedom of speech = so'z erkinligi.

kahoot.q: In South Africa, ___ was a system that separated people by race.
kahoot.explain: apartheid = irqiy ajratish siyosati (Janubiy Afrika).

kahoot.q: The government decided to ___ the old law (end it officially).
kahoot.explain: abolish = (qonunni) bekor qilmoq.

kahoot.q: The jury decided he was not ___, so he went home free.
kahoot.explain: not guilty = aybsiz deb topildi → ozod.

kahoot.q: "qonunni buzmoq" = ___ the law
kahoot.explain: break the law = qonunni buzmoq; obey the law = bo'ysunmoq.

kahoot.q: Nobody may be outside after 10 p.m. — there is a ___.
kahoot.explain: curfew = komendantlik soati (kechqurun chiqish taqiqi).

TAKROR: Kahoot — 6-dars (Be allowed to / be permitted to / be supposed to)
'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi → 6-dars savollari (20 ta). Bugungi darsning Kahooti bu yerda EMAS — u 8-darsda o'ynaladi. Oxirgi 1 daqiqa: eng ko'p xato qilingan 2 savol izohi.

Normativ — belgilangan vaqtda bajariladigan qisqa o'lchov; natijasiga qarab coin beriladi. 6-dars CORE 20: ustoz o'zbekchasini aytadi, o'quvchi inglizchasini yozadi — 4 daq; 1 daq sherik bilan almashib tekshirish. 18–20 = 2 coin; 15–17 = bajarildi; 14 va kam = 8-darsda qayta topshiradi.
PT1 NATIJA TAHLILI — pt1

Ustoz tekshirilgan varaqlarni qaytaradi. Eng ko'p uchragan 5 xato doskada — o'quvchilar juftlikda tuzatadi (4 daq); test darsida uyga berilgan reading kaliti proyektorda (1 daq); <70% olganlar ro'yxati va qayta topshirish sanasi (2 daq).
YANGI GRAMMATIKA — The definite article (the / —) + CCQ

intro: THE — aniq, ma'lum narsa: ikkinchi marta, yagona narsa (the sun, the internet), superlativ/tartib (the biggest, the first, the same, the only).
THE — geografiya: daryo, dengiz, okean, tog' tizmasi (the Amu Darya, the Aral Sea, the Tian Shan); United/Republic/Kingdom/States bilan davlat (the UK, the USA).
THE'siz: shahar, ko'pchilik davlat va qit'a, yakka tog' (Mount Everest), ko'l (Lake Baikal), umumiy ma'no (Cities are noisy), muassasa maqsadida (go to school). Qolganlari — ZAXIRA (formulas 7–8).

notes: Superlativ oldida odatda 'the': the most crowded city; shuningdek 'the same / the only / the first / the last'. (Lekin egalik bilan: my best friend.)
Writing Task 1: "the number of", "the percentage of", "the majority of", "in the world", "over the period".

O'quvchi so'raydi: Nega the Amu Darya, lekin Lake Baikal? — Javob: daryo nomi oldida 'the' qo'yiladi; ko'l nomi 'Lake' so'zi bilan boshlansa, 'the' qo'yilmaydi. The Aral Sea — dengiz, shuning uchun 'the'.

O'quvchi so'raydi: Nega the UK, lekin Uzbekistan? — Javob: UK = the United Kingdom; Kingdom, Republic, States — umumiy ot ('qirollik', 'respublika'), shuning uchun 'the'. Oddiy nom (Uzbekistan, France) — 'the'siz.

O'quvchi so'raydi: 'go to school' va 'go to the school' — ikkalasi ham to'g'rimi? — Javob: ha, lekin ma'nosi boshqa: go to school — o'qishga (o'quvchi sifatida); go to the school — binoga (masalan, ota-ona majlisiga).

items: KARTOCHKA A: Describe a city you have visited and liked. You should say: where it is ; when you went there ; what you did there ; and explain why you liked it.
KARTOCHKA B: Describe your favourite place in your hometown. You should say: what and where it is ; how often you go there ; what people do there ; and explain why it is your favourite place.
Part 3: Why do many young people move to big cities?
Part 3: What can be done to reduce traffic in cities?
Part 3: Is life in the countryside better for children?
answers: NAMUNA A (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6, ~130 so'z): I'd like to talk about Samarkand, a city in the centre of Uzbekistan. I went there last spring with my family, and we stayed for three days. First, we visited the Registan, the most famous landmark in the city, and in the evening we took photos of it. The next day we walked around the old town and bought fresh Samarkand bread at the Siab Bazaar. I liked the city for two reasons. Firstly, history is everywhere — old buildings stand next to modern hotels, so you feel both the past and the present. Secondly, it is not as crowded as the capital, so the pace of life is slower, and the people were very friendly and helpful. I would love to go back there one day.

NAMUNA B: My favourite place in my hometown is the central park. It is in the city centre, ten minutes from my house on foot. I go there about three times a week. Older people walk and talk, children play, and teenagers like me play football. I love it because it is a green space in the middle of a busy city and the best place to relax after school.
Part 3 namuna: There are more job opportunities and better universities in big cities, and life there is more exciting.
Part 3 namuna: The government should improve public transport, for example build new metro lines, so fewer people drive.
Part 3 namuna: In some ways, yes — the air is cleaner and it is safer to play outside. But schools are often worse, so it depends.

class_ex.instr: (15 daq) 3 daq — savol tahlili (savol turi, kalit so'zlar, 2 body rejasi); 5 daq — box dagi NAMUNA kirish + Body 1 tahlili (topic sentence, bog'lovchilar, the / —, EW 7 so'zlari); 5 daq — yakka Body 2 (qishloq: + va –), 60–80 so'z, qolip: Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link; 2 daq — sherik bilan almashib W-CHECK-4.0 bo'yicha tekshirish. ICQ: Body 2 nima haqida va necha so'z? (Qishloq, 60–80) Shaxsiy fikr qaysi abzatsda yoziladi? (Xulosada)
box: Question: Many people prefer to live in cities, while others enjoy life in the countryside. What are the pros and cons of both?

MODEL — Introduction: Some people would rather live in a big city, whereas others are happier in the countryside, where life is calmer. Both places have clear advantages and disadvantages. This essay will discuss both sides and then give my own opinion.

MODEL — Body 1: On the one hand, life in cities has many benefits. Big cities have more companies, so it is easier to find a well-paid job, and their infrastructure is better, with modern hospitals, good universities and fast public transport. For example, every year thousands of young people move to Tashkent from the regions to work or study. However, cities also have serious problems. Congestion makes every journey long and stressful, and housing in the centre is so expensive that many families can only rent a small flat.
items: Insho qolipi (4 abzats): Introduction (savol parafrazi + reja) -> Body 1 (shahar: + / –) -> Body 2 (qishloq: + / –) -> Conclusion (xulosa + qisqa shaxsiy fikr).
1. Savol turi qanday: agree/disagree, advantages/disadvantages yoki causes/solutions? 'both' so'zi nimani talab qiladi?
2. Kirishda savoldagi qaysi so'zlar parafraz qilingan? Shaxsiy fikr qayerda beriladi?
3. Body 1 ning topic sentence'i qaysi? Qaysi so'z '+' dan '–' ga o'tkazadi? Misol qaysi gapda?
4. Bugungi grammatika: 'life in cities', 'the countryside', 'Tashkent', 'the centre' — qaysi biri the bilan, qaysi biri the'siz va nega?
5. Essential Words 7 (Cities) so'zlaridan qaysilari bor?

TASK: Write Body 2 (60–80 words): Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link. Idea: the countryside — pros (clean air, cheap life, friendly neighbours) and cons (few jobs, weak schools and hospitals).
answers: Kalit 1: advantages/disadvantages ('pros and cons of both') — ikkala joyning HAM ijobiy, HAM salbiy tomoni kerak; faqat bitta joy yoki faqat '+' yozilsa TR ko'pi bilan 1. Shaxsiy fikr so'ralmagan, lekin xulosada 1 gap bilan berish mumkin.

Kalit 2: 'prefer to live in cities' -> 'would rather live in a big city'; 'enjoy life in the countryside' -> 'are happier in the countryside'; 'pros and cons' -> 'advantages and disadvantages'. Shaxsiy fikr — xulosada ('In my opinion, …'). Advantages/disadvantages savolida kirishdagi pozitsiya — 'Both places have clear advantages and disadvantages' + reja gapi ('This essay will discuss both sides…'); shaxsiy fikr xulosada beriladi, W-CHECK 1-band shu bilan bajarilgan hisoblanadi.

Kalit 3: topic sentence — 'On the one hand, life in cities has many benefits.'; '–' ga o'tish — 'However, cities also have serious problems.'; misol — 'For example, every year thousands of young people move to Tashkent…'.

Kalit 4: life in cities — the'siz (umumiy ma'no); the countryside — the bilan ('in the countryside' — qotgan ibora: qishloq joy umuman); Tashkent — shahar nomi, the'siz; the centre — aniq joy (shu shaharning markazi). Body 2 da: the Fergana Valley (vodiy — the), rural areas, big cities (umumiy — the'siz).
Kalit 5: infrastructure, public transport, congestion, housing (box da); rural, migration (Body 2 da).

NAMUNA Body 2 (faqat ustoz uchun): On the other hand, the countryside offers a quieter and cheaper way of life. The air is cleaner, food is fresher, and neighbours know and help each other. For instance, in many villages in the Fergana Valley, families grow their own fruit and vegetables and share them with the whole mahalla. Nevertheless, rural areas often lack good schools, hospitals and jobs. This is the main reason for migration to big cities, as young people cannot build a career at home.

NAMUNA Conclusion (faqat ustoz uchun): In conclusion, cities offer jobs and modern services but are crowded and expensive, while the countryside is calm but has fewer opportunities. In my opinion, the city is the better choice for young people who want to study and start a career, whereas the countryside suits older people who want a quieter life.
To'liq namuna: 258 so'z (kirish 39, Body 1 86, Body 2 80, xulosa 53).
Baholash: W-4.0 (jadval shu darsda); sinfdagi Body 2 — W-CHECK-4.0, to'liq insho uyda W-4.0 bilan.
why: Grammatika (the / —): life in cities, big cities, rural areas — umumiy ma'no, the'siz; Tashkent — shahar nomi, the'siz; the countryside, the Fergana Valley, the centre — the bilan (qotgan ibora / vodiy nomi / aniq joy).
Xulosadagi 'the city' va 'the countryside' — yashash muhiti turi sifatida (bitta aniq shahar emas); 'the better choice' — ikkitadan biri tanlanganda the.
EW 7 so'zlari: infrastructure (infratuzilma), public transport (jamoat transporti), congestion (tirbandlik), housing (uy-joy), rural (qishloqqa oid), migration (ko'chish) — 6 ta, mavzuga tabiiy.
Bog'lovchilar: On the one hand / On the other hand, However, Nevertheless, For example, For instance, so, In conclusion — CC uchun 4+ xil.
O'zbek hayotidan misol: viloyatlardan Toshkentga o'qish/ishga ko'chish va Farg'ona vodiysidagi qishloqlarda meva-sabzavotni mahalla bilan baham ko'rish.

reading.title: Mahmud Kashgari — the man who described the Turkic world
text: A. Mahmud Kashgari lived in the 11th century. His name shows that his family came from Kashgar, a city on the Silk Road in the Karakhanid state. He came from an educated family and studied Arabic, which was the main language of science at the time. As a young man, he left his home and spent many years travelling through the steppes, the deserts and the mountain valleys of Central Asia. He lived with different Turkic tribes, listened to the way they spoke and wrote down their words. He was interested in everyday words too, such as the names of food, animals and tools.

B. In the 1070s, in Baghdad, he finished his great book, "Diwan Lughat al-Turk". It is one of the earliest dictionaries of the Turkic languages. It explains thousands of Turkic words in Arabic and gives examples from poems, proverbs and songs. It also describes the dialects of many tribes and notes where each group lived. Kashgari wanted to show Arab readers that Turkic was a rich language and worth studying.

C. The book also contains a round world map. At the centre of the map is not Baghdad but Balasagun, a Karakhanid city in the Chu Valley. Around it are the lands of the Turkic peoples, with their towns, rivers, seas, deserts and mountains.

D. For centuries the book was almost forgotten. The only manuscript that survives was found in Istanbul in the early 20th century, and scholars later translated it into other languages. Today Kashgari is honoured in many Turkic countries, and students of history and language still use his dictionary. The book is still important because it shows how people spoke almost a thousand years ago, and his map is one of the oldest pictures we have of the geography of the Turkic world.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; monolog — gid rolini ustoz o'qiydi (sekin va aniq).
Guide: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Tashkent city tour. My name is Dilnoza, and I'll be your guide today.
Guide: The tour usually finishes at two o'clock, but today we'll finish a little later, at half past two.

Guide: We start here in the old town, at Chorsu Bazaar, one of the best-known markets in the capital. You'll have forty minutes to look around — sorry, I mean thirty minutes, because the bus can't wait long.
Guide: Then we take the metro. It was the first metro in Central Asia. Many visitors think it opened in the 1980s, but in fact it opened in 1977. Please stay together on the platform.

Guide: Many tours stop at Amir Timur Square, but we get off at Independence Square. It's the main square of the city, and we'll walk through the park there — not for an hour, just for about twenty minutes.

Guide: After that, a bus takes us to the Tashkent TV Tower. Some people think it's 350 metres tall, but in fact it's 375 metres — the tallest structure in Central Asia. From the viewing platform you can see the whole city.
Guide: Lunch is at a café on the outskirts of the city — not in the centre, as it says in your programme. After lunch, the bus brings you back here to the bazaar.
Guide: Oh, and one more thing: please bring some water and comfortable shoes, because we'll walk a lot.

The sun rises in the east.
The Amu Darya is a long river.

kahoot.q: Qaysi qoida TO'G'RI?

kahoot.q: Traffic ___ is a big problem in Tashkent at rush hour.

kahoot.q: The metro is very crowded at ___ hour, when people go to work.

intro: HAD BETTER + V1 — "yaxshisi …, aks holda …": kuchli tavsiya/ogohlantirish (hozir/kelajak). Qisqa: 'd better; inkor: had better not.
WOULD RATHER + V1 (+ than + V1) — aniq holatda afzal ko'rish: "I'd rather read than watch TV." Inkor: would rather not.
WOULD RATHER + boshqa ega + PAST SIMPLE — boshqa odam qilishini xohlash: "I'd rather you didn't post that."
PREFER — umumiy afzallik: prefer A to B, prefer V-ing to V-ing; prefer to V1 rather than V1. would prefer to — aniq holat, muloyim.
formulas: Had better
S + had better (+ not) + V1
You had better go now. / You'd better not be late.
Yaxshisi hozir ketsang bo'ladi. / Kech qolmaganing ma'qul.
Would rather
S + would rather (+ not) + V1 (+ than + V1)
I would rather stay home tonight. / I'd rather read than watch TV.
Bugun uyda qolishni afzal ko'raman. / TV ko'rishdan ko'ra o'qishni afzal ko'raman.
Would rather + boshqa ega
S + would rather + S2 + Past Simple
I'd rather you didn't post that photo.
O'sha suratni joylamaganing ma'qul.
Prefer + ot / V-ing
S + prefer + ot/V-ing + to + ot/V-ing
She prefers tea to coffee. / I prefer reading to watching TV.
U choyni qahvadan afzal ko'radi. / O'qishni TV ko'rishdan afzal ko'raman.
Prefer + to V1
S + prefer + to V1 + rather than + V1
I prefer to stream music rather than buy CDs.
Disk sotib olishdan ko'ra musiqani striming qilishni afzal ko'raman.
Would prefer
S + would prefer + to V1 (muloyim, aniq holat)
I'd prefer to sit near the stage.
Sahna yoniga o'tirishni afzal ko'rardim.
presentation: Would you rather go to a concert or watch it online?
I'd rather go to the concert — nothing beats live music.
Do you prefer streaming or CDs?
I prefer streaming to CDs — it's cheaper.
Would you rather I didn't play music while you study?
I'd rather you turned it down a little.
Why did Taylor Swift re-record her old albums?
She decided she'd better own her music, so she did.
CCQ: You'd better leave now.
Is it advice or a warning? (a warning) Is there a problem if you don't? (Yes)
CCQ: I prefer tea to coffee.
Is it about today or in general? (in general) Which do I like more? (tea)
CCQ: I'd rather you didn't post that photo.
Is 'didn't' about the past? (No — now) Who may post it? (you) Do I want it online? (No)
notes: had better — hozir/kelajak uchun; o'tgan voqeaga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri ishlatilmaydi (faqat bilvosita: She decided she'd better own her music). should'dan kuchli.
would rather + V1 (to yo'q); prefer + to V1 yoki V-ing.
"would rather + S2 + Past Simple" — hozir/kelajak; o'tgan afsus: would rather + S2 + Past Perfect.
O'quvchi so'raydi: 'You'd better go' da 'had' bor-u, nega gap hozir haqida? — Javob: had better — qotib qolgan ibora; bu yerda 'had' o'tgan zamonni bildirmaydi.
O'quvchi so'raydi: 'I'd rather you didn't …' — nega 'didn't'? — Javob: would rather dan keyin boshqa ega kelsa, Past Simple ishlatiladi; u istakni bildiradi, o'tgan zamonni emas.
mistakes: I'd rather you don't post it.
I'd rather you didn't post it.
You had better go. / You'd better go.

class_ex.title: Ex1 — Qolipni tanlang
class_ex.instr: (4 daq, yakka) had better / would rather / prefer — har gapda mos qolipni tanlang (6 gap). ICQ: Nechta gap? Yakka yoki juftlikda?
items: You had better / would rather check the source before sharing. (ogohlantirish)
I would rather / prefer stay home tonight. (hozirgi tanlov)
She prefers / would rather tea to coffee. (umumiy)
We'd better / 'd rather not be late — they won't let us in after 8. (ogohlantirish)
I prefer / would rather reading to watching TV.
I'd rather / prefer you didn't play music now.
class_ex.note: Kuchsiz: 1–5-bandlar; Kuchli: + 2 ta o'z gapi.

class_ex.title: Ex2 — Qayta yozing
class_ex.instr: (4 daq, juftlik) Gapni qavsdagi qolip bilan qayta yozing, ma'no saqlansin (5 gap). ICQ: Nechta gap? Yakka yoki juftlikda?
items: I like live music more than recordings. (prefer)
I want to stay home tonight, not go out. (would rather)
You should check the facts, or you'll spread fake news. (had better)
I don't want you to share my photo. (would rather)
I choose streaming, not CDs. (prefer to … rather than)

I'd rather stay home tonight than go out.
You'd better check the facts, or you'll spread fake news.
I'd rather you didn't share my photo.

class_ex.title: Ex3 — Lug'at + qolip
class_ex.instr: (5 daq, yakka) Fe'lning to'g'ri shakli + qutidagi so'z (6 gap). ICQ: Nechta gap? Yakka yoki juftlikda?
items: I'd rather ___ (read) the whole article than just the ___.
My dad prefers ___ (watch) the news to watching a ___.
You'd better ___ (not / believe) every story online — it may be ___.
I'd rather you ___ (not / share) my video — I don't want it to go ___.

class_ex.title: Ex4 — Xatoni toping (paragraf)
class_ex.instr: (4 daq, juftlik) Paragrafda 5 ta xato bor — toping va tuzating. ICQ: Nechta xato? (5) Yakka yoki juftlikda? (juftlik)
items: My cousin Aziz loves music. He prefers rock than pop, and he would rather to spend his money on concert tickets than on clothes. Last week he said, 'We'd better buy tickets before they sell out!' I told him I'd rather he doesn't buy one for me, because I prefer watch concerts online. Then my mum said, 'You had better not to come home late.'

box: Question: Some people think watching TV is bad for children. Others believe it has educational value. Discuss both sides and give your opinion.

MODEL — Introduction: Television is part of almost every child's daily routine, but people disagree about its effect. Some think it harms children, while others believe it can teach them a lot. In my opinion, TV can be useful for children, but only when parents control what they watch and for how long.

MODEL — Body 1: On the one hand, watching too much TV can damage children's health and studies. Children who sit in front of a screen for hours usually move less and go to bed later, so they feel tired at school. In addition, the entertainment industry fills children's programmes with advertising for sweets and toys. Many children would rather watch cartoons than read a book or play outside, and as a result, they lose interest in active hobbies.
items: Savol turi qaysi? Nechta body kerak va har biri nima haqida?
Pozitsiya (o'z fikri) kirishning qaysi gapida?
Body 1 da bugungi grammatika (had better / would rather / prefer) qayerda?
Kirish va Body 1 da qaysi Essential Words 8 so'zlari bor? Savoldagi qaysi so'zlar parafraz qilingan?
TASK: Write Body 2 (60–80 words) about the educational value of TV: Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link
answers: Tahlil kaliti: 1) discuss both views + opinion — 2 body: Body 1 — zarari, Body 2 — ta'limiy foydasi; xulosada o'z fikri. 2) Kirishning 3-gapi: 'In my opinion, TV can be useful … only when parents control …'. 3) 'Many children would rather watch cartoons than read a book' (would rather + V1 + than + V1). 4) EW: entertainment industry, advertising; parafraz: watching TV -> sit in front of a screen; bad for -> harms / damage; educational value -> teach them a lot.

NAMUNA Body 2 + Conclusion (faqat ustoz uchun): On the other hand, TV and online streaming can have real educational value. Good programmes explain nature, science and history in a simple and colourful way that young viewers remember easily. For example, the Uzbek children's channel Bolajon broadcasts cartoons that teach the alphabet, numbers and good manners, and many children learn their first English words from educational cartoons on YouTube. In this way, the screen becomes a teacher, not just a toy. In conclusion, although too much TV is bad for children, carefully chosen programmes can help them learn. I believe parents had better choose shows for their children and set a time limit, such as one hour a day. Most children prefer cartoons to documentaries, but a good mix of fun and learning keeps this young audience happy and curious.
why: 'would rather watch cartoons than read' — would rather + V1 + than + V1: bolalarning hozirgi afzal ko'rishi (Body 1).
'parents had better choose shows' — had better + V1: kuchli maslahat; xulosada tavsiya berish uchun qulay.
'prefer cartoons to documentaries' — prefer + ot + to + ot: umumiy afzallik (xulosa).
EW so'zlari: entertainment industry, advertising (Body 1), streaming, broadcast (Body 2), audience (xulosa) — LR mezonida ball beradi.
O'zbek misoli: Bolajon telekanali va YouTube'dagi ta'limiy multfilmlar — aniq, tanish misol TR balini oshiradi.
class_ex.note: Manba: Kitob IELTS 4.0, SAMPLE ESSAYS, Topic 4 — faqat savol olindi; namuna insho Jony Academy original matni.

rows: Vazifaga javob (TR; Task 1 da TA)

Savolning BARCHA qismiga javob (sabab VA yechim; ikki fikr VA o'z fikri; ijobiy VA salbiy tomon); pozitsiya kirishda aniq va xulosagacha saqlanadi; har asosiy g'oya izoh va aniq misol bilan. Insho: kirish + 2 body + xulosa, 220–260 so'z; paragraf: talab qilingan so'z soni. Task 1: overview bor, asosiy raqamlar to'g'ri.
Savolga javob va pozitsiya bor, lekin bir qismi yuzaki yoki misol umumiy; insho 180–219 so'z yoki xulosa 1 gapdan iborat. Task 1: overview bor, ayrim raqamlar keraksiz.
Savolning faqat bir qismiga javob (masalan, faqat sabablar); pozitsiya noaniq yoki o'zgarib ketadi; g'oyalar takrorlanadi; insho 120–179 so'z. Task 1: overview yo'q.
Savolga javob yo'q, mavzudan tashqari, yodlangan boshqa matn yoki so'z soni talabning yarmidan kam.
Izchillik va bog'lanish (CC)

Abzatslar aniq: kirish -> Body 1 -> Body 2 -> xulosa; har body: topic sentence -> izoh -> misol -> link; 4+ xil bog'lovchi to'g'ri (however, as a result, for example, on the other hand); ishora so'zlari (this, they, such) to'g'ri.
Abzatslar bor, mantiq tushunarli; 2–3 bog'lovchi, ba'zan mexanik (Firstly, Secondly…); 1–2 noaniq ishora.
Abzatsga bo'linmagan yoki body da topic sentence yo'q; bog'lovchilar 1–2 ta yoki noto'g'ri.
G'oyalar tartibsiz, bog'lanish yo'q.
Lug'at boyligi (LR)
Shu darsning Essential Words so'zlaridan 4+ ta va 2+ kollokatsiya to'g'ri; savol so'zlari parafraz qilingan; imlo xatosi 1–2 ta.
Mavzu so'zlari bor, lekin takror ko'p yoki 3–4 so'z noto'g'ri tanlangan; savol so'zlari ko'chirilgan; imlo xatolari ma'noga xalaqit bermaydi.
Oddiy, takroriy lug'at; so'z tanlash va imlo xatolari ma'noni qiyinlashtiradi.
Juda cheklangan lug'at, ma'no tushunarsiz.
Grammatika aniqligi va xilma-xilligi (GRA)
Sodda va qo'shma gaplar aralash (because, although, which, if); bugungi struktura 1–3 marta to'g'ri va tabiiy; gaplarning ko'pi xatosiz.
Qo'shma gap urinishlari bor; xatolar bor, lekin ma'no tushunarli; artikl/zamon xatolari takrorlanadi.
Asosan sodda gaplar; xatolar ko'p, ayrim gaplar tushunarsiz.
Gap tuzilishi deyarli yo'q.
Jami (12 ball) -> taxminiy band
11–12 ball ≈ Band 5.5–6
8–10 ball ≈ Band 5
5–7 ball ≈ Band 4–4.5
0–4 ball ≈ Band 3.5 va past
Qoidalar (ustoz uchun)
Vaqt: insho 40 daq (uyda, taymer), WRITING NORMATIV 10 daq; vaqt tugaganda chiziq tortiladi, chiziqdan keyingi qism baholanmaydi.
So'z sonini o'quvchi oxirida yozadi; ustoz 2 qatorni sanab tekshiradi; insho 180 so'zdan kam — TR ko'pi bilan 1.
Namuna yoki boshqa manbadan ko'chirilgani aniqlansa — 0 ball, sinfda boshqa savol bilan qayta yozadi.
Ustoz har ish chetiga TR/CC/LR/GRA ballarini va 1 ta eng muhim tuzatishni yozadi; umumiy 2–3 xato keyingi darsning 'Xatolar ustida ishlash' bosqichiga.

reading.title: Taylor Swift — she'd rather own her music
text: A. Taylor Swift was born in 1989 in Pennsylvania, USA. As a young teenager she decided that she would rather write songs in Nashville, the home of country music, than wait for success at home, and her family moved to Tennessee. One record company wanted her to wait until she was older, but she preferred to find a label that would release her music straight away. Her first album came out in 2006, when she was sixteen.

B. By the mid-2010s she was one of the biggest pop stars in the world. However, like many young artists, she did not own the master recordings of her first six albums — her record label did. In 2019 the label was sold, and the masters went with it. Swift had wanted to own them herself, so she was very unhappy about the sale and spoke about it publicly.

C. Most artists simply accept this situation, but Swift decided she'd better take control. She began to re-record her old albums and released the new recordings as "Taylor's Versions". Between 2021 and 2023 she re-recorded four of the six albums, and many fans preferred to stream the new copies rather than the originals. Finally, in 2025, she bought the original masters back.

D. Her Eras Tour (2023–2024) became the highest-earning concert tour in history, with more than two billion dollars in ticket sales. Hotels, restaurants and shops in many host cities reported extra business when the tour came to town.

E. Swift writes or co-writes her own songs, and many of them are based on her own life. The media often prefers to write about her relationships, while her fans would rather talk about her lyrics. For many young musicians, her story has a simple message: if you want to control your future, you'd better read your contract carefully and own your work.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; 1-rol — ustoz, 2-rol — kuchli o'quvchi (yoki ovozni o'zgartiring).
Clerk: Good afternoon, City Arena box office. How can I help?
Caller: Hi. I'd like two tickets for the Silk Road Band concert. I'd rather go on Friday — oh no, sorry, Friday is my sister's birthday. Saturday, please.
Clerk: Saturday is nearly sold out, so you'd better decide now. Can I have your surname?
Caller: Yes, it's Karimova. K-A-R-I-M-O-V-A.
Clerk: Thank you. Standing tickets are 300,000 sums, and seats are 450,000 each.
Caller: I'd prefer seats. My friend has a bad knee.
Clerk: Fine. The doors open at 6 pm, and the show starts at 8 — sorry, at 7.30 this time.
Caller: So when should we arrive?
Clerk: You'd better be here by 7 because of the security checks. And you can't bring any food or drinks.
Caller: What about cameras?
Clerk: Phones are fine, but no professional cameras.
Caller: OK. Can I pay by card?
Clerk: Yes, but I'd rather you paid online — it's faster. We'll send the tickets by email.
Caller: Great, thank you. And is there any parking near the arena?
Clerk: The car park is very small. Most people prefer to take the metro. The nearest station is Park Street.

intro: SEE + O + V1 — harakat BUTUNLAY ko'rildi (boshidan oxirigacha) yoki takroriy odat: "I saw him cross the street." / "We often see birds fly here."
SEE + O + V-ING — harakat DAVOM ETAYOTGAN paytda ko'rildi (bir qismi): "I saw him crossing the street."
Xuddi shunday: hear, watch, notice, feel, listen to: "I heard the bell ring" (butun) / "I heard someone singing" (jarayon).
Passiv: V1 → to V1 ("He was seen to leave the ring"); V-ing o'zgarmaydi ("He was seen leaving the ring").
Ma'no farqi: "I saw the match end" (oxirini ko'rdim) — "I saw the match ending" (tugayotganida ko'rdim).
formulas: See + ob'ekt + V1
S + see/hear/watch + O + V1 (to'liq)
I saw him cross the street.
Uning ko'chani kesib o'tganini ko'rdim (boshidan oxirigacha).
See + ob'ekt + V1 (odat)
S + often see + O + V1
We often see birds fly here.
Bu yerda qushlar uchishini tez-tez ko'ramiz.
See + ob'ekt + V-ing
S + see/hear/watch + O + V-ing (jarayon)
I saw him crossing the street.
Uning ko'chani kesib o'tayotganini ko'rdim.
Hear / notice / feel
S + hear/notice/feel + O + V1 / V-ing
I heard the bell ring. / I noticed him training.
Qo'ng'iroq chalinganini eshitdim. / Uning mashq qilayotganini payqadim.
Passiv
O + was seen/heard + to V1 / V-ing
He was seen to leave. / He was seen leaving.
Uning ketgani ko'rildi. / Uning ketayotgani ko'rildi.
Sport
S + watch + O + V1 (natija) / V-ing (jarayon)
I watched Chagaev beat his opponent on points. / I watched him training in the ring.
Chagayevning raqibini ochko bilan yenganini tomosha qildim. / Uning ringda mashq qilayotganini tomosha qildim.
presentation: Did you see Chagaev win the title?
Yes, I watched a recording of the whole fight — I saw him win it on points.
Did you see him training this morning?
I saw him training at 6 when I passed the gym.
Was the boxer seen to leave the ring?
Yes — he was seen leaving the ring with his coach.
CCQ: I saw him cross the street.
Did I see the whole action? (Yes) Did he reach the other side? (Yes)
CCQ: I saw him crossing the street.
Did I see the end? (Not necessarily) Was he in the middle of the action? (Yes)
CCQ: I heard the bell ring.
Did I hear it from start to finish? (Yes) Can we say 'heard the bell to ring'? (No)
CCQ: He was seen to leave the ring.
Is this active or passive? (Passive) Why 'to'? (Passivda V1 oldidan to keladi)
notes: V1 — "nima bo'ldi" (natija, to'liq); V-ing — "nima bo'layotgan edi" (jarayon, bir lahza).
watch va listen to + O: V1 ham, V-ing ham tabiiy; farq — butun harakat (I watched him lift the belt) yoki jarayon (I watched him training).
can/could see + O + V-ing juda ko'p ishlatiladi: "I could see him coming."

Qaysi biri tabiiyroq va nega? "I heard the phone ring for ten minutes" yoki "I heard the phone ringing for ten minutes"? — Javob: ringing; uzoq davom etgan jarayon → V-ing (ring ham grammatik to'g'ri, lekin kamroq tabiiy).
O'quvchi so'raydi: Nega "I saw him to cross" emas? — Javob: aktivda see/hear/watch + O dan keyin to'siz V1 keladi; to faqat passivda: He was seen to cross.
O'quvchi so'raydi: Passivda V-ing o'zgaradimi? — Javob: Yo'q: They saw him leaving → He was seen leaving.
mistakes: I saw him to cross the street.
I saw him cross the street.
I heard the bell to ring.
I saw him crossed the street.
I saw him cross / crossing the street.
He was seen leave the ring.
He was seen to leave the ring.
He was seen to leaving the gym.
He was seen leaving / to leave the gym.
to + V-ing aralashmaydi: yo to + V1, yo V-ing.
