class_ex.title: Ex1 — V1 yoki V-ing
class_ex.instr: (5 daq, yakka) Ma'noga qarab to'g'ri shaklni tanlang; qavsdagi izoh (to'liq / jarayon / odat) yordam beradi. 8 ta gap. ICQ: Nechta gap? (8) Yakka yoki juftlikda? (Yakka)
items: I saw him cross / crossing the street and go into the gym. (to'liq)
I saw him cross / crossing the street when I drove past. (jarayon)
We often see birds fly / flying here. (odat)
I heard the bell ring / ringing and stood up. (to'liq)
I heard someone sing / singing in the next room. (jarayon)
I watched him lift / lifting the belt. (to'liq)
I noticed him hide / hiding an injury during the fight. (jarayon)
She felt the ground shake / shaking for a minute. (jarayon)
class_ex.note: Kuchsiz: 1–5-bandlar; Kuchli: + 2 ta o'z gapi (biri V1, biri V-ing bilan).

class_ex.title: Ex2 — Passivga aylantiring
class_ex.instr: (5 daq, juftlik) Gapni passivga aylantiring: V1 → to + V1, V-ing o'zgarmaydi. 5 ta gap. ICQ: Passivda V1 qanday o'zgaradi? (to + V1) Yakka yoki juftlikda? (Juftlikda)
items: People saw him leave the ring.
Fans saw him training at 6 am.
They heard the coach shout instructions.
Someone heard her crying after the fight.
Journalists heard him say he would retire.
answers: He was seen to leave the ring.
He was seen training at 6 am.
The coach was heard to shout instructions.
She was heard crying after the fight.
He was heard to say he would retire.
class_ex.note: Kuchsiz: 1–3-bandlar + formula proyektorda; Kuchli: + 2 ta o'z passiv gapi.

class_ex.title: Ex3 — Lug'at + grammatika
class_ex.instr: (5 daq, yakka) Qutidan so'z tanlang va qavsdagi fe'lni V1 yoki V-ing shaklida yozing. 6 ta gap. ICQ: Har gapda nechta bo'shliq? (2) Yakka yoki juftlikda? (Yakka)
items: Everyone expected him to lose — he was the ___, but we saw him ___ (win) the final.
I heard the ___ ___ (shout) instructions from the side of the pitch for the whole match.
In the last minute I saw the ___ ___ (stop) the game and show a red card.
At 6 a.m. we noticed some ___ ___ (run) around the stadium.
The fans watched the captain ___ (lift) the ___ and cheered.
When he fell, I saw his ___ ___ (help) him up — real sportsmanship!
class_ex.note: Kuchsiz: 1–4-bandlar, so'z qutisi bilan; Kuchli: + CORE'dan 2 so'z bilan o'z gapi.

class_ex.title: Ex4 — Xatoni toping (paragraf)
class_ex.instr: (3 daq, juftlik) Paragrafda see/hear/watch/feel + O + fe'l bilan 5 ta xato bor. Topib, tuzating. ICQ: Nechta xato? (5) Yakka yoki juftlikda? (Juftlikda)
items: Last Saturday I went to my cousin's first judo competition. When we arrived, we saw him to warm up with his coach. During his first fight, I heard the coach shouted "Keep going!" again and again. In the last minute I felt my phone vibrated in my pocket, but I didn't look at it. Then we watched the referee to raise my cousin's hand — he had won! Later he was seen cry with happiness in the changing room, and I noticed him smiling all the way home.
answers: saw him to warm up → saw him warming up (yoki warm up)
heard the coach shouted → heard the coach shouting (yoki shout)
felt my phone vibrated → felt my phone vibrate (yoki vibrating)
watched the referee to raise → watched the referee raise
was seen cry → was seen crying (yoki was seen to cry)
class_ex.note: Kuchsiz: ustoz xatoli 5 gapning birinchi so'zlarini aytadi; Kuchli: paragrafni davom ettirish (ZAXIRA) — uyga, homework 6.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Sports (og'zaki): Part 1, 2, 3
class_ex.instr: (12 daq, juftlik) 2' — Part 1: A 4 savolni so'raydi, B javob beradi (javob + sabab + misol), keyin almashadi. 1' — tayyorgarlik: Kartochka A bo'yicha faqat 5–6 kalit so'z. 2' — A gapiradi, B S-CHECK-4.0 ni belgilaydi. 2' — ustoz NAMUNA A ni o'qiydi, o'quvchilar box'dagi eshitgan iboralarini belgilaydi. 2' — B shu kartochkada gapiradi (box'dan 2+ ibora bilan). 2' — Part 3 juftlikda. 1' — ustoz feedback (S-4.0). ICQ: Tayyorgarlikka necha daqiqa? (1) Kartochkada nechta band bor? (4 — 3 ta 'You should say' + 'explain')
items: Part 1: Do you like doing sport? Which one?
Part 1: Did you do much sport when you were a child?
Part 1: Do you prefer watching sport or playing it?
Part 1: Is sport popular in your family?

KARTOCHKA A: Describe a sports match or competition you watched (live or on TV). You should say: what it was ; where and when you watched it ; who you watched it with ; and explain why you remember it.
Part 3: Why do so many people enjoy watching sport?
Part 3: Should PE lessons be compulsory at school?
Part 3: Do top athletes earn too much money?
box: I'd like to talk about a … match I watched …
Our team was the underdog, because …
I saw our players make a lot of mistakes …
I could hear the coach shouting instructions …
I watched the youngest player jump and hit the winning point.
It was a real comeback against the odds.
answers: Part 1 namunalari (faqat ustoz uchun): 1) Yes, I do. I go to a basketball club twice a week after school, because it helps me relax after lessons. Last month our team even played in a city tournament.
2) Quite a lot, actually. When I was seven, my parents took me to a swimming club, and I went there twice a week for four years. I can still hear the coach shouting 'Faster!' in my head.
3) I prefer playing, because I get bored if I just sit and watch. But I enjoy big matches on TV, especially when I can see our national team win.
4) Yes, especially among the men. My father and my brother never miss a football match on TV, and my mother walks for an hour every evening to stay fit.

NAMUNA A (Band 5.5–6, 162 so'z, ~1.5–2 daqiqa): I'd like to talk about a volleyball match I watched last October. It was the final of our regional youth tournament, and I watched it live at the sports hall in our district centre. I went there with my cousin, who plays volleyball herself, so she explained the rules to me. Our local team was the underdog, because the other team had won this tournament three years in a row. In the first set I saw our players make a lot of silly mistakes, and I could hear their coach shouting instructions from the bench. But they didn't give up. In the final set I watched the youngest player jump and hit the winning point, and the whole hall stood up. I remember it because it was a real comeback against the odds. After the match the losing team clapped for the winners, which showed great sportsmanship. For me, it was a lesson that team spirit matters more than a famous name.

Part 3 namunalari: 1) I think people enjoy it because it is exciting and nobody knows the result in advance. It also unites strangers: for example, when fans watch their national team win, the whole country celebrates in the streets.
2) Yes, I believe they should be. Many teenagers have a sedentary lifestyle because they spend hours on their phones, so PE may be the only exercise they get. It also teaches them team spirit.

3) In some cases, yes. A top footballer can earn more in a week than a doctor earns in a year, which seems unfair. However, athletes' careers are short and they entertain millions of fans, so high pay is partly understandable.

ICQ: Nechta abzats yozasiz? (2 — kirish va bitta body) Telefon yoki uydagi inshodan foydalanish mumkinmi? (Yo'q)
items: Question: Some people think watching TV is bad for children. Others believe it has educational value. Discuss both sides and give your opinion.
TASK: In 9 minutes write an introduction + ONE body paragraph (110–140 words). No notes, no phone, no model.
Introduction (2 sentences): paraphrase the question + give your clear opinion.
Body: Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link. Use today's grammar once: see / hear / watch + object + V1 / V-ing.
At the end write the number of words. Check with W-CHECK-4.0: points 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7.
answers: Tahlil: savol turi — discuss both views + opinion; kirishda ikkala fikr parafraz qilinadi va pozitsiya aniq aytiladi; normativda bitta body yoziladi (qaysi tomon — o'quvchi tanlaydi, xulosa shart emas).

NAMUNA — kirish + 1 body (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6; g'oya 8-dars namunasidan farqli — televizor bolani sportga ilhomlantiradi): Many parents worry that television harms their children, while others believe it can teach them useful things. In my opinion, TV is not bad in itself, as long as children watch the right programmes for a limited time. One benefit that people often forget is that TV can inspire children to take up sport. When young viewers see their favourite athletes win a medal, many of them want to copy their heroes. For example, last year my younger brother watched a kurash championship on TV, and a week later he joined a wrestling club. Now he trains three times a week, and his coach says he is very competitive. I have also seen him become more disciplined at school. Therefore, sports programmes can turn screen time into a reason to get off the sofa.
Baholash: W-4.0 (jadval shu mashqdan keyin), NORM-4.0: 10–12 ball — 2 coin; 7–9 — bajarildi; ≤6 — uyda qayta yozadi.

answers: NAMUNA B (Band 5.5–6, 134 so'z, faqat ustoz uchun): A sport I'd really like to try in the future is rock climbing. I became interested in it last summer, when I saw some young people climbing a huge rock in the Chimgan mountains. Beginners can start on an indoor climbing wall in Tashkent, and later, with a coach, they can climb real rocks. You don't need much equipment at first: special shoes, a harness, a helmet and a rope, and most clubs let beginners rent them. I want to try it for two reasons. Firstly, it builds self-confidence, because you have to control your fear. Secondly, it needs mental toughness as well as strength. In a short documentary I watched a climber make a comeback after a serious injury, and it really inspired me. I hope I can join a club next year.

reading.title: Ruslan Chagaev — the night Uzbekistan saw a giant fall
text: A  Ruslan Chagaev was born in 1978 in Andijan. He started boxing as a boy, and people who watched him train soon realised that he had a special talent. He became an amateur world champion and fought for Uzbekistan at the Olympic Games, where many fans expected to see him win a medal. However, he came home without an Olympic medal. Later he turned professional and moved to Germany.

B  In April 2007, in Stuttgart, Chagaev faced Nikolay Valuev, a Russian boxer and the WBA heavyweight champion. Valuev was more than two metres tall, much heavier than Chagaev and had never lost a professional fight. Very few experts expected the smaller man to win; in their eyes, Chagaev was the underdog.

C  Back home, many families stayed up late to watch the fight on television. Round after round they saw the giant move forward, and they could hear the commentators shouting with excitement. Some people were too nervous to sit down. After twelve rounds they heard the final bell ring and watched the judges give a majority decision — to Chagaev. He was now a world heavyweight champion, and fans all over Uzbekistan celebrated his victory.

D  His career was never simple. Health problems and injuries caused some of his fights to be cancelled. In 2009 fans watched him lose to Wladimir Klitschko, one of the best heavyweights of that time. But Chagaev did not give up: in 2014, at the age of 35, he made a comeback and won a WBA title again.

E  Today young boxers can be seen training in gyms all over Uzbekistan, and many of them see Chagaev as a role model. Coaches often say that when children watch a champion win, they want to copy him — and that is how a sport lives.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

Guide: Next to the hall is our swimming pool. Many people think it's fifty metres long, but actually it's twenty-five. On Saturday mornings you can watch small children learn to swim there.
Guide: The centre opened in 2012, not 2010 as some websites say, and today it trains about four hundred young athletes.

kahoot.q: I saw him ___ the street. (boshidan oxirigacha ko'rdim)
kahoot.explain: To'liq harakat → see + ob'ekt + V1: I saw him cross. Aktivda "to" yo'q.

kahoot.q: I heard the bell ___ at exactly 8 o'clock.
kahoot.explain: hear + ob'ekt + V1 (to'liq): heard the bell ring.

kahoot.q: When I passed the park, I saw them ___ football. (jarayonda)
kahoot.explain: Davom etayotgan harakatning bir qismini ko'rdim → V-ing: saw them playing.

kahoot.q: He was seen ___ the building at midnight.
kahoot.explain: Passivda V1 → TO + V1: He was seen to leave.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: I saw him to cross the road.
I saw him cross the road.
I saw him crossing the road.
He was seen to cross the road.
kahoot.explain: Aktivda see + O + V1 (to'siz). "to" faqat passivda: was seen to cross.

kahoot.q: "I saw him cross" va "I saw him crossing" farqi?
kahoot.explain: V1 — nima bo'ldi (boshidan oxirigacha); V-ing — nima bo'layotgan edi (bir lahza).

kahoot.q: I watched Chagaev ___ his opponent on points.
kahoot.explain: To'liq harakat (jang oxirigacha ko'rildi): watch + ob'ekt + V1 → beat. "to", V3 va -s ishlatilmaydi.

kahoot.q: I noticed a man ___ outside my house when I came home.
kahoot.explain: O'sha paytda davom etayotgan jarayon → notice + O + V-ing: a man standing.

kahoot.q: During the earthquake I felt the ground ___.
kahoot.explain: feel + ob'ekt + V1 (yoki V-ing). "to" va V2/V3 ishlatilmaydi.

kahoot.q: The boxer was heard ___ at the referee.
kahoot.explain: Passivda V-ing o'zgarmaydi: was heard shouting (yoki was heard to shout).

kahoot.q: Tarjima: "Uning ringda mashq qilayotganini tomosha qildim."
options: I watched him training in the ring.
I watched him to train in the ring.
I watched him trained in the ring.
I watched to him training in the ring.
kahoot.explain: Jarayon → watch + O + V-ing: watched him training.

kahoot.q: We often see eagles ___ over these mountains. (odat)
kahoot.explain: Takroriy odat → see + ob'ekt + V1: see eagles fly.

kahoot.q: A team or fighter that most people expect to lose is the ___.
kahoot.explain: underdog = kuchsiz hisoblangan tomon.

kahoot.q: He lost the title last year, but this year he made a great ___.
kahoot.explain: make a comeback = kuchli qaytish.

kahoot.q: The ___ stopped the fight after the third knockdown.
kahoot.explain: referee = hakam (jangni to'xtatadi).

kahoot.q: Fair play and respect for your opponent is called ___.
kahoot.explain: sportsmanship = sportcha xulq (halollik, hurmat).

kahoot.q: Taking illegal drugs to perform better in sport is ___.
kahoot.explain: doping = taqiqlangan dori-darmon qabul qilish.

kahoot.q: A cup that you receive for winning a competition is a ___.
kahoot.explain: trophy = kubok (g'olibga beriladi).

kahoot.q: He has never lost a professional fight — he is ___.
kahoot.explain: unbeaten / undefeated = mag'lubiyatsiz.

kahoot.q: "unvonni himoya qilmoq" = ___ a title
kahoot.explain: defend a title = unvonni himoya qilmoq (sport kollokatsiyasi).

intro: ONE / ONES — noaniq o'rinbosar: "I need a pen. Have you got one?" ("one apple" — son, o'rinbosar emas).
THE ONE / THE ONES — aniq: "He is the one I was talking about."
ANOTHER — yana bir; THE OTHER — ikkinchisi; OTHERS — boshqalar; THE OTHERS — qolgan hammasi.
formulas: One — noaniq
one = a + sanaladigan ot (takrorlanmaydi); izoh: "one apple" — son, o'rinbosar emas
I need a pen. Have you got one? / I'd like one, please.
Menga ruchka kerak. Sizda bittasi bormi? / Bittasini bering.
The one — aniq
the one + relative clause / sifat
He is the one I was talking about. / This is the one I like best.
U — men aytgan odam. / Bu — menga eng yoqqani.
Ones / the ones
ko'plik
These shoes are nice — I'll take the red ones. / The ones on sale are cheaper.
Bu tuflilar chiroyli — qizillarini olaman. / Chegirmadagilari arzonroq.
Sifat + one / which one
a/the + sifat + one; Which one?
Have you got a bigger one? / Which one do you prefer?
Kattarog'i bormi? / Qaysi birini afzal ko'rasan?
Another / the other
another one (yana bir); the other one (ikkinchisi)
This bag is small — show me another one. / I'll take the other one.
Bu sumka kichik — boshqasini ko'rsating. / Ikkinchisini olaman.
Others / the others
others (boshqalar); the others (qolgan hammasi)
Some people love brands; others don't care. / I'll buy this one; the others are too expensive.
Ba'zilar brendni sevadi; boshqalarga farqi yo'q. / Buni olaman; qolganlari juda qimmat.
presentation: Which phone do you want?
The one with the best camera.
Do you like these trainers?
I like the white ones, not the black ones.
CCQ: I need a pen. Have you got one?
Do I want a particular pen? (No) Is any pen OK? (Yes)
CCQ: I'll take the red ones. (shoes)
Do we know which shoes? (Yes) Is it one pair or any pair? (the red pair)
CCQ: He's the one I was talking about.
Is it any man? (No) Do we know which man? (Yes — the man I mentioned)
CCQ: I've got two bags. I'll take this one; the other one is too heavy.
How many bags are left? (One) Do we know which one? (Yes)
notes: one — faqat sanaladigan ot o'rnida; sanalmas ot o'rnida some: "Do you want some?"
"the one" odatda aniqlovchi bilan: the one I like / the red one / the one on the left; kontekstdan aniq bo'lsa yolg'iz ham: "Yes, this is the one."
one = umumiy odam (rasmiy Writing): "One should save money."
O'quvchi so'raydi: "Give me one apple" dagi one — o'rinbosarmi? — Javob: yo'q, bu son. O'rinbosar one otsiz keladi: Have you got one?
O'quvchi so'raydi: Nega tuflilar haqida "the red ones"? — Javob: shoes — ko'plik, ko'plik ot o'rnida ones.
O'quvchi so'raydi: "those ones" deyish mumkinmi? — Javob: og'zaki nutqda uchraydi; Writing'da these / those yolg'iz: cheaper than those.
mistakes: He is one I was talking about.
He is the one I was talking about.
I like the red one. (ko'plik tuflilar)
Show me another one. / Show me the other one.
Do you have a milk? — Yes, I have one.
Do you have any milk? — Yes, I have some.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Shopping (og'zaki): Part 1, 2, 3
class_ex.instr: (12 daq, juftlik) 2' — Part 1: A 4 savolni so'raydi, B javob beradi (javob + sabab + misol), keyin almashadi. 1' — tayyorgarlik: Kartochka A bo'yicha faqat 5–6 kalit so'z. 2' — A gapiradi, B S-CHECK-4.0 ni belgilaydi. 2' — ustoz NAMUNA A ni o'qiydi, o'quvchilar box'dagi eshitgan iboralarini belgilaydi. 2' — B shu kartochkada gapiradi (box'dan 2+ ibora bilan). 2' — Part 3 juftlikda. 1' — ustoz feedback (S-4.0). ICQ: Tayyorgarlikka necha daqiqa? (1) Kartochkada nechta band bor? (4 — 3 ta 'You should say' + 'explain')
items: Part 1: Do you like shopping? Why or why not?
Part 1: Where do you usually buy your clothes?
Part 1: Do you prefer shopping alone or with friends?
Part 1: Have you ever bought something online?
KARTOCHKA A: Describe something you bought recently that you are happy with. You should say: what it is ; where you bought it ; how much it cost ; and explain why you are happy with it.
Part 3: Why do young people like buying brand-name clothes?
Part 3: Is it better to shop in markets or in shopping centres?
Part 3: Do people today buy more things than they need?
box: I'd like to talk about a … that I bought about … ago.
My old one was …, so I really needed a new one.
The shop assistant showed me two …: a … one and a … one.
I chose the black one / the cheaper one because …
It cost about … so'm, which was real value for money.
It wasn't an impulse buy, because I had compared prices …
I don't need a luxury label; I just need …
I'm happy with this purchase for a few reasons. First, …
answers: Part 1 namunalari (faqat ustoz uchun): 1) Yes, I do, but only when I have a clear reason to go. I enjoy looking for a bargain, for example during end-of-season sales, when good jackets are half price.

2) Mostly at the bazaar near my house, because the clothes there are affordable and you can choose from many sellers. If I need something smart, like a shirt for a wedding, I go to a shopping centre with my parents.
3) I prefer shopping alone, because I can take my time and I don't spend money just because my friends are buying something. But when I choose a present, I sometimes ask my sister to help me.
4) Yes, a few times. Last month I ordered a phone case online and it arrived in three days. The only problem was that the colour was different from the one in the photo.

NAMUNA A (Band 5.5–6, 179 so'z, ~1.5–2 daqiqa): I'd like to talk about a backpack that I bought about three weeks ago. My old one was torn and the zip was broken, so I really needed a replacement before the new term. I went to a sports shop near Chorsu bazaar with my older brother. The shop assistant showed me two backpacks: a grey backpack from a famous brand and a black one without a big logo. The grey one was nearly twice as expensive, so I chose the black one. It cost about two hundred and fifty thousand so'm, which I think was real value for money. I'm happy with this purchase for a few reasons. First, it is light but strong, and it has a special pocket for my laptop. Second, it wasn't an impulse buy, because I had compared prices in three shops before I decided. And finally, I paid for half of it with my own pocket money, so I feel proud every time I take it to school. Honestly, I don't need a luxury label; I just need a bag that works.

Part 3 namunalari: 1) I think the main reason is that a famous logo is a status symbol at school or university, so young people want to look successful in front of their friends. Advertising campaigns with popular bloggers also make these brands look cool.

2) It depends on what people need. Markets are usually cheaper and customers can bargain, especially for fruit and vegetables. However, shopping centres are more comfortable in hot weather, and the quality of clothes there is often more reliable.

3) Yes, I believe many people do. Online sales encourage impulse buying, so people order things they never use. For example, some families already have several phones at home, but they still buy a new one every year, and this overconsumption creates a lot of waste.
class_ex.note: S-CHECK-4.0 (sherik belgilaydi: Ha / Yo'q): 1) kartochkadagi 4 band aytildimi; 2) 1.5 daqiqadan uzoq, uzun pauzasiz; 3) box'dan 2+ ibora; 4) bugungi grammatika (one / ones / the one(s), another / the other) 1–2 marta to'g'ri; 5) Part 3 javobi: fikr + sabab + misol. class_ex.title: WRITING — Brand-name clothes (yozma): Task 2 body paragraf
class_ex.instr: (12 daq, yakka) 2 daq — savol tahlili: savol turi, savolda nechta savol bor, sinfda qaysi qismini yozamiz. 8 daq — BITTA body paragraf, faqat sabablar ('Why is this?'), 100–120 so'z, qolip: Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link; oxirida so'z sonini yozing. 2 daq — sherik bilan almashib W-CHECK-4.0 bo'yicha tekshirasiz; ustoz 1 paragrafni W-4.0 bo'yicha ovoz chiqarib baholaydi. ICQ: Sinfda paragraf nima haqida? (Sabablar — nega yoshlar brendga ko'p pul sarflaydi) Necha so'z? (100–120)
box: Question: Many young people spend a lot of money on brand-name clothes. Why is this? Is it a positive or negative development?
Useful: There are several reasons why … / The main one is that … / In addition, … / For example, … / As a result, …
Ideas: status symbol · advertising campaigns and bloggers · peer pressure · quality vs label
items: Savol turi qanday? Savolda nechta savol bor va to'liq inshoda nechta body kerak?
Sinfda qaysi savolga javob beramiz: 'Why is this?' yoki 'positive or negative'?
Kalit so'zlarni qanday parafraz qilasiz (young people, spend a lot of money, brand-name clothes)?
Bugungi grammatika qayerga mos keladi: the main one, cheaper ones, the other …?
Qaysi EW10 so'zlari bu mavzuga mos (kamida 4 ta)?
TASK: Write ONE body paragraph about the reasons (100–120 words): Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link.
answers: 1) Ikki qismli savol (reasons + positive/negative development): 2 ta savol -> to'liq inshoda 2 ta body. Body 1 — sabablar, Body 2 — ijobiy yoki salbiy (pozitsiya kirishda aytiladi va Body 2 da asoslanadi).
2) Sinfda faqat 'Why is this?' — sabablar paragrafi. Positive/negative — uyga QO'SHIMCHA (Body 2).
3) young people -> teenagers / the young generation; spend a lot of money -> pay so much / are ready to pay; brand-name clothes -> designer labels / famous brands.
4) The main one is that … (one = reason), cheaper ones (ones = trainers), the other children (aniq qolgan guruh).
5) EW10: status symbol, advertising campaign, disposable income, brand loyalty, trend, materialism, affordable, value for money, luxury.

NAMUNA paragraf — sabablar (faqat ustoz uchun, 110 so'z): There are several reasons why young people are ready to pay so much for brand-name clothes. The main one is that a famous logo works as a status symbol: teenagers want their classmates to see them as modern and successful. In addition, advertising campaigns on Instagram and TikTok use popular bloggers, so a plain T-shirt with the right logo suddenly looks cool. Peer pressure also plays a role. For example, if most students in a class wear expensive trainers, a teenager who wears cheaper ones may feel left out. As a result, many young people spend their pocket money, or their parents' disposable income, on labels rather than on quality.
Namuna: 110 so'z (Topic sentence -> 3 sabab -> misol -> As a result). Bugungi struktura 2 marta: The main one, cheaper ones.
Baholash: W-4.0 (jadval shu darsda) + W-CHECK-4.0 (7-band: paragraf 100–120 so'z); NORM-4.0 — body paragraf: 10–12 — 1 coin; ≤6 — uyda qayta.
why: Bugungi grammatika: 'The main one is that …' — one avval aytilgan 'reason' o'rnida keladi, so'z takrorlanmaydi; 'cheaper ones' — ko'plik 'trainers' o'rnida ones (sifat + ones).
Writing'da 'those ones' emas, 'cheaper ones / the ones in the window' kabi aniqlovchi bilan ishlatamiz.

EW10 so'zlari: status symbol — obro' belgisi; advertising campaign — reklama kampaniyasi; disposable income — erkin sarflanadigan daromad; label — yorliq/brend; peer pressure — tengdoshlar bosimi (izohli ibora).
Bog'lovchilar: In addition, also, For example, As a result — 4 xil, W-CHECK 4-band uchun yetarli.
O'zbek misoli: sinfdagi qimmat krossovkalar — aniq, hayotiy misol TR va CC uchun ball beradi.

homework.instr: MAJBURIY. 1 daqiqa tayyorgarlik (faqat 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1.5–2 daqiqa to'xtamasdan gapirib, ovozli yozuvni ilovaga yuboring. Matndan o'qimang. items: KARTOCHKA B: Describe a shop or market that you like to visit. You should say: where it is ; what it sells ; how often you go there ; and explain why you like it.
answers: NAMUNA B (Band 5.5–6, 158 so'z, faqat ustoz uchun): I'm going to describe a small second-hand clothes shop near my school in Samarkand. It's on a quiet street, so it's easy to miss. The shop sells used jackets, jeans and shoes, and some of them look almost new. I go there about once a month, usually on Saturday after my English lesson. There are two reasons why I like it. First, the prices are really affordable: last time I found a denim jacket for only eighty thousand so'm, which was a real bargain. The owner always shows me the ones that have just arrived, and if I don't like a jacket, she quickly finds another one in my size. Second, I think buying used clothes is a kind of sustainable fashion. Fast fashion creates a lot of waste, while this shop gives old clothes a second life. So for me, it's the one place where I can save money and help the environment at the same time.
Bugungi struktura: the ones that have just arrived, another one in my size, the one place; EW10: affordable, bargain, sustainable fashion, fast fashion.

homework.instr: STRONG 20 ni o'rganing; ovozli normativ: CORE 20 + tarjima + 1 gap, 2 daqiqa (Jony Student).
homework.answers: Ovozli normativ (CORE 20, 2 daq) — 1 coin; STRONG 20 yozma — +2 coin.

homework.title: 7. QO'SHIMCHA — WRITING — Brand-name clothes: Body 2 (positive or negative), 100–120 so'z (yozma)
homework.instr: Sinfdagi sabablar paragrafini W-CHECK-4.0 bo'yicha tuzating va ikkinchi body paragraf yozing: bu holat ijobiymi yoki salbiymi? Pozitsiya 1-gapda aniq, 2 dalil + O'zbekistondan 1 misol + xulosa gap. 100–120 so'z; bugungi struktura 1–2 marta; oxirida so'z sonini yozing.
items: Question: Many young people spend a lot of money on brand-name clothes. Why is this? Is it a positive or negative development?
Plan: Topic sentence (your position) -> Reason 1 + explain -> Reason 2 -> Example -> Link.
answers: NAMUNA Body 2 (Band 5.5–6, 110 so'z, Jony Academy original, faqat ustoz uchun): In my opinion, this trend is mostly a negative development. Firstly, brand-name clothes are often no better than cheaper ones, so customers mainly pay for the label, not for the quality. Secondly, this kind of materialism can damage friendships, because teenagers start to judge each other by what they wear. It also puts pressure on families with a small budget. For instance, some parents in Uzbekistan borrow money to buy their child the same jacket as the other children in the class. Instead, young people could choose affordable, good-quality clothes and spend the money they save on courses or books. Therefore, following brands so closely does more harm than good.
Bugungi struktura: cheaper ones, the other children; EW10: trend, materialism, affordable.
Baholash: W-4.0 (class_ex dagi jadval), NORM-4.0: 10–12 ball — 1 coin; ≤6 — qayta yozadi.
homework.note: Namuna o'quvchiga baholangandan keyin ko'rsatiladi. Ijobiy pozitsiya ham qabul qilinadi, agar 2 dalil va misol bo'lsa.

normativ: CORE 20, 4 daqiqa yozish + 1 daqiqa tekshirish; 18–20 to'g'ri
Kombinatsiya — one / ones / the one(s) + aniqlovchi
juftlikda 3 daqiqada: 4 to'g'ri gap = warm-up; 6 = normativ; 8 = coin
CORE 20: inglizcha → o'zbekcha + 1 gap, 2 daqiqa; yozma — 11-darsda

reading.title: Rihanna — the one who found a gap in the beauty market
text: A. Robyn Rihanna Fenty was born in 1988 in Barbados, a small island in the Caribbean. As a teenager, she sang for an American music producer who was on holiday there, and he was the one who helped her start a career in the United States. Within a few years, her songs were playing on radio stations around the world, and she became one of the best-known pop stars of her generation.

B. Many famous singers make extra money by selling perfume with their name on it. Rihanna wanted to do something different. She had noticed that most makeup companies produced foundation in only a small number of shades, and very few of them were the ones that matched darker skin. Millions of women saw beauty products everywhere, but they rarely found one made for them.

C. In 2017 she launched Fenty Beauty. From the first day, its foundation came in 40 shades, and some of the darkest ones quickly sold out in many shops. Soon other companies started to offer more shades too, and people in the beauty industry began to talk about "the Fenty effect".

D. Rihanna did not simply lend her name to the brand. She kept a large share of the company, and this was the decision that made her rich: in 2021 Forbes magazine named her a billionaire, mainly because of her part of Fenty Beauty. Her fashion brand, Savage X Fenty, also became known for using models of many different sizes and skin colours. She often explains that customers want to see people like themselves in adverts.

E. In 2021 Barbados became a republic, and at the ceremony Rihanna was named a National Hero of the country. Today many young people see her as more than a singer. For them, she is the one who showed that a good business idea can start with a simple question: who has the market forgotten?
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; 1-rol — ustoz, 2-rol — kuchli o'quvchi (yoki ovozni o'zgartiring).
Assistant: Good afternoon. Can I help you?
Customer: Yes, please. I'm looking for a jacket — a warm one for the winter.
Assistant: We've got two winter jackets at the moment: a blue one and a grey one.
Customer: Which one is warmer?
Assistant: The grey one. The blue one is lighter — it's really for autumn.
Customer: Then I'll take the grey one. How much is it?
Assistant: The blue one is 400,000 sums, and the grey one is 380,000 — oh, sorry, it's on sale this week, so it's 350,000.
Customer: Great. Have you got it in large?
Assistant: I'm afraid the large ones have all sold out. This is the last one in medium; the others are small.
Customer: Medium is fine, thanks.
Assistant: Would you like a loyalty card? I just need your surname.
Customer: Sure. It's Karimova.
Assistant: Is that K-A-R-I-M-O-V-A?
Customer: Yes, that's right.
Assistant: Thank you. And if the jacket doesn't fit, you can bring it back.
Customer: How long do I have? Seven days?
Assistant: No, you have 14 days. But please bring the receipt — without it we can only exchange the jacket for another one.
Customer: OK, I'll keep the receipt. Thank you!

kahoot.q: These shoes are nice. I'll take the red ___.
kahoot.explain: Ko'plik ot (shoes) o'rnida → ones: the red ones.

kahoot.q: He is ___ I was talking about.
kahoot.explain: Aniq, ma'lum shaxs (relative clause bilan) → the one.

kahoot.q: I need a pen. Have you got ___?
kahoot.explain: Noaniq, istalgan bittasi → one (= a pen).

kahoot.q: This bag is too small. Can you show me ___ one?
kahoot.explain: Yana bir boshqasi → another one. "other one" — xato.

kahoot.q: I have two brothers. One is a doctor; ___ is a teacher.
kahoot.explain: Ikkitadan qolgan bittasi → the other.

kahoot.q: Some people love brands; ___ don't care about them.
kahoot.explain: Some people ... others ... = ba'zilar ... boshqalar ...

kahoot.q: Do you want some milk? — Yes, I'd like ___.
kahoot.explain: one faqat sanaladigan ot o'rnida; sanalmas (milk) → some.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
kahoot.explain: "other one" yolg'iz ishlatilmaydi: another one yoki the other one.

kahoot.q: ___ one do you prefer — the black or the white?
kahoot.explain: Tanlov orasidan → Which one?

kahoot.q: I'll buy this jacket; ___ are too expensive.
kahoot.explain: Qolganlarning hammasi (ko'plik, aniq) → the others.

kahoot.q: "___ should always save some money." (har bir odam)
kahoot.explain: Rasmiy yozuvda one = umumiy odam: One should save money.

kahoot.q: Tarjima: "Kattarog'i bormi?"
options: Have you got a bigger one?
Have you got a bigger ones?
kahoot.explain: Sifat + one: a bigger one (birlik, noaniq).

kahoot.q: Buying things you didn't plan to buy is ___.
kahoot.explain: impulse buying = o'ylamay (to'satdan) xarid qilish.

kahoot.q: Only 50,000 so'm for these jeans — what a ___!
kahoot.explain: bargain = arzon, foydali xarid.

kahoot.q: A fake designer bag sold at the bazaar is ___.
kahoot.explain: counterfeit = soxta (qalbaki).

kahoot.q: Cheap clothes made quickly and thrown away after a few months are ___.
kahoot.explain: fast fashion = tez moda (arzon, tez almashadigan kiyim).

kahoot.q: Money you can spend after paying taxes and basic needs is ___ income.
kahoot.explain: disposable income = erkin sarflasa bo'ladigan daromad.

kahoot.q: The phone was broken, so the shop gave me a ___.
kahoot.explain: refund = pulni qaytarish.

kahoot.q: Always buying the same brand is called brand ___.
kahoot.explain: brand loyalty = brendga sodiqlik.

kahoot.q: "hamyonbop" — inglizcha?
kahoot.explain: affordable = hamyonbop (narxi qo'l yetadigan).

timeline: Salomlashish
Ustoz 'John broke the window.' → 'It was John who broke the window.' deb aytadi: 'Nima o'zgardi?' (ta'kid).
TAKROR: Kahoot — 10-dars (One vs the one)
'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi → 10-dars savollari (20 ta). Bugungi darsning Kahooti bu yerda EMAS — u 12-darsda o'ynaladi. Oxirgi 1 daqiqa: eng ko'p xato qilingan 2 savol izohi.
TAKROR: Yozma normativ — Essential Words 10 (Consumerism, fashion and shopping)

Normativ — belgilangan vaqtda bajariladigan qisqa o'lchov; natijasiga qarab coin beriladi. 10-dars CORE 20: ustoz o'zbekchasini aytadi, o'quvchi inglizchasini yozadi — 4 daq; 1 daq sherik bilan almashib tekshirish. 18–20 = 2 coin; 15–17 = bajarildi; 14 va kam = 12-darsda qayta topshiradi.
PROGRESS TEST 2 (pt2) — 6–10-darslar

Test: tests/pt2 (tizim). Bo'limlar: A Grammatika 15 (10 daq) · B Lug'at 10 (5) · C Reading 8 (10) · D Listening 5 (5; ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi) · E Writing 12 (10; W-4.0) = 50 ball. O'tish: jami ≥ 70% va har bo'limda ≥ 50%. Telefonlar yig'iladi; javoblar test paytida ko'rsatilmaydi; natija tahlili 12-darsda.
YANGI GRAMMATIKA — Emphasis (cleft, what-clause, emphatic do) + CCQ

Lead-in misoli (John broke the window → 3 xil urg'u) → formula (proyektor, formulas 1–4) → 2–3 misol (presentation) → CCQ → 1 daqiqalik tez og'zaki tekshiruv. It-cleft 6 daq, what-clause 4, emphatic do 3, CCQ + tekshiruv 3. Fronting/inversiya — ZAXIRA.
LUG'AT — Essential Words 11 CORE 20

Ustoz 20 so'zni proyektorda talaffuz + tarjima bilan o'qitadi (2 daq); 5–6 qiyin so'zga (hypothesis, evidence, pioneer…) CCQ yoki misol (2 daq); juftlikda A o'zbekchasini, B inglizchasini aytadi (2 daq). Mustahkamlash — flashcard (uyga).
Kombinatsiya — It is/was … that/who · What … is/was · do/did + V1

Kombinatsiya — juftlikda formula → gap → tarjima zanjiri: A formulani yoki o'zbekcha gapni aytadi, B shu formula bilan inglizcha gap tuzib tarjima qiladi, keyin almashadi. 1 daq — ustoz grammar.formulas dan formulani va 1 misolni proyektorda ko'rsatadi; 2 daq — juftlikda (me'yor normativ[1] da); ustoz 2 juftlikni tinglaydi.
SINF MASHQLARI — Ex1–Ex3 (MAJBURIY) + ZAXIRA
Ex1 4 daq yakka · Ex2 6 daq juftlik · Ex3 6 daq yakka + juftlikda tekshirish; ZAXIRA (fronting/inversiya, WRITING paragrafi) — vaqt qolsa.
WRITING — Living longer

class_ex WRITING bo'yicha (test darsi taqsimoti). 2 daq — savol tahlili: savol turi (problems + solutions — ikkala qismga javob), kalit so'zlar (living longer, problems, solved), pozitsiya, nechta body. 4 daq — NAMUNA kirish + Body 1 tahlili (box, proyektorda: topic sentence, bog'lovchilar, bugungi grammatika — does create, It is … who, EW so'zlari). 4 daq — Body 2 (yechimlar) va xulosa REJASI: g'oya / izoh / misol jadvali, sherik bilan W-CHECK-4.0 bo'yicha solishtirish. To'liq insho uyda (40 daq, 220–260 so'z, W-4.0). Speaking kartochkalari uyga QO'SHIMCHA bo'ldi.
LISTENING — IELTS Part 4
1 daq — savollarni o'qish; 1-tinglash (3 daq); 2-tinglash (3 daq); 1 daq — javoblar proyektorda. Yakka.
Xatolar ustida ishlash + uyga vazifa

2 daq — dars davomida ustoz yozib borgan 3–4 ta og'zaki xato doskada, o'quvchilar tuzatadi (error log); 3 daq — uyga vazifa: 1–4 majburiy (4 — 'Living longer' inshosi, 40 daq, 220–260 so'z), 5–8 qo'shimcha. Vaqt yetmasa: ZAXIRA mashqlar va reading'ning 'find' topshirig'i uyga o'tadi.

intro: CLEFT (It-cleft): It + is/was + TA'KID + that/who + qolgan gap — kim, nima yoki qachon ekaniga urg'u.
WHAT-CLAUSE: What + ega + fe'l + is/was + TA'KID. Shunga o'xshash: "All I want is…", "The only thing that matters is…".
EMPHATIC DO: do/does/did + V1 — fe'lga urg'u (rostdan, haqiqatan); buyruqda ham: "Do sit down."
ZAXIRA (kuchlilar uchun): fronting ("This book, I really enjoyed.") va inkor so'zdan keyin inversiya ("Never had a woman won…").
formulas: It-cleft (kim)
It + was + SHAXS + who/that + …
It was John who broke the window.
Oynani sindirgan aynan Jon edi.
It-cleft (nima / qachon)
It + is/was + NARSA/VAQT + that + …
It is honesty that matters most. / It was in 1898 that radium was discovered.
Eng muhimi — halollik. / Radiy aynan 1898-da kashf etilgan.
What-clause
What + S + V + is/was + TA'KID
What I need is a break. / What he said was shocking.
Menga kerak narsa — dam olish. / U aytgan narsa hayratlanarli edi.
Emphatic do
S + do/does/did + V1
I do like this movie! / She did finish her work.
Men bu filmni rostdan yoqtiraman! / U ishini haqiqatan tugatdi.
ZAXIRA: Fronting
OB'EKT / HOLAT + S + V
This book, I really enjoyed.
Bu kitobni men rostdan yoqtirdim.
ZAXIRA: Inkor fronting + inversiya
Never / Not only / Rarely + yordamchi + S + V
Never had a woman won a Nobel Prize before 1903. / Not only did she win a Nobel Prize in physics, but she also won one in chemistry.
1903-yilgacha hech bir ayol Nobel mukofotini olmagan edi. / U nafaqat fizika bo'yicha Nobel mukofotini oldi, balki kimyo bo'yicha ham oldi.
presentation: Who discovered radium?
It was Marie and Pierre Curie who discovered radium.
What did she discover?
What she discovered was two new elements: polonium and radium.
Did she really work in a cold shed?
She did work in a cold shed for four years.
When did she win her first Nobel Prize?
It was in 1903 that she won her first Nobel Prize.
What is amazing about her notebooks?
What is amazing is that her notebooks are still radioactive today.
CCQ: It was Aziz who broke the window — not Bobur.
Are we talking about WHO broke the window? (Yes) Did Bobur break it? (No)
CCQ: What I need is a break.
Do I need a break? (Yes) What is the important information? (a break)
CCQ: I do like chemistry!
Do I like chemistry? (Yes) Does 'do' change the meaning or make it stronger? (stronger — 'really')
CCQ: It was in 1898 that she found radium.
Is the important information the year? (Yes) Is it 'that' or 'when' after 'It was in 1898'? (that)
notes: It-cleft: shaxs → who yoki that; narsa/vaqt/joy → that. "It was yesterday that…" (odatda when emas).
What-clause'dan keyin odatda is/was (What I need IS a break); ta'kid ko'plik ot bo'lsa, are ham mumkin (What we need are more teachers).
Emphatic do — Present Simple, Past Simple va buyruq gapda (Do sit down!); boshqa zamonlarda urg'u ohang bilan beriladi (I HAVE finished).
O'quvchi so'raydi: "I like" va "I do like" farqi nima? — Javob: ma'no bir xil, do "rostdan ham" urg'usini beradi, ko'pincha shubhaga javobda: "You don't like science." — "I do like it!"
O'quvchi so'raydi: It-cleft'da who yoki that? — Javob: shaxs bo'lsa ikkalasi ham to'g'ri (It was Marie who/that…); narsa, vaqt, joy bo'lsa — that.
mistakes: It was John that he broke the window.
It was John who broke the window.
What I need are a break.
What I need is a break.
Ta'kidlangan qism birlik ot (a break) → is.
Never a woman had won before.
Never had a woman won before.
It is in 1898 when radium was discovered.
It was in 1898 that radium was discovered.
O'tgan voqea → was; ta'kidlangan vaqtdan keyin → that.

how: CORE 20 — fan va tadqiqot asoslari; STRONG — ilmiy jarayon va fan sohalari; SUPER — fan mavzusidagi IELTS Writing/Speaking kollokatsiyalari.
Misolda so'zning o'zi albatta bo'ladi, gap tabiiy va faktik to'g'ri; bugungi grammatika qolipi — ixtiyoriy, faqat tabiiy tushsa.
core: It was her discovery of radium that changed medicine.
Aynan uning radiy kashfiyoti tibbiyotni o'zgartirdi.
What scientists need is a repeatable experiment.
It is the hypothesis that guides the experiment.
What convinces scientists is evidence, not opinion.
It was Einstein who published the theory of special relativity in 1905.
Maxsus nisbiylik nazariyasini 1905-yilda aynan Eynshteyn e'lon qildi.
What she asked for was a proper laboratory.
U so'ragan narsa — to'g'ri laboratoriya edi.
It is research that turns ideas into medicine.
What I would like to invent is a robot that cleans my room.
Men ixtiro qilmoqchi bo'lgan narsa — xonamni tozalaydigan robot.
What our school lab needs is a better microscope.
Maktab laboratoriyamizga kerak narsa — yaxshiroq mikroskop.
It was two elements that she discovered, not one.
U bitta emas, ikkita element kashf etdi.
What makes uranium dangerous is its radiation.
Uranni xavfli qiladigan narsa — uning nurlanishi.
It was a physicist and a chemist who worked together.
Birga ishlaganlar — fizik va kimyogar edi.
What the data shows is a clear pattern.
It is careful analysis that separates science from guessing.
What students must learn is the scientific method.
Talabalar o'rganishi shart narsa — ilmiy metod.
It was one observation that started the research.
What the experiment proved was that the hypothesis was wrong.
Tajriba isbotlagan narsa — gipotezaning noto'g'ri ekani edi.
She did become a pioneer, despite every obstacle.
U har qanday to'siqqa qaramay chinakam kashshof bo'ldi.
What matters most in science is curiosity.
It was knowledge that she valued above money.
U puldan ustun qo'ygan narsa — bilim edi.
strong: It was Curie who coined the word "radioactivity".
She named polonium after her homeland, Poland.
U poloniyni vatani Polsha sharafiga nomladi.
It was uranium rays that first caught her attention.
Uning e'tiborini birinchi tortgan — uran nurlari edi.
What took four years was isolating a tenth of a gram.
To'rt yil olgan narsa — o'ndan bir gramm ajratib olish edi.
It is peer review that keeps science honest.
What every researcher wants is to publish in a good journal.
Har bir tadqiqotchi xohlaydigan narsa — yaxshi jurnalda maqola chop etish.
What she refused was a patent — she wanted radium free for all.
U rad etgan narsa — patent; radiy hamma uchun bepul bo'lishini xohladi.
It was funding that she lacked, not ideas.
Unga yetishmagan narsa — g'oya emas, moliya edi.
What every young researcher needs is a good teacher.
Har bir yosh tadqiqotchiga kerak narsa — yaxshi ustoz.
Scientists usually need several years to develop a safe vaccine.
Olimlarga xavfsiz vaksina yaratish uchun odatda bir necha yil kerak bo'ladi.
Everything around us is made of atoms.
Atrofimizdagi hamma narsa atomlardan tashkil topgan.
It was her mobile X-ray units that helped doctors in the First World War.
Birinchi jahon urushida shifokorlarga yordam bergan narsa — uning ko'chma rentgen qurilmalari edi.
Radiation is still used in cancer treatment today.
Nurlanish bugun ham saraton davosida qo'llaniladi.
What a scientist needs is healthy scepticism.
It was her precision that convinced the doubters.
What she used was trial and error, tonne after tonne of ore.
U qo'llagan usul — sinov va xato, tonna-tonna ruda.
It is ethics that limits what science may do.
Fan nima qilishi mumkinligini cheklaydigan — axloq.
What genetics explains is why we look like our parents.
Genetika tushuntiradigan narsa — nega ota-onamizga o'xshashimiz.
What interests my brother most is robotics.
Akamni eng ko'p qiziqtiradigan narsa — robototexnika.

class_ex.title: A. Grammatika (15 ball: 15 × 1) — 10 daqiqa
class_ex.type: 1–8 — MCQ; 9–12 — bo'shliq; 13–15 — xatoni toping (har darsdan 3 ta: 6–10)
class_ex.instr: 1–8: Choose the correct answer A, B, C or D. 9–12: Write ONE word in each gap; use the word in brackets if there is one. 13–15: Each sentence has ONE mistake. Underline it and write the correct version. (1–8: to'g'ri javobni tanlang; 9–12: har bo'shliqqa BITTA so'z yozing, qavsdagi so'z bo'lsa — uni to'g'ri shaklda; 13–15: har gapda BITTA xato bor — tagiga chizing va to'g'ri variantini yozing.)
items: 1. In our school, students ___ use their phones during lessons — it's against the rules. A) aren't allowed to  B) don't allow to  C) aren't allowed  D) can't allowed to
2. Tom ___ meet us at the station at six, but he forgot and stayed at home. A) is supposed to  B) was supposed to  C) supposed to  D) was supposing to
3. ___ Syr Darya flows into ___ Aral Sea. A) The / the  B) — / the  C) The / —  D) — / —
4. My little brother is seven. He goes to ___ school every morning to study. A) the  B) a  C) — (no article)  D) an
5. The exam starts in ten minutes. You ___ hurry, or you'll be late. A) had better to  B) had better  C) would rather  D) prefer to
6. I don't feel like going out tonight. I'd rather ___ at home. A) to stay  B) staying  C) stay  D) stayed
7. I watched the runner ___ the finish line and raise his arms. A) to cross  B) crossed  C) cross  D) crosses
8. These trainers are too small. Have you got any bigger ___? A) one  B) ones  C) the one  D) the ones
9. Mount Everest is ___ highest mountain in the world.
10. Most teenagers prefer streaming music ___ buying CDs.
11. I noticed a boy ___ (sit) alone in the corner of the canteen, so I went to talk to him.
12. I've lost my pen, so I need to buy a new ___. (Do not write 'pen'.)
13. Visitors are not permitted take photos inside the museum.
14. I saw the goalkeeper to catch the ball with one hand.
15. This is one I told you about — the cheapest phone in the shop.
answers: 1. A — aren't allowed to (6-dars: be allowed to + V1).
2. B — was supposed to (6-dars: rejalashtirilgan, lekin bo'lmagan).
3. A — The / the (7-dars: daryo va dengiz nomi — the).
4. C — artiklsiz: go to school (7-dars: muassasa vazifa ma'nosida — the'siz).
5. B — had better (8-dars: had better + V1, ogohlantirish).
6. C — stay (8-dars: would rather + V1, to yo'q).
7. C — cross (9-dars: watch + O + V1 — butun harakat; 'raise' ham V1).

11. sitting (9-dars: notice + O + V-ing — bola allaqachon o'tirgan edi, jarayon/holat davom etayotgan edi). 'sit' — 0: V1 butun harakatni bildiradi ('I saw him sit down' — o'tirib olganini boshidan oxirigacha ko'rdim), bu gapda esa holat davom etmoqda.
12. one (10-dars: noaniq — a new one; 'pen' — 0, shartda taqiqlangan).
13. permitted take → permitted TO take (6-dars: be permitted to + V1).
14. saw the goalkeeper to catch → saw the goalkeeper CATCH (catching ham qabul) (9-dars: aktivda to yo'q).
15. This is one → This is THE ONE I told you about (10-dars: aniq, aniqlovchi bilan — the one).

class_ex.title: C. Reading (8 ball: 8 × 1) — 10 daqiqa: Fix It, Don't Throw It Away
class_ex.type: Original matn (EW10 — consumerism mavzusi); 1–4 — TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN; 5–8 — sentence completion
class_ex.instr: Read the text. 1–4: Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN. 5–8: Complete the sentences. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the text for each answer. (Matnni o'qing. 1–4: TRUE — matnga mos, FALSE — matnga zid, NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqda ma'lumot yo'q. 5–8: gaplarni to'ldiring — matndan ko'pi bilan IKKI so'z.)
box: FIX IT, DON'T THROW IT AWAY

A. Every year, people around the world throw away millions of phones, kettles and jackets that could still be used. Fast fashion and cheap electronics make it easy to buy a new one instead of repairing the old one. But a growing number of people would rather fix their things than replace them, and repair cafés are helping them do it.

B. A repair café is not really a café. It is a free meeting, usually held once a month in a school, a library or a community centre. Visitors bring broken items, and volunteers with practical skills — electricians, tailors and bike mechanics — show them how to repair them. Visitors are not supposed to leave their item and go home; they are expected to sit with the volunteer and learn. Tea is usually free, and that is where the name comes from.

C. Last spring, a group of university students started a monthly repair café in a Tashkent neighbourhood. At the first meeting only twelve people came, most of them pensioners with old radios. By the fourth meeting, more than sixty visitors arrived, and the most common items were not radios but phone chargers and school bags. The students say the biggest surprise was how many teenagers came.

D. Repair cafés cannot solve the problem of overconsumption alone. Some modern products are designed so that owners are not allowed to open them without losing the guarantee. Still, the organisers believe the idea changes the way people think. One volunteer explains that when you see an old kettle work again, you start to ask whether you really needed another one. So the next time an advertising campaign tells you to buy the newest model, you had better ask the same question.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)
items: 1. Repair cafés charge visitors a small fee for each repair.
2. At a repair café, visitors are expected to learn how to repair the item themselves.
3. Most of the people at the first Tashkent meeting were older people.
4. The Tashkent students are planning to open a second repair café next year.
5. Repair cafés usually take place in a school, a library or a ________.
6. At the first Tashkent meeting, many visitors brought old ________.
7. By the fourth meeting, the most common items were phone chargers and ________.
8. Owners of some modern products lose the ________ if they open them.
answers: 1. FALSE — B: 'It is a free meeting'.
2. TRUE — B: 'they are expected to sit with the volunteer and learn'.
4. NOT GIVEN — C: kelajakdagi reja haqida hech narsa aytilmagan.

items: RECEPTIONIST: Good afternoon, City Youth Sports Centre. How can I help you?
STUDENT: Hi. I'd like to join one of your evening courses. Can I register by phone?
RECEPTIONIST: Of course. What's your name, please?
STUDENT: Madina Rakhimova. That's R-A-K-H-I-M-O-V-A.
RECEPTIONIST: Thank you. And which sport are you interested in?
STUDENT: I wanted tennis, but my friend says the tennis group is full.
RECEPTIONIST: I'm afraid she's right. We still have places in basketball and volleyball.
STUDENT: Then I'd rather do volleyball. I played it at school.
RECEPTIONIST: Good choice. There are two groups: one meets on Tuesdays and the other on Thursdays. The Tuesday group is full now, so it's Thursday for you.
STUDENT: That's fine. What time does it start? Four thirty?
RECEPTIONIST: It used to start at four thirty, but this year it starts at five thirty and finishes at seven.
STUDENT: Great. Is there anything I need to bring?
RECEPTIONIST: You're supposed to bring a medical certificate on the first day. You aren't allowed to train without one. And you'd better bring your own water bottle.
STUDENT: No problem. How much is it?
RECEPTIONIST: It's three hundred thousand som a month for adults, but for school students it's two hundred and fifty thousand.
STUDENT: Perfect. See you on Thursday!

items: 1. Some people believe that teenagers should not be allowed to use mobile phones at school. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

2. Checklist: topic sentence bor; izoh + aniq misol; kamida 2 bog'lovchi (because, as a result, for example, therefore); 6–10-darslar strukturasidan 1–2 tasi (be allowed to, be supposed to, had better, would rather…) tabiiy joyda; 80–100 so'z.
answers: NAMUNA (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6, 92 so'z): In my opinion, students should not be allowed to use phones during lessons because phones take their attention away from learning. When a message arrives, most teenagers would rather check it than listen to the teacher. As a result, they miss important information and have to study it again at home. For example, in my school students are supposed to put their phones in a box before each lesson, and our teachers say that test results have improved since this rule started. Therefore, schools had better keep phones out of the classroom.

box: Question: In many countries, people are living longer. What problems does this cause, and how can they be solved?

MODEL — Introduction: Thanks to medical discoveries and healthier food, people in many countries now live much longer than their grandparents did. This is good news, but it does create some serious problems. In my view, the two main problems are crowded hospitals and loneliness, and both of them can be solved.

MODEL — Body 1: The first problem is that older people need more medical care. Many of them have several health problems at the same time, so they visit doctors more often and need expensive medicine. As a result, hospitals become crowded and younger patients have to wait longer. Another problem is loneliness. It is often the grandparents who stay at home alone, because their children work long hours or move to another city. For example, in many Uzbek villages, elderly people live alone while their sons work in Russia or Korea.
items: Insho qolipi (problems + solutions, 4 abzats): Introduction (parafraz + pozitsiya) -> Body 1: problems -> Body 2: solutions -> Conclusion.
1. Savol turi qanday? Savol nechta qismdan iborat?
2. Pozitsiya kirishning qaysi gapida? Savoldagi qaysi so'zlar parafraz qilingan?
3. Body 1 da nechta muammo bor? Qaysi gapda misol berilgan?
4. Bugungi grammatika (It is … that/who, What … is, emphatic do) namunaning qayerida?
5. Essential Words 11 (Science) so'zlaridan qaysilari bor?

TASK: Plan Body 2 (solutions) and the Conclusion — table Idea / Explain / Example for 2 solutions. At home: write Body 2 (60–80 words): Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link, then the full essay.
answers: Kalit 1: problems + solutions — 2 qismli savol: Body 1 — muammolar, Body 2 — yechimlar; faqat muammo yozilsa TR ko'pi bilan 1 ball.

Kalit 2: pozitsiya — 'In my view, the two main problems are crowded hospitals and loneliness, and both of them can be solved.'; parafraz: 'people are living longer' -> 'people now live much longer than their grandparents did'; 'cause problems' -> 'does create some serious problems'.

Kalit 3: 2 muammo — (1) ko'proq tibbiy yordam -> kasalxonalar gavjum, navbat uzun; (2) yolg'izlik. Misol — 'For example, in many Uzbek villages, elderly people live alone while their sons work in Russia or Korea.'

Kalit 4: kirishda 'it does create' (emphatic do); Body 1 da 'It is often the grandparents who stay at home alone' (It-cleft). Body 2 va xulosada (ustozda): 'What governments should do first is train…' (what-clause), 'it is medical research, home care and community support that can make…' (It-cleft).
Kalit 5: discoveries (kirish); Body 2 / xulosada — evidence, knowledge, research.

Body 2 REJA kaliti: Yechim 1 — oilaviy shifokor va hamshiralar uyga boradi / izoh: muntazam tekshiruv keksalarni sog'lom saqlaydi, kasalxonaga kamroq tushadi / misol: haftalik uy tashrifi. Yechim 2 — mahalla yordami / izoh: yolg'izlik kamayadi, keksalar o'zini kerakli his qiladi / misol: kunduzgi markaz, shaxmat, bilimini maktab o'quvchilariga o'rgatish.

NAMUNA Body 2 (faqat ustoz uchun): However, these problems can be solved. What governments should do first is train more family doctors and nurses who visit old people at home. There is good evidence that regular check-ups at home keep older people healthier and out of hospital. Secondly, local communities can help. For instance, a mahalla could open a small day centre where elderly people meet, play chess and share their knowledge with schoolchildren.

NAMUNA Conclusion (faqat ustoz uchun): In conclusion, longer lives put pressure on hospitals and leave many older people lonely. However, it is medical research, home care and community support that can make a long life a healthy and happy one.
To'liq namuna: 240 so'z (kirish 49, Body 1 88, Body 2 68, xulosa 35).
Baholash: W-4.0 — shu darsdagi E bo'lim jadvali; sinfdagi reja — W-CHECK-4.0, to'liq insho uyda W-4.0 bilan.
why: Emphatic do: 'it does create some serious problems' — 'haqiqatan ham muammo tug'diradi' (yaxshi xabar bilan qarama-qarshilikni kuchaytiradi).
It-cleft: 'It is often the grandparents who stay at home alone' — kim yolg'iz qolishiga urg'u (shaxs -> who); xulosada 'it is medical research … that can make…' — yechimga urg'u (narsa -> that).
What-clause: 'What governments should do first is train…' — birinchi yechimni ta'kidlaydi (What + S + V + is).
EW 11 so'zlari: discovery (kashfiyot), evidence (dalil), knowledge (bilim), research (tadqiqot) — mavzuga tabiiy mos 4 ta so'z.
Bog'lovchilar: As a result, For example, However, Secondly, For instance, In conclusion — CC uchun 4+ xil.
O'zbek hayotidan misol: farzandlari Rossiya yoki Koreyada ishlayotgan qishloqdagi keksalar; mahalla kunduzgi markazi.

She was born in Poland, but it was in Paris that she did most of her research. With her husband Pierre, she discovered two new elements, polonium and radium. I first learnt about her at school and later read more online. What impresses me most is that she worked in an old shed with very little funding, but she never gave up. reading.title: Marie Curie: curiosity in a leaking shed
text: A. Maria Skłodowska was born in 1867 in Warsaw, when Poland was ruled by Russia and women were not allowed to go to university there. What she did for several years was work as a governess to pay for her sister's studies in Paris; then her sister paid for hers. It was in 1891 that she arrived at the Sorbonne, so poor that she often went hungry.

B. In Paris she met Pierre Curie, and they married in 1895. What caught her attention was a strange discovery: uranium gave off invisible rays. She wanted to know why. In an old, leaking wooden shed, she boiled tonnes of pitchblende ore. It was in 1898 that she and Pierre found two new elements — polonium, named after her homeland, and radium, which glowed in the dark. Some scientists doubted their results, but they did find them, and Marie also invented the word for what these elements did: radioactivity.

C. Never had a woman won a Nobel Prize before 1903, when she shared the physics prize with Pierre and Henri Becquerel. Pierre died in 1906, and it was Marie who took his post — the first female professor at the Sorbonne. In 1911 she won a second Nobel, in chemistry. Nobody had ever won two in different sciences before.

D. What she refused to do was patent radium; she believed that it should belong to everyone. In the First World War she built mobile X-ray units, drove some of them to the front herself and helped doctors to treat many thousands of wounded soldiers. Years of work with radiation damaged her health, and she died in 1934. Her notebooks are still radioactive today and are kept in lead-lined boxes. What she left behind was more than two elements: it was proof that curiosity, not permission, is what makes a scientist.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; monolog (Part 4 — ma'ruza), raqam va tuzatishlarni aniq ayting.
Lecturer: Good morning. Today I want to talk about how scientific discoveries really happen.
Lecturer: What most people believe is that great discoveries happen by accident, or simply through luck. In fact, it is patience that produces most of them.
Lecturer: Take Marie Curie. People sometimes say she worked for three years to isolate radium, but it was actually closer to four years, and most of that time she spent in an old shed.
Lecturer: The shed had a leaking roof and no proper heating, so in winter it was freezing inside. The work was hard, but she did continue, year after year.

Lecturer: So what can we learn from her? The method is simple. First, you observe something carefully. Second, you form a hypothesis — an idea that you can check. Third, you test it with an experiment.

Lecturer: And remember, the first experiment rarely works. In our department last year, students needed on average twelve attempts — sorry, I mean twenty-one attempts — before an experiment gave clear results.
Lecturer: Some students think that intelligence is the key. Intelligence helps, of course, but what a scientist needs most is curiosity: the wish to ask 'why?' again and again.

kahoot.explain: It-cleft'da shaxsga urg'u → who (yoki that).

kahoot.q: It was in 1898 ___ radium was discovered.
kahoot.explain: It-cleft'da vaqt/joy/narsa → that (odatda when emas).

kahoot.q: What I need now ___ a long holiday.
kahoot.explain: Ta'kid birlik ot (a long holiday) → is.

kahoot.q: I ___ like this film! It's brilliant.
kahoot.explain: Urg'u: do/does/did + V1. I → do: I do like.

kahoot.q: Yesterday she ___ finish all her work, I promise!
kahoot.explain: O'tgan zamonda urg'u: did + V1 (did finish).

kahoot.q: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She does work hard, believe me.
She does works hard, believe me.
She do work hard, believe me.
She did works hard, believe me.
kahoot.explain: he/she/it → does + V1: She does work.

kahoot.q: Not only ___ a Nobel Prize in physics, but she also won one in chemistry.
kahoot.explain: Not only gap boshida → yordamchi + ega: did she win; ikkinchi qismda — but … also.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: It was John that he broke the window.
It was John who broke the window.
What I want is to rest.
It was in Paris that she studied.
kahoot.explain: Cleft'da ega takrorlanmaydi: It was John who/that broke...

kahoot.q: Qaysi gap WHAT-CLAUSE (urg'u) ga misol?
options: What she discovered was a new element.
Did she discover a new element?
kahoot.explain: What + S + V + is/was + URG'U: What she discovered was...

kahoot.q: Emphatic DO (I do like...) qaysi zamonlarda ishlatiladi?
options: Present Simple, Past Simple va buyruq gapda
kahoot.explain: do/does/did + V1 — Present Simple, Past Simple va buyruq gapda (Do sit down!).

kahoot.q: "Honesty matters most." → It is ___ matters most.
kahoot.explain: It is + URG'U + that + qolgan qism: It is honesty that matters.

kahoot.q: Tarjima: "Menga kerak narsa — dam olish."
options: What I need is a rest.
What I need are a rest.
That I need is a rest.
What do I need is a rest.
kahoot.explain: What + S + V (savol tartibi emas) + is + urg'u.

kahoot.q: An idea that scientists test in an experiment is a ___.
kahoot.explain: hypothesis = gipoteza (sinaladigan faraz).

kahoot.q: Facts that show something is true are called ___.
kahoot.explain: evidence = dalil (sanalmaydi: some evidence).

kahoot.q: Marie Curie was a ___ in the study of radioactivity — one of the first.
kahoot.explain: pioneer = kashshof (birinchilardan).

kahoot.q: Before a study is published, other scientists check it. This is ___.
kahoot.explain: peer review = hamkasblar ekspert tekshiruvi.

kahoot.q: Research can't continue without money. It needs ___.
kahoot.explain: funding = moliyalashtirish.

kahoot.q: A person who doubts new claims until they see proof is ___.
kahoot.explain: sceptical = shubha bilan qaraydigan (British spelling).

kahoot.q: Curie managed to ___ radium from a mineral.
kahoot.explain: isolate = moddani ajratib olmoq (element ixtiro qilinmaydi — invent emas).

kahoot.q: "qiziquvchanlik" — inglizcha?
kahoot.explain: curiosity = qiziquvchanlik.

lessons.title: The + adjectives (The more…, the more…)
lessons.grammar_topic: THE + COMPARATIVE, THE + COMPARATIVE (qanchalik… shunchalik…) + the + sifat = guruh (the rich, the poor, the elderly)
lessons.vocab_topic: Essential Words 12 — Poverty, wealth and development (qashshoqlik, boylik va taraqqiyot)
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 4.0: Lesson 12 – The + adjectives (ixtiyoriy; dars kitobsiz o'tadi). Writing: Jony Academy savoli (kitob SAMPLE ESSAYS uslubida); namuna original. Listening: Audio 61–65 ishlatilmaydi; transcript'ni 2 marta o'qing (tutor — ustoz, student — kuchli o'quvchi). Reading — Muhammad Yunus (Jony Academy matni).
objectives: Dars oxirida o'quvchi "the …, the …" qolipida (birinchi qismda will'siz) kamida 5 ta yangi gap tuzadi, qisqa shaklni (the sooner, the better) ishlatadi.
Dars oxirida o'quvchi the + sifat guruhlarini (the poor, the rich, the unemployed) ko'plik fe'l bilan to'g'ri ishlatadi.
Dars oxirida o'quvchi Part 2 kartochkasi bo'yicha 1.5 daqiqa gapiradi.

Dars oxirida o'quvchi 'Helping the poor' savoli (discuss both views + opinion) bo'yicha Body 2 ni 60–80 so'zda yozadi, unda the + sifat (the poor / the unemployed) yoki 'the …, the …' ni kamida 1 marta to'g'ri ishlatadi va W-CHECK ning 7 bandidan kamida 5 tasini bajaradi.
materials: Grammatika formulalari — tizimdagi grammar.formulas (proyektor).
Essential Words 12 CORE 20 — tizimdagi lug'at ro'yxati / Lug'at PDF (chop etish ixtiyoriy).
Kahoot: 'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi (11-dars savollari).
Speaking kartochkalari (class_ex SPEAKING) — proyektor yoki juftlikka 1 varaq.
Writing: 'Helping the poor' savoli + namuna kirish va Body 1 (class_ex WRITING, box) + W-4.0 va W-CHECK-4.0 jadvallari — proyektor.
Reading matni — proyektor yoki chop etilgan nusxa.
Listening transcript — faqat ustoz ekranida (o'quvchiga ko'rsatilmaydi).
Rubrikalar: W-4.0 / S-4.0 + W-CHECK / S-CHECK — class_ex dagi jadval (proyektor): S-4.0 va S-CHECK — SPEAKING dan keyin, W-4.0 va W-CHECK — WRITING dan keyin.
timeline: Salomlashish + kirish savoli
Lead-in: ustoz doskaga "The more you read, the more you learn." yozib so'raydi: "What happens when you practise more?" 3–4 o'quvchi "The more I …, the … I …" bilan javob beradi.
TAKROR: Kahoot — 11-dars (Emphasis)
'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi → 11-dars savollari (20 ta). Bugungi darsning Kahooti bu yerda EMAS — u 13-darsda o'ynaladi. Oxirgi 1 daqiqa: eng ko'p xato qilingan 2 savol izohi.
TAKROR: Yozma normativ — Essential Words 11 (Science, research and discovery)

Normativ — belgilangan vaqtda bajariladigan qisqa o'lchov; natijasiga qarab coin beriladi. 11-dars CORE 20: ustoz o'zbekchasini aytadi, o'quvchi inglizchasini yozadi — 4 daq; 1 daq sherik bilan almashib tekshirish. 18–20 = 2 coin; 15–17 = bajarildi; 14 va kam = 13-darsda qayta topshiradi.
PT2 NATIJA TAHLILI — pt2

Ustoz tekshirilgan varaqlarni qaytaradi. Eng ko'p uchragan 5 xato doskada — o'quvchilar juftlikda tuzatadi (4 daq); test darsida uyga berilgan reading kaliti proyektorda (1 daq); <70% olganlar ro'yxati va qayta topshirish sanasi (2 daq).
YANGI GRAMMATIKA — The + comparative, the + comparative; the + sifat + CCQ

Lead-in misoli → formula (proyektor, grammar.formulas) → 2–3 misol → CCQ (presentation) → 1 daq tez og'zaki tekshiruv: ustoz gapning birinchi yarmini aytadi, o'quvchilar davom ettiradi; will qoidasi (notes).
LUG'AT — Essential Words 12 CORE 20

Ustoz 20 so'zni proyektorda talaffuz + tarjima bilan o'qitadi (3 daq); 6–8 ta qiyin so'zga CCQ yoki misol (3 daq) (inequality, welfare, debt, savings…); juftlikda A o'zbekchasini, B inglizchasini aytadi (2 daq). Mustahkamlash — flashcard (uyga).
Kombinatsiya — The + comparative + S + V, the + comparative + S + V

Kombinatsiya — juftlikda formula → gap → tarjima zanjiri: A formulani yoki o'zbekcha gapni aytadi, B shu formula bilan inglizcha gap tuzib tarjima qiladi, keyin almashadi. 1 daq — ustoz grammar.formulas dan formulani va 1 misolni proyektorda ko'rsatadi; 3 daq — juftlikda (me'yor normativ[1] da); ustoz 2 juftlikni tinglaydi.
SINF MASHQLARI — Ex1–Ex4 (MAJBURIY) + ZAXIRA
Ex1 4 daq yakka · Ex2 4 daq juftlik · Ex3 3 daq yakka · Ex4 2 daq juftlik; ZAXIRA (reading'dagi 'the …, the …' topish topshirig'i) — uyga (WRITING bosqichiga 2 daq berildi).
SPEAKING — Part 2 + Part 3
class_ex SPEAKING, juftlikda — instr'dagi tartib: kartochkalar + ICQ (1) · tayyorgarlik (1) · A (2) · B (2) · Part 3 (3) · feedback S-4.0 (1).
READING — Muhammad Yunus
1 daq — gist (1-topshiriq, sarlavhalar); 7 daq — o'qish + TFNG; 3 daq — completion; 2 daq — tekshirish, NOT GIVEN izohi. Yakka; tekshirish juftlikda.
LISTENING — IELTS Part 3
Audio 61–65 ishlatilmaydi; transcript'ni 2 marta o'qing (tutor — ustoz, student — kuchli o'quvchi). 1 daq — savollarni o'qish; 1-tinglash (3 daq); 2-tinglash (3 daq); 1 daq — javoblar proyektorda.
WRITING — Helping the poor

class_ex WRITING bo'yicha. 3 daq — savol tahlili: savol turi (discuss both views + opinion), kalit so'zlar (help the poor, give money, education and jobs), pozitsiya kirishda, 2 body (Body 1 — pul berish tarafdorlari, Body 2 — ta'lim va ish + o'z fikri). 5 daq — NAMUNA kirish + Body 1 tahlili (box, proyektorda: topic sentence, bog'lovchilar On the one hand / In addition / For example, bugungi grammatika, EW 12 so'zlari). 5 daq — yakka Body 2 (60–80 so'z). 2 daq — sherik W-CHECK-4.0 bilan tekshiradi; to'liq insho uyga (W-4.0).
Xatolar ustida ishlash + uyga vazifa

4 daq — dars davomida ustoz yozib borgan 4–5 ta og'zaki/yozma xato doskada, o'quvchilar tuzatadi (error log); 3 daq — uyga vazifa: 1–4 majburiy, 5–6 qo'shimcha; insho savoli ('Helping the poor', 40 daq, 220–260 so'z) proyektorda; 13-darsda shu savol bo'yicha WRITING NORMATIV bo'lishini ayting. Vaqt yetmasa: ZAXIRA mashqlar va reading'ning 'find' topshirig'i uyga o'tadi.

intro: THE + COMPARATIVE, THE + COMPARATIVE — ikki o'zgarish bir-biriga bog'liq: "The more you read, the more you learn.".
Qisqa, fe'lsiz shakl ham bor: "The sooner, the better."
THE + SIFAT = GURUH (the rich, the poor, the elderly, the unemployed) — fe'l KO'PLIKDA: "The poor are getting poorer."
formulas: The more + V, the more + V
The more + S + V, the more + S + V
The more you read, the more you learn.
Qanchalik ko'p o'qisang, shunchalik ko'p o'rganasan.
The + comparative, the + comparative
The + -er/more + S + V, the + -er/more + S + V
The faster we run, the sooner we arrive.
Qanchalik tez yugursak, shunchalik tez yetib boramiz.
The less…, the better…
The less + S + V, the better + S + V
The less you worry, the better you feel.
Qanchalik kam xavotir olsang, shunchalik yaxshi bo'lasan.
Comparative + ot
The more + OT + S + V, the …
The more money the poor borrow from moneylenders, the deeper into debt they sink.
Kambag'allar sudxo'rdan qancha ko'p qarz olsa, qarzga shuncha chuqur botadi.
Qisqa shakl
The + comparative, the + comparative (fe'lsiz)
The sooner, the better. / The more, the merrier.
Qancha tez bo'lsa, shuncha yaxshi. / Qancha ko'p bo'lsa, shuncha quvnoq.
The + sifat = guruh
The + sifat + KO'PLIK fe'l
The poor are getting poorer; the rich are getting richer.
Kambag'allar kambag'allashmoqda; boylar boyimoqda.
presentation: Should we leave early?
Yes — the sooner, the better.
CCQ: The more you read, the more you learn.
Are the two things connected? (Yes) If you read less? (You learn less.)
CCQ: The sooner we start, the sooner we finish.
Have we started? (No) Is it about the future? (Yes) Is there will after 'the sooner'? (No)
CCQ: The poor are getting poorer.
Is it one person? (No, a group) Singular or plural verb? (Plural — are)
notes: So'z tartibi: comparative gap BOSHIDA, keyin ega + fe'l ("The harder you work", "You work the harder" emas).

Ikkinchi qismda ham "the" shart. Birinchi qismda will ishlatilmaydi (kelajakda ham Present Simple): "The sooner we start, the sooner we finish." Ikkinchi qismda will mumkin: "…, the more you will achieve."
the + sifat = guruh — birlik shaxs emas ("a poor man / a poor person" = bitta odam; "the poor" = barcha kambag'allar).
O'quvchi so'raydi: "the poors" deyish mumkinmi? — Javob: yo'q, the + sifat -s olmaydi, lekin fe'l ko'plikda: The poor are…
O'quvchi so'raydi: the less yoki the fewer? — Javob: sanaladigan ot bilan the fewer (the fewer jobs), sanalmaydigan bilan the less (the less money).
mistakes: More you read, more you learn.
The more you read, the more you learn.
The harder you will work, the more you achieve.
The harder you work, the more you achieve. / The harder you work, the more you will achieve.
Birinchi qismda will ishlatilmaydi; ikkinchi qismda will mumkin.

answers: NAMUNA A (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6, 120–160 so'z): I'd like to talk about a small charity in my neighbourhood. It was started about ten years ago by local teachers, who noticed that some pupils came to school hungry. Now it helps the poor and the elderly. Every month they collect food, warm clothes and school books and take them to families who live on a low income. In winter they also visit old people who live alone and help them with their bills. I think their work is important, because the government can't reach every family. Last winter I helped them on two Saturdays: we packed boxes of rice, oil and tea. I saw that the more people join, the more families get help. It also showed me that you don't need to be rich to make a difference.

NAMUNA B (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6, 120–160 so'z): I'm going to talk about a laptop I saved money for last year. I needed it for IELTS practice and online lessons. It took me about eight months. I didn't have a job, so I saved most of my pocket money and helped my uncle in his shop at weekends. I also made a simple plan: I wrote down every som I spent in a notebook, and I stopped buying snacks after school. Sometimes it was hard, because my friends were going to cafés and I had to say no. But the longer I saved, the more I wanted it. When I finally bought it, I felt really proud, because I had paid for it myself. Now I use it every day, and I think saving taught me to be patient.

Part 3 namuna javoblari (1 gapdan): 1) Good jobs need a good education, which the poor often can't afford. 2) A little more, yes — but very high taxes may push businesses away. 3) They can help, but loans alone can't end poverty.
