class_ex.title: WRITING — Helping the poor (yozma): Task 2 insho — tahlil va Body 2
class_ex.instr: (15 daq) 3 daq — savol tahlili: savol turi, kalit so'zlar, pozitsiya, nechta body; 5 daq — box dagi NAMUNA kirish + Body 1 tahlili (topic sentence, bog'lovchilar, the + sifat / 'the …, the …', EW 12 so'zlari); 5 daq — yakka Body 2, 60–80 so'z, qolip: Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link; 2 daq — sherik bilan almashib W-CHECK-4.0 bo'yicha tekshirish. ICQ: Body 2 qaysi fikr haqida — pul yoki ta'lim va ish? (ta'lim va ish + o'z fikringiz) Body 2 necha so'z? (60–80)
box: Question: Some people think that the best way to help the poor is to give them money. Others believe it is better to give them education and jobs. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

MODEL — Introduction: Many people agree that society should support families who live in poverty, but they disagree about how to do it. Some think that people on a low income should simply receive money, while others prefer education and jobs. In my opinion, cash helps in an emergency, but training and work are the better long-term solution.

MODEL — Body 1: On the one hand, giving money directly has clear advantages. When a family suddenly has nothing to live on, a cash payment lets parents buy food, medicine and other basic needs at once. In addition, the poor know their own problems best, so they can decide how to spend the money. For example, a mother who loses her job can use welfare payments to pay the rent instead of falling into debt.
items: Insho qolipi (discuss both views + opinion): Introduction (parafraz + pozitsiya) -> Body 1 (1-fikr) -> Body 2 (2-fikr + o'z fikri) -> Conclusion.
1. Savol turi qanday: agree/disagree, discuss both views + opinion yoki causes/solutions? Nechta qismga javob kerak?
2. Pozitsiya kirishning qaysi gapida? Savoldagi qaysi so'zlar parafraz qilingan?
3. Body 1 ning topic sentence'i qaysi? Misol qaysi gapda?
4. Box da the + sifat qayerda? Fe'l birlikmi yoki ko'plik? Siz Body 2 da 'the …, the …' yoki the unemployed / the poor ni qanday ishlatasiz?
5. Essential Words 12 (Poverty, wealth) so'zlaridan qaysilari bor?

TASK: Write Body 2 (60–80 words): Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link. Idea: money is soon spent; education and jobs give a regular income (example from Uzbekistan: vocational courses / mahalla support). Use 'the …, the …' or the unemployed / the poor once.
answers: Kalit 1: discuss both views + opinion — 3 qismga javob kerak: (1) pul berish tarafdorlari, (2) ta'lim va ish tarafdorlari, (3) o'z fikringiz. Faqat bitta tomonni yozsa — TR ko'pi bilan 1.

Kalit 2: pozitsiya — 'In my opinion, cash helps in an emergency, but training and work are the better long-term solution.'; parafraz: 'the poor' -> 'families who live in poverty' / 'people on a low income'; 'give them money' -> 'receive money'.
Kalit 3: topic sentence — 'On the one hand, giving money directly has clear advantages.'; misol — 'For example, a mother who loses her job can use welfare payments…'.

Kalit 4: box da — Body 1: 'the poor know their own problems best' (the + sifat = odamlar guruhi, fe'l ko'plikda: know, knows emas); kirishda savoldagi 'the poor' parafraz qilingan ('families who live in poverty'). Ustoz uchun (proyektorda yo'q): namuna Body 2 da — 'the unemployed can join…' (ko'plik), 'The more skills people have, the more choices they get' (birinchi qismda will yo'q); xulosada — 'help the poor', 'the rich should invest' (ko'plik).
Kalit 5: poverty, income (low income), basic needs, welfare, debt (box da); income, savings (namuna Body 2 da).

NAMUNA Body 2 (faqat ustoz uchun): On the other hand, money alone rarely solves the problem, because it is soon spent and the family is poor again. Education leads to jobs, and jobs give people a regular salary and more confidence. The more skills people have, the more choices they get. For instance, in many Uzbek mahallas the unemployed can join free vocational courses and learn to sew, cook or repair phones. In this way, help becomes a regular income and savings, not a one-off gift.

NAMUNA Conclusion (faqat ustoz uchun): In conclusion, although direct payments can help families through a difficult period, I believe that education and jobs are the best way to help the poor. They allow people to escape poverty for good, so the government and the rich should invest more in training.
To'liq namuna: 252 so'z (kirish 55, Body 1 72, Body 2 80, xulosa 45).
Baholash: W-4.0 (jadval shu darsda); sinfdagi Body 2 — W-CHECK-4.0, to'liq insho uyda W-4.0 bilan.
why: Grammatika (the + sifat): the poor, the unemployed, the rich — 'odamlar guruhi' ma'nosida, fe'l doim ko'plikda (the poor know, the unemployed can join, the rich should invest); 'the poors' deyilmaydi.
Grammatika (the …, the …): 'The more skills people have, the more choices they get' — birinchi qismda will yo'q; sabab -> natija bog'lanishini qisqa ko'rsatadi.
EW 12 so'zlari: poverty (qashshoqlik), income (daromad), basic needs (asosiy ehtiyojlar), welfare (ijtimoiy ta'minot), debt (qarz), savings (jamg'arma) — 6 ta, mavzuga tabiiy.

Bog'lovchilar: On the one hand, On the other hand, In addition, For example, For instance, because, In this way, In conclusion — CC uchun 4+ xil; 'discuss both' inshosida On the one hand / On the other hand juftligi qulay. Har body Link gapi bilan tugaydi (Body 2: 'In this way, help becomes a regular income…').
O'zbek hayotidan misol: mahalladagi bepul kasb-hunar kurslari (tikuvchilik, oshpazlik, telefon ta'miri) — ishsizlar ish topadi yoki kichik biznes ochadi.

Some think that people on a low income should simply receive money, while others prefer education and jobs. On the other hand, money alone rarely solves the problem, because it is soon spent and the family is poor again. Education leads to jobs, and jobs give people a regular salary and more confidence. The more skills people have, the more choices they get. For instance, in many Uzbek mahallas the unemployed can join free vocational courses and learn to sew, cook or repair phones. In this way, help becomes a regular income and savings, not a one-off gift.

In conclusion, although direct payments can help families through a difficult period, I believe that education and jobs are the best way to help the poor. They allow people to escape poverty for good, so the government and the rich should invest more in training.

reading.title: Muhammad Yunus — the smaller the loan, the bigger the change
text: A. Muhammad Yunus was born in 1940 in Chittagong, in what is now Bangladesh. He studied economics in the United States and then came home to teach it at a university. In 1974 a terrible famine hit the country, and he found that the more theories he taught in the classroom, the less they explained the hunger outside the window. So he walked into a nearby village to see real poverty for himself.

B. There he met a woman who made bamboo stools. She had to borrow money from a moneylender to buy bamboo, and the moneylender took nearly all her profit: the more she worked, the poorer she stayed. Yunus found 42 people in the village in the same trap. Together they needed just 27 dollars. He lent the money from his own pocket, and they paid it back.

C. Ordinary banks refused to lend to the poor because they had no collateral. Yunus argued the opposite: the poorer people are, the more carefully they repay, because a loan is their only chance. In 1983 he founded Grameen Bank, which means "village bank". It lends small sums, with no collateral, to groups of five borrowers who support one another.

D. Almost all of the borrowers are women. Yunus believed that the more money women control, the more of it reaches their children. The bank says that its repayment rate is higher than at many ordinary banks. Today it has millions of borrowers, and the idea — microcredit — has been copied in many countries. Not everyone agrees, however: some researchers say that small loans alone cannot end poverty.

E. In 2006 Yunus and Grameen Bank shared the Nobel Peace Prize. His dream has not changed: he believes that the sooner poverty is found only in museums, the better, and that the poor should be seen as part of the solution, not as the problem.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

items: Main point: the more a government spends on primary ___, the faster poverty falls.
Each extra year at school raises income by about ___ per cent.

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; Tutor — ustoz, Student — kuchli o'quvchi (yoki ovozni o'zgartiring). IELTS Part 3.
Tutor: Hi, Aziz. So, how is your presentation on poverty going?
Student: Quite well, thanks. At first I wanted to focus on health care, but now my main point is simple: the more a government spends on primary education, the faster poverty falls.
Tutor: Good. Have you got any figures?
Student: Yes. One study I read says that every extra year at school raises a person's income by about eight per cent — sorry, ten per cent.
Tutor: And does the age matter?
Student: A lot. Many people think the cost matters most, but the younger a child starts school, the bigger the effect.
Tutor: What will you say about foreign aid?
Student: I'll say it helps after a disaster, but the more a country depends on aid, the less self-sufficient it becomes.
Tutor: Are you going to mention microcredit?
Student: Yes, I'll use Grameen Bank as my example. Its borrowers work in groups of five — not ten, as I first thought.
Tutor: How long is your talk?
Student: Twelve minutes. I've got fifteen slides, but I think that's too many.
Tutor: I agree — the fewer slides, the better. Try to cut them to ten. And add one slide on the young — no, actually, on the elderly: the older the population, the more welfare it needs.
Student: OK. When is the deadline?
Tutor: Friday — no, sorry, Thursday, because Friday is a holiday.

Uy vazifasi tekshiruvi

Tarjima kaliti proyektorda (1 daq, o'quvchi o'zi belgilaydi). 12-dars inshosi ('Helping the poor', 40 daq) yig'ib olinadi — W-4.0 bo'yicha keyingi darsgacha tekshiriladi; bugun shu savol bo'yicha WRITING NORMATIV bo'lishini eslating; 12-darsdagi eng ko'p uchragan 2 xato doskada (2 daq). Bajarmaganlar jurnalga.
YANGI GRAMMATIKA — even / even though / even if; in case; as long as / provided / providing + CCQ

Lead-in (2 daq): "Take an umbrella in case it rains." → formula (proyektor, grammar.formulas 1–6) + presentation dialoglari (8 daq) → CCQ (presentation oxiridagi 5 ta, 4 daq) → tez og'zaki tekshiruv: ustoz o'zbekcha vaziyat aytadi, o'quvchilar bog'lovchini aytadi (2 daq) → grammar.mistakes: nega xato? (2 daq).

Ustoz 20 so'zni proyektorda talaffuz + tarjima bilan o'qitadi (3 daq); 6–8 ta qiyin so'zga CCQ yoki misol: itinerary, accommodation, precaution, hazard, embassy, hospitality (3 daq); juftlikda A o'zbekchasini, B inglizchasini aytadi (2 daq). Mustahkamlash — flashcard (uyga).

Kombinatsiya — juftlikda formula → gap → tarjima zanjiri: A formulani yoki o'zbekcha gapni aytadi, B shu formula bilan inglizcha gap tuzib tarjima qiladi, keyin almashadi. 1 daq — ustoz grammar.formulas dan formulani va 1 misolni proyektorda ko'rsatadi; 3 daq — juftlikda (me'yor normativ[1] da); ustoz 2 juftlikni tinglaydi.

intro: EVEN — "hatto": ta'kid, kutilmagan holat: "Even he didn't know the answer." (hatto u ham). EVEN THOUGH + haqiqat (garchi… bo'lsa ham): "She smiled even though she was tired." EVEN IF + faraz (agar … bo'lsa ham): "I'll go even if it rains."

IN CASE — "ehtimol … bo'lib qolar deb, ehtiyot uchun": harakat OLDINDAN qilinadi: "Take an umbrella in case it rains." (yomg'ir yog'ishi mumkin deb — hozir ol). Taqqoslang: "Take an umbrella if it rains" (yog'sa — keyin ol). IN CASE OF + ot (ogohlantirish yozuvlarida): "In case of fire, use the stairs."
AS LONG AS — "faqat … bo'lsa, … sharti bilan": "You can stay as long as you're quiet."
PROVIDED (THAT) — rasmiy/yozma shart: "You can go out provided that you finish your work." PROVIDING (THAT) — xuddi shu, og'zaki: "Providing you have a ticket, you can enter."
as long as / provided / providing / in case dan keyin kelasi zamon EMAS, Present Simple: "as long as you ARE quiet", "provided you FINISH".
formulas: Even
Even + ega/ot (hatto)
Even he didn't know the answer.
Hatto u ham javobni bilmadi.
Even though / even if
S + V + even though + HAQIQAT / even if + FARAZ
She smiled even though she was tired. / I'll travel even if it's expensive.
U charchagan bo'lsa ham jilmaydi. / Qimmat bo'lsa ham sayohat qilaman.
In case
Harakat + in case + S + V (Present)
Take an umbrella in case it rains.
Yomg'ir yog'ib qolsa deb, soyabon ol.
In case of + ot
In case of + OT, + buyruq
In case of emergency, call 112.
Favqulodda holatda 112 ga qo'ng'iroq qiling.
As long as
S + V + as long as + S + V (Present)
You can stay as long as you're quiet.
Agar tinch bo'lsang, qolishing mumkin.
Provided / providing (that)
Provided (that) + S + V, + S + V
You can go out provided that you finish your work. / Providing you have a ticket, you can enter.
Ishni tugatsang, chiqishing mumkin. / Chiptang bo'lsa, kirishing mumkin.
presentation: Was the exam difficult?
Yes, very. Even the best students found it hard.
Why did he carry letters from rulers?
In case he needed help in a foreign city.
Can I travel alone?
You can travel alone as long as you tell someone your route.
Can tourists visit the mosque?
Yes, provided that they dress respectfully.
Can I enter without a visa?
Providing you have an Uzbek passport, you can visit many countries without a visa.
Did he keep travelling even though it was dangerous?
Yes, even though he lost almost everything on the way to China.
CCQ: Take an umbrella in case it rains.
Is it raining now? (No) Do you take it before or after it rains? (Before)
CCQ: I'll take a map if I get lost.
Do I take the map now? (No) When do I take it? (After I get lost)
CCQ: She smiled even though she was tired.
Was she tired? (Yes) Did she smile? (Yes) Is it a real fact? (Yes)
CCQ: I'll go even if it rains.
Do we know if it will rain? (No) Will I go? (Yes)
CCQ: You can stay as long as you're quiet.
Can you stay if you're noisy? (No) Is being quiet a condition? (Yes)
notes: even — ravish (hatto), bog'lovchi emas: "Even he came" ✓; "Even he was tired, he smiled" ✗ → "Even though he was tired…".
O'quvchi so'raydi: in case va if bir xilmi? — Javob: Yo'q. "I'll take a map in case I get lost" — xaritani HOZIR, ehtiyot uchun olaman. "I'll take a map if I get lost" — adashsam, KEYIN olaman.

O'quvchi so'raydi: nega "in case it will rain" emas? — Javob: in case, as long as, provided, if dan keyin kelajak ma'nosida Present Simple ishlatiladi. O'tgan zamon hikoyasida — Past Simple: "He carried letters in case he needed help."
O'quvchi so'raydi: even if va even though farqi nima? — Javob: even though — haqiqat (u haqiqatan charchagan edi); even if — faraz (yomg'ir yog'ishi ham, yog'masligi ham mumkin).
as long as / provided / providing = if (faqat shu shart bilan). provided ko'proq yozma uslubda, providing — og'zakiroq; ikkalasi ham to'g'ri.
mistakes: Take an umbrella in case it will rain.
Take an umbrella in case it rains.
Even he was tired, he smiled.
Even though he was tired, he smiled.
You can stay as long as you will be quiet.
You can stay as long as you're quiet.
In case fire, use the stairs.
In case of fire, use the stairs.
Provided you will finish your work, you can go.
Provided you finish your work, you can go.

class_ex.instr: (12 daq, juftlik) 2 daq — Part 1: A 4 savolni so'raydi, B javob beradi (javob + sabab + misol), keyin almashadi; 1 daq — Kartochka A bo'yicha tayyorgarlik (faqat 5–6 kalit so'z); 2 daq — A gapiradi, B S-CHECK-4.0 ni to'ldiradi; 2 daq — ustoz NAMUNA A ni o'qiydi, o'quvchilar box'dagi iboralarni belgilaydi; 2 daq — B shu kartochkada gapiradi (box'dan 2+ ibora bilan); 2 daq — Part 3 juftlikda; 1 daq — ustoz feedback (S-4.0). ICQ: Necha daqiqa tayyorlanasiz? (1) B o'z navbatida nimadan foydalanadi? (Box'dagi kamida 2 ibora)
items: Part 1: Do you like travelling? Why?
Part 1: How do you usually travel — by train, bus or plane?
Part 1: Who do you usually travel with?
Part 1: Where did you go on your last holiday?
KARTOCHKA A: Describe a trip you really enjoyed. You should say: where you went ; who you went with ; what you did there ; and explain why you enjoyed it.
Part 3: Why do people like travelling to other countries?
Part 3: Is tourism good for small towns? Why?

box: I'd like to talk about a trip I took to …
It was a perfect destination for …
Even though the journey took …, nobody complained.
Our accommodation was …, and the owners showed us real hospitality.
Trips are safe as long as you take simple precautions.
I'd love to go back, provided I have enough time.
answers: Part 1 namunalari (faqat ustoz uchun): 1) Yes, I really enjoy it, because I like seeing new places and meeting new people. Even a short journey to another region helps me relax after a busy school week. 2) I usually travel by train, because it's comfortable and not too expensive. For example, the fast train from Tashkent to Samarkand takes just over two hours. 3) Mostly with my family, because my parents don't let me travel alone yet. But I can go on school trips with my classmates as long as a teacher goes with us. 4) Last summer we went to Chimyon, in the mountains near Tashkent. We stayed there for three days and spent most of the time walking.

NAMUNA A (Band 5.5–6, 176 so'z, ~1.5–2 daqiqa, faqat ustoz uchun): I'd like to talk about a trip I took to Zomin last May. Zomin is a national park in the mountains of the Jizzakh region, and it was a perfect destination for a short break after our exams. I went with six classmates and our biology teacher, who was also our guide. We travelled by bus, and even though the journey took almost five hours, nobody complained, because the views were amazing. Our accommodation was a small wooden guesthouse, and the owners showed us real Uzbek hospitality: there was always hot tea when we came back. During the day we explored the forest paths and climbed up to a waterfall. Our teacher made us carry raincoats and a first-aid kit in case the weather changed, and of course it rained on the second day! I enjoyed this trip because I felt free from my phone and my lessons for three whole days. It also showed me that mountain trips are safe and fun as long as you take simple precautions. I'd love to go back next summer.

Part 3 namunalari (faqat ustoz uchun): 1) I think people travel abroad to see a different culture and to take a break from their daily routine. For example, many Uzbek families now spend their holidays in Turkey or Georgia, because flights have become cheaper. 2) Mostly yes, because tourists bring money and jobs. Local people can open guesthouses or sell crafts, for instance. However, it helps only as long as the town keeps its traditions and does not become too crowded. 3) It depends on their age. Older teenagers can travel without their parents provided that they plan the route carefully and keep in touch with their family. Younger ones, however, should travel with an adult in case of an emergency.
Baholash: S-4.0 (jadval shu darsda); juftlikda — S-CHECK-4.0.
why: Bugungi grammatika NAMUNA A da: even though the journey took… (qarama-qarshilik), in case the weather changed (ehtiyot uchun, oldindan), as long as you take simple precautions (shart) — 3 joy, tabiiy.
EW 13 so'zlari: destination (borish manzili), guide (gid), journey (yo'l, safar), accommodation (turar joy), hospitality (mehmondo'stlik), explore (o'rganib chiqmoq), precaution (ehtiyot chorasi).
Kartochkaning 4 bandi tartib bilan: where (Zomin) -> who (sinfdoshlar va ustoz) -> what (o'rmon yo'llari, sharshara) -> why (telefonsiz 3 kun, xavfsizlik saboqi).
class_ex.note: S-CHECK-4.0 (sherik belgilaydi): 1) kartochkaning 4 bandi aytildimi; 2) 1.5 daqiqadan uzoq, uzun pauzasiz; 3) box'dan 2+ ibora; 4) bugungi grammatika 1–2 marta; 5) Part 3 javobi fikr + sabab + misol. Ustoz 3–4 o'quvchini S-4.0 bo'yicha jurnalga qayd etadi. class_ex.title: WRITING NORMATIV — Helping the poor (yozma, 10 daqiqa)
class_ex.instr: (12 daq, yakka) 1 daq — ustoz savolni proyektorda ko'rsatadi va qoidani aytadi: kirish + 1 body, 110–140 so'z; daftar, telefon va namuna yopiq; taymer 10 daq shu daqiqadan boshlanadi. 9 daq — yakka yozish; vaqt tugaganda chiziq tortiladi. 2 daq — W-CHECK-4.0 bilan o'zini tekshiradi, so'z sonini oxirida yozadi; ish yig'iladi. ICQ: Nechta abzats yozasiz? (2 — kirish va 1 body) Daftar yoki namunaga qarash mumkinmi? (Yo'q) Eslatma: bu normativda W-CHECK-4.0 ning 6-bandi uchun EW12 (Poverty, wealth) so'zlari hisoblanadi.
items: Question: Some people think that the best way to help the poor is to give them money. Others believe it is better to give them education and jobs. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
TASK: Write an introduction + ONE body paragraph (110–140 words) in 10 minutes. No notebook, no phone, no model.
Introduction: paraphrase the question + your clear position (2–3 sentences).
Body: choose ONE view (money OR education and jobs): Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link.
Use 1–2 of today's structures (even though / even if / as long as / provided that) and 4+ Essential Words 12 words.
answers: Tahlil kaliti: savol turi — discuss both views + opinion; ikkala fikr va o'z pozitsiyasi kirishda aniq bo'lishi kerak; normativda bitta body yetarli (qaysi fikrni tanlash — o'quvchi ixtiyorida).

NAMUNA kirish + Body (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6, 137 so'z): People disagree about how to support those who live below the poverty line. Some argue that cash payments are the answer, whereas others prefer to invest in education and employment. I believe that education and jobs matter more because they stop poverty from passing from parents to children.

Education is the best way to break the cycle of poverty. Children from poor families often leave school early to earn money, so they remain on a low income. However, as long as they receive real support, such as free textbooks or a university grant, they can get a well-paid job and a better standard of living. For example, some Uzbek universities offer special grants to students from low-income families. Even though competition for these places is strong, many of them win these grants, and this slowly reduces inequality.

Namunadagi g'oya 12-dars namunasidan farqli: 12-darsda inqirozdagi pul yordami va kattalar uchun kasb kurslari ko'rilgan edi; bu yerda ta'lim kambag'allikning ota-onadan bolalarga o'tishini to'xtatishi (bepul darslik, kam ta'minlangan oilalar farzandlariga universitet granti) himoya qilinadi. Pozitsiya ham boshqacha ifodalangan. O'quvchi pul tomonini ham tanlashi mumkin.
Baholash: W-4.0 (jadval shu darsda); NORM-4.0: 10–12 ball — 2 coin; 7–9 — bajarildi; ≤6 — uyda qayta yozadi. So'z soni 110 dan kam — TR ko'pi bilan 1.
why: Bugungi grammatika: as long as they receive real support (shart — 'faqat ... bo'lsa'), Even though competition for these places is strong, many of them win these grants (qarama-qarshilik: raqobat kuchli, lekin baribir yutishadi) — 2 joy, tabiiy.

EW 12 so'zlari: poverty line, poverty, the poor (poor families), income (low income, low-income), standard of living, inequality — 5+ ta; kollokatsiya: live below the poverty line, the cycle of poverty, a better standard of living.
Bog'lovchilar: whereas, because, so, However, such as, For example, Even though — CC uchun 4+ xil.
O'zbek hayotidan misol: kam ta'minlangan oilalar farzandlari uchun universitetlardagi qo'shimcha grant o'rinlari.
class_ex.note: Savol — 12-dars savoli (Jony Academy savoli, kitob SAMPLE ESSAYS uslubida); namuna Jony Academy original matni. Ustoz ishlarni W-4.0 bilan baholab, ballni normativ[] dagi WRITING NORMATIV qatoriga yozadi; umumiy 2–3 xato 14-darsning 'Xatolar ustida ishlash' bosqichiga.

Shu darsning Essential Words so'zlaridan 4+ ta va 2+ kollokatsiya to'g'ri; savol so'zlari parafraz qilingan; imlo xatosi 1–2 ta.
Mavzu so'zlari bor, lekin takror ko'p yoki 3–4 so'z noto'g'ri tanlangan; savol so'zlari ko'chirilgan; imlo xatolari ma'noga xalaqit bermaydi.

items: KARTOCHKA B: Describe a place in Uzbekistan you would like to visit. You should say: where it is ; how you would get there ; what you would do there ; and explain why you want to go there.
answers: NAMUNA B (Band 5.5–6, 160 so'z, ~1.5 daqiqa): I'd like to talk about Karakalpakstan, especially Nukus and Moynaq near the old Aral Sea. They are in the north-west of Uzbekistan, so they are an unusual destination for teenagers. I would get there by overnight train. The journey takes almost a day, but I'd choose the train even though a plane is faster, because it is cheaper and I'd like to see the desert. My itinerary would be simple. In Nukus, I would visit the Savitsky Museum, with its famous collection of paintings. Then I would explore Moynaq and see the old ships lying in the sand where the sea used to be. I'd pack plenty of water and sun cream in case it is hot. I want to go there because we learnt about the Aral Sea disaster at school, and I want to see it with my own eyes. My parents say I can go next year as long as I travel with a tour group.

reading.title: Ibn Battuta — the man who never travelled the same road twice
text: A. In 1325 a 21-year-old law student left Tangier, in Morocco, to make the hajj to Mecca. His journeys lasted almost 29 years, and in that time he travelled about 120,000 kilometres — much farther than Marco Polo — even though travel in his time was slow and dangerous. His name was Ibn Battuta.

B. He crossed North Africa with caravans in case bandits attacked lone travellers. In those days, a traveller could join a caravan provided that he paid his share of the costs. He reached Mecca in 1326 and then, instead of going home, made a rule for himself: never travel the same road twice as long as another road existed. He went on to Iraq and Persia, sailed down the coast of East Africa and crossed the cold steppes of the Golden Horde, where he had to wear three fur coats at once. Later he reached Khwarazm and praised Urgench as one of the greatest cities of the Turks. From there he visited Bukhara and Samarkand before crossing the Hindu Kush mountains to India.

C. He always carried letters from rulers in case he needed help in a foreign city. In Delhi the Sultan made him a qadi, a judge, and paid him well. He stayed for several years, even though the Sultan was famous for his dangerous temper. Then he was sent to China as an ambassador, but he lost almost everything on the way and reached the Maldives with nothing. There he worked as a judge again.

D. In 1348 he came back to Damascus, hoping to see his family there again, but he received only sad news. At that time the Black Death was killing thousands of people a day. He reached Morocco in 1349, but soon set out again — this time across the Sahara to the Mali Empire, when he was nearly 50. His travels ended in 1354. Back home, he dictated his whole story to a scholar, and the book, the Rihla, survives today. Even now, historians use it as one of the most important records of the 14th-century Muslim world, from Central Asia to East Africa.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

tasks.title: 1. Multiple choice (gist)
tasks.instr: (1 daq, yakka) Matnni tez ko'z yugurtirib o'qing va A, B, C yoki D ni tanlang.
items: Why did Ibn Battuta first leave Tangier? A) to work as a judge B) to make the hajj C) to meet Marco Polo D) to study in Delhi
What was his travel rule? A) to travel only with caravans B) not to use the same road again if another existed C) to visit every city twice D) to travel only in winter
What is the Rihla? A) a map B) a letter from the Sultan C) the story of his travels, written down by a scholar D) a caravan route

tasks.title: 2. TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: (7 daq, yakka) Matnga ko'ra: TRUE — matn bilan mos; FALSE — matnga zid; NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqda ma'lumot yo'q.
items: Ibn Battuta travelled a shorter distance than Marco Polo.
Travellers could join a caravan for free.
He learned several new languages during his journeys.
The steppes were so cold that he needed more than one coat.
The Sultan of Delhi gave him a well-paid job.
The scholar who wrote down the Rihla also travelled to Mali.
why: A: "much farther than Marco Polo".
B: "provided that he paid his share of the costs".
Tillar haqida matnda ma'lumot yo'q.
B: "cold steppes … three fur coats at once".
C: "made him a qadi … and paid him well".
D: olimning o'z sayohati haqida ma'lumot yo'q.

in case (B)

in case (C)

listening.audios: Audio fayl yo'q — ustoz transcript'ni o'qiydi (kitobdagi Audio 66–70 bu darsda ishlatilmaydi).
intro: You will hear a tour guide giving information to a group of tourists in Samarkand.
1-tinglash: savollarni o'qib chiqing va javoblarni yozing; 2-tinglash: javoblaringizni tekshiring.
Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

tasks.title: Note completion — ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER
tasks.instr: Samarkand Old City walking tour — eslatmalarni to'ldiring (7 band).
items: Tour starts at: ______ a.m. (in summer)
Bring a bottle of ______
Temperature in July: up to ______ degrees
Length of tour: ______ hours
Ticket includes entry to the city ______
If it rains, the group moves ______
Guide's phone number: ______

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; monolog — ustoz gid rolida o'qiydi (ovozni sekin va aniq).
Guide: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Samarkand Old City walking tour. My name is Dilnoza, and I'll be your guide today.
Guide: Our group meets every day at the main entrance of the Registan. Our website says the tour starts at 9 a.m., but in summer we start earlier — at 8.30 — because the afternoons are so hot.
Guide: So please bring a bottle of water in case it gets hot. Some visitors think it's only about 30 degrees here in July, but it can reach 38 degrees in the shade.
Guide: The tour usually lasts two hours — sorry, I mean three hours, as long as the group stays together and nobody gets lost.
Guide: Provided that you have a ticket, entry to the city museum is included. The mausoleum is not included — you pay for that separately.
Guide: Even if it rains, the tour continues. We simply move inside and visit the old madrasah rooms instead.
Guide: In case of emergency, call me on 90 123 45 76 — no, sorry, 90 123 45 67. I'll repeat that at the end.
Guide: Lunch is not included, but there are nice cafés on Tashkent Street. Right, let's start!

kahoot.q: Take an umbrella in case it ___.
kahoot.explain: in case dan keyin kelasi zamon emas → Present Simple: in case it rains.

kahoot.q: ___ the teacher didn't know the answer — and she knows everything!
kahoot.explain: Even + ot/ega = hatto ... ham. Even though/if dan keyin to'liq gap kerak.

kahoot.q: She smiled ___ she was very tired.
kahoot.explain: Haqiqat bo'lgan qarama-qarshilik → even though (garchi ... bo'lsa ham).

kahoot.q: I'll travel next summer ___ it's expensive — I don't care.
kahoot.explain: Faraz (agar ... bo'lsa ham) → even if.

kahoot.q: ___ fire, use the stairs.
kahoot.explain: In case OF + ot (ogohlantirish yozuvlari): In case of fire.

kahoot.q: You can stay at my place ___ you're quiet.
kahoot.explain: as long as = faqat ... sharti bilan.

kahoot.q: Provided you ___ your work, you can go out.
kahoot.explain: provided / as long as / in case dan keyin Present Simple (will emas).

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: Even he was tired, he smiled.
Even though he was tired, he smiled.
I'll go even if it rains.
kahoot.explain: even bog'lovchi emas — ikki gapni bog'lash uchun even though kerak: Even though he was tired, he smiled.

kahoot.q: "I'll take a map in case I get lost." — ma'nosi?
options: Adashishim mumkin deb, xaritani oldindan olaman.
kahoot.explain: in case = ehtiyot uchun OLDINDAN; if = shart bajarilgandan keyin.

kahoot.q: Providing you ___ a ticket, you can enter the stadium.
kahoot.explain: providing (that) + Present Simple: Providing you have a ticket...

kahoot.q: "as long as / provided" ma'nosi qaysi so'zga eng yaqin?
kahoot.explain: as long as / provided / providing = if (faqat shu shart bajarilsa).

kahoot.q: Tarjima: "Uxlab qolsam deb, ikkita budilnik qo'ydim."
options: I set two alarms in case I overslept.
I set two alarms if I overslept.
I set two alarms in case of I overslept.
I set two alarms even I overslept.
kahoot.explain: Ehtiyot uchun oldindan qilingan harakat → in case; o'tgan zamon hikoyasida in case + Past Simple (overslept). 'in case of' dan keyin faqat ot keladi; 'even' gapni bog'lamaydi.

kahoot.q: A detailed plan of a journey (places, dates, times) is an ___.
kahoot.explain: itinerary = sayohat rejasi (marshrut).

kahoot.q: Hotels, hostels and guesthouses are types of ___.
kahoot.explain: accommodation = turar joy.

kahoot.q: You need a ___ to enter many countries, so apply at the embassy.
kahoot.explain: visa = viza (elchixonadan olinadi).

kahoot.q: Feeling confused in a new country with a very different way of life is ___.
kahoot.explain: culture shock = madaniy shok. homesick = uyni sog'inish.

kahoot.q: Uzbek people are famous for their ___ — they welcome guests warmly.
kahoot.explain: hospitality = mehmondo'stlik.

kahoot.q: Buy travel ___ in case you get ill abroad.
kahoot.explain: travel insurance = sayohat sug'urtasi.

kahoot.q: Travel that protects nature and local people is ___.
kahoot.explain: eco-tourism = ekoturizm (tabiatni asrovchi sayohat).

kahoot.q: "esdalik sovg'a" — inglizcha?
kahoot.explain: souvenir = esdalik sovg'a.

Uy vazifasi tekshiruvi

Tarjima kaliti proyektorda (1 daq, o'quvchi o'zi belgilaydi). Yozma ishlar yig'ib olinadi (W-4.0 bo'yicha keyingi darsgacha tekshiriladi); eng ko'p uchragan 2 xato doskada (2 daq). Bajarmaganlar jurnalga.
YANGI GRAMMATIKA — Referencing (it / this / one / so / the former) + CCQ

Lead-in misoli (kirishdagi 3 gap) → formula (proyektor, grammar.formulas 1–7) → har turga 2–3 misol (grammar.presentation) → CCQ (presentation dagi CCQ qatorlari) → 1 daqiqalik tez og'zaki tekshiruv: ustoz 'I need a pen — a blue …', 'A: I love music. — B: …' deydi, o'quvchilar davom ettiradi.

Ustoz 20 so'zni proyektorda talaffuz + tarjima bilan o'qitadi (3 daq); 6–8 ta qiyin so'zga CCQ yoki misol (3 daq) — dialect, bilingual, native speaker, mother tongue, interpreter, slang, commentary, linguistics; juftlikda A o'zbekchasini, B inglizchasini aytadi (2 daq). Mustahkamlash — flashcard (uyga).
Kombinatsiya — ot → it / this / one; A: … — B: So do I / Neither do I

Kombinatsiya — juftlikda formula → gap → tarjima zanjiri: A formulani yoki o'zbekcha gapni aytadi, B shu formula bilan inglizcha gap tuzib tarjima qiladi, keyin almashadi. 1 daq — ustoz grammar.formulas dan formulani va 1 misolni proyektorda ko'rsatadi; 3 daq — juftlikda (me'yor normativ[1] da); ustoz 2 juftlikni tinglaydi.

Ex1 5 daq yakka (ishora so'zini tanlash) · Ex2 5 daq juftlik (takrorni olib tashlash) · Ex3 5 daq yakka (IELTS Reading ishora savollari + lug'at) · Ex4 3 daq juftlik (paragrafdagi 5 xato). intro: ANAPHORIC reference — OLDIN aytilgan narsaga ishora: "Tom bought a car. He loves it." (He = Tom, it = car). Eng ko'p uchraydi: he/she/it/they, this/that, the + ot.
CATAPHORIC (qo'shimcha) — KEYIN aytiladigan narsaga: "When he arrived, Tom sat down." (he = Tom).
EXOPHORIC — matndan TASHQARIDAGI vaziyatga: "Look at that!" (osmonga ishora qilib); "Pass me that."
COMPARATIVE — taqqoslash orqali bog'lash: "My house is bigger than hers." (hers = her house); "the same", "other", "such".
SUBSTITUTION — iborani boshqa so'z bilan ALMASHTIRISH: "A: I like apples. — B: So do I." (so do I = I like apples too); "one/ones" ("a red one"); "do so"; "I think so / I hope not".
ELLIPSIS — so'zni TUSHIRIB qoldirish: "She likes tea. I don't (like tea)." / "Can you come? — I can (come)."

DEMONSTRATIVES — this/that/these/those: "I like this book. That one is boring." Yozma matnda "this" ko'pincha hozirgina aytilgan fikrga ishora qiladi: "Prices rose. This surprised everyone." (that ham to'g'ri — masofa yoki ta'kid beradi).
formulas: Anaphoric
OT … + he/she/it/they/this/the + ot
Tom bought a car. He loves it.
Tom mashina sotib oldi. U uni yaxshi ko'radi.
Exophoric
this/that/it + tashqi vaziyat
Look at that! (osmonga ishora)
Ana unga qara!
Comparative
comparative + than + hers/mine/the other; the same/such
My house is bigger than hers.
Mening uyim unikidan katta.
Substitution
So do I / Neither do I / one, ones / do so
A: I like apples. — B: So do I. / I need a pen — a blue one.
A: Men olmani yaxshi ko'raman. — B: Men ham. / Menga ruchka kerak — ko'k rangdagisi.
Ellipsis
S + yordamchi (fe'l tushiriladi)
She likes tea. I don't. / Can you come? — I can.
U choyni yaxshi ko'radi. Men esa yo'q. / Kela olasanmi? — Ha.
Demonstratives
this/that/these/those (+ one)
I like this book. That one is boring. / Prices rose. This surprised everyone.
Bu kitob yoqadi. Unisi zerikarli. / Narxlar oshdi. Bu hammani hayratga soldi.
The former / the latter
A va B … the former (= A) / the latter (= B)
Tea and coffee are both popular; the former is cheaper.
Choy va qahva ikkalasi ham mashhur; birinchisi arzonroq.
presentation: "Zamakhshari wrote a dictionary. It is still used." — what is "it"?
"It" refers to the dictionary — anaphoric.
"Look at that manuscript!" — what kind of reference?
Exophoric — the speaker points at something outside the text.
"Arabic grammar is harder than that of Persian." — what does "that" refer to?
that = the grammar (Persian grammar) — comparative reference.
"I speak Uzbek. So does my teacher." — what does "so does" replace?
"Speaks Uzbek" — substitution.
"He learned Arabic; his brother didn't." — what is missing?
"Learn Arabic" — ellipsis.
CCQ: Tom bought a car. He loves it.
Is "he" a person? (Yes, Tom) Is "it" a person? (No, the car)
CCQ: A: I speak Uzbek. — B: So do I.
Does B speak Uzbek? (Yes) Does B repeat the whole sentence? (No, "so do I" replaces it)
CCQ: She likes tea. I don't.
Do I like tea? (No) Which words are missing? (like tea)
CCQ: I need a pen — a blue one.
Is "one" a number here? (No) What does it replace? (pen)
CCQ: Russian and Korean are popular here; the latter is newer.
Which language is newer? (Korean) Which one is "the former"? (Russian)
notes: IELTS Reading: "What does 'this' in line 12 refer to?" — javob odatda OLDINGI gapdagi ot yoki butun fikr.
Substitution vs ellipsis: substitution so'z QO'YADI (so, one, do), ellipsis so'z OLIB TASHLAYDI.
Writing: "This" + ot aniqroq: "This increase surprised…" (this/that farqi — quyidagi savolda).
O'quvchi so'raydi: "Prices rose. That surprised everyone." xatomi? — Javob: yo'q, to'g'ri; this ko'proq ishlatiladi, that esa masofa yoki ta'kid beradi.
O'quvchi so'raydi: Nega "a blue" emas, "a blue one"? — Javob: sanaladigan birlik ot takrorlanmasa, sifatdan keyin one qo'yiladi; ko'plikda — ones (the red ones).
O'quvchi so'raydi: "So do I" va "Me too" farqi bormi? — Javob: ma'nosi bir xil; Me too — so'zlashuv uslubi, So do I — neytral; Speaking'da ikkalasi ham to'g'ri.
mistakes: Tom bought a car. It loves it.
Tom bought a car. He loves it.
A: I like apples. — B: So I do.
A: I like apples. — B: So do I.
'Men ham' ma'nosida: So + yordamchi + ega. (So I do — 'ha, rostdan ham' degan boshqa ma'no.)
She likes tea. I don't like.
I need a pen, a blue.
I need a pen, a blue one.
Butun fikr (birlik) → this (that ham to'g'ri); these — faqat ko'plik otga.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Books (og'zaki): Part 1, 2, 3
class_ex.instr: (12 daq, juftlik) 2 daq — Part 1: 4 savolga juftlikda navbat bilan javob (javob + sabab + misol). 1 daq — Kartochka A bo'yicha tayyorgarlik: faqat 5–6 kalit so'z. 2 daq — A Kartochka A bo'yicha gapiradi, B S-CHECK-4.0 ni to'ldiradi. 2 daq — ustoz NAMUNA A ni o'qiydi, o'quvchilar box'dagi iboralar eshitilganda belgilaydi. 2 daq — B shu kartochka bo'yicha gapiradi (box'dan kamida 2 ibora bilan), A belgilaydi. 2 daq — Part 3: 3 savolni juftlikda muhokama qilish. 1 daq — ustoz 1 ta umumiy feedback (S-4.0). ICQ: Necha daqiqa tayyorlanasiz va nima yozasiz? (1 daqiqa, 5–6 kalit so'z) B box'dan nechta ibora ishlatadi? (kamida 2)
items: Part 1: Do you like reading? What do you usually read?
Part 1: Do you prefer paper books or e-books?
Part 1: Did you read a lot as a child?
Part 1: Where do you usually read?
KARTOCHKA A: Describe a book you enjoyed reading. You should say: what the book is ; who wrote it ; what it is about ; and explain why you enjoyed it.
Part 3: Do young people read less than in the past? Why?
Part 3: Should schools make students read more books?
Part 3: Are films better than books for learning about a story?
box: I'd like to talk about …, which I read …
I read it in translation and in English; the former was …, but the latter …
… and so did my sister / so does my friend
It taught me a lot of new vocabulary.
In my view, the former is …, while the latter is …
answers: Part 1 (1) namuna: Yes, I do, although I don't read as much as I'd like. I usually read short stories and articles in English on my phone, and they really help my vocabulary. My best friend prefers fantasy novels, and so does her brother.

Part 1 (2) namuna: I prefer paper books, because I can write notes in them and they don't hurt my eyes. E-books are cheaper, though, and they are easier to carry on a long trip, so I use the latter when I travel.
Part 1 (3) namuna: Yes, quite a lot. My parents bought me books of Uzbek folk tales, and I read them again and again. That habit helped me a lot with spelling at school.

Part 1 (4) namuna: Mostly in my room, before I go to sleep, because it is the only quiet place in our flat in the evening. Sometimes I read on the bus too, but I find this difficult when it is crowded.

NAMUNA A (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6, 172 so'z, ~1.5–2 daqiqa): I'd like to talk about a novel called Wonder, which I read last year. It was written by R. J. Palacio, an American author, and it was her first book for young readers. The story is about a boy called Auggie, who has a different face because of a medical condition. He goes to a normal school for the first time, and some children are unkind to him, while others become his real friends. What I liked is that the story is told by several characters, not only by Auggie. This helped me understand how each person felt. I read the book twice, in an Uzbek translation and in English; the former was easy, but the latter taught me a lot of new vocabulary. I enjoyed it for two reasons. Firstly, the English is simple, even though it was written for native speakers. Secondly, it taught me to be kind to people who look different. It isn't classic literature, but my younger sister read it after me, and so did my cousin.
Namunadagi bugungi grammatika: which I read / it was written (it), This helped me, the former … the latter, so did my cousin. EW14: translation, vocabulary, native speakers, literature.

Part 3 (1) namuna: Yes, I think young people read fewer books than before. The main reason is smartphones: teenagers spend hours on social media, and this leaves little time for long novels. However, they still read a lot of short texts online, so the picture is not all bad.

Part 3 (2) namuna: I believe schools should, but in a smart way. If students can choose their own books, they usually enjoy reading; when a book is forced on them, they often don't. For example, a school could run a monthly reading competition with a free choice of books.

Part 3 (3) namuna: It depends on the purpose. A film is faster and easier to follow, but a book shows the characters' thoughts in much more detail. In my view, the former is good for entertainment, while the latter is better for learning and for building vocabulary.
class_ex.note: S-CHECK-4.0 (sherik B tinglab belgilaydi, Ha / Yo'q): 1) kartochkadagi 4 band aytildimi; 2) 1.5 daqiqadan uzoq, uzun pauzasiz; 3) box'dagi iboralardan 2+ ta; 4) bugungi grammatika (it / this / one / so do I / the former – the latter) 1–2 marta to'g'ri; 5) Part 3 javobi: fikr + sabab + misol. Ustoz 3–4 o'quvchini S-4.0 bo'yicha jurnalga qayd etadi. box: Number of students learning four foreign languages at a language centre, 2015 and 2025 (o'quv maqsadida to'qilgan ma'lumot)
items: Task: The table shows the number of students learning four foreign languages at a language centre in 2015 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

Reja: Overview — eng mashhur til (English), eng tez o'sgan til (Korean) va yagona kamaygan til (Russian) / Detail 1: English / Detail 2: Russian va Korean (the former / the latter) / Detail 3: Arabic. this figure / the former / the latter / that of — 1–2 marta, tabiiy joyda.

Checklist: 1) overview bor; 2) har detailda raqam va yil; 3) kamida 2 bog'lovchi (while, whereas, by contrast); 4) ishora so'zlari (this figure, the former / the latter, that of) nimaga ishora qilishi aniq.
answers: NAMUNA (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6): The table compares the number of students who were learning four foreign languages at a language centre in 2015 and 2025. Overall, English was the most popular language in both years and Korean grew the fastest, while Russian was the only language that lost students. In 2015, 320 students studied English, and by 2025 this figure had risen to 540. Russian and Korean moved in opposite directions: the former fell from 210 to 150 students, whereas the latter more than quadrupled, from 40 to 180. The number of Arabic learners also went up, from 60 to 90, but the growth in Korean was much faster than that of Arabic.

answers: NAMUNA B (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6, 147 so'z): The person I want to describe is my literature teacher from secondary school, Dilnoza opa. I know her well, because she taught our class from the fifth to the eighth grade. What she did was very simple: every Friday she brought a box of books to the classroom and let us choose one. She never asked for long reports; she only asked us to tell the class one interesting thing about it. At first I always chose the thinnest books. She noticed this, but she didn't criticise me. Instead, she gave me a short adventure story and said I would love it, and she was right. This changed me a lot. I started reading every evening, my spelling and vocabulary improved, and literature became my favourite subject. Today I still read before bed, and so does my younger brother, because I pass my books on to him.

homework.title: Yozma ish: TO'LIQ INSHO (250 so'z, 40 daqiqa)
homework.instr: Savol: "Some people think minority languages should be protected; others believe one global language would be better. Discuss both views and give your opinion." Kamida 250 so'z, 40 daqiqa. Reja: Intro — savolni o'z so'zingiz bilan + pozitsiya / Body 1 — bitta global til tarafdorlari: 2 sabab + misol / Body 2 — ozchilik tillarini himoya qilish tarafdorlari: 2 sabab + misol / Conclusion — xulosa + fikringiz.
answers: NAMUNA (Band 5.5–6, original, faqat ustoz uchun): Today many small languages are disappearing, while English is spoken almost everywhere. Some people believe that one global language would make life easier, but others argue that minority languages must be protected. In my opinion, both goals are possible: everyone can learn a global language and still keep their own. On the one hand, a single global language has clear advantages. Firstly, it makes communication much easier in business, science and travel. When doctors or engineers from different countries share one language, they can work together faster and avoid costly misunderstandings. Secondly, it saves money and time. Countries spend large amounts on translation, and a common language would reduce this cost. For these reasons, many parents want their children to learn English as early as possible. On the other hand, a minority language is much more than a tool for communication. It carries a community's history, songs and traditional knowledge, and when a language dies, so does much of this knowledge. Moreover, people who lose their mother tongue often lose touch with their roots and their cultural identity. For example, children who speak only a global language may not be able to talk to their grandparents or understand their own folk songs. In conclusion, a global language is useful, but it should not replace other languages. I believe governments should support minority languages through bilingual education, local media and books, while schools also teach a global language such as English. In this way, people can enjoy the benefits of a global language without losing their own.
Baholash: W-4.0 (class_ex dagi jadval, 4 mezon × 0–3 = 12), NORM-4.0

reading.title: Mahmud az-Zamakhshari — a Khwarazmian master of Arabic
text: A. In 1075 a boy called Mahmud was born in Zamakhshar, a village in Khwarazm. The village later gave him the name the world remembers: az-Zamakhshari. As a young man he travelled to Bukhara and other cities to study. On one of his journeys he lost a leg — many sources say because of frostbite in heavy snow — and for the rest of his life he walked on a wooden one. It is said that he carried a letter from witnesses in case anyone thought he had lost it as a punishment.

B. Arabic was not his mother tongue. In Khwarazm at that time people spoke Khwarazmian, Persian and Turkic, and he probably grew up hearing more than one of them. Yet it was Arabic, the language of science and religion in the region, that he mastered best. Later he lived in Mecca for several years; this earned him the title Jar Allah, 'God's neighbour'. His grammar book, Al-Mufassal, was so clear that teachers in many Arab lands used it for centuries.

C. His most famous book is Al-Kashshaf, a commentary on the Quran that explains the meaning of the verses through language and rhetoric. Some scholars disagreed with his religious views, but they still used this book, because it was so useful for understanding the language. He also wrote Asas al-Balagha, a dictionary that separates the literal meanings of words from their figurative ones.

D. Another of his books, Muqaddimat al-Adab, explains Arabic words in Persian, and one copy also gives Khwarazmian translations. The latter are priceless today: the Khwarazmian language is extinct, and this copy is one of the few written records of it. Linguists still study the copy to learn how people in Khwarazm once spoke.

E. Zamakhshari returned to Khwarazm and died in Gurganj, its old capital, in 1144. Nearly nine centuries later, students of Arabic still open his books, and linguists still use his dictionaries. This is the unusual story of a man who lost a leg but never lost a word.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; 1-rol (Tutor) — ustoz, 2-rol (Laylo) — kuchli o'quvchi (yoki ovozni o'zgartiring).
Tutor: So, Laylo, your project is on an endangered language. Which community did you choose?
Laylo: A small mountain village. Its language has no written form, and only older people speak it well.
Tutor: How many fluent speakers did you find?
Laylo: About ninety — sorry, I checked again: about sixty. The others have moved to the city.
Tutor: And how did you collect your data?
Laylo: We recorded interviews. At first we planned to use a questionnaire, but most of the older speakers can't read, so that didn't work.
Tutor: That makes sense. How long were the recordings?
Laylo: Twelve hours in total. The longest one was with a woman of eighty-five. She sang old songs and explained the words of each one.
Tutor: Excellent. Why do you think young people stop using the language?
Laylo: Mainly because of school. Lessons are in Uzbek, so children speak it all day, and when they come home, they speak it with their parents too.
Tutor: So what do you suggest?
Laylo: A small dictionary with pictures. The village teacher likes this idea, and so do the parents.
Tutor: Good. When is your report due?
Laylo: On the 14th of May — no, wait, it's the 21st. The 14th is our presentation.
Tutor: Fine. Send me the first draft by Friday.

kahoot.q: She likes green tea, but I ___.

kahoot.q: A: Can you come to the party on Saturday? B: Yes, I ___.

kahoot.explain: I hope not = I hope it won't rain. Ijobiysi: I hope so.

kahoot.explain: Comparative reference: hers = her house. her's — apostrof bilan yozilmaydi.

kahoot.q: When ___ arrived, Tom sat down near the window.

A: I like apples. — B: So do I.

intro: LINKING VERB — egani uning HOLATi bilan bog'laydi; keyin SIFAT (ravish emas): "He seems tired." / "The soup tastes delicious."
3 guruh: HOLAT — be, seem, appear, remain, stay; SEZGI — feel, look, sound, taste, smell; O'ZGARISH — become, get, grow, turn.
FARQ: "She looked sad" (holat — sifat) vs "She looked at me sadly" (harakat — ravish).
+ OT: look/sound/feel like + ot ("It sounds like a good idea"); seem + to be ("He seems to be ill"). feel like + V-ing ("I feel like dancing") = xohlamoq, linking verb emas.
formulas: Holat: be / seem / appear
S + be/seem/appear + SIFAT
She is happy. / He seems tired. / She appears nervous.
U baxtli. / U charchagandek. / U asabiydek ko'rinadi.
Holat: remain / stay
S + remain/stay + SIFAT
He remained calm. / She stayed silent.
U xotirjam qoldi. / U jim turdi.
Sezgi: feel / look
S + feel/look + SIFAT
I feel cold. / You look great!
Sovuq sezyapman. / Sen zo'r ko'rinyapsan!
Sezgi: sound / taste / smell
S + sound/taste/smell + SIFAT
That sounds interesting. / The soup tastes delicious. / The flowers smell nice.
Bu qiziqarli eshitilyapti. / Sho'rva mazali. / Gullar yoqimli hidli.
O'zgarish: become / get
S + become/get + SIFAT (yoki become + ot)
They became friends. / It's getting dark.
Ular do'st bo'lib qolishdi. / Qorong'i tushyapti.
O'zgarish: grow / turn
S + grow/turn + SIFAT
He grew angry. / She turned pale.
U asta-sekin g'azablanib bordi. / Uning rangi oqarib ketdi.
presentation: CCQ: She looked sad.
Is she doing an action with her eyes? (No) Are we describing her? (Yes)
CCQ: She looked at me sadly.
Is she doing an action? (Yes) Does 'sadly' say how she did it? (Yes)
CCQ: It's getting dark.
Is it completely dark now? (Not yet) Is it changing? (Yes)
CCQ: He remained calm.
Was the situation difficult? (Yes) Did his feeling change? (No)
notes: be, become, remain + ot: "He became a teacher". seem/look/sound + ot — odatda like bilan (BrE da 'It sounds a good idea' ham to'g'ri). Sifat oldidan like yo'q.
get/grow/turn ≈ become: get — og'zaki (get tired); grow — asta-sekin … bo'lib bormoq (grew older); turn — rang/keskin o'zgarish (turned pale), + artiklsiz kasb (turned professional).
O'quvchi so'raydi: Nega 'I feel bad', 'badly' emas? — Javob: feel bu yerda holat (linking verb), shuning uchun sifat; ravish harakat qanday bajarilganini bildiradi.
O'quvchi so'raydi: look doim sifat bilan keladimi? — Javob: yo'q. 'ko'rinmoq' — sifat (She looks happy); 'look at' (qaramoq) — ravish (She looked at me happily).
mistakes: sound + sifat; like faqat ot oldidan (It sounds like a plan).
He became angry. / He grew angry.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Music (og'zaki): Part 1, 2, 3
class_ex.instr: (10 daq, juftlik) 1 daq — Part 1: 4 savolga juftlikda qisqa javob (javob + sabab). 1 daq — tayyorgarlik: Kartochka A uchun faqat 5–6 kalit so'z yoziladi. 2 daq — A gapiradi, B S-CHECK-4.0 ni to'ldiradi. 2 daq — ustoz NAMUNA A ni o'qiydi, o'quvchilar box'dagi iboralarni eshitganda belgilaydi. 2 daq — B shu kartochkada gapiradi (box'dan kamida 2 ibora bilan). 1 daq — Part 3 juftlikda: umumiy, 3-shaxsda javob. 1 daq — ustoz 1 ta umumiy feedback (S-4.0). ICQ: Necha daqiqa tayyorlanasiz? (1) Box'dan nechta ibora ishlatasiz? (kamida 2)
items: Part 1: What kind of music do you like?
Part 1: When do you usually listen to music?
Part 1: Did you learn to play an instrument at school?
Part 1: Do you prefer listening alone or with friends?
KARTOCHKA A: Describe a song or piece of music that is special to you. You should say: what it is ; when you first heard it ; how often you listen to it ; and explain why it is special to you.
Part 3: Can music change people's mood?
Part 3: Should children learn a musical instrument at school?
Part 3: Is traditional music still popular with young people?
box: It's a song that really means a lot to me.
I first heard it when I was …
The melody sounds calm / sad / cheerful.
Whenever I play it, I feel relaxed.
It helps me cope with stress and improves my mood.
It became popular with teenagers because …
That's why it is so special to me.
answers: 1) I mostly like calm pop songs and some Uzbek folk music, because they help me relax. For example, when I do my homework, soft music sounds perfect in the background.
2) Usually on my way to school and in the evening. The bus is often noisy, so music keeps my mood good and I feel less stressed before lessons.
3) Not really. In music lessons we mostly sang and tried the doira a little, but I never learned it properly. I'd like to try the dutar one day.
4) I prefer listening alone with headphones, because I can focus on the words. But at birthday parties it's fun to listen with friends and sing together.

NAMUNA A (Band 5.5–6, 174 so'z, ~1.5–2 daqiqa, faqat ustoz uchun): I'd like to talk about a song that is really special to me. It's an old Uzbek folk song, and I first heard it when I was about seven, at my cousin's wedding in Samarkand. Musicians played it on the dutar and the doira, and everybody started dancing. Later I found it online, and now I listen to it two or three times a week, usually in the evening or on the bus. The melody sounds calm and a little sad at the beginning, but then it gets fast and cheerful. Why is it special? Firstly, whenever I play it, I feel relaxed, even after a long day at school. When I'm stressed before an exam, it helps me cope with my nerves and improves my mood. Secondly, it reminds me of my family and that wonderful day. Last year a young singer recorded a modern version, and it became popular with teenagers in our city. So for me this song connects the past and the present, and it's good for my wellbeing too.
1) Yes, I think it can. Fast songs make people feel energetic, while slow music sounds calm and can reduce stress levels. For example, many cafes play quiet music so that customers stay relaxed.

2) I believe it would be useful, because playing an instrument teaches children patience and builds their confidence. However, it should not be compulsory, since some children are more interested in sport or art.

3) Partly. Most teenagers listen to pop or rap online, but traditional music remains important at weddings and holidays. Also, some young singers mix folk melodies with modern beats, so it is becoming popular again.
why: Bugungi grammatika (linking verb + SIFAT): sounds calm, gets fast and cheerful, I feel relaxed, became popular — fe'ldan keyin ravish emas, sifat.

Insho umumiy, 3-shaxsda yoziladi. ICQ: Savolda nechta savol bor? (2 — sabablar va yechimlar) Body 2 da nima haqida yozasiz va necha so'z? (Yechimlar, 60–80 so'z)
box: Question: People today find it difficult to balance their work and personal life. What are the causes? What solutions can you suggest?

MODEL — Introduction: These days, many adults find it hard to give enough time to both their jobs and their private lives. In my opinion, this problem is mainly caused by long working days and constant contact through phones, but it can be reduced if employers and workers make a few practical changes.

MODEL — Body 1: There are two main causes of this problem. Firstly, the cost of living keeps rising, so many people take a second job or work late into the evening. As a result, they often feel exhausted when they get home and have little energy for their families. Secondly, smartphones keep work close all the time. For example, in Tashkent many office workers receive new tasks in Telegram groups late at night, so they become stressed even at weekends, and some of them start to suffer from insomnia.
items: Savol turi qanday? Savolda nechta savol bor va shuning uchun nechta body kerak?
Pozitsiya (asosiy javob) kirishning qaysi gapida?
Bugungi grammatika qayerda? Body 1 dan linking verb + sifat birikmalarini toping (kamida 2 ta).
Qaysi EW 15 (Psychology, emotions and mental health) so'zlari ishlatilgan?
Body 1 dagi bog'lovchilarni toping: sabablar qanday tartiblangan?
TASK: Write Body 2 (60–80 words) about solutions: Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link. Ideas: rules for companies / personal habits / family time.
answers: 1) Causes + solutions (sabab va yechim) — savolda 2 ta savol: Body 1 — sabablar, Body 2 — yechimlar.
2) Kirishning 2-gapi: 'In my opinion, this problem is mainly caused by long working days and constant contact through phones, but it can be reduced if …' — ikkala savolga ham qisqa javob beradi.
3) Linking verb + sifat: feel exhausted, become stressed (Body 1); Body 2 da yana: stay calm.
4) EW 15: exhausted, stressed, insomnia (suffer from insomnia) — Body 1; Body 2 da yana: wellbeing, cope with (pressure).
5) Bog'lovchilar: Firstly, Secondly, so, As a result, For example — 2 ta sabab: yashash narxi (ikkinchi ish, kechgacha ishlash) va smartfon orqali doimiy ish xabarlari.

NAMUNA Body 2 + Conclusion (faqat ustoz uchun): However, this situation can be improved in several ways. To begin with, companies should agree on a clear time after which managers do not send messages, except in a real emergency. This would help workers stay calm in the evening. On the other hand, people also need to protect their own wellbeing, for example by keeping one evening a week for sport or a family dinner. Small habits like these help them cope with pressure much better. / In conclusion, people struggle to balance work and home life because they work long hours and are always connected to their jobs. If employers respect free time and workers plan their week carefully, a healthier and happier lifestyle is possible.
To'liq namuna: 253 so'z (kirish 50 · Body 1 86 · Body 2 77 · xulosa 40).
why: Bugungi grammatika: feel exhausted, become stressed, stay calm — linking verbdan keyin SIFAT (exhaustedly, calmly emas): bu yerda harakat emas, odamning holati tasvirlanadi.
O'quvchi o'z Body 2 sida kamida 1 ta linking verb + sifat ishlatsin (masalan, feel relaxed, remain healthy).
EW 15 so'zlari: exhausted — holdan toygan; stressed — stressda; insomnia — uyqusizlik; wellbeing — farovonlik; cope with (pressure) — (bosimga) bardosh bermoq.
O'zbek misoli: Toshkentda ofis xodimlariga kechasi Telegram guruhida topshiriq kelishi — aniq, mahalliy misol TR va CC uchun ball beradi.

items: Question: People today find it difficult to balance their work and personal life. What are the causes? What solutions can you suggest?
Plan: 1) Introduction — paraphrase the question + your short answer (main causes and main solutions).
Plan: 2) Body 1 — causes: Topic sentence -> 2 causes with explanation -> example from Uzbekistan.
Plan: 3) Body 2 — solutions: Topic sentence -> 2 solutions (employers / workers) -> example -> link.

answers: NAMUNA (Band 5.5–6, 253 so'z, Jony Academy original, faqat ustoz uchun):

These days, many adults find it hard to give enough time to both their jobs and their private lives. In my opinion, this problem is mainly caused by long working days and constant contact through phones, but it can be reduced if employers and workers make a few practical changes.

There are two main causes of this problem. Firstly, the cost of living keeps rising, so many people take a second job or work late into the evening. As a result, they often feel exhausted when they get home and have little energy for their families. Secondly, smartphones keep work close all the time. For example, in Tashkent many office workers receive new tasks in Telegram groups late at night, so they become stressed even at weekends, and some of them start to suffer from insomnia.

However, this situation can be improved in several ways. To begin with, companies should agree on a clear time after which managers do not send messages, except in a real emergency. This would help workers stay calm in the evening. On the other hand, people also need to protect their own wellbeing, for example by keeping one evening a week for sport or a family dinner. Small habits like these help them cope with pressure much better.

In conclusion, people struggle to balance work and home life because they work long hours and are always connected to their jobs. If employers respect free time and workers plan their week carefully, a healthier and happier lifestyle is possible.

reading.title: Billie Eilish — she looked nothing like a pop star, and that became the point
text: A. Billie Eilish was born in Los Angeles in 2001 and was home-schooled by parents who both worked in acting and music. As a young teenager, she recorded a song called "Ocean Eyes" with her older brother, Finneas, in a small bedroom studio at the family home. The song sounded quiet and unusual, and it quickly became popular online. A few years later she seemed to be everywhere, and at 18 she became the youngest artist to win all four main Grammy awards in one night.

B. From the start, she looked different from a typical pop star, and that was deliberate. She wore baggy clothes because she did not want people to judge her body. Her songs about nightmares and dark feelings sounded honest, and many teenagers felt understood.

C. Fame, however, did not always feel exciting. Eilish has Tourette syndrome, which causes small tics, and she kept it private for years before she talked about it in public. She has also said that she felt very low and lonely in her early teens. Instead of hiding these problems, she has spoken openly about depression, body image and therapy.

D. Her openness seemed surprising at first, but it soon became part of a wider change. Mental health, which used to remain a private subject, turned into something that young people and celebrities discuss openly. Many fans have said that her interviews made them feel less alone.

E. Her music kept growing too. The title song of her album "Happier Than Ever" starts soft and turns loud and angry. Her theme for a James Bond film won an Oscar, and "What Was I Made For?", written for the Barbie film, won a second one, which made her the youngest person to win two Oscars. She also stays active on climate issues. The message of her story seems simple: you can feel strange and still turn out fine.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

tasks.instr: Ma'ruza bo'yicha 7 ta bo'shliqni to'ldiring.
items: Number of students in the survey: ___
Most common problem: poor ___

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; monolog (IELTS Part 4, ma'ruza) — raqamlarni aniq ayting.
Lecturer: Good morning. Today we're looking at a survey of stress among students at one college, and at what seems to help them stay calm.
Lecturer: The college asked six hundred students — sorry, six hundred and fifty — to answer questions about their feelings before exams.

Lecturer: The researchers expected fear of failure to be the biggest problem. In fact, the most common problem was poor sleep. Students who slept less than seven hours a night felt anxious far more often.
Lecturer: The second problem was time online. Mood seemed to get worse after about three hours a day on social media — not two hours, as an earlier study suggested.
Lecturer: So what helped? First, exercise. A twenty-minute walk made most students feel calmer.
Lecturer: Second, talking. Students who spoke to a friend or a counsellor stayed more relaxed than those who kept their worries to themselves.
Lecturer: As a result, the college has opened a quiet room in the library. At first it was open on Mondays only, but now it's open every weekday.
Lecturer: Next week we'll look at how teachers can notice stress. Please read chapter five — no, chapter six — before then.

intro: BACKSHIFT — reporting fe'l o'tgan zamonda (said, told) bo'lsa, ichki gap bir qadam ORQAGA: Present Simple → Past Simple; Present Continuous → Past Continuous; Present Perfect → Past Perfect; Past Simple → Past Perfect; Past Continuous → Past Perfect Continuous.
MODALLAR: will → would; can → could; may → might; must → had to (yoki must qoladi); should/could/might/would — o'zgarmaydi.
OLMOSH: "I" → he/she; "we" → they; "my" → his/her; "you" → me/us (kim bilan gaplashganiga qarab).

VAQT/JOY: now → then; today → that day; yesterday → the day before; tomorrow → the next/following day; last week → the week before; next year → the following year; here → there; this → that; ago → before.
SAY vs TELL: said (that) + gap; told + KIMGA + (that) + gap. "He said he was tired." / "He told me he was tired."
Umumiy haqiqat va hozir ham to'g'ri gap — backshift shart emas: "She said the Earth goes round the Sun."
formulas: Present Simple → Past Simple
S + said (that) + S + V2
He said, "I work hard." → He said he worked hard.
U qattiq ishlashini aytdi.
Present Continuous → Past Continuous
S + said + S + was/were + V-ing
She said, "I am studying." → She said she was studying.
U o'qiyotganini aytdi.
Present Perfect / Past Simple → Past Perfect
S + said + S + had + V3
"We have finished." → They said they had finished. / "I lost my key." → I said I had lost my key.
Ular tugatganini aytishdi. / Kalitimni yo'qotganimni aytdim.
will / can / may → would / could / might
S + said + S + would/could/might + V1
"I will call you." → She said she would call me. / "I can swim." → He said he could swim. / "I may come." → She said she might come.
U menga qo'ng'iroq qilishini aytdi. / U suza olishini aytdi. / U kelishi mumkinligini aytdi.
Vaqt so'zlari + tell
S + told + OB'EKT + (that) + gap; now → then, tomorrow → the next day
"I'll see you here tomorrow." → She told me she would see me there the next day.
U meni ertasi kuni o'sha yerda ko'rishini aytdi.
ZAXIRA: Past Continuous → Past Perfect Continuous
S + said + S + had been + V-ing
"I was watching TV." → He said he had been watching TV.
U TV ko'rayotgan bo'lganini aytdi.
presentation: What did your grandmother tell you?
She told me she had raised six children alone.
What did she say about tomorrow?
She said she would visit her parents the next day.
CCQ: She said she was tired.
Is she tired now? (Maybe — we don't know) Who said it? (she)
CCQ: He told me he would call.
Did he say 'I will call'? (Yes) Who did he speak to? (me)
CCQ: She said she had lost her phone.
Did she lose it before she spoke? (Yes) Which came first — losing or speaking? (losing)
CCQ: (last week) "I'll see you tomorrow." → He said he would see me the next day.
Is it today's 'tomorrow'? (No) Which day? (the day after he spoke)
notes: Reporting fe'l HOZIRGI zamonda (says, tells) — backshift yo'q: "He says he is tired."
"that" tushirilishi mumkin; tell + kimga (told me), say — odamsiz yoki said to me. Istisno: tell the truth / a lie / a story.
Past Perfect ichki gapda o'zgarmaydi (had lost → had lost).
O'quvchi so'raydi: Nega "He said me" xato? — Javob: say dan keyin odam to'g'ridan-to'g'ri kelmaydi; told me yoki said to me.
O'quvchi so'raydi: Past Simple doim Past Perfect ga o'tadimi? — Javob: yo'q; tartib aniq bo'lsa qolishi mumkin: He said he moved here in 2010. Mashqlarda ikkalasi qabul qilinadi.
O'quvchi so'raydi: Bugun, shu yerda aytilgan gapda ham tomorrow o'zgaradimi? — Javob: yo'q; vaqt/joy o'zgarmasa so'z ham qoladi: She said she would call me tomorrow.
mistakes: He said me he was tired.
He told me he was tired. / He said he was tired.
Last week she told me she was studying now.
Last week she told me she was studying then (at that time).
They told that they had left.
They told me that they had left. / They said that they had left.

items: 1. Darsdan oldin: o'quvchi varag'ini (A, B, C savollari va matni, D shakli, E savoli) har o'quvchiga chop eting. Listening skripti, javob kalitlari va namuna paragrafni o'quvchilarga ko'rsatmang. Listening skriptini ovoz chiqarib 1 marta mashq qilib oling (rollar: AGENT — ustoz, AZIZ — ovozni o'zgartirib ustozning o'zi yoki ikkinchi ustoz; o'quvchi o'qimaydi, chunki u javobni oldindan ko'radi).

2. 0–1 daq: telefonlar yig'iladi, o'quvchilar alohida o'tiradi, varaqqa ism va sana yoziladi. Proyektorga faqat taymer va joriy bo'lim nomi chiqariladi; bu sahifa proyektorda ochilmaydi, 'Javobni ko'rsat' tugmasi test davomida bosilmaydi.

3. Vaqt: A Grammatika — 10 daq, B Lug'at — 5 daq, C Reading — 10 daq, D Listening — 5 daq, E Writing — 10 daq (jami 40 daq). Har bo'lim tugashiga 1 daqiqa qolganda ogohlantiring va keyingi bo'limni e'lon qiling; kech qolganga vaqt qo'shilmaydi.

4. D Listening tartibi (5 daq): 30 soniya — o'quvchilar 1–5 shaklni o'qiydi; skript 1-marta o'qiladi (taxminan 1 daq 20 s, oddiy tezlikda, raqam va harflarni aniq); 20 soniya tanaffus; 2-marta o'qiladi; 40 soniya — javoblarni tekshirish. Distraktorlarni (five → four, twelfth → fourteenth, tent → guesthouse, map → torch) ta'kidlamang va takrorlamang.
5. 40-daqiqada varaqlar yig'iladi. Kalit va natija test paytida aytilmaydi; natija tahlili 17-darsda (PT3 NATIJA TAHLILI, 8 daqiqa).

6. Tekshirish (24 soat ichida): A — har savol 1 ball (9–15-savollarda faqat to'g'ri shakl/tuzatish; 13–15 da xato so'zni topib, to'g'ri tuzatsa 1 ball, faqat topsa 0.5 ball). B — har so'z 1 ball; bitta harf imlo xatosi 0.5 ball. C — har savol 1 ball; 5–8 da uch so'z va undan uzun javob 0, ma'noni buzmaydigan imlo xatosi kechiriladi. D — har bo'shliq 1 ball; ismda imlo aniq bo'lishi shart (Rahimov), raqamlar raqam yoki so'z bilan qabul qilinadi. E — W-4.0 rubrikasi, 4 mezon × 0–3 = 12 ball; 70 so'zdan kam bo'lsa TR ko'pi bilan 1 ball.

7. Ball jadvali (maks. / 50% chegarasi): A Grammatika 15 / 7.5; B Lug'at 10 / 5; C Reading 8 / 4; D Listening 5 / 2.5 (butun ballda — 3); E Writing 12 / 6; JAMI 50 — 70% = 35 ball, 60% = 30 ball, 80% = 40 ball, 90% = 45 ball.
8. Natijani tizimga bo'limlar kesimida (A, B, C, D, E va jami) kiriting; qaror TEST-4.0 jadvali bo'yicha (javoblar maydonida).
answers: O'TDI: jami 35–50 ball (≥ 70%) VA har bo'limda ≥ 50% (A ≥ 7.5, B ≥ 5, C ≥ 4, D ≥ 2.5 — amalda 3, E ≥ 6) → guruh bilan davom etadi. Coin: 45–50 ball (90%+) — 5 coin; 40–44 ball (80–89%) — 3 coin; 35–39 ball — coin yo'q.

SHARTLI: jami 30–50 ball (≥ 60%), lekin O'TDI sharti bajarilmagan — jami 30–34.5 ball (60–69%) YOKI bir yoki bir necha bo'lim 50% dan past. Qayta topshirish: 50% dan past bo'lim(lar); jami 60–69% bo'lsa — eng past 1–2 bo'lim (bo'lim foizi bo'yicha). 15 daqiqa, keyingi 2 dars ichida, dars vaqtidan tashqari, yangi savollar. Qayta topshirilgan bo'lim(lar) bali bilan qayta hisoblangan natija O'TDI shartiga yetsa (jami ≥ 35 va har bo'lim ≥ 50%) — O'TDI.
O'TMADI: jami 0–29.5 ball (< 60%) → ota-onaga xabar beriladi, 1 ta qo'shimcha (remedial) mashg'ulot zaif bo'limlar bo'yicha, keyin qayta topshirish (to'liq test, yangi savollar bilan).

Foiz = olingan ball / 50 × 100 (bo'lim foizi = bo'lim bali / bo'lim maksimumi × 100). Natija tahlili — 17-darsda (PT3 NATIJA TAHLILI, 8 daqiqa): eng ko'p uchragan 5 xato doskada — o'quvchilar juftlikda tuzatadi; < 70% olganlar ro'yxati va qayta topshirish sanasi e'lon qilinadi.

class_ex.title: A. Grammar — 15 ball (15 × 1), 10 daqiqa
class_ex.instr: Questions 1–8: choose A, B, C or D. Questions 9–12: write ONE word — the correct form of the word in brackets or the missing word. Questions 13–15: each sentence has ONE mistake. Find it and correct it. (1–8: to'g'ri variantni tanlang. 9–12: bitta so'z yozing — qavsdagi so'zning to'g'ri shakli yoki tushib qolgan so'z. 13–15: har gapda BITTA xato bor — toping va tuzating.)
items: 1. It was my grandfather ____ taught me to play chess. A) which B) who C) what D) where
2. ____ surprised me most was the price of the tickets. A) That B) Which C) What D) It
3. The longer you wait, ____ the tickets will be. A) more expensive B) the most expensive C) the more expensive D) most expensive
4. In our city, the young ____ usually more interested in online shopping than in markets. A) is B) are C) was D) has been
5. Take some cash with you ____ the card machine doesn't work. A) in case B) even C) provided D) as long as
6. Our team lost the match ____ we played really well. A) even B) even though C) in case D) provided that
7. A: I can't swim very well. B: ____ . A) Neither can I B) Neither do I C) So can I D) Neither I can
8. The new student seemed ____ on her first day, but she soon relaxed. A) nervously B) nerve C) nervous D) nervousness
9. The ____ (hot) the weather gets, the more water you should drink.
10. You can borrow my laptop as long as you ____ (bring) it back tomorrow.
11. I lost my old umbrella, so yesterday I bought a new ____ . (one word)
12. When the head teacher came in, the whole class stayed ____ (silence).
13. We did enjoyed the science museum last weekend.
14. My brother bought a new phone, but he doesn't like them.
15. The medicine tasted terribly, but I took it.
answers: B) who (that ham to'g'ri, lekin variantlarda yo'q)
why: L11: It-cleft, ta'kidlangan qism shaxs → who (yoki that).
L11: What-clause — What + V + was + ta'kid (What surprised me most was …).
L12: The + comparative, the + comparative — ikkala qismda ham 'the' + comparative (the longer …, the more expensive …).
L12: the + sifat = guruh (the young = yoshlar) → ko'plik fe'l: are.
L13: in case — ehtiyot uchun, oldindan (+ Present Simple).
L13: even though + gap (haqiqat: yaxshi o'ynadik, baribir yutqazdik); 'even' yolg'iz gapni bog'lamaydi.
L14: Substitution — inkor gapga qo'shilish: Neither + gapdagi yordamchi (can) + ega; 'do' emas, chunki gapda can bor.
L15: Linking verb (seem) + SIFAT (nervous), ravish emas.
L12: birinchi qismda ham comparative: the hotter …, the more ….
L13: as long as + Present Simple (shart); will ishlatilmaydi.
L14: Substitution — a new one (umbrella takrorlanmaydi).
L15: stay + sifat (silent); 'silence' (ot) yoki 'silently' (ravish) xato.
L11: Emphatic do — did + V1 (enjoy), V2 emas.
L14: Anaphoric ishora — birlik ot (a phone) → it.
L15: taste + sifat (terrible), ravish emas.

class_ex.title: C. Reading: matn — A dictionary in your pocket
class_ex.instr: Read the text. Then answer questions 1–8 in the next part. (Matnni o'qing va keyingi qismdagi 1–8-savollarga javob bering. Reading uchun jami 10 daqiqa.)
items: A dictionary in your pocket

A. In one small mountain village, only the oldest people still speak the local dialect fluently. Their grandchildren understand some words, but at school and online they use other languages. It was a young teacher, Dilnoza, who decided to do something about this before it was too late.

B. In 2021 she started visiting her elderly neighbours with a notebook and a phone. She recorded their stories, songs and proverbs, and she wrote down every word that she could not find in an ordinary dictionary. What surprised her most was the number of words for the weather: she collected more than forty words for different kinds of snow and wind. At first some of the old people seemed shy, but they soon became proud of their knowledge.

C. After two years, Dilnoza had about 1,500 words. She did not want the collection to stay in a notebook, so she asked two students from the city to help her build a simple phone app. Each word in the app has a translation, an example sentence and a recording of a native speaker. The app also works without the internet in case users are in the mountains with no signal.

D. The results have been encouraging. Children now use the app as a game, and the more words they learn, the more questions they ask their grandparents. Some teachers believe that this contact between generations is even more important than the dictionary itself. However, Dilnoza says that the work is not finished. Her next plan is to add grammar notes, provided that she can find enough time and money.
class_ex.answers: Matn — savollar va javob kaliti keyingi bo'limda (C. Reading: savollar). Matn Jony Academy uchun yozilgan original matn, qahramon va qishloq to'qima (14-dars mavzusi: til va muloqot).
