items: 1. Young people in the village speak the dialect as well as their grandparents.
2. Some of the old people did not feel comfortable when Dilnoza first visited them.
3. The local government paid Dilnoza for her work.
4. Users need an internet connection to use the app.
5. Dilnoza found more than forty words that describe snow and ____ .
6. Two ____ helped Dilnoza to build the app.
7. Every word in the app comes with a translation, an example sentence and a ____ .
8. In the future, Dilnoza wants to add ____ to the app.

B paragraf: "At first some of the old people seemed shy" — did not feel comfortable = seemed shy (parafraz).
Pul haqida faqat D paragrafda (kelajak rejasi uchun "enough time and money"); hukumat yoki to'lov haqida ma'lumot yo'q.
C paragraf: "The app also works without the internet".
B paragraf: "more than forty words for different kinds of snow and wind".
C paragraf: "two students from the city" — 'students from the city' 3 so'z, shuning uchun 'students' yoki 'city students'.
C paragraf: "a recording of a native speaker" — 'a recording' ham qabul qilinadi.
D paragraf: "Her next plan is to add grammar notes".

class_ex.title: D. Listening skripti (faqat ustozga, o'qib beriladi)
class_ex.instr: Faqat ustoz o'qiydi, 2 marta, oddiy tezlikda. Rollar: AGENT (sayohat agentligi xodimi) va AZIZ (mijoz). Skript o'quvchi varag'ida YO'Q va proyektorga chiqarilmaydi. Skript original (Jony Academy), agentlik nomi to'qima.
items: AGENT: Good morning, Peak Trips. How can I help you?
AZIZ: Hi. I'd like to book the two-day mountain walk for my friends and me.
AGENT: Of course. Can I have your surname, please?
AZIZ: Yes, it's Rahimov. That's R-A-H-I-M-O-V.
AGENT: Thank you. And how many people are going?
AZIZ: Well, at first there were five of us, but one friend can't come, so it's four.
AGENT: Four, fine. Which date would you like?
AZIZ: The twelfth of July, if possible.
AGENT: I'm sorry, the twelfth is already full. We still have places on the fourteenth.
AZIZ: OK, the fourteenth is fine.
AGENT: Great. For the night you can choose a tent or a guesthouse. The tent is cheaper, but it gets very cold up there.
AZIZ: Then the guesthouse, please. The warmer we are, the better we'll sleep!
AGENT: Good choice. We give every group a map, so you don't need to bring one. But please bring warm clothes and a torch in case you come back after dark.
AZIZ: A torch. No problem. Thank you very much!
AGENT: You're welcome. See you on the fourteenth.

class_ex.title: E. Writing — 12 ball (W-4.0: 4 mezon × 0–3), 10 daqiqa
class_ex.instr: Read the IELTS Task 2 question. Write ONE body paragraph (80–100 words) that gives your opinion with a reason and an example. Write the number of words at the end. (IELTS Task 2 savolini o'qing. Fikringizni sabab va misol bilan beradigan BITTA body paragraf yozing, 80–100 so'z. Oxirida so'z sonini yozing.)
items: 1. Question: Nowadays many young people learn two or more foreign languages. Is this a positive or a negative development?
2. Write ONE body paragraph only (no introduction or conclusion): topic sentence → reason → example → result. (Faqat bitta body paragraf: topic sentence → sabab → misol → natija.)

3. Try to use at least TWO structures from lessons 11–15, for example: It is … that … / What … is … / the more …, the more … / this + noun / a linking verb + adjective (feel confident). (11–15-darslar strukturalaridan kamida ikkitasini ishlating.)
4. Use topic words from Essential Words 14 (for example: bilingual, fluent, native speaker, communication, language barrier). (14-dars mavzu so'zlaridan foydalaning.)
5. Length: 80–100 words. Fewer than 70 words — Task Response gets 1 point maximum. (70 so'zdan kam bo'lsa, TR ko'pi bilan 1 ball.)
answers: Savol (o'quvchiga): Nowadays many young people learn two or more foreign languages. Is this a positive or a negative development?
Tuzilma: topic sentence (pozitsiya) → 1 sabab → izoh → aniq misol → natija/xulosa gapi.
Struktura: kamida 2 ta 11–15-dars strukturasi to'g'ri ishlatilgan bo'lsa, GRA da '3 ball' mumkin; struktura yo'q, lekin gaplar xatosiz — GRA ko'pi bilan 2.
Lug'at: EW 14 so'zlari (bilingual, fluent, native speaker…) — LR mezonida hisobga olinadi.
So'z soni: 80–100; 70 dan kam — TR maksimal 1 ball. Baholash — W-4.0 rubrikasi (keyingi bo'lim), namuna — undan keyingi bo'limda.

head: Mezon

2 ball (≈ Band 5)

rows: Vazifaga javob (TR; Task 1 da TA)
Savolning barcha qismiga javob beradi; pozitsiya aniq va oxirigacha saqlanadi; har g'oya izoh va aniq misol bilan. Task 1: overview bor, asosiy raqamlar to'g'ri tanlangan.
Savolga javob va pozitsiya bor, lekin bir qismi yuzaki yoki misol umumiy. Task 1: overview bor, lekin ba'zi raqamlar keraksiz yoki noaniq.
Savolga qisman javob; pozitsiya noaniq; g'oyalar takrorlanadi yoki mavzudan chetga chiqadi. Task 1: overview yo'q, raqamlar ro'yxat qilib sanaladi.
Savolga javob yo'q, mavzudan tashqari yoki so'z soni talabning yarmidan kam.
Izchillik va bog'lanish (CC)
Aniq tuzilma: topic sentence → izoh → misol → xulosa; 4+ xil bog'lovchi to'g'ri (however, as a result, for example); ishora so'zlari (this, they, the former) to'g'ri.
Tuzilma bor; 2–3 bog'lovchi, ba'zan mexanik (Firstly, Secondly…) yoki bitta noaniq ishora.
Abzatsga bo'linmagan yoki mantiq uziladi; bog'lovchi 1–2 ta yoki noto'g'ri ishlatilgan.
G'oyalar tartibsiz, bog'lanish yo'q.
Lug'at boyligi (LR)
Mavzu lug'ati (Essential Words) va 2+ kollokatsiya to'g'ri; takror kam; imlo xatosi 1–2 ta.
Mavzu so'zlari bor, lekin takror ko'p yoki 3–4 so'z noto'g'ri tanlangan; imlo xatolari ma'noga xalaqit bermaydi.
Oddiy, takroriy lug'at; so'z tanlash/imlo xatolari ma'noni qiyinlashtiradi.

Sodda va qo'shma gaplar aralash; bugungi struktura 1–3 marta to'g'ri va tabiiy; gaplarning ko'pi xatosiz.
Qo'shma gap urinishlari bor; xatolar bor, lekin ma'no tushunarli; artikl/zamon xatolari takrorlanadi.
Asosan sodda gaplar; xatolar ko'p, ayrim gaplar tushunarsiz.
Gap tuzilishi deyarli yo'q.
Jami (12 ball) → taxminiy band

O'tish chegarasi (50%) — E ≥ 6. class_ex.title: E. Writing: namuna paragraf (Band 5.5–6, faqat ustozga)
items: In my opinion, learning several foreign languages is a positive development because it opens many doors for young people. First of all, it is language skills that employers often look for. For example, a bilingual graduate can work with foreign partners, and this ability usually leads to a better salary. Moreover, the more languages people know, the easier it becomes for them to travel abroad and understand other cultures. They also feel more confident when they talk to native speakers. As a result, learning languages helps young people to build a successful and interesting life.
answers: TR 3: pozitsiya aniq (positive), sabab + aniq misol (bilingual graduate → better salary) + natija.
CC 3: topic sentence → First of all → For example → Moreover → As a result; ishora: this ability, them, They.
LR 3: bilingual, native speakers, graduate, foreign partners, travel abroad; kollokatsiya: open many doors, lead to a better salary.
GRA 3: it is … that (L11), the more …, the easier … (L12), this ability (L14), feel more confident (L15); sodda va qo'shma gaplar aralash.

class_ex.instr: (10 daq, juftlik) 1' — Part 1: A 2 savolni, B 2 savolni so'raydi (javob + sabab + misol). 1' — tayyorgarlik: Kartochka A bo'yicha faqat 5–6 kalit so'z. 2' — A gapiradi, B S-CHECK-4.0 ni belgilaydi. 2' — ustoz NAMUNA A ni o'qiydi, o'quvchilar box'dagi eshitgan iboralarini belgilaydi. 2' — B shu kartochkada gapiradi (box'dan 2+ ibora, 1–2 reported gap bilan). 1' — Part 3 juftlikda. 1' — ustoz feedback (S-4.0). ICQ: Tayyorgarlikka necha daqiqa? (1) Kartochkada nechta band bor? (4 — 3 ta 'You should say' + 'explain')
items: Part 1: How many people are there in your family?
Part 1: Do you spend a lot of time with your family?
Part 1: Who are you most similar to in your family?
Part 1: What do you usually do together at weekends?
KARTOCHKA A: Describe a piece of good advice a family member gave you. You should say: who gave you the advice ; when they gave it ; what they said ; and explain how it helped you.
Part 3: Are families smaller today than in the past?
Part 3: Who should look after elderly parents?
Part 3: What can grandparents teach young people?
box: I'd like to talk about a piece of advice my … gave me …
At that time I was … , and I wanted to …
He / She said he / she had …
… where three generations live under one roof
His / Her words really helped me.
It was the most useful advice I've ever had.
answers: Part 1 namunalari (faqat ustoz uchun): 1) There are five of us: my parents, my two younger brothers and me. We are a nuclear family, but my grandparents live just two streets away, so we see them almost every day.
2) Not as much as I'd like, because I'm busy with school and English lessons. But we always have dinner together, and my mum says it is the most important hour of the day.
3) Probably my father. We are both quiet, and we both love fixing things. My aunt often says I walk and talk exactly like him.
4) We usually visit my grandparents on Sunday. The women cook together and the children play in the yard; sometimes the whole extended family comes, so there are more than twenty people.

NAMUNA A (Band 5.5–6, 163 so'z, ~1.5–2 daqiqa): I'd like to talk about a piece of advice my grandfather gave me about two years ago. At that time I was fourteen, and I wanted to leave my music school because the dutor lessons felt boring and difficult. One evening we were sitting in the yard of our family house, where three generations live under one roof, and I complained to him. He listened quietly, and then he told me that every skill felt boring before it became easy. He said he had wanted to give up carpentry many times when he was young. He also told me that I would be proud of myself one day. His words really helped me. I decided to stay, and last spring I played at a school concert in front of my whole extended family. Now I understand that his own upbringing made him patient, and he is trying to nurture the same quality in me. It was the most useful advice I've ever had.

Part 3 namunalari: 1) Yes, especially in cities. In the past many couples had five or six children, but now most have two or three, because raising children is expensive. Also, more young couples live separately from their parents.

2) In Uzbekistan most people believe that their children should do it, because respect for elders is a strong tradition. I agree, but I think all the siblings should share this duty, not only one son or daughter.

3) They can teach practical things, such as traditional cooking or crafts, and they know the family history. They have also lived through hard times, so they can teach patience. For example, many grandparents say that they had very little but were still happy.

Baholash: S-4.0 (jadval keyingi mashqda); ustoz 3–4 o'quvchini jurnalga qayd etadi. class_ex.title: WRITING — Starting school (yozma): Task 2 insho — tahlil va Body 2 rejasi
class_ex.instr: (8 daq, test darsi) 2 daq — savol tahlili: savol turi, kalit so'zlar, pozitsiya, nechta body. 3 daq — NAMUNA kirish va Body 1 ni proyektorda birga tahlil qilamiz (topic sentence, bog'lovchilar, bugungi grammatika — reported statement, EW16 so'zlari). 3 daq — yakka: Body 2 va xulosa REJASI jadvalini daftarga to'ldiring (Body 2 sinfda to'liq yozilmaydi; to'liq insho — uyda). ICQ: Bugun sinfda Body 2 ni to'liq yozamizmi? (Yo'q — faqat reja: g'oya, izoh, misol.) To'liq insho qayerda va necha daqiqada yoziladi? (Uyda, 40 daqiqa taymer bilan, 220–260 so'z.)
box: Question: Some think children should start school as early as possible. Others believe they should start later. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

MODEL — Introduction: People have different opinions about the best age for children to begin school. Some parents want their children to enter a classroom as soon as possible, while others prefer to wait. In my opinion, most children should start school at six or seven, after a happy childhood at home.

MODEL — Body 1: On the one hand, there are good reasons to start school early. At school, young children learn to follow a timetable and make friends outside their own household. Many teachers say that pupils who start early are more confident in the first grade. For example, in my town some parents send their five-year-olds to reading courses, and these children can already read simple words before school. As a result, the first months of lessons are less stressful for them.
items: 1) Savol turi qanday? Insho nechta body paragrafdan iborat bo'ladi va har birida nima yoziladi?
2) Kirishda yozuvchining pozitsiyasi qaysi gapda? Savoldagi qaysi so'zlar boshqacha aytilgan (parafraz)?
3) Body 1 da bugungi grammatika (reported statement) qayerda? Nega u yerda backshift yo'q?
4) Body 1 da qaysi bog'lovchilar va qaysi EW16 (Family, upbringing) so'zlari bor?
5) Body 1 ning tuzilishi: topic sentence -> explain -> example -> link — har birini toping.

TASK (3 min, plan only): Body 2 (the 'start later' view) — Idea: … | Explain: … | Example (Uzbekistan / your family): … | Link: … ; Conclusion — restate your opinion in new words (1–2 sentences): … Use 1 reported statement (… said that … / A study reported that …) and 2+ EW16 words (bond, siblings, upbringing, nurture, respect for elders, childhood).
answers: Tahlil kaliti: 1) Discuss both views + opinion: 2 body — Body 1 erta boshlash tarafdorlari fikri, Body 2 kechroq boshlash tarafdorlari fikri; o'z fikr kirishda va xulosada.

2) Pozitsiya — kirishning oxirgi gapi: 'In my opinion, most children should start school at six or seven, after a happy childhood at home.' Parafraz: start school -> begin school / enter a classroom; as early as possible -> as soon as possible; start later -> wait.

3) 'Many teachers say that pupils who start early are more confident…' — reporting fe'l HOZIRGI zamonda (say), shuning uchun backshift yo'q (grammar.notes 1). Body 2 dagi 'A study reported that … felt …' — o'tgan zamon, backshift bor.

4) Bog'lovchilar: On the one hand, For example, As a result (+ and). EW16: household (Body 1); kirishda childhood. Qolgan EW16 so'zlari Body 2 da: bond, siblings, respect for elders, nurture, upbringing.

5) Topic: 'there are good reasons to start school early' -> Explain: follow a timetable, make friends outside the household -> Example: five-year-olds on reading courses read simple words -> Link: 'As a result, the first months of lessons are less stressful for them.'

NAMUNA REJA (faqat ustoz uchun): Body 2 — Idea: early years belong to the family | Explain: time to play, bond with parents, siblings, grandparents | Example: grandparents tell stories, teach respect for elders; a study — five-year-olds tired and anxious after long lessons | Link: too early = less childhood. Conclusion: early start = confidence, family time = also valuable; six or seven is the right age.

NAMUNA Body 2 + Conclusion (faqat ustoz uchun): On the other hand, others believe that the first years of life should belong to the family. Small children need time to play and to build a strong bond with their parents, siblings and grandparents. In many Uzbek families, grandparents tell stories, teach respect for elders and nurture good habits, and this upbringing is as important as reading. Moreover, a study reported that many five-year-olds felt tired and anxious after long lessons. Therefore, starting school too early may take away part of childhood. || In conclusion, an early start can build confidence, but time with the family is also valuable. I believe that six or seven is the right age, because by then children are ready for lessons and have already learned important values at home.
To'liq namuna: 253 so'z (box dagi kirish va Body 1 + yuqoridagi Body 2 va xulosa).
Baholash: W-4.0 — shu darsdagi E bo'lim jadvali (PT3; insho uchun 'Qoidalar' qatori global W-4.0 da); tekshiruv — quyidagi W-CHECK-4.0.
why: Bugungi grammatika namunada 2 marta: 'Many teachers say that pupils who start early are…' (Body 1 — say hozirgi zamonda, backshift yo'q; umumiy fikr) va 'a study reported that many five-year-olds felt tired and anxious' (Body 2 — reported o'tgan zamonda: feel -> felt).

EW16 so'zlari: childhood (bolalik), household (xonadon), bond (rishta), siblings (aka-uka, opa-singil), respect for elders (kattalarga hurmat), nurture (parvarish qilib o'stirmoq), upbringing (tarbiya).
O'zbek hayotidan misol: bobo-buvilar ertak aytib, kattalarga hurmatni o'rgatishi (Body 2) va besh yoshli bolalarning o'qish kurslari (Body 1) — umumiy emas, aniq misol TR uchun muhim.
Discuss both views inshosida o'z fikr faqat xulosada emas, kirishda ham aniq aytiladi — W-CHECK 1-band; xulosada fikr yangi so'zlar bilan takrorlanadi.
class_ex.note: Manba: Kitob IELTS 4.0, SAMPLE ESSAYS, Topic 7 — faqat savol olindi; namuna insho Jony Academy original matni (kitob inshosining g'oya va iboralari ishlatilmadi). Baholash: W-4.0 — shu darsdagi E bo'lim jadvali (PT3), ikkinchi nusxa qo'shilmadi. Namuna Band 5.5–6.

homework.instr: MAJBURIY. 1 daqiqa tayyorgarlik (faqat 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1.5–2 daqiqa to'xtamasdan gapirib, ovozli yozuvni ilovaga yuboring. Matndan o'qimang. items: KARTOCHKA B: Describe a family member you admire. You should say: who this person is ; what they do ; what they are like ; and explain why you admire them.
answers: NAMUNA B (Band 5.5–6, 141 so'z, faqat ustoz uchun): The family member I admire most is my aunt, my father's elder sister. She works as a nurse in a children's hospital in our district, and she has done this job for more than twenty years. She is a calm and very caring person. Even after a night shift, she always finds time to ask her nephews and nieces about school. I admire her for two reasons. Firstly, she became the main breadwinner of her household when her husband was ill, but she never complained. Secondly, she is generous with her time. When my cousin was in hospital, she visited him every day. Last year she told me that helping sick children was the best part of her day, and she said she would never change her job. I hope I can be as strong and kind as her one day.
Bugungi struktura: told me that helping sick children was…, said she would never change… (backshift: is -> was, will -> would); EW16: caring, breadwinner, household.

items: Last Sunday my grandfather told to me about his childhood. He said that he grow up in a small village near Samarkand. He told that his family had kept sheep and that he had walked five kilometres to school every day. He said me that life was hard, but people were kind. He also said he will teach me to play chess the next weekend.
answers: he grow up → he had grown up (he grew up)
He told that → He said that (He told me that)
He said me → He told me
he will teach → he would teach

reading.title: Zulfiya — a poet of family, loyalty and courage
text: A  Last spring our English class visited a small exhibition about Zulfiya, one of the best-known Uzbek poets of the twentieth century. Our guide, a retired literature teacher, told us that Zulfiya had been born in Tashkent in 1915 into a family of craftsmen. She said that the girl had loved poems and songs from an early age, and that her first book of poetry had come out when she was still a teenager.

B  The guide explained that in the 1930s Zulfiya had married the poet Hamid Olimjon and that they had had two children. She said that the two poets had shared a great love of literature. In her opinion, this marriage was one of the reasons why family is so important in Zulfiya's poetry.

C  In 1944 Hamid Olimjon died in a car accident, and Zulfiya was left alone with two small children. She never remarried. The guide said that Zulfiya had continued to work and write while she brought up her children on her own. Many of her later poems are about loss, loyalty and love, but readers often say that they also show hope and inner strength.

D  Zulfiya also worked as an editor. For many years she was the editor of "Saodat", a magazine for women, and she translated poetry from other languages into Uzbek. In the guide's opinion, the magazine was important because it gave women a place to share their ideas.

E  Zulfiya died in 1996, but her name is still well known in Uzbekistan. Today a state prize named after her is given to talented young women. At the end of the visit, our guide told us that Zulfiya's life showed how one family's story could become part of a country's history. On the way home, my friend Aziz said he would read one of her poems that evening — and the next day he told me he had read three.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

tasks.title: Family history project — form completion (ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER)
tasks.instr: Har bo'shliqqa BITTA SO'Z VA/YOKI RAQAM.
items: Woman's surname: ___
Grandmother came to Tashkent in: ___
First home: lived in a tent for ___ months
Main job: ___ at the city hospital
Her advice: family comes ___
Lived in the same house for ___ years
Number of grandchildren: ___
Family tradition: plov every ___

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; Student — ustoz, Woman — kuchli o'quvchi.
Student: Good afternoon. I'm from the school history club, and we're collecting family stories. What's your surname, please?
Woman: Karimova. That's K-A-R-I-M-O-V-A. I'd like to talk about my grandmother.
Student: When did she come to Tashkent?
Woman: She told me she came in 1966 — no, sorry, in 1967, a year after the earthquake.
Student: Where did the family live at first?
Woman: In a tent. Some relatives think it was a whole year, but she always said they had lived there for eight months.
Student: What was her job?
Woman: First she worked in a bakery, but for most of her life she was a nurse at the city hospital.
Student: Did she give you any advice?
Woman: Yes. She always told me that family came first and that money would follow.
Student: Did she ever move house again?
Woman: Never. She said she would never move again, and she lived in the same house for fifty years.
Student: How many grandchildren did she have?
Woman: Twelve — sorry, fourteen. She said she could remember every birthday.
Student: And did the family have a special tradition?
Woman: Plov every Friday — no, I'm wrong, it was Sunday. The whole family came for lunch.

kahoot.q: 'I live near the park,' Madina said. → Madina said she ___ near the park.
kahoot.explain: Present Simple → Past Simple: live → lived.

kahoot.q: 'I am cooking dinner,' Mum said. → Mum said she ___ dinner.
kahoot.explain: Present Continuous → Past Continuous: am cooking → was cooking.

kahoot.q: 'We have bought a new car,' they said. → They said they ___ bought a new car.
kahoot.explain: Present Perfect → Past Perfect: have bought → had bought.

kahoot.q: 'I missed the bus,' Aziz said. → Aziz said he ___ the bus.
kahoot.explain: Past Simple → Past Perfect: missed → had missed.

kahoot.q: 'I will help you,' she said to me. → She said she ___ me.
kahoot.explain: will → would + V1: would help.

kahoot.q: 'I can drive,' he said. → He said he ___ drive.
kahoot.explain: can → could + V1: He said he could drive.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gap TO'G'RI?
options: He told me he was hungry.
He said me he was hungry.
He told to me he was hungry.
kahoot.explain: tell + kimga: told me; say — odamsiz: He said he was hungry.

kahoot.q: 'I'll meet you here tomorrow,' she said last week. → She told me she would meet me there ___.
kahoot.explain: O'tgan haftadagi suhbat: tomorrow → the next day; here → there.

kahoot.q: 'My mother is a doctor,' Aziz said. → Aziz said ___ mother was a doctor.
kahoot.explain: Olmosh gapiruvchiga moslanadi: my (Aziz) → his.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: She said me that she was busy.
She told me she had finished.
kahoot.explain: say dan keyin odam kelmaydi: She told me / She said (that)...

kahoot.q: 'I may be late,' she said. → She said she ___ be late.
kahoot.explain: may → might: She said she might be late.

kahoot.q: My wife's parents are my ___.
kahoot.explain: in-laws — turmush o'rtog'ining oilasi (qaynona, qaynota).

kahoot.q: Qaysi holatda backshift SHART EMAS?
kahoot.explain: Umumiy haqiqat hozir ham to'g'ri — zamon o'zgarmasligi mumkin: She said the Earth goes round the Sun.

kahoot.q: The difference in ideas between young and old people is the generation ___.
kahoot.explain: generation gap — avlodlar tafovuti.

kahoot.q: A family with parents, children, grandparents and aunts living together is an ___ family.
kahoot.explain: extended family — katta oila; nuclear family — ota-ona va bolalar.

kahoot.q: My brothers and sisters are my ___.
kahoot.explain: sibling — aka-uka, opa-singil. ancestor — ajdod.

kahoot.q: The person who earns money for the whole family is the ___.
kahoot.explain: breadwinner — oila boquvchisi.

kahoot.q: My friend has no brothers or sisters. She is ___.
kahoot.explain: only child — oilada yolg'iz farzand; single parent — bolani yolg'iz o'stirayotgan ota yoki ona.

kahoot.q: Qaysi so'z 'strict' so'zining ANTONIMI?
kahoot.explain: strict — qattiqqo'l, lenient — yumshoq (ota-ona haqida).

kahoot.q: 'Upbringing' ma'nosi?
kahoot.explain: upbringing — bolalikda olingan tarbiya: a strict upbringing.

Ustoz tekshirilgan varaqlarni qaytaradi. Eng ko'p uchragan 5 xato doskada — o'quvchilar juftlikda tuzatadi (4 daq); test darsida uyga berilgan reading kaliti proyektorda (1 daq); <70% olganlar ro'yxati va qayta topshirish sanasi (2 daq).

Lead-in misoli ("Where do you live?" → "I asked Aziz where he lived.") → formula (proyektor) → 2–3 misol + notes → CCQ (presentation) → 1 daqiqalik tez og'zaki tekshiruv: ustoz savol aytadi, o'quvchi reported shaklini aytadi.

Ustoz 20 so'zni proyektorda talaffuz + tarjima bilan o'qitadi (3 daq); 6–8 ta qiyin so'zga CCQ yoki misol (3 daq); juftlikda A o'zbekchasini, B inglizchasini aytadi (2 daq). Mustahkamlash — flashcard (uyga).

Kombinatsiya — juftlikda formula → gap → tarjima zanjiri: A formulani yoki o'zbekcha gapni aytadi, B shu formula bilan inglizcha gap tuzib tarjima qiladi, keyin almashadi. 1 daq — ustoz grammar.formulas dan formulani va 1 misolni proyektorda ko'rsatadi; 3 daq — juftlikda (me'yor normativ[1] da); ustoz 2 juftlikni tinglaydi.

intro: YES/NO SAVOL → asked + IF / WHETHER + ega + fe'l (backshift).
WH-SAVOL → asked + WH-WORD + ega + fe'l (DARAK tartibi, do/does/did yo'q).
SO'Z TARTIBI: savoldagi inversiya yo'qoladi: "is your name" → "your name was"; do/does/did yordamchisi tushadi: "did he leave" → "he had left".
Savol belgisi (?) yo'q; olmosh va vaqt so'zlari 16-darsdagidek o'zgaradi (this → that, now → then).
REPORTING FE'LLAR: asked (me), wanted to know, wondered, enquired, was curious to know.
formulas: Yes/No (Present)
S + asked + if/whether + S + V2
"Do you like coffee?" he asked. → He asked if I liked coffee.
U mendan qahva yoqadimi deb so'radi.
Yes/No (be)
S + asked + whether + S + was/were
"Are you busy?" she asked. → She asked whether I was busy.
U mendan bandmisiz deb so'radi.
Yes/No (will)
S + asked + if + S + would + V1
"Will he come?" they asked. → They asked if he would come.
Ular u keladimi deb so'rashdi.
Wh- (Present)
S + asked + wh-word + S + V2
"Where do you live?" → She asked where I lived.
U mendan qayerda yashashimni so'radi.
Wh- (Past → Past Perfect)
S + asked + wh-word + S + had + V3
"Why did he leave early?" → They asked why he had left early.
Ular nega u erta ketganini so'rashdi.
Wh- (modal)
S + asked + wh-word + S + could/would + V1
"How can I do this?" → She asked how she could do that.
U buni qanday qilsa bo'lishini so'radi.
presentation: CCQ: She asked me where I lived.
Is it a question now? (No — a report) Do we use did? (No)
CCQ: He asked if I liked history.
Did he want a yes/no answer? (Yes) Do we write a question mark? (No)
CCQ: They asked why he had left early.
Did he leave before they asked? (Yes) Is 'did' in the sentence? (No — had left)
CCQ: The teacher wanted to know what my name was.
Did the teacher ask a question? (Yes) 'was my name' or 'my name was'? (my name was)
notes: Wh-savolda "if" qo'shilmaydi: asked where I lived (asked if where — xato).
Ega — savol so'zining o'zi bo'lsa tartib o'zgarmaydi: "Who called?" → She asked who had called.
O'quvchi so'raydi: if yoki whether — farqi bormi? — Javob: ma'no bir xil; whether rasmiyroq va 'or not' bilan keladi: She asked whether or not I agreed.
O'quvchi so'raydi: Backshift har doim shartmi? — Javob: yo'q; gap hozir ham to'g'ri bo'lsa, zamon saqlanishi mumkin: She asked where I live / lived. Imtihonda backshift xavfsizroq.
O'quvchi so'raydi: Nega 'She asked where did I live' xato? — Javob: reported savol — darak gap: did tushadi, ega fe'ldan oldin keladi: where I lived.
mistakes: He asked me did I like coffee.
He asked me if I liked coffee.
She asked where did I live.
They asked if he would come.
Yes/No → if + darak tartibi; will → would.
The teacher asked what was my name.
The teacher asked what my name was.
She asked me that I was busy.
She asked me whether I was busy.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Hometown (og'zaki): Part 1, 2, 3
class_ex.instr: (10 daq, juftlik) 1 daq — Part 1: 4 savolga juftlikda navbat bilan qisqa javob (javob + sabab). 1 daq — Kartochka A bo'yicha tayyorgarlik: faqat 5–6 kalit so'z. 2 daq — A Kartochka A bo'yicha gapiradi, B S-CHECK-4.0 ni to'ldiradi. 2 daq — ustoz NAMUNA A ni o'qiydi, o'quvchilar box'dagi iboralar eshitilganda belgilaydi. 2 daq — B shu kartochka bo'yicha gapiradi (box'dan kamida 2 ibora bilan), A belgilaydi. 1 daq — Part 3: 3 savoldan 1–2 tasini juftlikda muhokama qilish. 1 daq — ustoz 1 ta umumiy feedback (S-4.0). ICQ: Necha daqiqa tayyorlanasiz va nima yozasiz? (1 daqiqa, 5–6 kalit so'z) B box'dan nechta ibora ishlatadi? (kamida 2)
items: Part 1: Where is your hometown?
Part 1: What do you like most about it?
Part 1: Has your hometown changed much in recent years?
Part 1: Would you like to live there in the future?
KARTOCHKA A: Describe an old building or historical place in your hometown. You should say: what it is ; where it is ; what you know about its history ; and explain why it is important to people.
Part 3: Why is it important to protect old buildings?
Part 3: What can young people learn from local history?
Part 3: Why do many young people leave small towns?
box: I'd like to talk about …, in my hometown.
As far as I know, it was built in the … century.
Tourists often ask me where / whether …
Once my little brother asked me if …
It is part of our legacy.
Only the ruins of … are left.
This place is important to people because …
For me, it is a symbol of …
answers: Part 1 (1) namuna: My hometown is Shahrisabz, a town in the Kashkadarya region in the south of Uzbekistan. It's about two hours by car from Samarkand, on the other side of the mountains.
Part 1 (2) namuna: I like its history most of all, because Amir Temur was born near there. Visitors often ask me where his palace is, and I'm always happy to show them.
Part 1 (3) namuna: Yes, quite a lot. The old centre was rebuilt a few years ago, and now there are wide parks and new hotels for tourists, although some people say the old streets had more character.
Part 1 (4) namuna: Maybe later in life. Right now I want to study in Tashkent, but I'd like to come back one day and work in tourism, because the town really needs good guides who speak English.

NAMUNA A (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6, 179 so'z, ~1.5–2 daqiqa): I'd like to talk about the Ak-Saray Palace in Shahrisabz, my hometown. It's right in the centre of the town, next to a statue of Amir Temur. It isn't a whole building any more — only the ruins of a huge entrance gate are left, but they are more than thirty metres high. As far as I know, the palace was built at the end of the fourteenth century, when Temur was the ruler of a big empire. Tourists often ask me where the rest of the palace is, and I tell them that most of it was destroyed long ago. Once my little brother asked me if the palace had been made of gold, because its name means 'white palace'. I laughed and explained that the walls were covered with beautiful blue and white tiles. This place is important to people because it is part of our legacy. Local families take their guests there, and newly married couples often take photos in front of the gate. For me, it is a symbol of how great our town once was.

Namunadagi bugungi grammatika: 'Tourists often ask me where the rest of the palace is' (wh-word + darak tartibi), 'my little brother asked me if the palace had been made of gold' (if + backshift). EW17: ruins, century, ruler, empire, legacy.

Part 3 (1) namuna: Old buildings show us how people lived centuries ago, so once they are destroyed, that knowledge is lost for ever. They also attract tourists, which brings money and jobs to local people.

Part 3 (2) namuna: They can learn where their families and traditions come from. For example, when students ask older people why a street or a mahalla has a certain name, they often discover an interesting story.

Part 3 (3) namuna: Mainly because there are more universities and better-paid jobs in big cities. Many young people also want a more exciting lifestyle, although some of them return later to start a business at home.

class_ex.title: WRITING — Young people and history (yozma): Task 2 insho — tahlil va Body 2
class_ex.instr: (15 daq) 3 daq — savol tahlili: savol turi (causes + solutions), kalit so'zlar, pozitsiya, nechta body; 5 daq — box dagi NAMUNA kirish + Body 1 tahlili (topic sentence, bog'lovchilar, reported questions, EW 17 so'zlari); 5 daq — yakka Body 2, 60–80 so'z, qolip: Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link; 2 daq — sherik bilan almashib W-CHECK-4.0 bo'yicha tekshirish. ICQ: Body 2 nima haqida — sabablar yoki yechimlar? (yechimlar) Body 2 necha so'z? (60–80)
box: Question: Many young people today know very little about the history of their own country. Why is this? What can be done to change this?

MODEL — Introduction: It is true that many teenagers can name famous footballers and singers but know surprisingly little about their own country's past. In my view, this happens mainly because history lessons are dull and social media takes up much of young people's free time. However, more interesting teaching and the support of families can change the situation.

MODEL — Body 1: The first reason is the way history is taught. Lessons are often based on memorising dates and the names of rulers, so pupils find the subject boring. Teachers often ask why students forget everything after the exam, but the answer is simple: nobody shows them how the past is connected to their lives. Moreover, teenagers spend hours online, where they see entertainment rather than their nation's legacy. For example, in one school survey, researchers asked students whether they knew in which century Amir Temur had lived, and many could not answer.
items: Insho qolipi (causes + solutions): Introduction (parafraz + asosiy sabab va yechim) -> Body 1 (sabablar) -> Body 2 (yechimlar) -> Conclusion.
1. Savol turi qanday: agree/disagree, discuss both views yoki causes + solutions? Nechta qismga javob kerak?
2. Pozitsiya kirishning qaysi gapida? Savoldagi qaysi so'zlar parafraz qilingan?
3. Body 1 ning topic sentence'i qaysi? Nechta sabab bor? Misol qaysi gapda?
4. Bugungi grammatika (reported questions: asked whether… / ask why…) qayerda? Darak tartibi va backshift to'g'rimi?
5. Essential Words 17 (History) so'zlaridan qaysilari bor?

TASK: Write Body 2 (60–80 words): Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link. Idea: what schools and families can do (museums, trips, family stories; example from Uzbekistan). Use one reported question (e.g. Pupils often ask how… / The guide asked us whether…).
answers: Kalit 1: causes + solutions — 2 qismga javob kerak: (1) nega yoshlar tarixni kam biladi, (2) nima qilish mumkin. Faqat sabablar yozilsa — TR ko'pi bilan 1.

Kalit 2: pozitsiya — 'In my view, this happens mainly because history lessons are dull and social media takes up much of young people's free time. However, more interesting teaching and the support of families can change the situation.'; parafraz: 'young people' -> 'teenagers'; 'know very little about the history' -> 'know surprisingly little about their own country's past'.

Kalit 3: topic sentence — 'The first reason is the way history is taught.'; 2 sabab (zerikarli darslar; internet), 2-sabab 'Moreover' bilan; misol — 'For example, in one school survey, researchers asked students whether…'.

Kalit 4: Body 1 da 2 ta reported question: 'Teachers often ask why students forget everything…' (wh-word + ega + fe'l, do yo'q; ask — hozirgi zamon, backshift yo'q); 'researchers asked students whether they knew in which century Amir Temur had lived' (whether + darak tartibi; lived -> had lived).
Kalit 5: rulers, legacy, century (Body 1 da); monuments, artefacts, ruins (Body 2 da).

NAMUNA Body 2 (faqat ustoz uchun): This problem can be solved if schools and families work together. Teachers should make lessons more active and take pupils to museums and monuments, where they can see real artefacts instead of only reading about them. For instance, a class trip to the ruins of Afrosiyob in Samarkand can teach more than ten pages of a textbook. In addition, grandparents can share family stories, which helps children learn about their roots.

NAMUNA Conclusion (faqat ustoz uchun): In conclusion, many young people know little about their country's past because lessons are often dull and the internet fills their free time. I believe that lively teaching and the help of families can make the next generation proud of its history.
To'liq namuna: 260 so'z (kirish 56, Body 1 91, Body 2 71, xulosa 42).
Baholash: W-4.0 (jadval shu darsda); sinfdagi Body 2 — W-CHECK-4.0, to'liq insho uyda W-4.0 bilan.
why: Grammatika (wh- reported question): 'Teachers often ask why students forget everything' — savol tartibi yo'q ('why do students forget' emas), do tushadi; reporting fe'l hozirgi zamonda bo'lgani uchun backshift kerak emas.

Grammatika (yes/no reported question): 'researchers asked students whether they knew in which century Amir Temur had lived' — whether + ega + fe'l; 'Do you know…?' -> whether they knew; o'tgan voqea -> had lived (backshift).
EW 17 so'zlari: ruler (hukmdor), legacy (meros), century (asr), monument (yodgorlik), artefact (tarixiy buyum), ruins (xarobalar) — 6 ta, mavzuga tabiiy; SUPER dan: learn about our roots.

Bog'lovchilar: However, so, but, Moreover, For example, For instance, In addition, In conclusion — CC uchun 4+ xil; causes + solutions inshosida 'The first reason is…' / 'This problem can be solved if…' topic sentence qoliplari qulay.
O'zbek hayotidan misol: Samarqanddagi Afrosiyob xarobalariga sinf sayohati va Amir Temur haqidagi so'rov — o'quvchiga tanish va aniq.

Abzatslar bor, mantiq tushunarli; 2–3 bog'lovchi, ba'zan mexanik (Firstly, Secondly…); 1–2 noaniq ishora.
Abzatsga bo'linmagan yoki body da topic sentence yo'q; bog'lovchilar 1–2 ta yoki noto'g'ri.

Juda cheklangan lug'at, ma'no tushunarsiz.

Gap tuzilishi deyarli yo'q.

homework.title: 3. WRITING — Young people and history: to'liq insho (yozma, uyga)
homework.instr: MAJBURIY. 40 daqiqa taymer bilan, 220–260 so'z, 4 abzats. Sinfda yozgan Body 2 ni sherik/ustoz izohi bo'yicha tuzatib qo'shing; kirish va Body 1 ni o'z so'zlaringiz bilan yozing (namunani ko'chirmang). Savolning ikkala qismiga (sabablar VA yechimlar) javob bering. Oxirida so'z sonini yozing.
items: Question: Many young people today know very little about the history of their own country. Why is this? What can be done to change this?
Introduction: savol parafrazi + asosiy sabab va yechim (pozitsiya) — 2–3 gap.
Body 1: sabablar (masalan, darslar uslubi, internet) — Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link.
Body 2: yechimlar (maktab va oila nima qila oladi) + misol — sinfdagi Body 2, tuzatilgan.
Conclusion: sabab va yechimni boshqa so'zlar bilan takrorlang — 1–2 gap. Reported questions (asked whether… / ask why…) — 2–3 marta, tabiiy joyda.
answers:
NAMUNA (260 so'z, Band 5.5–6, Jony Academy original): It is true that many teenagers can name famous footballers and singers but know surprisingly little about their own country's past. In my view, this happens mainly because history lessons are dull and social media takes up much of young people's free time. However, more interesting teaching and the support of families can change the situation.

The first reason is the way history is taught. Lessons are often based on memorising dates and the names of rulers, so pupils find the subject boring. Teachers often ask why students forget everything after the exam, but the answer is simple: nobody shows them how the past is connected to their lives. Moreover, teenagers spend hours online, where they see entertainment rather than their nation's legacy. For example, in one school survey, researchers asked students whether they knew in which century Amir Temur had lived, and many could not answer.

This problem can be solved if schools and families work together. Teachers should make lessons more active and take pupils to museums and monuments, where they can see real artefacts instead of only reading about them. For instance, a class trip to the ruins of Afrosiyob in Samarkand can teach more than ten pages of a textbook. In addition, grandparents can share family stories, which helps children learn about their roots.

In conclusion, many young people know little about their country's past because lessons are often dull and the internet fills their free time. I believe that lively teaching and the help of families can make the next generation proud of its history.

homework.title: 4. SPEAKING NORMATIV — Hometown (og'zaki, ovozli): Kartochka B
homework.instr: MAJBURIY. Kartochka B: 1 daqiqa tayyorgarlik (faqat 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1.5–2 daqiqa to'xtamasdan gapirib, ovozli yozuvni ilovaga yuboring. Box'dagi iboralardan kamida 2 tasini va 1–2 ta reported question (… asked me if / where …) ishlating. Matnni o'qimang — 1 marta qayta yozish mumkin.
items: KARTOCHKA B: Describe your hometown or a town you know well. You should say: where it is ; what it is famous for ; what people do there ; and explain how you feel about it.
answers: NAMUNA B (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6, 140 so'z): I'd like to describe Gijduvan, a town I know well because my grandparents live there. It's in the Bukhara region, about forty kilometres from Bukhara city, on the road to Navoi. Gijduvan is famous for two things: its pottery and its shashlik. The local potters make bright yellow, green and brown plates, and tourists often ask whether they can watch the masters at work. The shashlik is so popular that drivers stop there just to eat it. Most people in the town work in small workshops, cafes or on farms, and in the evening neighbours sit together and talk. Last summer my grandfather asked me if I wanted to try making a bowl, and it was much harder than I expected. I feel very relaxed when I'm there, because life is slower than in the city and everyone is friendly.
Baholash: S-4.0 (class_ex dagi jadval), NORM-4.0: 10–12 ball — 2 coin; 7–9 — bajarildi; ≤6 — qayta yozib yuboradi.

reading.title: Imam al-Bukhari — the scholar who asked whether every story was true
text: A. Muhammad ibn Ismail, known today as Imam al-Bukhari, was born in Bukhara in 810. His father died when he was a baby. By the age of ten he was memorising hadiths — reports of what the Prophet had said and done. At sixteen he travelled to Mecca with his mother and brother, and he then spent many years away from home.

B. In every place he visited — Mecca, Medina, Baghdad, Damascus and the cities of Egypt — he listened to scholars and then asked questions. He asked who had told the scholar the story, and who had told that person. He asked whether each of them had actually met, and whether the narrator had been known for honesty. If one link in the chain was weak, he rejected the report.

C. In this way, it is said, he examined about 600,000 reports and kept around 7,000. The book he made from them, Sahih al-Bukhari, is still one of the most respected collections in the Muslim world. Students today read it in Arabic and in many other languages.

D. One well-known story describes a test in Baghdad. Ten men each read him ten hadiths with the chains deliberately mixed up. They asked him whether he recognised them. He said he did not — and then he repeated all one hundred, correcting every error from memory.

E. Back in Bukhara, the governor asked whether the imam would teach his sons privately at the palace. Bukhari refused: he believed the boys could come to his lessons like everyone else. After this he had to leave the city, and he died in 870 in Khartank, a village near Samarkand, where a memorial complex stands today. Many people see his method — ask who said it, ask how they knew — as an early example of careful research.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)
glossary: Sahih al-Bukhari — Imom Buxoriy tuzgan hadislar to'plami

tasks.title: 1. Multiple choice
tasks.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
items: 1 Paragraph B is mainly about A) the cities Bukhari liked most B) how Bukhari checked each report C) why Bukhari left Bukhara D) how scholars tested Bukhari
2 In the Baghdad test, the ten men wanted to find out whether Bukhari A) could read Arabic B) had visited Baghdad before C) could notice and correct mistakes D) knew the governor
3 Why did Bukhari have to leave Bukhara? A) He refused to teach the governor's sons separately. B) He wanted to study in Samarkand. C) He was ill. D) The governor's sons failed a test.

tasks.title: 2. TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: Bayonot matnga mos bo'lsa TRUE, zid bo'lsa FALSE, matnda ma'lumot bo'lmasa NOT GIVEN.
items: Al-Bukhari lost his father when he was very young.
He made his first journey to Mecca alone.
He accepted every report that a scholar told him.
The Baghdad test took place in front of a large crowd.
Sahih al-Bukhari can be read in languages other than Arabic.
The governor's sons later became famous scholars.
why: A: "His father died when he was a baby."
A: "with his mother and brother" — yolg'iz emas.
B: weak link → he rejected the report.
D: tomoshabinlar soni aytilmagan.
C: "in many other languages".
E: o'g'illarning keyingi hayoti haqida ma'lumot yo'q.

tasks.title: 3. Sentence completion — NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS
tasks.instr: Har bo'shliqqa matndan NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS yozing.
items: Hadiths are ______ of what the Prophet had said and done.
A report was rejected when one ______ of the chain was not strong.
In Baghdad, the chains of the hadiths had been ______ mixed up.
Bukhari died in a village near ______.

items: B: who bilan (2 ta)
B: whether bilan (2 ta)
D: whether bilan (1 ta)
E: whether bilan (1 ta)

listening.audios: Audio fayl yo'q — ustoz transcript'ni o'qiydi (Jony Academy skripti, 2 marta).
intro: You will hear a museum guide answering the questions that visitors often ask.
1-tinglash: eslatmalarni to'ldiring; 2-tinglash: javoblarni tekshiring.
Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

tasks.title: Note completion — ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER
tasks.instr: Eslatmalarni to'ldiring.
items: The museum building was built in ___
Photos are allowed, but visitors must not use a ___
Dressing-up room for children: on the ___ floor
Total number of coins in the collection: almost ___
The library is closed on ___
The gift shop is next to the ___
The gift shop closes at ___

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; monolog — ustoz yoki kuchli o'quvchi o'qiydi.
Guide: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Old Town History Museum. First, I'll answer the questions that visitors ask me most often.
Guide: First, people usually ask me how old the building is. It looks medieval, but it was actually built in 1870 — sorry, in 1880 — as a school for merchants' children.
Guide: Many visitors want to know whether they can take photos. You can, but please don't use a flash, because strong light can damage the old paintings.

Guide: Families often ask if there's anything for children. Yes — there's a room where children can dress up as merchants. It used to be on the second floor, but we moved it last month, so it's now on the third floor.
Guide: Someone asked me yesterday how many coins we have. The main hall shows about three hundred, but in total the collection has almost two thousand coins.
Guide: Students often ask whether the library is open to the public. It is — every day except Monday. People sometimes think it's closed at weekends, but it's open on Saturdays and Sundays too.
Guide: And finally, everyone asks where they can buy souvenirs. The gift shop isn't by the entrance any more; it's next to the café. It closes at half past five. Right, let's begin!

kahoot.q: 'Is the museum open today?' she asked. → She asked ___ the museum was open that day.
kahoot.explain: Yes/No savol → if/whether + ega + fe'l (is → was, today → that day).

kahoot.q: 'Where do you live?' → She asked where ___.
kahoot.explain: Darak tartibi: where + I + lived; do/did tushadi.

kahoot.q: 'What is your name?' → The teacher asked what ___.
kahoot.explain: Inversiya yo'qoladi: what + my name + was.

kahoot.q: 'Why did he leave early?' → They asked why he ___ early.
kahoot.explain: did leave → had left; did tushadi.

kahoot.q: 'Will he come?' they asked. → They asked if he ___.
kahoot.explain: will → would + V1, darak tartibi: They asked if he would come. 'will he come' — savol tartibi.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gap TO'G'RI?
options: She asked if we had met.
She asked that we had met.
She asked if had we met.
kahoot.explain: asked + if + ega + fe'l; 'had we' (savol tartibi) va 'that' — xato.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: She asked how old was the tower.
She asked how old the tower was.
They asked if it was open.
kahoot.explain: Ega fe'ldan OLDIN: how old the tower was.

kahoot.q: 'How can I do this?' → She asked how she ___ that.
kahoot.explain: can → could, darak tartibi. 'could she do' — savol tartibi.

kahoot.q: 'Are you busy?' she asked. → She asked ___ I was busy.
kahoot.explain: Yes/No savol → if / whether. are → was.

kahoot.q: Reported savolda nima YO'QOLADI?
kahoot.explain: Reported savol — darak gap: do/does/did va '?' tushadi.

kahoot.q: 'When did the empire begin?' → She asked when the empire ___.
kahoot.explain: did begin → had begun; darak tartibi.

kahoot.q: 'Have you visited Bukhara?' → My friend wanted to know ___ Bukhara.
kahoot.explain: wanted to know + if + ega + had V3 (Present Perfect → Past Perfect).

kahoot.q: A series of rulers from the same family is a ___.
kahoot.explain: dynasty — sulola; empire — imperiya.

kahoot.q: An old object made by people long ago and found by archaeologists is an ___.
kahoot.explain: artefact — tarixiy buyum; evidence sanalmaydi (an evidence — xato).

kahoot.q: A diary written by a soldier during a battle is a ___ source.
kahoot.explain: primary source — voqea paytida yozilgan manba; secondary — keyingi tahlil.

kahoot.q: Qaysi so'z 'reliable' so'zining ANTONIMI?
kahoot.explain: reliable — ishonchli, unreliable — ishonchsiz.

kahoot.q: After the earthquake, only the ___ of the old castle were left.
kahoot.explain: ruins — xarobalar; ruler — hukmdor, reign — hukmronlik, era — davr.

kahoot.q: Historians must ___ facts before they publish them.
kahoot.explain: verify — tekshirib tasdiqlamoq; conquer — zabt etmoq.

kahoot.q: To learn a text by heart is to ___ it.
kahoot.explain: memorise — yod olmoq; compile — to'plab tuzmoq.

kahoot.q: 'Legacy' ma'nosi?
kahoot.explain: legacy — meros, qoldirilgan iz.

lessons.title: Reported speech (imperatives)
lessons.grammar_topic: REPORTED IMPERATIVES — told/asked + object + to V1 (buyruq/iltimos); told/warned + object + not to V1 (taqiq); advised + object + to V1 (maslahat); suggested + V-ing (taklif); + ordered, begged, reminded, encouraged, forbade

Speaking: Kitob SAMPLE SPEAKING, Topic: Daily Routine — faqat mavzu; namunalar original. Essential Words 18 — Jony Academy ro'yxati (faqat tizimda). Dars oxirida o'quvchi suggest + V-ing / suggest that … va offer / promise / refuse + to V1 ni to'g'ri tanlaydi (Ex3: 8 banddan kamida 6 tasi).

timeline: Salomlashish + kirish savoli

Kirish savoli: 'What was the last instruction your coach or teacher gave you?' — 2–3 javob (1 daq). Ustoz buyruq beradi, o'quvchi reported qiladi: 'Open the window.' → 'The teacher told me to open the window.'; 'Don't shout.' → 'She told us not to shout.'; 'Let's take a break.' → 'She suggested taking a break.' (3 daq).
TAKROR: Kahoot — 17-dars (Reported speech (questions))
'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi → 17-dars savollari (20 ta). Bugungi darsning Kahooti bu yerda EMAS — u 19-darsda o'ynaladi. Oxirgi 1 daqiqa: eng ko'p xato qilingan 2 savol izohi.
TAKROR: Yozma normativ — Essential Words 17 (History, civilisation and knowledge)

Normativ — belgilangan vaqtda bajariladigan qisqa o'lchov; natijasiga qarab coin beriladi. 17-dars CORE 20: ustoz o'zbekchasini aytadi, o'quvchi inglizchasini yozadi — 4 daq; 1 daq sherik bilan almashib tekshirish. 18–20 = 2 coin; 15–17 = bajarildi; 14 va kam = 19-darsda qayta topshiradi.
Uy vazifasi tekshiruvi

Tarjima kaliti proyektorda (1 daq, o'quvchi o'zi belgilaydi). Yozma ishlar yig'ib olinadi (W-4.0 bo'yicha keyingi darsgacha tekshiriladi); eng ko'p uchragan 2 xato doskada (2 daq). Bajarmaganlar jurnalga.
YANGI GRAMMATIKA — Reported imperatives (told/asked/warned/advised + to V1; suggest + V-ing) + CCQ

Lead-in: ustoz 'Don't look at your phones!' deydi va so'raydi: 'What did I tell you?' → 'You told us not to look at our phones.' (2 daq) → formula (proyektor, grammar.formulas 1–6): buyruq, taqiq, iltimos, maslahat, taklif, o'zi bajaradigan ish (7 daq) → 2–3 misol: presentation savol-javoblari, juftlikda (4 daq) → 4–5 ta CCQ (3 daq) → tez og'zaki tekshiruv: ustoz to'g'ridan-to'g'ri gap aytadi ('You should rest.'), o'quvchi reported shaklini aytadi ('You advised me to rest.') (2 daq).
LUG'AT — Essential Words 18 CORE 20

Ustoz 20 so'zni proyektorda talaffuz + tarjima bilan o'qitadi (3 daq); 6–8 ta qiyin so'zga CCQ yoki misol (3 daq): delegate, prioritise, accountability, morale, decisive, guidance; juftlikda A o'zbekchasini, B inglizchasini aytadi (2 daq). Mustahkamlash — flashcard (uyga).
Kombinatsiya — told/asked/warned/advised + O + (not) to V1; suggested + V-ing

Kombinatsiya — juftlikda formula → gap → tarjima zanjiri: A formulani yoki o'zbekcha gapni aytadi, B shu formula bilan inglizcha gap tuzib tarjima qiladi, keyin almashadi. 1 daq — ustoz grammar.formulas dan formulani va 1 misolni proyektorda ko'rsatadi; 3 daq — juftlikda (me'yor normativ[1] da); ustoz 2 juftlikni tinglaydi.
SINF MASHQLARI — Ex1–Ex4 (MAJBURIY) + ZAXIRA

Ex1 5 daq yakka (buyruq va iltimos) · Ex2 4 daq juftlik (taqiq, maslahat, taklif) · Ex3 4 daq juftlik (reporting fe'l + lug'at) · Ex4 4 daq yakka (paragrafdagi 5 xato); kalit proyektorda. intro: Bilvosita nutqda buyruq, taqiq, iltimos va maslahat reporting fe'l + KIMGA + (not) to + V1 bilan beriladi: told / asked / warned / advised me (not) to…
Taklif ('Let's…') → suggested + V-ing yoki suggested (that) + S + (should) + V1 — ob'ektsiz.
Gapiruvchi o'zi bajaradigan ish → offered / promised / refused / agreed + to V1 (ob'ektsiz). Batafsil — formulas jadvalida.
formulas: Buyruq
S + told/ordered + O + to + V1
"Open the window," he said. → He told me to open the window.
U menga derazani ochishni buyurdi.
Taqiq
S + told/warned + O + not to + V1
"Don't shout," she said. → She told me not to shout.
U menga baqirmaslikni aytdi.
Iltimos
S + asked/requested/begged + O + to + V1
"Please sit down," the teacher said. → The teacher asked us to sit down.
O'qituvchi bizdan o'tirishni iltimos qildi.
Maslahat
S + advised/recommended + O + to + V1
"You should drink water," he said. → He advised me to drink water.
U menga suv ichishni maslahat berdi.
Taklif
S + suggested + V-ing / suggested (that) + S + V1
"Let's take a break," she said. → She suggested taking a break.
U tanaffus qilishni taklif qildi.
O'zi bajaradigan
S + offered/promised/refused/agreed + to + V1
"I'll help you." → He offered to help me. / "I won't go." → She refused to go.
U menga yordam berishni taklif qildi. / U borishdan bosh tortdi.
presentation: What did the coach tell the players?
He told them to press high and to pass quickly.
What did he warn them about?
He warned them not to lose the ball in their own half.
What did the doctor advise the striker?
She advised him to rest for two weeks.
What did the manager suggest?
He suggested training in the morning.
CCQ: He told me not to shout.
Did he give permission or an order? (An order) Did he want me to shout? (No)
CCQ: She asked us to sit down.
Was it an order or a polite request? (A polite request) Did she want us to stand? (No)
CCQ: The doctor advised him to rest.
Did the doctor order him to rest? (No) Did the doctor think rest was a good idea? (Yes) Is it his choice? (Yes)
CCQ: She suggested taking a break.
Did she say 'Let's…'? (Yes) Is there a person (object) after 'suggested'? (No) Will she probably take a break too? (Yes)
CCQ: He offered to help me.
Who will help — he or I? (He) Is there an object before 'to'? (No)
notes: tell / order / warn / remind + ob'ekt + to V1: told ME to…, warned US not to…; ask / advise kimgadir qaratilsa ob'ekt kerak: asked me to…, advised me to… ('He advised to drink water' — xato; 'He advised drinking water' — mumkin). suggest ob'ektsiz: suggested going ('suggested me to go' — xato).
"Don't" → not to: told me not to shout. Inkor 'not' to dan OLDIN keladi; 'to not shout' og'zaki nutqda uchraydi, lekin yozma ish va imtihon uchun standart shakl — not to.
Buyruqda "please" tushadi, ma'no asked bilan beriladi: "Please sit down." → She asked us to sit down.

O'quvchi so'raydi: suggested taking va suggested that we take — farqi bormi? — Javob: ma'no bir xil. V-ing shaklida kim qilishi aytilmaydi (odatda hammamiz); that + S + (should) + V1 kim qilishini aniq ko'rsatadi: She suggested that I (should) take a break. 'She suggested me to take' — xato.

O'quvchi so'raydi: Nega 'He said me to sit down' emas? — Javob: say dan keyin kishi to'g'ridan-to'g'ri kelmaydi va say + to V1 buyruq bermaydi; buyruq/iltimos uchun told me to… / asked me to… ishlatiladi.

O'quvchi so'raydi: offered to help va told me to help — farqi nima? — Javob: offered / promised / refused + to V1 — ishni gapiruvchining o'zi qiladi (ob'ektsiz); told / asked / advised + ob'ekt + to V1 — ishni boshqa odam qiladi.
mistakes: He told me open the window.
He told me to open the window.
She told me not to shout.
He suggested me to take a break.
He suggested taking a break. / He suggested that I take a break.
The teacher said us to sit down.
The teacher told/asked us to sit down.
He advised me to drink water.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Daily routine (og'zaki): Part 1, 2, 3
class_ex.instr: (10 daq, juftlik) 1 daq — Part 1: 4 savolga juftlikda qisqa javob (javob + sabab). 1 daq — tayyorgarlik: Kartochka A uchun faqat 5–6 kalit so'z yoziladi. 2 daq — A gapiradi, B S-CHECK-4.0 ni to'ldiradi. 2 daq — ustoz NAMUNA A ni o'qiydi, o'quvchilar box'dagi iboralarni eshitganda belgilaydi. 2 daq — B shu kartochkada gapiradi (box'dan kamida 2 ibora va 1–2 reported imperative bilan). 1 daq — Part 3 juftlikda: fikr + sabab + misol. 1 daq — ustoz 1 ta umumiy feedback (S-4.0). ICQ: Necha daqiqa tayyorlanasiz? (1) Box'dan nechta ibora ishlatasiz? (kamida 2)
items: Part 1: What time do you usually get up?
Part 1: What is the busiest part of your day?
Part 1: Is your routine different at weekends?
Part 1: Do you plan your day in the morning?
KARTOCHKA A: Describe a busy day you had recently. You should say: when it was ; what you had to do ; how you organised your time ; and explain how you felt at the end of the day.
Part 3: Is it important for students to plan their day?
Part 3: What skills does a good leader need to manage time?
Part 3: Why do many people say they have no free time?
box: It was one of the busiest days I've had recently.
On top of that, I had to …
My mum / teacher asked me to …
Our coach always tells us to prioritise …
So I organised my time like this: first …, then …
By the end of the day I was exhausted, but I felt proud.
I reached every goal I had for that day.
answers: 1) On school days I get up at about seven, because my classes start at eight. At weekends I sleep a bit longer, usually until nine.
2) Probably the afternoon. I have football training or extra English classes, and after that I still need to do my homework, so I hardly have a break.
3) Yes, it's quite different. At weekends I don't follow a strict timetable, so I help my parents at home, meet my friends and sometimes visit my grandparents.
4) Not really, but I'm trying. My English teacher advised us to write down three main goals every morning, and it really helps me prioritise.

NAMUNA A (Band 5.5–6, 160 so'z, ~1.5–2 daqiqa, faqat ustoz uchun): I'd like to talk about last Thursday, which was probably the busiest day I've had this month. In the morning I had a maths test, after school I had football training, and in the evening I had to finish an English presentation with two team members. On top of that, my mum asked me to collect my little brother from kindergarten at five. At first I panicked, but then I remembered that our coach always tells us to prioritise the most important task. So I revised for the test on the bus, and during the lunch break I sent my slides to the group and asked them to give me feedback. Our captain suggested leaving training a little early, so I picked up my brother on time. Later we checked the presentation together on a video call. By ten o'clock I was exhausted, but I felt really proud, because I had reached every goal for that day without forgetting anything.

1) Yes, I think it is. Students have lessons, homework and clubs, so a simple plan helps them prioritise and avoid stress. For example, many successful students check their timetable the night before.

2) A good leader needs to be decisive and organised. He or she should also delegate tasks, because nobody can do everything alone. For example, a team captain often asks other players to help with the warm-up.
3) Partly because of phones: people spend hours on social media and then feel they have no time left. Also, many adults work long hours, so they come home too tired to do anything else.
why: Bugungi grammatika (reported imperatives): my mum asked me to collect, our coach tells us to prioritise, asked them to give me feedback, our captain suggested leaving (suggest + V-ing, ob'ektsiz).
EW 18 so'zlari: team members — jamoa a'zolari; prioritise — ustuvorlikni belgilamoq; feedback — fikr-mulohaza; goal — maqsad; Part 3 da: decisive, delegate.
Part 3 javoblari 3 qismli: fikr + sabab + misol (I think … because … For example, …).
class_ex.note: S-CHECK-4.0: 1) kartochkaning 4 bandi aytildimi; 2) 1.5 daqiqadan uzoq, uzun pauzasiz; 3) box'dan 2+ ibora; 4) reported imperative (told/asked/advised + O + to V1, suggested + V-ing) 1–2 marta to'g'ri; 5) Part 3: fikr + sabab + misol. Ustoz 3–4 o'quvchini S-4.0 bo'yicha jurnalga qayd etadi. Kuchsiz: Kartochka A ni box iboralari bilan 1 daqiqa; Kuchli: + Part 3 ga qarshi fikr. Manba: Kitob IELTS 4.0, SAMPLE SPEAKING, Topic: Daily Routine — faqat mavzu olindi; savollar va namunalar Jony Academy original.

ICQ: Insho nechta qarashni muhokama qiladi va fikringiz qayerda bo'ladi? (2 ta; kirishda va Body 2 / xulosada) Body 2 necha so'z? (60–80)
box: Question: Some people believe school should prepare students for work. Others think it should help them become better individuals. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

MODEL — Introduction: Some people think that the main job of a school is to get young people ready for a career, while others believe it should help them grow into good and responsible people. In my opinion, both aims matter, but schools should pay more attention to character, because good values are useful in every job.

MODEL — Body 1: On the one hand, supporters of the first view say that students need practical skills to find work after school. Many employers advise schools to teach teamwork and decision-making, because new workers often cannot cooperate or solve problems without help. For example, some schools in Tashkent now run short projects with local companies, where pupils plan a small business and present it to real managers. As a result, these students understand what employers expect and feel more confident in their first job.
items: Savol turi qanday? Nechta qarash bor va har biri qaysi body da?
Pozitsiya (o'z fikri) kirishning qaysi gapida?
Bugungi grammatika qayerda? Body 1 dan reported imperative (advise + O + to V1) ni toping.
Qaysi EW 18 (Leadership, teamwork and management) so'zlari ishlatilgan?
Body 1 dagi bog'lovchilarni toping: misol va natija qanday bog'langan?

TASK: Write Body 2 (60–80 words): the second view (school should help students become better individuals) + your opinion. Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link. Use 1 reported imperative (tell … not to / encourage … to).
answers: 1) Discuss both views + opinion: Body 1 — maktab ishga tayyorlashi kerak degan qarash, Body 2 — yaxshi inson bo'lishga yordam berishi kerak degan qarash + o'z fikri; xulosada fikr takrorlanadi.
2) Kirishning 2-gapi: 'In my opinion, both aims matter, but schools should pay more attention to character, because good values are useful in every job.'
3) Body 1: 'Many employers advise schools to teach teamwork and decision-making' (advise + O + to V1). Body 2 da yana: tell students not to cheat, encourage them to take the initiative.
4) EW 18: decision-making, cooperate — Body 1; Body 2 da: initiative, leader, feedback.
5) Bog'lovchilar: On the one hand, because, For example, As a result — sabab -> misol (Toshkent maktablari va kompaniyalar loyihasi) -> natija.

NAMUNA Body 2 + Conclusion (faqat ustoz uchun): On the other hand, a school should also help young people become honest and responsible. Good teachers tell students not to cheat in exams and encourage them to take the initiative when a classmate needs help. I believe these lessons matter more, because a person with strong values can learn job skills quickly. For instance, a class leader who listens to feedback and treats everyone fairly is already preparing for a career. / In conclusion, schools should prepare students for work, but their more important role is to help them become good people. If teachers combine practical projects with clear lessons about honesty, young people will be ready for both their careers and their lives.
To'liq namuna: 250 so'z (kirish 54 · Body 1 82 · Body 2 72 · xulosa 42).
why: Bugungi grammatika: employers advise schools to teach (maslahat: advise + O + to V1), teachers tell students not to cheat (taqiq: tell + O + not to V1), encourage them to take the initiative — Task 2 da boshqalarning fikrini aytishning tabiiy usuli.
O'quvchi o'z Body 2 sida kamida 1 ta reported imperative ishlatsin (masalan, parents tell children to …, teachers warn students not to …).
EW 18 so'zlari: decision-making — qaror qabul qilish; cooperate — hamkorlik qilmoq; initiative — tashabbus (take the initiative); leader — rahbar (class leader); feedback — fikr-mulohaza.
O'zbek misoli: Toshkentdagi ayrim maktablarda mahalliy kompaniyalar bilan qisqa loyihalar — aniq, mahalliy misol TR va CC uchun ball beradi.

items: Question: Some people believe school should prepare students for work. Others think it should help them become better individuals. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Plan: 1) Introduction — paraphrase both views + your clear opinion.
Plan: 2) Body 1 — view 1 (prepare for work): Topic sentence -> explain -> example from Uzbekistan -> link.
Plan: 3) Body 2 — view 2 (better individuals) + your opinion: Topic sentence -> explain -> example -> link.

answers: NAMUNA (Band 5.5–6, 250 so'z, Jony Academy original, faqat ustoz uchun):

Some people think that the main job of a school is to get young people ready for a career, while others believe it should help them grow into good and responsible people. In my opinion, both aims matter, but schools should pay more attention to character, because good values are useful in every job.

On the one hand, supporters of the first view say that students need practical skills to find work after school. Many employers advise schools to teach teamwork and decision-making, because new workers often cannot cooperate or solve problems without help. For example, some schools in Tashkent now run short projects with local companies, where pupils plan a small business and present it to real managers. As a result, these students understand what employers expect and feel more confident in their first job.

On the other hand, a school should also help young people become honest and responsible. Good teachers tell students not to cheat in exams and encourage them to take the initiative when a classmate needs help. I believe these lessons matter more, because a person with strong values can learn job skills quickly. For instance, a class leader who listens to feedback and treats everyone fairly is already preparing for a career.

In conclusion, schools should prepare students for work, but their more important role is to help them become good people. If teachers combine practical projects with clear lessons about honesty, young people will be ready for both their careers and their lives.

Two years ago I was always late with my homework, and my marks were getting worse. One evening she visited us and noticed that I looked stressed. She told me to divide big tasks into small steps, and she advised me not to use my phone while I was studying. She also suggested making a list of tasks every Sunday evening, with the most urgent ones at the top. At first it was difficult, but I put my phone in another room and stuck my weekly list on the wall above my desk. After about a month, I was finishing my homework earlier and had more free time for football. Her guidance really helped me, because now I know how to prioritise and I feel much calmer before exams.

reading.title: Pep Guardiola — the coach who asked Messi to change position
text: A. Josep "Pep" Guardiola was born in 1971 in Santpedor, a small town in Catalonia. His father was a bricklayer. At the age of 13, Pep joined La Masia, Barcelona's famous academy, where coaches taught young players to control the ball quickly and to think before every pass. In 1990 Johan Cruyff, the first-team coach, gave him his debut, and he soon became a key midfielder in Cruyff's "Dream Team".

B. In 2008 Barcelona asked him to manage the first team. He was only 37 and had coached the club's reserve team for just one season. From the start, he asked his players to win the ball back quickly and to keep it with short, accurate passes. In May 2009, before a match against Real Madrid, he asked Lionel Messi, who usually played on the wing, to play in the centre as a "false nine". Barcelona won 6–2, and by the end of that year the club had won six trophies.

C. In 2012 he left Barcelona and took a year off. Bayern Munich then asked him to bring his ideas to Germany, and in 2016 Manchester City asked him to do the same in England. At City he won the Premier League several times, and in 2023 the club won the treble, including its first Champions League.

D. Guardiola is famous for changing the roles of his players. At Bayern, he asked his full-backs to move into midfield when the team had the ball. Many other coaches have since copied this idea, which is now known as the "inverted full-back". He also dislikes simple labels for his style: he has said that he does not like the term "tiki-taka", because passing without a clear purpose is useless.

E. What makes him a good leader? Former players often describe him as demanding and extremely hard-working. He expects everyone to prepare in detail, but he also explains his ideas patiently, one player at a time. He has often said that Cruyff was the biggest influence on his career, and several coaches who once worked with him now lead top teams of their own.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

B paragraf (1)

listening.audios: Audio fayl yo'q — ustoz transcript'ni 2 marta o'qiydi (Jony Academy skripti; kitob audiolari bu darsda ishlatilmaydi).
intro: You will hear a student telling her tutor about a leadership workshop.
1-tinglash: eslatmalarni to'ldiring; 2-tinglash: javoblarni tekshiring.
Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

tasks.title: Note completion — ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER (IELTS Part 3)
tasks.instr: Eslatmalarni to'ldiring. 7 band.
items: Number of goals to set for the project: ___
Give feedback within ___ hours
Praise in public, correct in ___
Stand-up meetings: maximum ___ minutes
Read chapter ___ of the course book
Date of the next session: ___ October
Bring a ___, not a laptop

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; 1-rol (Tutor) — ustoz, 2-rol (Student) — kuchli o'quvchi (yoki ovozni o'zgartiring).
Tutor: So, Dilnoza, how was the leadership workshop on Saturday?
Student: Really useful. The trainer started by telling us to set three goals for our project — not ten, like most of us had written.
Tutor: Sensible. What else did she say?
Student: She warned us not to micromanage. She said one manager in her last company had lost half of his team that way.
Tutor: And what about feedback?
Student: She asked us to give feedback within 48 hours — sorry, no, within 24 hours — while the task is still fresh. And she advised us to praise people in public but correct them in private.
Tutor: What about meetings?
Student: She suggested holding stand-up meetings. I thought she said twenty minutes, but actually the limit is fifteen, so nobody gets bored.
Tutor: Did she recommend any reading?
Student: Yes. She reminded us to read chapter four of the course book. At first she said chapter three, but that one is about budgets.
Tutor: And when is the next session?
Student: It's on the 12th of October, not the 10th as the website says. She told us not to bring laptops — just a notebook.
Tutor: Good. Then you'll actually listen to each other.

kahoot.q: 'Open the window,' he said. → He told me ___ the window.
kahoot.explain: Buyruq → told + KIMGA + to + V1: told me to open.

kahoot.q: 'Don't shout,' she said. → She told me ___.
kahoot.explain: Taqiq → told + KIMGA + NOT TO + V1: told me not to shout. Inkor 'not' to dan oldin keladi.

kahoot.q: 'Let's take a break,' she said. → She suggested ___ a break.
kahoot.explain: suggest + V-ing (ob'ektsiz): suggested taking. Yoki: suggested that we take.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gap TO'G'RI?
options: He advised me to drink more water.
He advised to drink more water.
He advised me drink more water.
He advised me drinking more water.
kahoot.explain: Maslahat → advised + KIMGA + to + V1: advised me to drink.

kahoot.q: 'Please sit down,' the teacher said. → The teacher ___ us to sit down.
kahoot.explain: Iltimos → asked + KIMGA + to V1. say + ob'ekt + to V1 — xato; suggest + to V1 — xato.

kahoot.q: 'I'll help you,' he said. → He ___ to help me.
kahoot.explain: O'zi bajaradigan ish → offered + to V1 (ob'ektsiz): He offered to help me.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: He suggested me to take a break.
She reminded me to call my mum.
They warned us not to swim.
kahoot.explain: suggest + ob'ekt + to V1 bo'lmaydi: He suggested taking a break / that I take a break.

kahoot.q: 'Don't touch it — it's hot!' → He ___ me not to touch it.
kahoot.explain: Ogohlantirish → warned + KIMGA + not to V1.

kahoot.q: 'I won't go,' she said. → She ___ to go.
kahoot.explain: Rad etish → refused + to V1: She refused to go. deny + V-ing bilan ishlatiladi.

kahoot.q: Qaysi fe'ldan keyin odatda OB'EKTsiz 'to + V1' keladi (ishni o'zi qiladi)?
kahoot.explain: promised to come — o'zi keladi. tell/advise/remind + KIMGA + to V1.

kahoot.q: After a painful defeat, a good captain tries to ___ the team, so that everyone works together again.
kahoot.explain: unite — birlashtirmoq, jipslashtirmoq. supervise — nazorat qilmoq; prioritise — ustuvorlikni belgilamoq.

kahoot.q: 'Finish the report by Friday!' → The manager ___ us to finish the report by Friday.
kahoot.explain: Qat'iy buyruq → ordered + KIMGA + to V1.

kahoot.q: The coach encouraged the team ___ harder.
kahoot.explain: encourage + KIMGA + to V1: encouraged the team to try.

kahoot.q: A good leader doesn't do everything alone; she ___ tasks to her team.
kahoot.explain: delegate — ishni boshqalarga topshirmoq (vakolat bermoq).

kahoot.q: A manager who controls every small detail of your work likes to ___.
kahoot.explain: micromanage — mayda-chuydagacha nazorat qilmoq.

kahoot.q: When everyone in the meeting finally agrees, they reach a ___.
kahoot.explain: reach a consensus — umumiy kelishuvga kelmoq.

kahoot.q: Team ___ was low after they lost three matches in a row.
kahoot.explain: morale — jamoa ruhi, kayfiyati. moral — axloqiy (boshqa so'z!).

kahoot.q: The manager told us to ___ our tasks: urgent ones first, less important ones later.
kahoot.explain: prioritise — eng muhimini birinchi o'ringa qo'ymoq (ustuvorlikni belgilamoq).

kahoot.q: A leader who makes quick, firm decisions is ___.
kahoot.explain: decisive — qat'iyatli. hesitant — ikkilanuvchi (antonim).

kahoot.q: Lead by ___: do what you want your team to do.
kahoot.explain: lead by example — shaxsiy namuna bilan yetaklamoq.

lessons.title: Phrasal verbs — LOOK
lessons.grammar_topic: PHRASAL VERBS with LOOK — 8 asosiy: look after / for / forward to / up / up to / down on / into / out + ajraladigan va ajralmaydigan (separable / inseparable) qoidasi; ZAXIRA: look over / around / back on
lessons.vocab_topic: Essential Words 19 — Literature, art and creativity (adabiyot, san'at va ijod)

Speaking: Kitob SAMPLE SPEAKING, Topic: Hobbies — faqat mavzu; namunalar original. Writing: 18-dars savoli (Kitob SAMPLE ESSAYS, 2-o'rin) — faqat savol; namuna original. Dars oxirida o'quvchi olmoshni to'g'ri joylaydi (look it up / look after her) va look forward to dan keyin ot yoki V-ing ishlatadi (Ex2, Ex4).
