intro: PHRASAL VERB = fe'l + zarracha (up, after, into…); ma'no ko'pincha so'zma-so'z emas: look up to = hurmat qilmoq.
LOOK AFTER (qaramoq, g'amxo'rlik) / LOOK FOR (qidirmoq) / LOOK INTO (tekshirmoq) — ajralmaydi, obyekt zarrachadan keyin: "look after her brother", "look into the case".
LOOK UP (lug'atdan qidirmoq) — ajraladi: "look up the word" = "look the word up"; olmosh bo'lsa FAQAT o'rtada: "look it up".
LOOK FORWARD TO (+ V-ing / ot), LOOK UP TO (hurmat), LOOK DOWN ON (mensimaslik) — 3 so'zli, ajralmaydi: "I look forward to seeing you."

LOOK OUT! (ehtiyot bo'l!) — odatda obyektsiz; look out for + ot — ko'zdan qochirmaslik, izlab topmoq (Look out for the small door). ZAXIRA: look over (ko'zdan kechirmoq), look around (aylanib ko'rmoq), look back on (o'tmishni eslamoq).
formulas: look after / look for
S + look after/for + OBYEKT (ajralmaydi)
She looks after her little brother. / I'm looking for my keys.
U ukasiga g'amxo'rlik qiladi. / Kalitlarimni qidiryapman.
look forward to
S + look forward to + V-ing / ot
We look forward to the holidays. / I look forward to seeing you.
Biz ta'tilni intiqlik bilan kutyapmiz. / Sizni ko'rishni intiqlik bilan kutaman.
look up (ajraladi)
S + look up + ot / look + OT/OLMOSH + up
You can look the word up in a dictionary. / Look it up.
So'zni lug'atdan qidirsang bo'ladi. / Uni qidirib ko'r.
look up to / look down on
S + look up to / down on + KIM (ajralmaydi)
I look up to my grandfather. / Don't look down on others.
Men bobomni hurmat qilaman. / Boshqalarga past nazar bilan qarama.
look into / look out
S + look into + ISH (tekshirmoq) / Look out! (ehtiyot bo'l!)
The police are looking into the case. / Look out! There's a car coming!
Politsiya ishni tekshiryapti. / Ehtiyot bo'l! Mashina kelyapti!
ZAXIRA: look over / look around / look back on
look over + HUJJAT (ajraladi: look it over) / look around + JOY / look back on + O'TMISH
He looked over the report quickly. / Let's look around the museum. / She looked back on her childhood.
U hisobotni tezda ko'zdan kechirdi. / Muzeyni aylanib chiqaylik. / U bolaligini esladi.
presentation: CCQ: She looks after her little brother.
Is she searching for him? (No) Does she take care of him? (Yes)
CCQ: I look up to my grandfather.
Do I respect him? (Yes) Am I looking at something above me? (No)
CCQ: Look it up.
Where does 'it' go — before or after 'up'? (In the middle, before 'up') Can we say 'look up it'? (No)
CCQ: I'm looking forward to the trip.
Is the trip in the past or in the future? (Future) Am I happy about it? (Yes) Noun or V-ing after 'to'? (Both are possible)
CCQ: The police are looking into the case.
Are they only looking at it with their eyes? (No) Are they trying to find the facts? (Yes)
notes: look for (qidirmoq) vs look after (qaramoq) vs look at (qaramoq — ko'z bilan) — zarracha ma'noni belgilaydi.

look up to — odatda odamga nisbatan ("look up to a poet", lekin "look up to his imagery" emas); look down on — odamga ham, ish yoki narsaga ham ishlatiladi ("look down on others", "look down on comic books").

O'quvchi so'raydi: Nega "look up the word" to'g'ri-yu, "look up it" xato? — Javob: ajraladigan fe'lda ot ikki joyda tura oladi (look up the word / look the word up), olmosh esa faqat o'rtada: look it up.
O'quvchi so'raydi: look forward to dan keyin nega "meet" emas? — Javob: bu to — predlog (infinitiv belgisi emas); predlogdan keyin ot yoki V-ing keladi: look forward to meeting you / to the holidays.
mistakes: Look up it in the dictionary.
Look it up in the dictionary.
I look forward to meet you.
I look forward to meeting you.
She looks after for her brother.
I respect my grandfather. I look up him.
Hurmat — look up TO; olmosh oxirida.
Police are looking the case into.
Police are looking into the case.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Hobbies (og'zaki): Part 1, 2, 3
class_ex.instr: (12 daq, juftlik) 2' — Part 1: A 4 savolni so'raydi, B javob beradi (javob + sabab + misol), keyin almashadi. 1' — tayyorgarlik: Kartochka A bo'yicha faqat 5–6 kalit so'z. 2' — A gapiradi, B S-CHECK-4.0 ni belgilaydi. 2' — ustoz NAMUNA A ni o'qiydi, o'quvchilar box'dagi eshitgan iboralarini belgilaydi. 2' — B shu kartochkada gapiradi (box'dan 2+ ibora bilan). 2' — Part 3 juftlikda. 1' — ustoz feedback (S-4.0). ICQ: Tayyorgarlikka necha daqiqa? (1) Kartochkada nechta band bor? (4 — 3 ta 'You should say' + 'explain')
items: Part 1: What do you like doing in your free time?
Part 1: Did you have the same hobbies as a child?
Part 1: Do you prefer hobbies at home or outdoors?
Part 1: Do your friends have the same hobbies as you?
KARTOCHKA A: Describe a hobby you enjoy. You should say: what it is ; when you started it ; how often you do it ; and explain why you enjoy it.
Part 3: Why are hobbies important for young people?
Part 3: Should schools have more art and music lessons?
Part 3: Can a hobby become a good job?
box: I'd like to talk about my hobby, which is …
I started it about … years ago, when / because …
I looked up a few tutorials online …
Now I do it two or three times a week, usually …
It's a really creative process: I choose a theme …
I decide how to portray each character …
It also teaches me patience, because …
At the moment I'm looking forward to …
answers: Part 1 namunalari (faqat ustoz uchun): 1) Mostly I edit short videos on my phone or play football with my friends in the yard. On rainy days I stay at home and look up new editing tricks online.
2) Not really. As a child I collected football stickers and built things from Lego. I only became interested in creative hobbies when I was about fourteen.
3) I'd say outdoors, because I sit at a desk all day at school. For example, in summer I love filming in the mountains, so I get fresh air and enjoy my hobby at the same time.
4) Some of them do. Two of my classmates also make videos, so we often help each other. But my best friend prefers chess, and he looks down on video editing a little, which is quite funny.

NAMUNA A (Band 5.5–6, 166 so'z, ~1.5–2 daqiqa): I'd like to talk about my hobby, which is making and editing short videos. I started it about two years ago, before my cousin's wedding, because nobody in the family knew how to put all the clips together. I looked up a few free tutorials online, downloaded a simple editing app and made a five-minute film. Everyone loved it, so I kept going. Now I edit videos two or three times a week, usually at the weekend. Most of them are short stories about my neighbourhood, for example an old man who repairs bicycles in our mahalla. I enjoy it because it's a really creative process: I choose a theme, decide how to portray each character and add music that matches the mood. It also teaches me patience, because one minute of video can take three hours of work. I look after my old phone very carefully, because it's my only camera. At the moment I'm looking forward to a film competition for teenagers next spring.

Part 3 namunalari: 1) I think hobbies help young people relax after long hours of study. They also build creativity and self-confidence: for example, a teenager who acts in a school drama learns to speak in front of people.

2) Yes, I believe they should, but not instead of maths or science. Art and music stimulate the imagination, and many children discover a talent there. Unfortunately, these lessons are often the first to be cancelled before exams.

3) Definitely, if a person develops it seriously. For instance, many young people who started by editing videos for fun now work for TV channels or advertising companies. However, a hobby can lose its fun when it becomes an obligation.

class_ex.title: WRITING NORMATIV — The purpose of school (yozma, 10 daqiqa)
class_ex.instr: (12 daq, yakka) 1' — savol va qoida proyektorda (18-dars savoli; uydagi insholar yig'ib olingan). 9' — yakka: kirish + 1 body paragraf, 110–140 so'z; daftar, telefon va namunasiz. 2' — W-CHECK-4.0 bilan o'zini tekshiradi, so'z sonini oxirida yozadi; ish yig'iladi. ICQ: Nechta abzats yozasiz? (2 — kirish va bitta body) Telefon yoki uydagi inshodan foydalanish mumkinmi? (Yo'q)
items: Question: Some people believe school should prepare students for work. Others think it should help them become better individuals. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
TASK: In 9 minutes write an introduction + ONE body paragraph (110–140 words). No notes, no phone, no model.
Introduction (2 sentences): paraphrase both views + give your clear opinion.
Body: Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link. Use today's grammar once or twice: a LOOK phrasal verb (look up to, look forward to, look after …).
At the end write the number of words. Check with W-CHECK-4.0: points 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7.
answers: Tahlil: savol turi — discuss both views + opinion; kirishda ikkala qarash parafraz qilinadi va pozitsiya 2-gapda aniq aytiladi; normativda bitta body yoziladi (qaysi qarash — o'quvchi tanlaydi, xulosa shart emas). 18-dars inshosidagi abzatsni yoddan ko'chirish emas, yangi misol bilan yozish rag'batlantiriladi.

NAMUNA — kirish + 1 body (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6; g'oya 18-dars namunasidan farqli — adabiyot va san'at orqali xarakter tarbiyasi): Some people think that the main aim of school is to prepare young people for their future jobs, while others believe it should help them grow into good people. In my view, both aims matter, but schools should not forget about students' character. Through literature and art, school can make pupils kinder and more open-minded. When students read a novel or act in a school drama, they see the world through the eyes of another character. As a result, they begin to look up to people who are honest and brave, and they learn not to look down on those who are different. For example, last spring our theatre club performed a play about a lonely old man, and afterwards several classmates started visiting elderly neighbours in our mahalla. Therefore, creative subjects deserve as much attention as exam subjects.
Baholash: W-4.0 (jadval shu mashqdan keyin), NORM-4.0: 10–12 ball — 2 coin; 7–9 — bajarildi; ≤6 — uyda qayta yozadi.
why: look up to people who are honest and brave — look up to + KIM: hurmat qilmoq, o'ziga namuna bilmoq (ajralmaydi).
not to look down on those who are different — look down on + KIM: mensimaslik; 3 so'zli, ajralmaydi.
EW19 so'zlari: novel, drama, character, creative (creativity) — mavzuga mos; 'open-minded', 'deserve attention' — tabiiy kollokatsiyalar.
O'zbek misoli: maktab teatr to'garagi va mahalladagi keksalarga yordam — aniq misol (TR va LR uchun ball beradi).
class_ex.note: Manba: savol — 18-dars savoli (Kitob IELTS 4.0, SAMPLE ESSAYS, 2-o'rin — faqat savol olindi); namuna Jony Academy original matni. Namuna o'quvchiga ish yig'ib olingandan keyin ko'rsatiladi.

homework.instr: MAJBURIY. 1 daqiqa tayyorgarlik (faqat 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1.5–2 daqiqa to'xtamasdan gapirib, ovozli yozuvni ilovaga yuboring. Matndan o'qimang. items: KARTOCHKA B: Describe a creative activity you would like to take up. You should say: what it is ; where you could learn it ; what you need for it ; and explain why you want to try it.
answers: NAMUNA B (Band 5.5–6, 140 so'z, faqat ustoz uchun): A creative activity I would like to take up is calligraphy, the art of beautiful handwriting. I became interested in it last year, when our class looked around an exhibition of old manuscripts at a gallery in Tashkent. Some pages looked like real masterpieces, and every letter was almost a small painting. I found out that a local art centre runs calligraphy courses at weekends. To start, you don't need much: a special pen, ink, good paper and, most of all, patience. I have already looked up a few videos and tried to copy simple letters, but my lines are still shaky. I want to try it because it combines creativity and concentration, and it connects me with our history. Also, a hand-written card would be a lovely present for my grandmother. I'm really looking forward to my first lesson.
Bugungi struktura: looked around an exhibition, looked up a few videos, looking forward to my first lesson; EW19: gallery, masterpieces, painting, creativity (+ STRONG: exhibition).

reading.title: Cho'lpon — the poet whose readers looked after his books
text: A. Abdulhamid Sulaymon o'g'li was born in Andijan in 1897. His father was a merchant who also wrote poetry, and the boy looked up to him. He studied at a madrasa and later at a Russian school, so he learned several languages. While he was still a teenager, he began to publish poems under the name Cho'lpon, which means "the morning star".

B. The young poet looked around him and did not like what he saw: few modern schools, few newspapers and almost no theatre. He joined the Jadids, reformers who looked forward to an educated and modern nation, and he wrote for their journals. His first collection of poems, "Uyg'onish" ("Awakening"), came out in 1922. Readers who were looking for the old style of classical poetry found something new: short lines, everyday words and images — night, spring, wind, a bird — that meant more than they said.

C. Not everyone liked this new voice. In the poem "Go'zal", a man speaks about a beautiful girl, but many readers believed that "the beautiful one" was really the nation. His novel "Kecha va kunduz" ("Night and Day") tells the story of Zebi, a young woman whose life is destroyed by an unfair system. Officials looked over every page of the novel and called it nationalist. He also translated Shakespeare's Hamlet into Uzbek, but his situation became more and more dangerous.

D. In 1937 he was arrested, and in 1938 he was shot in Tashkent, together with other writers such as Abdulla Qodiriy and Fitrat. For decades his books were banned. Families looked after hidden copies, copied poems by hand and taught them to their children in whispers.

E. In 1956 the state looked into his case again and cleared his name, but his books stayed hard to find for many more years. Today students look up his poems on their phones, and every year on 31 August the country remembers the victims of repression, including the writers it lost. It took half a century, but his poems finally flew free.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)
glossary: Jadids — jadidlar (XX asr boshidagi ma'rifatparvar islohotchilar)
"Kecha va kunduz" — Cho'lponning romani; bosh qahramoni Zebi
31 August — qatag'on qurbonlarini yod etish kuni

tasks.title: Multiple choice
tasks.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
items: 1 What does paragraph A mainly describe? A) the history of Andijan B) the poet's early life and education C) the Jadid journals D) his father's poems

2 Why did many readers find his first collection new? A) it was very long B) it followed the rules of classical poetry C) it used short lines, everyday words and images with deeper meanings D) it was written in Russian
3 What is the main idea of paragraph E? A) his name was cleared and he is remembered today B) his books were lost forever C) students no longer read poetry D) the state banned his poems again in 1956

tasks.title: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN

Cho'lpon went to a Russian school before he studied at a madrasa.
The Jadids published their journals in several languages.
His first collection followed the style of classical poetry.
"Kecha va kunduz" has been translated into many languages.
His name was cleared less than twenty years after his death.
why: A: 'a merchant who also wrote poetry'.
A: avval madrasa, keyin ('later') rus maktabi.
B: jurnallar tili haqida ma'lumot yo'q.
B: o'quvchilar eski uslubni qidirib, 'something new' topdi.
C: tarjimalar haqida ma'lumot yo'q.
D–E: 1938-yilda otilgan, 1956-yilda oqlangan — 18 yil.

items: Length of the tour: ___ minutes
Manuscripts: Room ___
In the manuscript room: no flash photography, no food or ___
Reading room: look up any poet on the ___
Poetry evening starts at ___
Student ticket: ___ sums
The library is closed on ___

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; monolog — ustoz Guide rolida o'qiydi (yoki kuchli o'quvchi), tempni sekinroq tuting.
Guide: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the House of Uzbek Poetry. Before we start, let me give you some information about today's visit.
Guide: The tour takes about ninety minutes — sorry, I mean seventy minutes, because the second floor is closed today for repairs.

Guide: If you're looking for the manuscripts, they're in Room 4, not Room 2 as it says on the old map. Please look after them: no flash photography, and no food, and — this is new this year — no drinks either.
Guide: In Room 5 you can see early Jadid newspapers. Many visitors think they're copies, but they're originals, so please don't touch the glass.
Guide: Look out for the small door on the left before the café — that's the reading room. It's quiet, and you can look up any poet on our computers there — the tablets are only for children.

Guide: This evening we have a poetry evening, which we're all looking forward to. It starts at half past six — not six o'clock, as some posters say. Tickets cost 25,000 sums for adults and 10,000 for students.

Guide: If you'd like to look into the history of Uzbek literature further, our library is open from Tuesday to Sunday. It used to close on Sundays, but now it's closed on Mondays. It has more than 3,000 books, so you'll certainly find something.
Guide: Finally, the gift shop sells notebooks and posters. Any questions? No? Then let's begin.

kahoot.q: I'm looking ___ my keys. Have you seen them?
kahoot.explain: look for — qidirmoq (look after — qaramoq, look into — tekshirmoq).

kahoot.q: She looks ___ her little brother while her parents are at work.
kahoot.explain: look after — g'amxo'rlik qilmoq, qarab turmoq.

kahoot.q: I don't know this word. I'll look ___ in the dictionary.
kahoot.explain: look up ajraladi, olmosh o'rtada keladi: look it up ('look up it' — xato).

kahoot.q: I look forward to ___ you next week.
kahoot.explain: look forward TO + V-ing: to — predlog, shuning uchun seeing.

kahoot.q: I really look ___ my grandfather — he is so wise and kind.
kahoot.explain: look up TO — hurmat qilmoq (look up — lug'atdan qidirmoq).

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: Police are looking the case into.
Police are looking into the case.
You can look the word up.
kahoot.explain: look into ajralmaydi: looking into the case.

kahoot.q: Rich people shouldn't look ___ poor people.
kahoot.explain: look down on — past nazar bilan qaramoq, mensimaslik.

kahoot.q: ___! There's a car coming!
kahoot.explain: Look out! — Ehtiyot bo'l! (xavf haqida ogohlantirish).

kahoot.q: Our teacher is looking ___ why the test results were so low.
kahoot.explain: look into — tekshirmoq, sababini o'rganmoq.

kahoot.q: Qaysi phrasal verb AJRALADI (olmosh o'rtaga kiradi)?
kahoot.explain: look up ajraladi (look it up), look after/for/into esa ajralmaydi.

kahoot.q: The students are looking forward ___ the poetry evening.
kahoot.explain: look forward TO + ot yoki V-ing: looking forward to the evening.

kahoot.q: 'Javobingizni intiqlik bilan kutaman' — to'g'ri tarjima?
options: I look forward to hearing from you.
I look forward to hear from you.
I look for to hearing from you.
I look forward hearing from you.
kahoot.explain: look forward to + V-ing: to hearing — rasmiy xat oxirida ishlatiladi.

kahoot.q: The Mona Lisa is a ___ — one of the greatest works of art.
kahoot.explain: masterpiece — shoh asar.

kahoot.q: The main character of a story is the ___.
kahoot.explain: protagonist — asarning bosh qahramoni.

kahoot.q: A group of lines in a poem is called a ___.
kahoot.explain: stanza — she'rdagi band (prose — nasr).

kahoot.q: A person who writes plays for the theatre is a ___.
kahoot.explain: playwright — teatr uchun pyesa yozuvchi dramaturg.

kahoot.q: Writing that makes fun of politicians or society is ___.
kahoot.explain: satire — jamiyat kamchiliklarini kulgili tarzda tanqid qilish.

kahoot.q: A book of poems by many different writers is an ___.
kahoot.explain: anthology — to'plam (antologiya).

kahoot.q: Some Jadid writers faced ___: they were arrested and their books were banned.
kahoot.explain: persecution — ta'qib (hibsga olish, kitoblarni taqiqlash).

kahoot.q: 'Illustrator' ma'nosi?
kahoot.explain: illustrator — kitob uchun rasm (illyustratsiya) chizuvchi rassom.

intro: TRANSPORT: get IN / get OUT OF — mashina, taksi (egilib kiriladigan kichik transport); get ON / get OFF — avtobus, poyezd, samolyot, velosiped.
MUNOSABAT: get on (well) with / get along with + kim — yaxshi chiqishmoq.
QIYINCHILIK: get over + kasallik/ayriliq — tuzalmoq, yengib o'tmoq; get through + qiyin davr/imtihon — o'tib chiqmoq; get through to + kim — (telefonda) bog'lanmoq.
QAYTISH / QUTULISH: get back (from / to) — qaytmoq; get rid of + ot — qutulmoq.
ZAXIRA (vaqt qolsa; Kahoot, normativ va testga kirmaydi): get by, get away (with), get across, get down to, get around, get together, get on with (ish), get ahead.
formulas: Transport
get in / out of + car, taxi; get on / off + bus, train, plane
She got in the taxi and left. / He got off the train.
U taksiga o'tirdi va ketdi. / U poyezddan tushdi.
Munosabat
get on (well) with / get along with + KIM
We get on well. / Do you get along with your classmates?
Biz yaxshi chiqishamiz. / Sinfdoshlaring bilan yaxshi chiqishasanmi?
Qiyinchilik
get over + kasallik/ayriliq; get through + davr/imtihon
She got over the flu in a week. / He got through a very hard year.
U bir haftada grippdan tuzaldi. / U juda og'ir yilni o'tkazdi.
Bog'lanish
get through to + KIM (telefon)
I couldn't get through to him.
Unga bog'lana olmadim.
Qaytish / qutulish
get back (from / to); get rid of + OT
When did you get back from Paris? / We need to get rid of this old sofa.
Parijdan qachon qaytding? / Bu eski divandan qutulishimiz kerak.
ZAXIRA: qo'shimcha fe'llar
get by, get away (with), get across, get down to, get together, get on with (ish), get ahead, get around
They get by on little money. / Let's get down to business.
Ular kam pul bilan kun ko'rishadi. / Keling, ishga kirishaylik.
presentation: How long did it take Serena to get back on court after her daughter was born?
Less than a year — she got over a serious illness and got back on court within a year.
Did the sisters get on well?
Yes, they got on well off the court, even when they played each other in finals.
What idea did she help to get rid of?
The idea that tennis is only for rich people.
CCQ: She got over the flu.
Is she ill now? (No) Was she ill before? (Yes)
CCQ: I couldn't get through to him.
Did we talk? (No) Did I try to phone him? (Yes)
CCQ: We got off the bus at the market.
Were we on the bus before? (Yes) Are we on it now? (No) Taxi bo'lsa? (got out of)
CCQ: She gets on well with her sister.
Do they argue a lot? (No) Is 'get along with' the same? (Yes)
CCQ: We got rid of the old sofa.
Do we have the sofa now? (No) Did we want to keep it? (No)
notes: Katta transport (avtobus, poyezd, samolyot) — get on / off; mashina, taksi — get in / get out of.
get over + ot: get over the flu ('get over from' — xato); get rid OF; get along WITH; get through TO + kim.

class_ex.instr: (12 daq, juftlik) 2' — Part 1: A 4 savolni so'raydi, B javob beradi (javob + sabab + misol), keyin almashadi. 1' — tayyorgarlik: Kartochka A bo'yicha faqat 5–6 kalit so'z. 2' — A gapiradi, B S-CHECK-4.0 ni belgilaydi. 2' — ustoz NAMUNA A ni o'qiydi, o'quvchilar box'dagi eshitgan iboralarini belgilaydi. 2' — B shu kartochkada gapiradi (box'dan 2+ ibora bilan). 2' — Part 3 juftlikda. 1' — ustoz feedback (S-4.0). ICQ: Tayyorgarlikka necha daqiqa? (1) Kartochkada nechta band bor? (4 — 3 ta 'You should say' + 'explain')
items: Part 1: Do you have many friends?
Part 1: Where do you usually meet your friends?
Part 1: What do you like doing with your friends?
Part 1: Do you have friends from other cities or countries?
KARTOCHKA A: Describe a good friend you get along with very well. You should say: who this person is ; how you met ; what you do together ; and explain why you get along so well.
Part 3: Is it easy to make real friends online?
Part 3: Are old friends more important than new friends?
Part 3: How can friends get over an argument?
box: I'd like to talk about my friend …, who is probably the person I get along with best.
We met about … years ago at …
At first he / she was just an acquaintance, but …
After that we became close friends.
These days we do a lot together: we … and we …
We have a lot in common, but we're not exactly the same.
There is real trust between us.
He / She helped me get through … / We always get over our arguments quickly.
answers: Part 1 namunalari (faqat ustoz uchun): 1) Not really. I have a lot of acquaintances at school, but only three or four close friends. I prefer a small group, because it's easier to stay in touch and really know each other.
2) Usually at school or in the park near our block of flats. At weekends we sometimes meet at a small café in the city centre, because it's a quiet place to talk.
3) We like playing volleyball, and sometimes we just walk and talk for hours. Before exams we also study together, which helps us get through the stress.
4) Yes, I have a friend in Bukhara whom I met at a summer camp. We keep in touch through video calls, although we don't talk very often because we're both busy with school.

NAMUNA A (Band 5.5–6, 171 so'z, ~1.5–2 daqiqa): I'd like to talk about my friend Jasur, who is probably the person I get along with best outside my family. We met about four years ago at a chess club in our neighbourhood. At first he was just an acquaintance, because we only played against each other on Saturdays. Then one evening we missed the bus home and walked for forty minutes, talking about games and films, and after that we became close friends. These days we do a lot together: we revise for exams in the library, we play chess online, and in summer we sometimes cycle to the lake outside the city. I think we get along so well for two reasons. First, we have a lot in common, but we're not exactly the same, so we learn from each other. Second, there is real trust between us. Last spring, when I was worried about my exams, he helped me get through that stressful month. Of course, we sometimes have arguments, but we always get over them quickly.

Part 3 namunalari: 1) Not really. People can find others with the same interests online very quickly, but trust usually needs time and real meetings. For example, someone may seem friendly in a chat but behave very differently in real life.
2) I think old friends are often more important, because they know your past and have supported you for years. However, new friends can bring new ideas and opportunities, so people need both.

3) The best way is to talk calmly and listen to each other instead of sending angry messages. If one person apologises and the other is ready to forgive, they can usually get over the argument quickly and even become closer.

class_ex.title: WRITING — Online friendship (yozma): Task 2 body paragraf
class_ex.instr: (12 daq, yakka) 2 daq — savol tahlili: savol turi (agree / disagree), kalit so'zlar, sinfda qaysi qarashni yozamiz. 8 daq — BITTA body paragraf: nega onlayn do'stlar odatda yuzma-yuz do'stlardek yaqin bo'lmaydi, 100–120 so'z, qolip: Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link; GET phrasal verb 1–2 marta; oxirida so'z sonini yozing. 2 daq — sherik bilan almashib W-CHECK-4.0 bo'yicha tekshirasiz; ustoz 1 paragrafni W-4.0 bo'yicha ovoz chiqarib baholaydi. ICQ: Nechta paragraf? (1) Necha so'z? (100–120)
box: Question: Some people say that friends we make online can never be as close as friends we meet in person. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Useful: There are good reasons to believe that … / Firstly, … / In addition, … / For example, … / As a result, …
Ideas: trust needs time together · online you show only your best side
items: Savol turi qanday? To'liq inshoda pozitsiya qayerda aytiladi va nechta body kerak?
Sinfda qaysi qarashni yozamiz: 'onlayn do'stlar yaqin bo'la olmaydi' yoki qarshi fikr?
Kalit so'zlarni qanday parafraz qilasiz (friends we make online, as close as, in person)?
Bugungi grammatika (GET) qayerga mos keladi: get along with, get through, get over?
Qaysi EW20 so'zlari bu mavzuga mos (kamida 4 ta)?
TASK: Write ONE body paragraph (100–120 words): why online friends are rarely as close. Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link.
answers: 1) Agree / disagree (To what extent …?) — pozitsiya kirishda bitta aniq gapda aytiladi va xulosagacha saqlanadi; to'liq inshoda 2 ta body (masalan, Body 1 — rozilik sabablari, Body 2 — qarshi fikr va o'z pozitsiyasi).
2) Sinfda — rozilik: onlayn do'stlar nega kamdan-kam yaqin bo'ladi. Qarshi fikr — uyga QO'SHIMCHA (Body 2).
3) friends we make online -> online friends / people we meet on the internet; as close as -> as deep / as strong as; in person -> face to face / in real life.
4) get through (the week / a hard time), get along with (people), get over (an argument).
5) EW20 CORE: trust, support, close friend, friendship, honesty, loyalty, acquaintance; SUPER: rely on each other, have a lot in common.

NAMUNA paragraf — rozilik (faqat ustoz uchun, 120 so'z): On the one hand, there are good reasons to believe that online friends are rarely as close as friends we meet in person. Firstly, real trust usually grows when people spend time together and see how loyal and honest the other person is in difficult situations. Online, it is easy to show only your best side, so it is hard to know someone's true character. In addition, friends who live nearby can give practical support. For example, when a student in Tashkent falls ill before an exam, a close friend from class can bring notes and help him get through the week, while an online friend can only send messages. As a result, face-to-face friendships are often deeper and stronger.

Namuna: 120 so'z (Topic sentence -> 2 sabab -> misol -> As a result). Bugungi struktura: help him get through the week. EW20 CORE: trust, loyal (loyalty), honest (honesty), support, close friend, friendships — 6 ta, W-CHECK 6-band bajarilgan.
Baholash: W-4.0 (jadval shu darsda) + W-CHECK-4.0 (7-band: paragraf 100–120 so'z); NORM-4.0 — body paragraf: 10–12 — 1 coin; ≤6 — uyda qayta.
why: Bugungi grammatika: 'help him get through the week' — get through + qiyin davr (o'tib chiqmoq); Writing'da get phrasal verb 1–2 marta yetarli, qolgan joyda rasmiyroq so'zlar ishlatiladi (masalan, give practical support).

EW20 CORE so'zlari namunada: trust — ishonch; loyal / honest (loyalty, honesty) — sadoqat, rostgo'ylik; support — qo'llab-quvvatlash; close friend — yaqin do'st; friendships — do'stlik. Jami 6 ta — W-CHECK 6-band (kamida 4 ta) bajariladi.
Bog'lovchilar: Firstly, In addition, For example, while, As a result — 4+ xil, W-CHECK 4-band uchun yetarli.
O'zbek misoli: Toshkentdagi o'quvchi imtihon oldidan kasal bo'lib qoladi — aniq, hayotiy misol TR va CC uchun ball beradi.
class_ex.note: Jony Academy savoli (kitob SAMPLE ESSAYS uslubida); namuna paragraf Jony Academy original matni. Kuchsiz: 2 ta sabab + 1 misol, 80–100 so'z; Kuchli: + Body 2 rejasi (qarshi fikr + o'z pozitsiyasi). Qarshi fikr — uyga QO'SHIMCHA (namuna homework answers da).

rows: Vazifaga javob (TR; Task 1 da TA)

Savolning BARCHA qismiga javob (sabab VA yechim; ikki fikr VA o'z fikri; ijobiy VA salbiy tomon); pozitsiya kirishda aniq va xulosagacha saqlanadi; har asosiy g'oya izoh va aniq misol bilan. Insho: kirish + 2 body + xulosa, 220–260 so'z; paragraf: talab qilingan so'z soni. Task 1: overview bor, asosiy raqamlar to'g'ri.
Savolga javob va pozitsiya bor, lekin bir qismi yuzaki yoki misol umumiy; insho 180–219 so'z yoki xulosa 1 gapdan iborat. Task 1: overview bor, ayrim raqamlar keraksiz.
Savolning faqat bir qismiga javob (masalan, faqat sabablar); pozitsiya noaniq yoki o'zgarib ketadi; g'oyalar takrorlanadi; insho 120–179 so'z. Task 1: overview yo'q.
Savolga javob yo'q, mavzudan tashqari, yodlangan boshqa matn yoki so'z soni talabning yarmidan kam.
Izchillik va bog'lanish (CC)

Abzatslar aniq: kirish -> Body 1 -> Body 2 -> xulosa; har body: topic sentence -> izoh -> misol -> link; 4+ xil bog'lovchi to'g'ri (however, as a result, for example, on the other hand); ishora so'zlari (this, they, such) to'g'ri.
Abzatslar bor, mantiq tushunarli; 2–3 bog'lovchi, ba'zan mexanik (Firstly, Secondly…); 1–2 noaniq ishora.
Abzatsga bo'linmagan yoki body da topic sentence yo'q; bog'lovchilar 1–2 ta yoki noto'g'ri.
G'oyalar tartibsiz, bog'lanish yo'q.
Lug'at boyligi (LR)
Shu darsning Essential Words so'zlaridan 4+ ta va 2+ kollokatsiya to'g'ri; savol so'zlari parafraz qilingan; imlo xatosi 1–2 ta.
Mavzu so'zlari bor, lekin takror ko'p yoki 3–4 so'z noto'g'ri tanlangan; savol so'zlari ko'chirilgan; imlo xatolari ma'noga xalaqit bermaydi.
Oddiy, takroriy lug'at; so'z tanlash va imlo xatolari ma'noni qiyinlashtiradi.
Juda cheklangan lug'at, ma'no tushunarsiz.
Grammatika aniqligi va xilma-xilligi (GRA)
Sodda va qo'shma gaplar aralash (because, although, which, if); bugungi struktura 1–3 marta to'g'ri va tabiiy; gaplarning ko'pi xatosiz.
Qo'shma gap urinishlari bor; xatolar bor, lekin ma'no tushunarli; artikl/zamon xatolari takrorlanadi.
Asosan sodda gaplar; xatolar ko'p, ayrim gaplar tushunarsiz.
Gap tuzilishi deyarli yo'q.
Jami (12 ball) -> taxminiy band
11–12 ball ≈ Band 5.5–6
8–10 ball ≈ Band 5
5–7 ball ≈ Band 4–4.5
0–4 ball ≈ Band 3.5 va past
Qoidalar (ustoz uchun)
Vaqt: insho 40 daq (uyda, taymer), WRITING NORMATIV 10 daq; vaqt tugaganda chiziq tortiladi, chiziqdan keyingi qism baholanmaydi.
So'z sonini o'quvchi oxirida yozadi; ustoz 2 qatorni sanab tekshiradi; insho 180 so'zdan kam — TR ko'pi bilan 1.
Namuna yoki boshqa manbadan ko'chirilgani aniqlansa — 0 ball, sinfda boshqa savol bilan qayta yozadi.
Ustoz har ish chetiga TR/CC/LR/GRA ballarini va 1 ta eng muhim tuzatishni yozadi; umumiy 2–3 xato keyingi darsning 'Xatolar ustida ishlash' bosqichiga.

homework.title: 4. SPEAKING NORMATIV — Friends (og'zaki, ovozli): Kartochka B
homework.instr: MAJBURIY. 1 daqiqa tayyorgarlik (faqat 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1.5–2 daqiqa to'xtamasdan gapirib, ovozli yozuvni ilovaga yuboring. Matndan o'qimang. Bugungi GET fe'llaridan (get along with, get through, get over) 1–2 tasini va EW20 so'zlaridan kamida 2 tasini ishlating. 1 marta qayta yozish mumkin.
items: KARTOCHKA B: Describe a time a friend helped you. You should say: when it was ; what the problem was ; how your friend helped ; and explain how you felt.
answers: NAMUNA B (Band 5.5–6, 155 so'z, faqat ustoz uchun): I'm going to describe a time when my friend Bekzod helped me last winter. I had just moved to a new school in the middle of the year, and it was a hard time for me. I didn't know anyone, my social life was almost zero, and I was behind in physics. Bekzod sat next to me, and on the second day he offered to explain the topics I had missed. For two weeks we stayed after lessons, and he patiently showed me his notes. He also introduced me to his friends, so I didn't have to eat lunch alone any more. Thanks to his support, I got through the end-of-term test and even got a good mark. I felt really grateful, and a bit surprised, because he did all this for someone he hardly knew. Now we get along with each other really well, and he has become a close friend I can trust.
Bugungi struktura: I got through the end-of-term test, we get along with each other; EW20: social life, support, close friend, trust (STRONG: gratitude -> grateful).
Baholash: S-4.0 (class_ex dagi jadval), NORM-4.0: 10–12 ball — 2 coin; 7–9 — bajarildi; ≤6 — qayta yozib yuboradi.

homework.title: 7. QO'SHIMCHA — WRITING — Online friendship: Body 2 (qarshi fikr), 100–120 so'z (yozma)
homework.instr: Sinfdagi paragrafni W-CHECK-4.0 bo'yicha tuzating va ikkinchi body paragraf yozing: qarshi fikr — onlayn do'stlik ham yaqin bo'la oladi — va oxirida o'z pozitsiyangiz. 100–120 so'z: Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example (O'zbekistondan) -> Link; GET fe'li 1–2 marta; oxirida so'z sonini yozing.
items: Question: Some people say that friends we make online can never be as close as friends we meet in person. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Plan: Topic sentence (the opposite view) -> Reason 1 + explain -> Reason 2 -> Example -> Link (your opinion).
answers: NAMUNA Body 2 (Band 5.5–6, 112 so'z, Jony Academy original, faqat ustoz uchun): On the other hand, online friendships can also become very close. Many teenagers meet people with the same interests in online games or study groups, and they often get along with them easily because they have a lot in common. Moreover, chatting online helps shy people talk about their problems more openly, and honesty is the basis of any real friendship. For instance, a girl from Nukus may get through a hard exam year with the support of an online study partner from Fergana, and later they may meet in person. Therefore, in my view, the closeness of a friendship depends more on loyalty and trust than on where people first met.
Bugungi struktura: get along with them, get through a hard exam year; EW20: have a lot in common, honesty, support, loyalty, trust.
Baholash: W-4.0 (class_ex dagi jadval), NORM-4.0: 10–12 ball — 1 coin; ≤6 — qayta yozadi.
homework.note: Namuna o'quvchiga baholangandan keyin ko'rsatiladi. Boshqa pozitsiya ham qabul qilinadi, agar 2 dalil va misol bo'lsa.

reading.title: Serena Williams — the girl from Compton who never let anything get her down
text: A. According to a well-known family story, Richard Williams was watching tennis on television when he saw a player receive a cheque for 40,000 dollars. He decided that his future children would play the sport, although he had never played it professionally himself, and he wrote a detailed plan for their careers. Venus was born in 1980 and Serena in 1981. The family lived in Compton, near Los Angeles, where money was often short. The girls practised on free public courts that were cracked and old, and their father coached them himself, often before school.

B. At that time tennis was mainly a sport for wealthy families, and many people did not expect the sisters to succeed. Serena's serve became one of the most feared shots in women's tennis, and in 1999, at the age of 17, she won her first Grand Slam title at the US Open. The sisters got on well off the court. Together they won 14 Grand Slam doubles titles, and they also met in nine Grand Slam finals as opponents without letting the rivalry damage their friendship.

C. Serena's career was not always easy. In 2003 the family lost their older sister, Yetunde, and it took them a long time to get over it. Two years earlier, part of the crowd at the Indian Wells tournament had treated Serena and her family unfairly, and she did not go back there for 14 years. When she finally returned in 2015, she received a warm welcome.

D. She also had to get through serious health problems. In 2017 she won the Australian Open while she was pregnant. After her daughter was born later that year, she was seriously ill for some time, but she got back on court within a year and reached four more Grand Slam finals.

E. Serena finished her career with 23 Grand Slam singles titles, more than any other woman in the Open era, and four Olympic gold medals. When she stepped away from tennis in 2022, she preferred the word "evolving" to "retiring". Today she invests in new companies, especially ones started by people who often find it hard to get money. For many young players, she helped to get rid of the idea that tennis is only for the rich.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

intro: You will hear a young woman phoning a tennis club to ask about beginners' classes.

tasks.title: Form completion — ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER (IELTS Part 1)
tasks.instr: Formani to'ldiring. 8 band.
items: Name: Dilnoza ___
Age: ___
Bus number: ___
Walk from the bus stop: ___ minutes
Monthly fee for students: ___ sums
Beginners' classes: Tuesdays and ___
Classes start at: ___ p.m.
Bring your own ___

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; 1-rol (Receptionist) — ustoz, 2-rol (Caller) — kuchli o'quvchi (yoki ovozni o'zgartiring).
Receptionist: Good afternoon, Chilonzor Tennis Club. How can I help you?
Caller: Hi. I'd like to join the club, please. I'm a complete beginner.
Receptionist: No problem. Can I have your name?
Caller: Dilnoza Karimova. That's K-A-R-I-M-O-V-A.
Receptionist: Thank you. And how old are you?
Caller: I'm sixteen — oh, sorry, my birthday was last week, so I'm seventeen now.
Receptionist: Great. How will you get here?
Caller: By bus, I think.
Receptionist: Then get on bus 51 — not 15, people often mix them up. Get off at the Chilonzor-9 stop, and from there it's a five-minute walk.
Caller: Fine. How much does it cost?
Receptionist: The normal fee is 300,000 sums a month, but students pay 250,000.
Caller: I'm a student, so that's good. When are the beginners' classes?
Receptionist: On Tuesdays and Thursdays. They used to start at five, but now they start at six p.m.
Caller: Do I need to bring anything?
Receptionist: Yes, your own racket. We got rid of the old club rackets last month. We give you the balls.
Caller: And if I can't get through to you on the phone?
Receptionist: Just send us a message online. See you on Tuesday!

kahoot.q: She got ___ the taxi and left.
kahoot.explain: Taksi, mashina (kichik) → get in / get out of. Avtobus, poyezd → get on / off.

kahoot.q: Hurry! We need to get ___ the bus now.
kahoot.explain: Avtobus, poyezd, samolyot → get on (chiqmoq) / get off (tushmoq).

kahoot.q: Do you get ___ with your classmates?
kahoot.explain: get along with — yaxshi chiqishmoq (= get on well with).

kahoot.q: It took her two weeks to get ___ the flu.
kahoot.explain: get over + kasallik/ayriliq — tuzalmoq, yengib o'tmoq. 'get over from' — xato.

kahoot.q: I was ill all week, but I got ___ the exams somehow.
kahoot.explain: get through + qiyin davr/imtihon — o'tib chiqmoq, eplamoq.

kahoot.q: We need to get rid ___ this old sofa.
kahoot.explain: get rid OF — qutulmoq. Boshqa predlog bo'lmaydi.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: She got out of the taxi.
kahoot.explain: Taksidan tushmoq — get out of the taxi. get off — avtobus, poyezd uchun.

kahoot.q: What time did you get ___ from school yesterday?
kahoot.explain: get back (from) — qaytmoq: get back from school.

kahoot.q: My brother and I get on well ___ each other.
kahoot.explain: get on (well) WITH + kim = get along with — yaxshi chiqishmoq.

kahoot.q: I called him ten times but couldn't get ___ to him.
kahoot.explain: get through to + KIM — (telefonda) bog'lanmoq.

kahoot.q: 'She got over the flu.' — Is she ill now?
options: She is catching the flu now.
kahoot.explain: get over — kasallikdan tuzalmoq: kasal edi, endi sog'.

kahoot.q: We've arrived. Everybody get ___ of the car!
kahoot.explain: Mashina, taksi → get in / get OUT OF. get off — avtobus, poyezd uchun.

kahoot.q: After a big ___, the two friends didn't talk for a week.
kahoot.explain: argument — janjal, bahs.

kahoot.q: After the argument, they finally ___ and became friends again.
kahoot.explain: reconcile — yarashmoq. betray — xiyonat qilmoq.

kahoot.q: He told her secret to everyone. It was a ___.
kahoot.explain: betrayal — xiyonat. loyalty — sadoqat (antonim).

kahoot.q: Losing the final was a ___, but she came back stronger.
kahoot.explain: setback — muvaffaqiyatsizlik, orqaga ketish. comeback — qaytish.

kahoot.q: A friend who tells you the truth, even when it is hard, shows ___.
kahoot.explain: honesty — rostgo'ylik. jealousy — hasad.

kahoot.q: The difference between what men and women earn is the pay ___.
kahoot.explain: pay gap — maosh tafovuti.

kahoot.q: Someone from a poor family with few chances in life is ___.
kahoot.explain: underprivileged — imkoniyati cheklangan, kambag'al.

kahoot.q: 'Close friend' ma'nosi?
kahoot.explain: close friend — yaqin do'st; acquaintance esa shunchaki tanish.

timeline: Salomlashish
Telefonlar test uchun yig'iladi. Kirish savoli: "Would you like to travel to space?" — 2 o'quvchi javob beradi.
TAKROR: Kahoot — 20-dars (Phrasal verbs — GET)
'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi → 20-dars savollari (20 ta). Bugungi darsning Kahooti bu yerda EMAS — u 22-darsda o'ynaladi. Oxirgi 1 daqiqa: eng ko'p xato qilingan 2 savol izohi.
TAKROR: Yozma normativ — Essential Words 20 (Relationships, social life and resilience)

Normativ — belgilangan vaqtda bajariladigan qisqa o'lchov; natijasiga qarab coin beriladi. 20-dars CORE 20: ustoz o'zbekchasini aytadi, o'quvchi inglizchasini yozadi — 4 daq; 1 daq sherik bilan almashib tekshirish. 18–20 = 2 coin; 15–17 = bajarildi; 14 va kam = 22-darsda qayta topshiradi.
PROGRESS TEST 4 (pt4) — 16–20-darslar

Test: tests/pt4 (tizim). Bo'limlar va ballar: A. Grammatika 15 (10 daq) · B. Lug'at 10 (5 daq) · C. Reading 8 (10 daq) · D. Listening 5 (5 daq, ustoz 2 marta o'qiydi) · E. Writing 12 (10 daq, W-4.0) = 50 ball; o'tish — jami ≥ 70% va har bo'limda ≥ 50%. Telefonlar yig'iladi; javoblar test paytida ko'rsatilmaydi; natija tahlili 22-darsda.
YANGI GRAMMATIKA — Phrasal verbs TAKE + CCQ

Lead-in (2 daq): "The plane took off. He took off his jacket." — bir fe'l, ikki ma'no → formula proyektorda (formulas 1–6, 7 daq) → 2–3 misol (presentation) → CCQ (4 daq) → olmosh o'rni: take it off, lekin take after him (2 daq) → 1 daq tez og'zaki tekshiruv. ZAXIRA fe'llar (formulas 7) — faqat vaqt qolsa.
LUG'AT — Essential Words 21 CORE 20

Ustoz 20 so'zni proyektorda talaffuz + tarjima bilan o'qitadi (2 daq); qiyin so'zlarga CCQ/misol — orbit, gravity, atmosphere (2 daq); juftlikda A o'zbekchasini, B inglizchasini aytadi (2 daq). Flashcard — uyga.
Kombinatsiya — take + zarracha → ma'no → gap

Kombinatsiya — juftlikda formula → gap → tarjima zanjiri: A formulani yoki o'zbekcha gapni aytadi, B shu formula bilan inglizcha gap tuzib tarjima qiladi, keyin almashadi. 1 daq — ustoz grammar.formulas dan formulani va 1 misolni proyektorda ko'rsatadi; 2 daq — juftlikda (me'yor normativ[1] da); ustoz 2 juftlikni tinglaydi.
SINF MASHQLARI — Ex1–Ex3 (MAJBURIY) + ZAXIRA
Ex1 5 daq yakka · Ex2 5 daq juftlik · Ex3 4 daq yakka · 2 daq — kalit proyektorda. ZAXIRA — vaqt qolsa: Xatoni toping (paragraf).
WRITING — Studying abroad

LISTENING — IELTS Part 2

2 daq — ustoz yozib borgan 3 ta xato doskada, o'quvchilar tuzatadi (error log); 3 daq — uyga vazifa: 1–4 majburiy (3 — reading uyga, kaliti 22-darsda; 4 — 'Studying abroad' inshosi, 40 daq, 220–260 so'z), 5–7 qo'shimcha. Vaqt yetmasa: ZAXIRA mashqlar va reading'ning 'find' topshirig'i uyga o'tadi.

intro: ASOSIY 8 (Kahoot, test va normativga kiradi): take off (uchmoq; yechmoq), take up (boshlamoq), take after (o'xshamoq), take over (boshqaruvni olmoq), take on (zimmaga olmoq; ishga olmoq), take back (qaytarib olib bormoq; gapidan qaytmoq), take care of (qaramoq), take part in (qatnashmoq).
AJRALADI: take off / up / over / on / back. Ot ikki joyda ham turadi (take off your jacket = take your jacket off), olmosh faqat o'rtada: take it off.
AJRALMAYDI: take after + shaxs (take after him), take care of + ob'ekt (take care of it), take part in + tadbir (take part in it).
take up + ot yoki V-ing: take up yoga / take up swimming (take up to swim — xato).
ZAXIRA — formulas 7 dagi fe'llar (vaqt qolsa; Kahoot, test, normativga kirmaydi).
formulas: take off (2 ma'no)
samolyot/raketa + take off; take off + kiyim (take it off)
The plane took off at 3 p.m. / He took off his jacket. → He took it off.
Samolyot soat 3 da havoga ko'tarildi. / U kurtkasini yechdi. → U uni yechdi.
take up
take up + sport/hobbi (ot yoki V-ing)
I took up yoga last year. / She took up swimming at twelve.
O'tgan yili yoga bilan shug'ullana boshladim. / U o'n ikki yoshida suzishni boshladi.
take after
S + take after + oila a'zosi (ajralmaydi)
He takes after his father — they are both quiet.
U otasiga o'xshaydi — ikkalasi ham kamgap.
take over / take on
take over + kompaniya/boshqaruv; take on + ish/mas'uliyat/xodim
His daughter took over the company in 2020. / She took on too much work. / We're taking on new staff.
Kompaniya boshqaruvini 2020-yilda qizi o'z qo'liga oldi. / U juda ko'p ishni zimmasiga oldi. / Yangi xodimlarni ishga olyapmiz.
take back
take + narsa + back (to …); take back + gap
I took the shoes back to the shop. / I take back what I said.
Poyabzalni do'konga qaytarib olib bordim. / Aytgan gapimni qaytib olaman.
take care of / take part in
take care of + shaxs/narsa; take part in + tadbir (ajralmaydi)
She takes care of her little brother after school. / Over 200 students took part in the science fair.
U maktabdan keyin ukasiga qaraydi. / Ilmiy ko'rgazmada 200 dan ortiq o'quvchi qatnashdi.
ZAXIRA: take in / to / through / down + iboralar
take in + ma'lumot; take to + narsa; take + kimni + through; take down; take for granted
I couldn't take in what he said. / She took to flying at once. / She took down the notes. / Don't take your parents for granted.
Uning aytganini tushunolmadim. / U uchishni darhol yoqtirib qoldi. / U yozib oldi. / Ota-onangning qadriga yet.
presentation: When did Apollo 11 take off?
It took off from Florida on 16 July 1969.
Why did NASA take Armstrong on?
NASA took him on as an astronaut in 1962 because he was an experienced test pilot.
What did Armstrong do when the autopilot was heading for rocks?
He took over and landed the lunar module himself.
Who do you take after — your mother or your father?
I take after my mother: we both love reading.
CCQ: He took over the company.
Did he start it? (No) Is he the boss now? (Yes)
CCQ: She took on too much work.
Did she agree to do the work? (Yes) Is she very busy now? (Yes) Did she become the boss? (No)
CCQ: I take after my grandfather.
Are we similar? (Yes) Is he older than me? (Yes) Did I choose to be like him? (No, not really)
CCQ: The plane took off. / He took off his coat.
Is the plane in the air now? (Yes) Is he wearing his coat now? (No)
notes: take up + V-ing/ot: "take up swimming" (take up to swim — xato).
take on ↔ take over: take on — ishni, mas'uliyatni yoki xodimni qabul qilmoq; take over — boshqaruvni boshqa kishidan o'z qo'liga olmoq.
O'quvchi so'raydi: Nega "take off it" emas, "take it off"? — Javob: ajraladigan phrasal verbda olmosh (it, them, him) fe'l bilan zarracha o'rtasida turadi; ot bo'lsa ikki joyda ham bo'ladi.
O'quvchi so'raydi: Unda nega "take after him", "take him after" emas? — Javob: take after ajralmaydi — ob'ekt, olmosh bo'lsa ham, zarrachadan keyin keladi.
mistakes: He takes after to his father.
She took over too much work.
She took on too much work.

class_ex.title: Progress Test 4 (16–20-darslar): ustoz uchun o'tkazish tartibi va ball jadvali
class_ex.instr: Test 40 daqiqa, 50 ball, 5 bo'lim: A. Grammatika 15 · B. Lug'at 10 · C. Reading 8 · D. Listening 5 · E. Writing 12. Qamrov — faqat 16–20-darslar: reported speech (darak gaplar — zamon siljishi, say/tell; savollar — if/whether va wh-so'z + darak tartibi; buyruq/iltimos/maslahat — told/asked/advised + O + (not) to V1, suggested + V-ing); LOOK va GET phrasal verblari (faqat asosiy fe'llar); Essential Words 16–20 CORE. ZAXIRA birliklar (masalan look over / look around / look back on, get by / get away with / get down to) testga kirmaydi.
items: 1. Dars oldidan: har o'quvchiga A–E bo'limli varaqdan 1 nusxa chop eting (C bo'lim matni varaqning o'zida; E bo'lim uchun 10–12 qator chiziqli joy qoldiring). Kalit, Listening skripti va rubrika o'quvchiga berilmaydi va proyektorga chiqarilmaydi. Listening skriptini oldindan 1 marta ovoz chiqarib o'qib chiqing: ikkala rolni o'zingiz o'qiysiz — ASSISTANT va STUDENT rollarini ovoz ohangi yoki turish joyini o'zgartirib ajrating (yoki STUDENT rolini oldindan tayyorlangan boshqa guruh o'quvchisi/hamkasb o'qiydi).

2. 21-dars tartibi: Salomlashish (3 daq) → TAKROR: Kahoot — 20-dars (8 daq) → TAKROR: Yozma normativ — Essential Words 20 (5 daq) → PROGRESS TEST 4 (40 daq, darsning 17–56-daqiqalari). Test oldidan telefonlar, lug'at va daftarlar yig'iladi; o'quvchilar alohida o'tiradi; varaqlar yuzini pastga qilib tarqatiladi; proyektorga faqat taymer (40:00) chiqariladi.

3. Vaqt (ustoz ovoz chiqarib e'lon qiladi, har bo'lim tugashidan 1 daqiqa oldin ogohlantiradi): 0–10 — A. Grammatika; 10–15 — B. Lug'at; 15–25 — C. Reading; 25–30 — D. Listening; 30–40 — E. Writing. A–C ni erta tugatgan o'quvchi E ga o'tishi mumkin, lekin D hamma uchun bir vaqtda — 25:00 da.

4. D. Listening (25:00–30:00): 'Pens down' deysiz; 30 soniya — o'quvchilar formani o'qiydi; skriptni odatiy tezlikda 1-marta o'qiysiz (≈ 1.5 daq); 20 soniya pauza; 2-marta o'qiysiz; 30 soniya — javoblarni tekshirish. Skript ekranga chiqarilmaydi, so'zlar alohida takrorlanmaydi va tushuntirilmaydi; familiyani skriptdagidek harfma-harf aytasiz.

5. Test paytida mazmunga oid savollarga javob bermang (faqat topshiriq tushunarsiz bo'lsa, qavsdagi o'zbekcha ko'rsatmani qayta o'qib bering). Gaplashish yoki ko'chirishni ko'rsangiz — 1 marta ogohlantiring; takrorlansa varaqni yig'ib oling va holatni varaq ustiga yozing.
6. 40:00 da varaqlar yig'iladi. Javoblar test kuni aytilmaydi va ko'rsatilmaydi; darsning qolgan qismi (Phrasal verbs — TAKE) odatdagidek davom etadi.

7. Tekshirish (48 soat ichida): A — har savol 1 yoki 0 (9–12: kalitdagi yoki kalitda ko'rsatilgan muqobil shakl, imlo xatosiz; 12 — faqat 'over'; 13–15: xato topilib, to'g'ri tuzatilgan bo'lsa 1; faqat belgilangan, tuzatilmagan — 0). B — 1 / 0.5 (ma'noni buzmaydigan bitta harf imlo xatosi) / 0. C — har savol 1 yoki 0 (5–8: 2 so'zdan ko'p yoki matndagi so'z emas — 0; 1–4: TRUE/FALSE/NOT GIVEN o'rniga YES/NO — 0). D — har bo'shliq 1 yoki 0 (1 — familiya harfma-harf to'g'ri bo'lishi shart; 2 — 24 / twenty-four; 4 — faqat raqam bilan: 15,000 / 15000; 'fifteen thousand' (ikki so'z) — bu testda istisno sifatida 1 ball, lekin 22-dars tahlilida raqam bilan yozish shartligi tushuntiriladi). E — W-4.0 rubrikasi, 4 mezon × 0–3 = 12; so'zlarni sanang: 70 so'zdan kam — TR maksimal 1 ball.

8. Bo'lim chegaralari (50%): A ≥ 8/15, B ≥ 5/10, C ≥ 4/8, D ≥ 3/5, E ≥ 6/12. Natijani tizimga bo'limlar kesimida (A, B, C, D, E + jami) kiriting. 22-darsda — PT4 NATIJA TAHLILI (8 daq): varaqlar qaytariladi, eng ko'p uchragan 5 xato doskada juftlikda tuzatiladi, 70% dan past olganlar ro'yxati va qayta topshirish sanasi aytiladi.
class_ex.answers: BALL → NATIJA → KEYINGI QADAM (jami 50 ball). (1) Jami 35–50 (≥ 70%) VA har bo'lim chegarada (A ≥ 8, B ≥ 5, C ≥ 4, D ≥ 3, E ≥ 6) → O'TDI → kurs odatdagidek davom etadi; 45–50 (90%+) — 5 coin, 40–44.5 (80–89%) — 3 coin. (2) Jami 30–34.5 (60–69%) YOKI jami ≥ 30 bo'lib, bir yoki bir necha bo'lim chegaradan past → SHARTLI → o'sha bo'lim(lar) (jami 60–69% bo'lsa — eng past 1–2 bo'lim) bo'yicha 15 daqiqalik qayta topshirish keyingi 2 dars ichida, dars vaqtidan tashqari (ustoz shu bo'lim formatida, 16–20-darslarning asosiy — ZAXIRA bo'lmagan — materialidan yangi savollar beradi); qayta topshirilgan bo'lim(lar) bilan qayta hisoblangan natija jami ≥ 35 (≥ 70%) va har bo'lim chegarada bo'lsa → O'TDI. (3) Jami 0–29.5 (< 60%) → O'TMADI → ota-onaga xabar beriladi, eng zaif bo'lim(lar) bo'yicha 1 qo'shimcha (remedial) mashg'ulot o'tkaziladi (masalan A past — reported speech jadvali: zamon siljishi, savol tartibi, to / not to; LOOK va GET asosiy fe'llari; C past — TRUE/FALSE/NOT GIVEN strategiyasi), keyin qayta topshirish. Barcha natijalar (asosiy va qayta) tizimga bo'limlar kesimida kiritiladi.
class_ex.note: Test uchun 40 daqiqa 21-dars rejasining o'zidan olingan: Writing (12 daq) va Reading (13 daq) shu darsda uyga o'tadi, uy vazifasi tekshiruvi (3 daq) bu darsda o'tkazilmaydi, qolgan bosqichlar biroz qisqartirilgan (Grammatika 16, Lug'at 6, Kombinatsiya 3, Sinf mashqlari 16, Salomlashish 3, Xatolar/uyga 5). 21-dars test oldidan 20-dars Kahooti bilan boshlanadi, shuning uchun GET savollari (8, 12, 15) Kahootdagi gaplardan boshqa kontekstda berilgan: 8 — poyezd yo'lovchilari (Kahootda — avtobus), 12 — ayriliqni yengish (Kahootda — gripp), 15 — eski daftarlar (Kahootda — eski divan). 10 (B) — aka-uka va idish yuvish (Kahootda — ikki do'st).

items: 1. "I am moving to Samarkand next year," Aziz said. → Aziz said he ___ to Samarkand the following year. A) is moving  B) was moving  C) has moved  D) moves
2. My sister ___ me that she had passed her driving test. A) said  B) told  C) spoke  D) asked

7. Could you ___ my cat while I'm on holiday? She needs food twice a day. A) look after  B) look for  C) look into  D) look up
8. The train stopped at Bukhara station, and all the passengers got ___ the train with their bags. A) out  B) off  C) over  D) away
9. "Are you ready for the match?" the coach asked. → The coach asked us ___ we were ready for the match.

answers: 1. B — was moving (16-dars: Present Continuous → Past Continuous; next year → the following year).
2. B — told (16-dars: tell + KIMGA; said me — xato).
3. B — if I lived (17-dars: Yes/No savol → if/whether + ega + fe'l, do tushadi). 'whether I lived' ham to'g'ri, lekin variantlarda yo'q.
4. B — I had bought (17-dars: wh-so'z + darak tartibi; Past Simple → Past Perfect).
5. C — not to touch (18-dars: taqiq — told + O + not to + V1).
6. B — practising (18-dars: suggest + V-ing; suggested us to — xato).
7. A — look after (19-dars: look after — g'amxo'rlik qilmoq, qaramoq).
8. B — off (20-dars: poyezd/avtobusdan tushmoq — get off; 'got out' bo'lsa 'of' kerak bo'lardi — got out of the train, shuning uchun A — xato).
9. if / whether (17-dars: Yes/No savol → if yoki whether; ikkalasi ham 1 ball).
10. to drink (18-dars: advise + O + to + V1). 'drink' yoki 'drinking' — 0.
11. seeing (19-dars: look forward to + V-ing). 'see' / 'to see' — 0.

12. over (20-dars: get over + ayriliq — yengib o'tmoq; never got over — hech qachon o'ziga kelolmadi). Faqat 'over' — 1 ball; 'through' — 0 (get through — qiyin davrni boshidan o'tkazmoq, 'never got through the death' tabiiy emas); 'rid of' — 0 (ma'no buziladi, ikki so'z).
13. will help → WOULD help (16-dars: said + will → would; va'da o'tmishda qolgan — but she never did).
14. look up it → look IT UP (19-dars: olmosh ajraladigan fe'lning o'rtasida).
15. got rid his → got rid OF his (20-dars: get rid of + ot — qutulmoq; 'of' shart).

box: A. When the robotics club at School No. 21 in Namangan entered its first national competition three years ago, it finished last out of forty teams. The club's teacher, Mr Karimov, said later that the students had been talented but had not worked as a team. "Everyone wanted to be the leader," he explained, "and nobody wanted to listen."

B. The next year, Mr Karimov changed the way the club worked. He asked the students to choose a new captain every month, so that everyone could learn something about leadership. He also told them to write down every decision in a shared notebook. At first, some students complained that the notebook wasted time. However, it soon became clear that it helped the team remember why each decision had been made.

C. The biggest change was in communication. Instead of arguing about whose idea was the best, the students met every Friday to give each other feedback. Mr Karimov advised them not to criticise a person, only an idea. One student, Nilufar, remembers that she had been too shy to speak at the first meetings. By the end of the year, she was presenting the team's robot to the judges.

D. Last spring, the team returned to the national competition. Their robot was not the fastest, and it broke down during the second round. But the team repaired it in eight minutes, and the judges said they had never seen such calm cooperation under pressure. The club won the prize for the best teamwork and finished fourth overall.
E. Mr Karimov says the result was not a surprise. When a journalist asked him what the secret was, he said that a team did not need a star; it needed people who trusted each other.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn; maktab va qahramonlar to'qima.)
items: 1. The robotics club finished in last place in its first national competition.

items: 1. In many countries, teenagers now spend more time with their friends than with their families. Is this a positive or negative development?

2. Checklist: topic sentence bor; izoh + aniq misol; kamida 2 bog'lovchi (because, as a result, for example, however); 16–20-darslar strukturasidan 1–2 tasi (reported speech — told me that…, asked…; get along with, look up to…) tabiiy joyda; 80–100 so'z.
answers: NAMUNA (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6, 93 so'z): In my view, spending more time with friends is mostly a positive development, because teenagers learn important social skills outside the family. When young people get along with their peers, they learn how to cooperate, deal with arguments and show empathy. As a result, they become more confident and independent. For example, my cousin told me that his football team had taught him more about teamwork than any lesson at school. However, this does not mean that family is less important, so teenagers should still spend quality time with their parents and siblings.

Baholash: W-4.0 rubrikasi (TR, CC, LR, GRA — har biri 0–3 = 12 ball). So'z soni: 70 dan kam — TR maksimal 1 ball; savolga javob bermagan yoki mavzudan tashqari — TR 0. Struktura kvotasi yo'q — to'g'ri va tabiiy ishlatilgani GRA da hisobga olinadi.

class_ex.title: WRITING — Studying abroad (yozma): Task 2 insho — tahlil va Body 2
class_ex.instr: (10 daq, test darsi) 2 daq — savol tahlili: savol turi, kalit so'zlar, pozitsiya, nechta body; 4 daq — box dagi NAMUNA kirish + Body 1 tahlili (topic sentence, bog'lovchilar, bugungi TAKE fe'llari, EW 21 so'zlari); 4 daq — Body 2 (kamchiliklar) va xulosa REJASI daftarda: g'oya / izoh / misol jadvali, sherik bilan W-CHECK-4.0 bo'yicha solishtiriladi. Insho uyda yoziladi. ICQ: Savol nimani so'rayapti — faqat afzalliklarnimi? (Yo'q — afzallik VA kamchilik) Bugun sinfda butun insho yozamizmi? (Yo'q — faqat Body 2 va xulosa rejasi; insho uyda, 40 daqiqa)
box: Question: Many students choose to study abroad. What are the advantages and disadvantages of studying in a foreign country?

MODEL — Introduction: Every year, thousands of young people leave their home country to get a degree at a foreign university. This choice has clear benefits for their studies and their character, but it also has some serious drawbacks. In my opinion, the advantages are more important, because they last for a whole lifetime.

MODEL — Body 1: The main advantage is a better chance to explore new subjects and ideas. Many foreign universities have modern laboratories, so a future engineer, for example, can work with equipment that is not available at home. Another benefit is personal growth. Students who live abroad have to take care of themselves: they cook, pay bills and solve problems without their parents. As a result, they become more independent. Many of them also take part in clubs and projects with classmates from other countries, and their English improves very quickly.
items: Insho qolipi (advantages / disadvantages, 4 abzats): Introduction (parafraz + pozitsiya) -> Body 1: advantages -> Body 2: disadvantages -> Conclusion.
1. Savol turi qanday? Savol nechta qismdan iborat?
2. Pozitsiya kirishning qaysi gapida? Savoldagi qaysi so'zlar parafraz qilingan?
3. Body 1 da nechta afzallik bor? Qaysi gapda misol berilgan?
4. Bugungi grammatika (TAKE phrasal verbs) namunaning qayerida? Qaysi ma'noda?
5. Essential Words 21 so'zlaridan qaysilari bor?

TASK: Plan Body 2 (disadvantages) and the Conclusion — table Idea / Explain / Example for 2 disadvantages. At home: write Body 2 (60–80 words): Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link, then the full essay.
answers: Kalit 1: advantages / disadvantages — 2 qismli savol: Body 1 — afzalliklar, Body 2 — kamchiliklar; faqat bir tomon yozilsa TR ko'pi bilan 1 ball. Savol fikr so'ramaydi, lekin kirishda qaysi tomon muhimroq ekani aytilsa insho aniqroq bo'ladi.

Kalit 2: pozitsiya — 'In my opinion, the advantages are more important, because they last for a whole lifetime.'; parafraz: 'study abroad' -> 'leave their home country to get a degree at a foreign university'; 'advantages and disadvantages' -> 'clear benefits … serious drawbacks'.

Kalit 3: 2 afzallik — (1) yangi fanlarni o'rganish imkoniyati (zamonaviy laboratoriyalar); (2) shaxsiy o'sish (mustaqillik, ingliz tili). Misol — 'a future engineer, for example, can work with equipment that is not available at home.'

Kalit 4: Body 1 da 'have to take care of themselves' (take care of — o'ziga qaramoq) va 'take part in clubs and projects' (take part in — qatnashmoq). Xulosada (ustozda): 'take on this challenge' (take on — zimmaga olmoq).
Kalit 5: explore, engineer (Body 1); Body 2 da (ustozda) — risks, launch.

Body 2 REJA kaliti: Kamchilik 1 — qimmat / izoh: chipta, ijara, kontrakt to'lovi; ko'p oila to'lay olmaydi / misol: El-yurt umidi stipendiyasi bu xavfni kamaytiradi. Kamchilik 2 — yolg'izlik / izoh: oila va do'stlardan uzoqda / misol: birinchi oylarda qiyin. Xulosa: ikkala tomon qisqa + pozitsiya takrori.

NAMUNA Body 2 (faqat ustoz uchun): On the other hand, studying abroad has two disadvantages. Firstly, it is very expensive, and many families cannot pay for flights, rent and tuition fees. Secondly, students often feel lonely because they are far from their families and friends. However, these risks can be reduced. For example, Uzbek students who win the El-yurt umidi scholarship do not have to pay for their studies, and later they come back to launch new projects at home.

NAMUNA Conclusion (faqat ustoz uchun): In conclusion, studying in a foreign country can be costly and lonely, but it gives young people knowledge, independence and useful skills. For this reason, I believe the benefits are greater, and more students should take on this challenge if they have the chance.
To'liq namuna: 257 so'z (kirish 51, Body 1 88, Body 2 74, xulosa 44).
Baholash: W-4.0 — shu darsdagi E bo'lim jadvali; sinfdagi reja — W-CHECK-4.0, to'liq insho uyda W-4.0 bilan.
why: take care of: 'Students who live abroad have to take care of themselves' — 'o'zlariga o'zlari qarashlari kerak'; ajralmaydi: take care of + ob'ekt (themselves).
take part in: 'take part in clubs and projects' — 'qatnashadi'; take part in + tadbir, ajralmaydi.
take on: 'more students should take on this challenge' — 'bu sinovni zimmasiga olishi kerak' (take over emas — boshqaruvni olish haqida gap yo'q).
EW 21 so'zlari: explore (tadqiq qilmoq, o'rganmoq), engineer (muhandis), risk (xavf), launch (boshlamoq, ishga tushirmoq) — koinot so'zlari ta'lim mavzusida ham ishlaydi.
Bog'lovchilar: for example, As a result, On the other hand, Firstly / Secondly, However, In conclusion — CC uchun 4+ xil.

class_ex.instr: (12 daq, yakka; vaqt qolsa yoki uyga) 2 daq — savol tahlili: savol turi (agree/disagree), kalit so'zlar, pozitsiya. 7 daq — BITTA body paragraf, 70–90 so'z: Topic sentence → Explain → Example → Link. 3 daq — juftlikda checklist bilan tekshirish; ustoz 1 paragrafni W-4.0 bo'yicha baholaydi. items: Some people think that the money spent on space exploration should be spent on solving problems on Earth instead. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Reja: Topic sentence: pozitsiya / Explain: 1 asosiy sabab / Example: aniq misol (GPS, ob-havo, kasalxona…) / Link: savolga qaytish.
Checklist: 1) topic sentence bor; 2) izoh + aniq misol; 3) kamida 2 bog'lovchi; 4) bugungi TAKE fe'llari 1–2 marta, tabiiy joyda.
answers: NAMUNA (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6): In my opinion, money spent on space exploration is not wasted, because it brings long-term benefits to people on Earth. Space research has led to many advances in technology. For example, satellites help farmers predict the weather, and GPS helps ambulances find patients quickly. Although problems such as poverty are serious, governments can fund both areas at the same time. Therefore, I believe space exploration should continue, but it should take up only a small part of the national budget.

homework.title: 4. WRITING — Studying abroad: to'liq insho (yozma, uyga)
homework.instr: MAJBURIY. 40 daqiqa taymer bilan, 220–260 so'z, 4 abzats. Sinfdagi Body 2 va xulosa rejasidan foydalaning; kirish va Body 1 ni o'z so'zlaringiz bilan yozing (namunani ko'chirmang). Bugungi TAKE fe'llaridan 2–3 marta (take part in, take up, take care of, take on), EW 21 so'zlaridan kamida 4 ta (explore, risk, launch, engineer…). Oxirida so'z sonini yozing.
items: Question: Many students choose to study abroad. What are the advantages and disadvantages of studying in a foreign country?
Introduction: savol parafrazi + pozitsiya (qaysi tomon muhimroq) — 2–3 gap.
Body 1 (advantages): 2 afzallik — Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link.
Body 2 (disadvantages): 2 kamchilik — sinfdagi reja, tuzatilgan (60–80 so'z); O'zbekistondan 1 misol.
Conclusion: ikkala tomonni boshqa so'zlar bilan qisqa takrorlang + pozitsiya — 1–2 gap.
answers:
NAMUNA (257 so'z, Band 5.5–6, Jony Academy original): Every year, thousands of young people leave their home country to get a degree at a foreign university. This choice has clear benefits for their studies and their character, but it also has some serious drawbacks. In my opinion, the advantages are more important, because they last for a whole lifetime.

The main advantage is a better chance to explore new subjects and ideas. Many foreign universities have modern laboratories, so a future engineer, for example, can work with equipment that is not available at home. Another benefit is personal growth. Students who live abroad have to take care of themselves: they cook, pay bills and solve problems without their parents. As a result, they become more independent. Many of them also take part in clubs and projects with classmates from other countries, and their English improves very quickly.

On the other hand, studying abroad has two disadvantages. Firstly, it is very expensive, and many families cannot pay for flights, rent and tuition fees. Secondly, students often feel lonely because they are far from their families and friends. However, these risks can be reduced. For example, Uzbek students who win the El-yurt umidi scholarship do not have to pay for their studies, and later they come back to launch new projects at home.

In conclusion, studying in a foreign country can be costly and lonely, but it gives young people knowledge, independence and useful skills. For this reason, I believe the benefits are greater, and more students should take on this challenge if they have the chance.

items: KARTOCHKA A: Describe a hobby you took up recently. You should say: what the hobby is ; when and why you took it up ; how often you do it ; and explain how it has changed your life.

KARTOCHKA B: Describe a family member (or another older person you know well) you take after. You should say: who this person is ; in what ways you are similar ; what you do together ; and explain how you feel about being like this person.
Part 3: Who should pay for space exploration?
Part 3: Is space exploration worth the money?
Part 3: Would you like to travel to space? Why?
answers: NAMUNA A (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6): I'd like to talk about running, a hobby I took up about six months ago. I started because I was spending too many hours at my desk. A friend who runs invited me to join her in the park. Now I run three times a week, early in the morning. At first it was hard, and I could only run for ten minutes, but I didn't give up, and last month I took part in a five-kilometre race. Now I can run for forty minutes without stopping. I didn't win, but I finished it! This hobby has changed my life: I feel healthier, I sleep better, and I've learnt that small steps every day lead to big results. I would recommend running to anyone.

NAMUNA B: I'd like to talk about my grandfather, because everyone says I take after him. He is a retired engineer. We are both tall, but the main similarity is our character: we are both patient and we love fixing things. At the weekend we often repair old radios together, and in summer I help him take care of the garden. I feel proud that I'm like him, because he is kind and hard-working.

Part 3 namuna javoblari: 1) Both governments and private companies should pay: governments can fund research, and companies can take on the cost of rockets. 2) I think it is worth the money, because it has given us weather satellites and GPS. 3) Yes, but only for a short trip — I'd love to see the Earth from above.
Baholash: S-4.0 (FC, LR, GRA, P — har biri 0–3 = 12 ball): 4 ta 'You should say' bandi aytilgan, 1.5–2 daqiqa, 1–2 ta TAKE fe'li — 2 coin; ≤6 — ustoz 1 ta maslahat yozadi.

reading.title: Neil Armstrong — the quiet man who took over at the last moment
text: A. Neil Armstrong was born in 1930 near Wapakoneta, a small farming town in Ohio, USA. When he was six, his father took him on his first aeroplane ride, and the boy took to flying at once. He took up flying at 15, paid for his lessons by working in a pharmacy, and got his student pilot's licence before his driving licence. All his life he was known as a quiet, private man.

B. He flew 78 combat missions in the Korean War and then took on one of the most dangerous jobs in aviation: test pilot. In 1962 NASA took him on as an astronaut. In 1966, on the Gemini 8 mission, a thruster stuck and the capsule began to spin faster and faster. The crew were close to blacking out, but Armstrong took over manual control and brought the spacecraft back under control.

C. On 16 July 1969, Apollo 11 took off from Florida with Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins on board. Four days later, Armstrong and Aldrin flew the lunar module, the Eagle, down towards the Moon, while Collins took care of the command module in orbit. During the landing, the computer showed an alarm, but mission control quickly told them it was safe to continue. Then Armstrong saw that the autopilot was taking them towards an area full of large rocks. He took over, flew the Eagle himself and landed with very little fuel left. Then Armstrong radioed mission control that the Eagle had landed.

D. A few hours later, he stepped onto the Moon and said the famous words, "That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind." Hundreds of millions of people watched on television. The astronauts took about 21.5 kg of Moon rocks back to Earth. Their footprints are probably still there, because there is no wind on the Moon to blow them away.

E. Armstrong did not enjoy being famous. He rarely gave interviews, took up teaching engineering at a university and later lived quietly on a farm. He often said that the success belonged to the thousands of people who had worked on the programme, not to him.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; monolog, ustoz gid rolida; raqam va tuzatishlarni aniq ayting.
Guide: Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the City Planetarium. Please take your seats.
Guide: Today's show, Journey to the Moon, used to last thirty minutes, but with our new part about Mars it now takes forty-five minutes.
Guide: You're welcome to take photos, and even videos, during the show, but please don't use flash, because it disturbs other visitors.

Guide: After the show, you can take part in a guided tour of our Apollo exhibition. The tour takes about twenty minutes — not half an hour, as some guidebooks say. We'll meet next to the gift shop — not at the main entrance, as it says on your ticket.

Guide: Now, a word for parents. If your children enjoy astronomy, they can join our Saturday club. Sessions used to start at nine, but from this month they start at ten a.m., so children can sleep a little longer.
Guide: The club costs eighty thousand soums a month. Last year it was a hundred thousand, so it's cheaper now.
Guide: Our café is on the second floor. Some people look for it on the first floor, but that's the library. Enjoy the show!
