intro: MAKE UP = (1) to'qimoq; (2) yarashmoq; (3) tashkil etmoq; (4) yetishmaganini to'ldirmoq (make up the difference).
MAKE UP FOR = qoplamoq (yo'qotilgan vaqt, xato).
MAKE OUT = zo'rg'a ko'rmoq / eshitmoq / tushunmoq. ZAXIRA: make X out to be Y — X ni Y qilib ko'rsatmoq (ko'pincha noto'g'ri).
MAKE INTO = aylantirmoq (ko'pincha passivda). ZAXIRA: make over — butunlay yangilamoq.

MAKE OF = fikr (What do you make of…?); MAKE DO WITH = bor narsa bilan qanoat qilmoq; MAKE FOR = sabab bo'lmoq / tomon yo'l olmoq. ZAXIRA: make off with — o'g'irlab qochmoq; make towards — tomon yurmoq.
formulas: make up (to'qimoq / yarashmoq)
make up + hikoya/bahona; S + make up (with KIM)
She made up a story. / They finally made up after the argument.
U hikoya to'qidi. / Ular oxiri yarashishdi.
make up (tashkil etmoq / to'ldirmoq)
X + make up + qism/foiz; make up + the difference
Students make up 70% of our customers. / Dad made up the difference.
Mijozlarimizning 70 foizini talabalar tashkil qiladi. / Yetishmaganini dadam to'ldirdi.
make up for
make up for + yo'qotish (ajralmaydi)
He worked hard to make up for lost time.
U yo'qotilgan vaqtni qoplash uchun ko'p ishladi.
make out
can't/couldn't + make out + nima (ko'rish, eshitish, o'qish)
I couldn't make out what he said. / Can you make out the sign from here?
Uning aytganini tushuna olmadim. / Bu yerdan yozuvni o'qiy olasanmi?
make into
make + X + into + Y; X + be made into + Y (passiv)
They made the garage into a studio. / The book was made into a movie.
Ular garajni studiyaga aylantirishdi. / Kitob filmga aylantirildi.
make of / make do with
What do you make of…? / make do with + narsa
What do you make of his behaviour? / We'll have to make do with what we have.
Uning xulqi haqida nima deb o'ylaysan? / Bor narsamiz bilan qanoat qilishimiz kerak.
make for
make for + natija (sabab bo'lmoq); make for + joy (tomon yo'l olmoq)
Good weather makes for a nice trip. / When the bell rang, he made for the exit.
Yaxshi ob-havo yaxshi sayohatga sabab bo'ladi. / Qo'ng'iroq chalinganda u chiqish tomon yo'l oldi.
ZAXIRA: make over / make out to be / make off with / make towards
make over + joy/narsa; make X out to be Y; make off with + o'lja; make towards + joy
They made over the old house. / He made himself out to be a hero. / The thief made off with the money. / He made towards the door.
Ular eski uyni butunlay yangilashdi. / U o'zini qahramon qilib ko'rsatdi. / O'g'ri pulni olib qochdi. / U eshik tomon yurdi.
presentation: Did Walt Disney make up Mickey Mouse on a train?
According to the famous story, yes — he made him up on the train home after losing Oswald.
What did Walt make the fairy tale "Snow White" into?
He made it into his first full-length animated film.
CCQ: He made up an excuse.
Was the excuse true? (No) Did he invent it? (Yes)
CCQ: She worked late to make up for lost time.
Did she lose time before? (Yes) Is she trying to get it back? (Yes)
CCQ: I couldn't make out the sign.
Could I see the sign? (Yes, but not clearly) Could I read it? (No)
CCQ: We made do with an old laptop.
Did we have a new laptop? (No) Was the old one perfect? (No) Did we manage? (Yes)
CCQ: What do you make of his plan?
Am I asking you to make something? (No) Am I asking for your opinion? (Yes)
notes: make up (tashkil etmoq) odatda aktivda: "Women make up half the team." Teskari yo'nalishda — be made up of (...dan iborat): "The team is made up of ten people." make up for + ot/V-ing: make up for being late.

O'quvchi so'raydi: make up for yoki make up? — Javob: yo'qotish yoki xatoni qoplash — make up FOR (make up for lost time, make up for a mistake); yetishmagan summani to'ldirish — make up the difference (for'siz).
O'quvchi so'raydi: "What do you make about…?" deyish mumkinmi? — Javob: yo'q, fikr so'rashda faqat make OF: What do you make of…? Javob: I think…

O'quvchi so'raydi: make up ni ajratish mumkinmi? — Javob: to'qimoq ma'nosida ha: make up a story / make a story up / make it up (olmosh doim o'rtada). make up for va make do with ajralmaydi: make up for it, make do with it (make up it for — xato).
mistakes: She made up with a story.
He apologised to make for his mistake.
He apologised to make up for his mistake.
Qoplamoq — make UP FOR (make for — sabab bo'lmoq / tomon yo'l olmoq).
The book was made to a movie.
The book was made into a movie.
What do you make about his plan?
What do you make of his plan?
We made do by what we had.
We made do with what we had.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Technology (og'zaki): Part 1, 2, 3
class_ex.instr: (10 daq, juftlik) 1 daq — Part 1: 4 savolga juftlikda qisqa javob (javob + sabab). 1 daq — tayyorgarlik: Kartochka A uchun faqat 5–6 kalit so'z yoziladi. 2 daq — A gapiradi, B S-CHECK-4.0 ni to'ldiradi. 2 daq — ustoz NAMUNA A ni o'qiydi, o'quvchilar box'dagi iboralarni eshitganda belgilaydi. 2 daq — B shu kartochkada gapiradi (box'dan kamida 2 ibora bilan). 1 daq — Part 3 juftlikda: fikr + sabab + misol. 1 daq — ustoz 1 ta umumiy feedback (S-4.0). ICQ: Necha daqiqa tayyorlanasiz? (1) Box'dan nechta ibora ishlatasiz? (kamida 2)
items: Part 1: How often do you use your phone?
Part 1: What do you use the internet for?
Part 1: Is there any technology you can't live without?
Part 1: Did you use computers at primary school?
KARTOCHKA A: Describe a piece of technology you use every day. You should say: what it is ; when you got it ; what you use it for ; and explain how your life would be different without it.
Part 3: Has technology made our lives easier or more stressful?
Part 3: At what age should children get a smartphone?
Part 3: Will computers replace teachers in the future?
box: It's a … that I use every single day.
I got it … years ago, when I started …
I mostly use it for …: I …, … and …
You can hardly make out … because …
Without it, I would have to make do with …
My life would be much harder / slower without it.
It isn't just a machine; it's my main tool for …
answers: 1) Honestly, many times a day — mostly to message my friends and check my homework. But I try not to use it during lessons, because it is really distracting.
2) Mainly for studying and entertainment. For example, I watch IELTS lessons on YouTube, and before I buy something, I look at a few online shops to compare prices.
3) Probably my headphones. I listen to podcasts on the way to school, and without them the bus ride would feel much longer.
4) Yes, but not very often. We had a computer class once a week, and we mostly learned to type and draw simple pictures.

NAMUNA A (Band 5.5–6, 172 so'z, ~1.5–2 daqiqa, faqat ustoz uchun): I'd like to talk about my laptop, which I use every single day. It's a grey, slightly old laptop of a well-known Asian brand, and you can hardly make out the logo on it now because I use it so much. I got it two years ago, when I started preparing for IELTS. My parents bought it second-hand from a small computer shop in our neighbourhood, and the owner was very friendly and even installed all the programs for free. I use it mostly for studying: I watch video lessons, write essays and do online tests. In the evenings I also edit short videos for my cousin's start-up, a small cake business, and she pays me a little, which is nice. Without it, my life would be much harder. I would have to make do with my phone, which has a tiny screen, and I would spend hours in the library. So for me this laptop isn't just a machine; it's my main tool for studying and for earning my first money.

1) I think it has made life easier in most ways, because people can pay, study and shop from home. However, many people feel stressed because they get messages all day, so they need to switch off their phones sometimes.
2) In my view, about twelve or thirteen is a sensible age. Younger children can make do with a simple phone for calls, and parents should control how much time they spend on screens.

3) I don't think so. Computers can give information and check tests, but students also need a real person who motivates them. For example, a good teacher notices when a student is worried and helps them.
why: Bugungi grammatika (MAKE phrasal verbs): can hardly make out the logo — zo'rg'a ko'rinadi/o'qiladi; make do with my phone — telefon bilan qanoat qilmoq; Part 3: make do with a simple phone.
EW 22 so'zlari NAMUNA A da: brand — brend; logo — logotip; owner — (do'kon) egasi; start-up — startap.
Part 3 javoblari 3 qismli: fikr + sabab + misol (I think … because … For example, …).
class_ex.note: S-CHECK-4.0: 1) kartochkaning 4 bandi aytildimi; 2) 1.5 daqiqadan uzoq, uzun pauzasiz; 3) box'dan 2+ ibora; 4) MAKE phrasal verb 1–2 marta to'g'ri; 5) Part 3: fikr + sabab + misol. Ustoz 3–4 o'quvchini S-4.0 bo'yicha jurnalga qayd etadi. Kuchsiz: Kartochka A ni box iboralari bilan 1 daqiqa; Kuchli: + Part 3 ga qarshi fikr (On the other hand, …). class_ex.instr: (15 daq) 3 daq — savol tahlili: savol turi (positive or negative development), kalit so'zlar, bitta aniq pozitsiya. 5 daq — box dagi NAMUNA kirish va Body 1 ni proyektorda tahlil qilamiz: topic sentence, bog'lovchilar, MAKE phrasal verb, EW 22 so'zlari. 5 daq — yakka Body 2 (60–80 so'z): salbiy tomon + unga javob. 2 daq — sherik bilan almashib W-CHECK-4.0 bo'yicha tekshirasiz. ICQ: Pozitsiya nechta bo'ladi? (bitta — mostly positive) Body 2 da nima haqida yozasiz va necha so'z? (salbiy tomon va unga javob, 60–80 so'z)
box: Question: Online shopping is replacing traditional shopping. Is this a positive or negative development?

MODEL — Introduction: Nowadays, more and more people buy clothes, food and electronics through apps instead of visiting shops and bazaars. Although this change has some drawbacks, I believe it is mostly a positive development for both buyers and sellers.

MODEL — Body 1: The main advantage of online shopping is that it gives customers more choice and saves their time. In the past, people in small towns often had to make do with whatever the nearest shop sold. Today, they can order almost anything from home and compare offers from many competitors, so prices usually go down. Online shopping is also good for small sellers. For example, a woman in Namangan who sews children's clothes at home can now become the owner of a small online shop and sell to customers all over Uzbekistan. As a result, she earns a steady profit and even employs two neighbours.
items: Savol turi qanday? Necha body kerak va har birida nima bo'ladi?
Pozitsiya (asosiy javob) kirishning qaysi gapida?
Bugungi grammatika qayerda? Body 1 dan MAKE phrasal verbni toping va ma'nosini ayting.
Qaysi EW 22 (Business, entrepreneurship) so'zlari ishlatilgan?
Body 1 dagi o'zbek misoli qaysi va u qaysi fikrni isbotlaydi?
TASK: Write Body 2 (60–80 words) about the negative side and your answer to it: Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link. Ideas: traditional bazaars / product quality / sellers going online.
answers: 1) Positive or negative development — bitta pozitsiya (mostly positive). Body 1 — ijobiy tomon (xaridor va kichik sotuvchi uchun), Body 2 — salbiy tomon + unga javob (muammoni hal qilsa bo'ladi).
2) Kirishning 2-gapi: 'Although this change has some drawbacks, I believe it is mostly a positive development for both buyers and sellers.'

3) had to make do with whatever the nearest shop sold — bor narsa bilan qanoat qilmoq (Body 1); Body 2 da yana: make out the real quality (aniq ko'rmoq), make up for the smaller number of visitors (qoplamoq).
4) EW 22: customers, competitors, owner, profit (Body 1); xulosada: consumer demand, market.
5) Namanganlik ayol uyda bolalar kiyimi tikib, onlayn do'kon egasi bo'ladi — onlayn savdo kichik sotuvchilarga ham foydali degan fikrni isbotlaydi.

NAMUNA Body 2 + Conclusion (faqat ustoz uchun): However, this trend also has a negative side. Traditional bazaars, such as Chorsu in Tashkent, are losing visitors, and some sellers there earn less than before. In addition, it is sometimes hard to make out the real quality of a product from a photo. Yet these problems can be solved. Many bazaar traders have already opened online pages, and these orders make up for the smaller number of visitors. / In conclusion, although online shopping creates difficulties for some traditional sellers, its benefits for customers and small businesses are greater. As long as consumer demand for fast and convenient shopping keeps growing, this development will remain mostly positive for the market.
To'liq namuna: 251 so'z (kirish 37 · Body 1 104 · Body 2 69 · xulosa 41).
why: Bugungi grammatika: make do with (ajralmaydi: make do with whatever…), make out (can't/hard to make out + nima), make up for (ajralmaydi: make up for the smaller number…). O'quvchi o'z Body 2 sida kamida 1 tasini ishlatsin.
EW 22 so'zlari: customer — mijoz; competitor — raqobatchi; owner — egasi; profit — foyda; consumer demand — iste'molchi talabi; market — bozor.
Pozitsiya bitta va xulosagacha saqlanadi: Body 2 salbiy tomonni tan oladi, lekin 'Yet these problems can be solved' bilan pozitsiyaga qaytadi — TR uchun 3 ball shu.
O'zbek misollari: Namangandagi uy tikuvchisi va Toshkentdagi Chorsu bozori — aniq, mahalliy misol TR va CC uchun ball beradi.

I found it last year, when our teacher asked everyone to install it for homework. At first I thought it was just another app, but I quickly changed my mind. I use it almost every day, usually on the bus or before bed. I review flashcards with new words, do short grammar tests and record my speaking homework. The app shows my results, so I can see which words I keep forgetting. When I miss a lesson, I use the materials there to make up for it. Why is it useful? Firstly, it saves time, because everything is in one place. Secondly, studying feels like a game: I collect coins for good results, and that motivates me a lot.

reading.title: Walt Disney — the man who made a cartoon mouse into an empire
text: A. Walt Disney was born in Chicago in 1901 and spent part of his childhood on a farm in Missouri, where he loved drawing the animals. According to a well-known story, a newspaper editor once fired him because he "lacked imagination". In the early 1920s he started a small studio in Kansas City, Laugh-O-Gram, but it soon went bankrupt. For a while he had to make do with almost nothing. Finally, he sold his camera and bought a one-way train ticket to Hollywood.

B. There, with his brother Roy, he started again, and his cartoon character Oswald the Lucky Rabbit became popular. In 1928 Walt travelled to New York to ask his distributor for more money. Instead, he learned that he did not own the rights to Oswald, and that most of his animators had agreed to work for the distributor. According to the famous story, Walt made up a new character on the long train home: a mouse. He wanted to call him Mortimer, but his wife suggested Mickey.

C. To make up for losing Oswald, Walt gave Mickey something that was still very new in cartoons: synchronised sound. "Steamboat Willie" opened in November 1928, and audiences loved hearing Mickey whistle. Sound, music and a likeable hero made for a huge success.

D. His biggest risk came next. No Hollywood studio had ever made a full-length animated film, so when Walt decided to make the fairy tale "Snow White" into one, many people called the project "Disney's folly". The film went far over budget, and Walt had to borrow money from a bank to make up the difference. When "Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs" opened in 1937, it became a huge hit. Later the Academy gave him a special Oscar for it: one full-size statue and seven small ones.

E. In 1955 Walt opened Disneyland. He took the idea of a noisy fairground and made it into a clean, safe park for whole families. He won 26 Oscars, more than any other person, and after losing Oswald he always tried to keep control of his characters. What would he make of today's Disney, which owns Pixar, Marvel and Star Wars? He would probably not be surprised.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

tasks.instr: Matnga ko'ra har bayonot TRUE, FALSE yoki NOT GIVEN.
items: Walt Disney spent some of his early years in the countryside.
Walt's first studio in Kansas City made a lot of money.
Roy Disney drew the first Oswald cartoons.
Mortimer was Walt's first choice of name for the mouse.
Walt paid for "Snow White" without borrowing any money.
Tickets to Disneyland cost more than tickets to other parks.
why: A: 'spent part of his childhood on a farm in Missouri'.
A: 'it soon went bankrupt'.
B: Roy bilan qayta boshlagani aytilgan, lekin kim chizgani aytilmagan.
B: 'He wanted to call him Mortimer, but his wife suggested Mickey'.
D: 'had to borrow money from a bank to make up the difference'.
E: chipta narxlari haqida ma'lumot yo'q.

tasks.title: Sentence completion — NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS
tasks.instr: Har bo'shliqqa matndan ko'pi bilan 2 so'z yozing.
items: Before he moved to Hollywood, Walt sold his ___.
In New York Walt learned that he did not own the ___ to Oswald.
In "Steamboat Willie", audiences loved hearing Mickey ___.
Many people called the "Snow White" project "___".

tasks.title: ZAXIRA: Matndan MAKE phrasal verblarini toping
tasks.instr: Matndan 5 ta gapni toping va yozing.
items: make do with (A)
make up — to'qimoq (B)
make up for (C)
make up — yetishmaganini to'ldirmoq (D)
make into (E)
answers: For a while he had to make do with almost nothing.
Walt made up a new character on the long train home.
To make up for losing Oswald, Walt gave Mickey … synchronised sound.
Walt had to borrow money from a bank to make up the difference.
He took the idea of a noisy fairground and made it into a clean, safe park.

listening.audios: Audio fayl yo'q — ustoz transcript'ni 2 marta o'qiydi (Jony Academy skripti; kitobdagi Audio 111–115 bu darsda ishlatilmaydi).
intro: You will hear a tutor talking to two students about their plan for a school business.
1-tinglash: bo'shliqlarni to'ldiring; 2-tinglash: javoblarni tekshiring.
Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

tasks.title: Note completion — ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER
tasks.instr: Suhbat bo'yicha 8 ta bo'shliqni to'ldiring.
items: Business idea: a school ___ run by students
Number of students asked: ___
Money needed to start: ___ million sums
Equipment: ___
The rest of the money: from a ___ sale
Expected customers during exam week: ___ a day
Share of profit for the library: ___ per cent
Opening time: at ___

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; 1-rol — ustoz (Tutor), 2- va 3-rol — ikki kuchli o'quvchi (Student A, Student B) (yoki ovozni o'zgartiring). IELTS Part 3.
Tutor: Right, let's hear about your business project. What's your idea?
Student A: We want to open a café in the school, run by students. We'd make up the menu ourselves — mostly sandwiches and fruit juice.
Tutor: Sounds good. Why a café and not a shop?
Student B: We asked 120 students — sorry, 150 — and most of them said they wanted somewhere to sit and eat.
Tutor: And how much money do you need to start?
Student A: About three million sums. We can make do with second-hand equipment, so we don't need to buy a new fridge.
Tutor: Where will the money come from?
Student B: Our parents will lend us two million, and we'll make up the difference with a cake sale.
Tutor: What if you lose money in the first month?
Student A: Normally we expect about 80 customers a day, but during exam week it should be around 200. Those busy days would make up for a slow start.
Tutor: What does the director make of your idea?
Student B: She likes it, but she has one condition: thirty per cent of the profit must go to the library.
Tutor: Twenty or thirty?
Student B: Thirty. Oh, and we can only open in the afternoon — no, sorry, at lunchtime, from twelve to two.
Tutor: Fine. Send me your business plan by Friday.

kahoot.q: She didn't want to go, so she made ___ an excuse.
kahoot.explain: make up — to'qib chiqarmoq (hikoya, bahona): made up an excuse.

kahoot.q: He worked at weekends to make up ___ lost time.
kahoot.explain: make up FOR — qoplamoq (yo'qotilgan narsani).

kahoot.q: It was dark and I couldn't make ___ the number on the bus.
kahoot.explain: make out — zo'rg'a ko'rib/eshitib tushunmoq.

kahoot.q: Her first novel was made ___ a film.
kahoot.explain: make X INTO Y — aylantirmoq: was made into a film.

kahoot.q: What do you make ___ his new business plan?
kahoot.explain: What do you make OF…? — …haqida nima deb o'ylaysan?

kahoot.q: We had no sugar, so we had to make do ___ honey.
kahoot.explain: make do WITH — bor narsa bilan qanoat qilmoq.

kahoot.q: We were 20 dollars short, so my dad made ___ the difference.
kahoot.explain: make up the difference — yetishmaganini to'ldirmoq (for'siz). make up FOR — yo'qotishni qoplamoq.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: The story wasn't true — she made up it.
The story wasn't true — she made it up.
The story wasn't true — she made up the whole thing.
They made up after the argument.
kahoot.explain: Ajraladigan fe'lda olmosh (it/them) o'rtada keladi: made it up. made up it — xato; ot bo'lsa ikkala tartib ham to'g'ri: made up the story / made the story up.

kahoot.q: Long queues don't make ___ a pleasant day out.
kahoot.explain: make for — sabab bo'lmoq, olib kelmoq: Long queues don't make for a pleasant day out.

kahoot.q: 'make up' qaysi ma'noni BILDIRMAYDI?
kahoot.explain: O'g'irlab qochmoq — make off with. make up: to'qimoq, yarashmoq, tashkil etmoq, yetishmaganini to'ldirmoq (make up the difference).

kahoot.q: Women make ___ more than half of the company's staff.
kahoot.explain: make up — tashkil etmoq (qism/foiz): Students make up 70% of…

kahoot.q: The two friends argued, but they made ___ the next day.
kahoot.explain: make up — yarashmoq: They made up the next day.

kahoot.q: The person who starts a company is its ___.
kahoot.explain: founder — asoschi. investor — sarmoyador (pul tikuvchi).

kahoot.q: If a company can't pay its debts, it goes ___.
kahoot.explain: go bankrupt — bankrot bo'lmoq. bankruptcy — ot (bankrotlik).

kahoot.q: The money a company keeps after paying all its costs is ___.
kahoot.explain: profit — sof foyda. revenue — umumiy tushum (xarajatlardan oldin).

kahoot.q: 'Toy Story 2' is the ___ to 'Toy Story'.
kahoot.explain: sequel — filmning davomi.

kahoot.q: When two companies join together to form one company, it is a ___.
kahoot.explain: merger — birlashish. acquisition — bir kompaniya boshqasini sotib olishi.

kahoot.q: A film that is extremely popular and earns a lot of money is a ___.
kahoot.explain: blockbuster — kassabop film (juda katta daromad keltirgan).

kahoot.q: A company that controls the whole market with no competitors has a ___.
kahoot.explain: monopoly — monopoliya: raqobatchisiz yakka hukmronlik.

kahoot.q: 'Risk-taker' ma'nosi?
kahoot.explain: risk-taker — tavakkal qilishdan qo'rqmaydigan odam.

lessons.title: Phrasal verbs — TURN
lessons.grammar_topic: PHRASAL VERBS with TURN — 8 asosiy: turn on / off / up / down / into / out / back / around (ZAXIRA: turn in / over / against)
lessons.vocab_topic: Essential Words 23 — Animals, nature and conservation (hayvonlar, tabiat va tabiatni muhofaza qilish)
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 4.0: Lesson 23 – Phrasal verbs TURN (ixtiyoriy; dars kitobsiz o'tadi). Speaking: Kitob SAMPLE SPEAKING, Topic: Environment — faqat mavzu; namunalar original (Kartochka A — L25 F bo'lim kartasi). Writing: 22-dars savoli — Kitob SAMPLE ESSAYS, Topic 10 — faqat savol; namuna original. Essential Words 23 — Jony Academy ro'yxati (faqat tizimda). Kitob audiolari ishlatilmaydi; listening — Jony Academy skripti. Reading — Jane Goodall (Jony Academy matni).
objectives: Dars oxirida o'quvchi 8 ta asosiy TURN phrasal verbdan (on, off, up, down, into, out, back, around) kamida 6 tasini yangi gapda to'g'ri ma'noda ishlatadi.
"It turned out (that)…" / "… turned out to be …" bilan natijani aytadi (Ex3 dagi 6 gapdan kamida 5 tasi to'g'ri) va olmoshni ajraladigan fe'lda to'g'ri joylaydi (turn it off).

Dars oxirida o'quvchi 'Environment' Kartochka A (Final Speaking 23-dars kartasi — place in nature) bo'yicha 1.5 daqiqa, box'dagi 2+ ibora bilan gapiradi; 3–5 o'quvchi S-4.0 bilan F bo'limga baholanadi (NAMUNA A eshitilishidan oldin).
Dars oxirida o'quvchi 'Online shopping' savoli bo'yicha 10 daqiqada kirish + 1 body (110–140 so'z) yozadi va W-CHECK ning 7 bandidan kamida 5 tasini bajaradi.
materials: Grammatika formulalari — tizimdagi grammar.formulas (proyektor).
Essential Words 23 CORE 20 — tizimdagi lug'at ro'yxati / Lug'at PDF (chop etish ixtiyoriy).
Kahoot: 'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi (22-dars savollari).

Speaking 'Environment': Part 1, Kartochka A (Final Speaking kartasi), Part 3 va box iboralari (class_ex SPEAKING) — proyektor; NAMUNA A — L25 F bo'lim; Kartochka B — uyga (ovozli normativ); ball varag'i (F ustuni).
WRITING NORMATIV: 'Online shopping' savoli (22-dars savoli, class_ex) — proyektor; o'quvchilarda daftar va telefon yopiq.
Reading matni — proyektor yoki chop etilgan nusxa.
Listening transcript — faqat ustoz ekranida (o'quvchiga ko'rsatilmaydi).
Rubrikalar: W-4.0 / S-4.0 + W-CHECK / S-CHECK — class_ex dagi jadval (proyektor).
timeline: Salomlashish + kirish savoli
Ustoz chiroqni yoqib-o'chiradi: "I turn on the light. I turn it off." Kirish savoli (juftlikda, 1 daq): "Which wild animal would you most like to see in the wild?"
TAKROR: Kahoot — 22-dars (Phrasal verbs — MAKE)
'O'tgan dars Kahooti' tugmasi → 22-dars savollari (20 ta). Bugungi darsning Kahooti bu yerda EMAS — u 24-darsda o'ynaladi. Oxirgi 1 daqiqa: eng ko'p xato qilingan 2 savol izohi.
TAKROR: Yozma normativ — Essential Words 22 (Business, entrepreneurship and entertainment)

Normativ — belgilangan vaqtda bajariladigan qisqa o'lchov; natijasiga qarab coin beriladi. 22-dars CORE 20: ustoz o'zbekchasini aytadi, o'quvchi inglizchasini yozadi — 4 daq; 1 daq sherik bilan almashib tekshirish. 18–20 = 2 coin; 15–17 = bajarildi; 14 va kam = 24-darsda qayta topshiradi.
Uy vazifasi tekshiruvi

Tarjima kaliti proyektorda (1 daq, o'quvchi o'zi belgilaydi). 22-dars inshosi ('Online shopping', 40 daq) yig'ib olinadi — W-4.0 bo'yicha keyingi darsgacha tekshiriladi; bugun shu savol bo'yicha WRITING NORMATIV bo'lishini eslating; 22-darsdagi eng ko'p uchragan 2 xato doskada (2 daq). Bajarmaganlar jurnalga.
YANGI GRAMMATIKA — Phrasal verbs TURN (8 asosiy) + CCQ

Lead-in misoli → formula (proyektor) → 2–3 misol → CCQ → 1 daqiqalik tez og'zaki tekshiruv. Lead-in (2 daq): chiroq va telefon ovozi — turn on / off / up / down. Formula (8 daq): grammar.formulas 1–5 — 8 fe'l; olmosh o'rtada (turn it off); X turns into Y / turn X into Y. CCQ (4 daq): presentation oxiridagi 5 ta CCQ. Tez tekshiruv (1 daq): ustoz ma'noni o'zbekcha aytadi, sinf fe'lni aytadi. Mistakes (3 daq): grammar.mistakes doskada. ZAXIRA: turn in / over / against (formulas oxirida) — vaqt qolsa.
LUG'AT — Essential Words 23 CORE 20

Ustoz 20 so'zni proyektorda talaffuz + tarjima bilan o'qitadi (3 daq); 6–8 ta qiyin so'zga CCQ yoki misol (3 daq): predator / prey, migrate, breed, threat; juftlikda A o'zbekchasini, B inglizchasini aytadi (2 daq). Mustahkamlash — flashcard (uyga).
Kombinatsiya — turn + zarracha → ma'no → gap

Kombinatsiya — juftlikda formula → gap → tarjima zanjiri: A formulani yoki o'zbekcha gapni aytadi, B shu formula bilan inglizcha gap tuzib tarjima qiladi, keyin almashadi. 1 daq — ustoz grammar.formulas dan formulani va 1 misolni proyektorda ko'rsatadi; 3 daq — juftlikda (me'yor normativ[1] da); ustoz 2 juftlikni tinglaydi.
SINF MASHQLARI — Ex1–Ex4 (MAJBURIY) + ZAXIRA

Ex1 5 daq yakka · Ex2 5 daq juftlik · Ex3 5 daq yakka · Ex4 3 daq juftlik; har Ex dan keyin javoblar proyektorda. ZAXIRA (Tabiat lug'ati — moslashtirish) — vaqt qolsa sinfda, aks holda ixtiyoriy uyga (homework_intro da ko'rsatilgan; SPEAKING bosqichiga 2 daq berildi).
SPEAKING — Environment

class_ex SPEAKING ('Environment'), juftlikda. 2 daq — Part 1 juftlikda (4 savol, A so'raydi, keyin almashadi); 1 daq — tayyorgarlik (Kartochka A = Final Speaking 23-dars kartasi, 5–6 kalit so'z); 2 daq — A Kartochka A bo'yicha gapiradi, B S-CHECK-4.0 ni to'ldiradi; 2 daq — B shu kartochkada gapiradi (box'dan 2+ ibora bilan); 2 daq — Part 3 juftlikda (3 savol); 2 daq — ustoz NAMUNA A ni (L25, F bo'lim namunasi) FAQAT shu darsdagi F baholashlari tugagandan keyin o'qiydi, o'quvchilar box'dagi iboralarni belgilaydi; 1 daq — ustoz feedback (S-4.0). FINAL SPEAKING (F bo'lim): 0–9 daqiqada, juftliklar ishlayotganda, ustoz o'quvchilarni navbat bilan yoniga chaqiradi — 1 daq tayyorgarlik (keyingi o'quvchi oldingisi gapirayotganda tayyorlanadi) -> 1–2 daq monolog (Kartochka A) -> 1 yakuniy savol; S-4.0 ballari ball varag'ining F ustuniga darhol yoziladi. Baholanadiganlar NAMUNA A ni eshitmasdan oldin baholanadi. Bir o'quvchiga ≈ 2.5–3 daq, shuning uchun 9 daqiqada odatda 3–4 o'quvchi ulguriladi (maqsad 4–5); ulgurmaganlar 24- yoki 25-darsda o'sha darsning kartasi bilan baholanadi. Baholanayotgan o'quvchining sherigi yonidagi juftlikka qo'shiladi (uchlik).
READING — Jane Goodall: from secretary to scientist
1 daq — gist (1-topshiriq, multiple choice); 7 daq — o'qish + TFNG (2-topshiriq); 3 daq — completion (3-topshiriq); 2 daq — tekshirish, NOT GIVEN izohi.
LISTENING — IELTS Part 4

intro: 8 asosiy fe'l: turn on / off / up / down (texnika: yoqmoq, o'chirmoq, oshirmoq, pasaytirmoq); turn down (taklifni rad etmoq); turn up (kelmoq, ko'pincha kechikib yoki kutilmaganda).
turn out (to be) / It turned out that … — bo'lib chiqmoq; turn out (olomon) — yig'ilmoq; turn into — aylanmoq; turn back — orqaga qaytmoq; turn around — o'girilmoq / ishni o'nglamoq.
Ob'ektli fe'l ajraladi, olmosh o'rtada: turn it off (turn off it — xato).
ZAXIRA (vaqt qolsa; Kahoot/normativga kirmaydi): turn in (topshirmoq), turn over (ag'darilmoq), turn against (qarshi chiqmoq).
formulas: turn on / off
turn on/off + qurilma; turn + OB'EKT + on/off; olmosh — o'rtada
He turned on the TV. / Please turn off the lights. / It's too bright — turn it off, please.
U televizorni yoqdi. / Iltimos, chiroqni o'chiring. / Juda yorug' — iltimos, uni o'chiring.
turn up / down (texnika)
turn up/down + ovoz/issiqlik
Can you turn up the volume? / Please turn down the music.
Ovozni ko'tarasanmi? / Iltimos, musiqani pasaytiring.
turn up / down (hayot)
S + turn up (kelmoq); turn down + taklif
She turned up late. / She turned down the job offer.
U kechikib keldi. / U ish taklifini rad etdi.
turn out / turn into
It turned out to be … / It turned out that …; X turns into Y; turn X into Y
It turned out to be true. / A huge crowd turned out for the concert. / The frog turned into a prince.
Bu haqiqat bo'lib chiqdi. / Konsertga katta olomon yig'ildi. / Qurbaqa shahzodaga aylandi.
turn back / around
S + turn back (orqaga qaytmoq); S + turn around (o'girilmoq); turn + ish/kompaniya + around (o'nglamoq)
We had to turn back because of the storm. / She turned around and waved. / The new manager turned the company around in a year.
Bo'ron tufayli orqaga qaytishga majbur bo'ldik. / U o'girilib qo'l silkidi. / Yangi menejer kompaniyani bir yilda o'nglab oldi.
ZAXIRA: turn in / over / against
turn in + hisobot; turn over (ag'darilmoq); turn against + KIM
I have to turn in my report tomorrow. / The car turned over twice. / The fans turned against the coach.
Ertaga hisobotni topshirishim kerak. / Mashina ikki marta ag'darildi. / Muxlislar murabbiyga qarshi chiqdi.
presentation: Did Jane Goodall turn down a place at university?
No. Her family couldn't afford university, so she trained as a secretary.
What did her research turn out to show?
It turned out that chimpanzees make and use tools.
What did David Greybeard turn into a tool?
A grass stem — he used it to fish for termites.
What turned her into an activist?
A conference in 1986: she learned how fast forests were disappearing.
CCQ: She turned down the job.
Did she get an offer? (Yes) Did she take the job? (No)
CCQ: Only ten people turned up.
Did ten people come? (Yes) Did we expect more? (Yes)
CCQ: The story turned out to be true.
Did we know it was true at first? (No) Do we know now? (Yes)
CCQ: We turned back because of the storm.
Did we get to the place we wanted? (No) Did we go in the opposite direction? (Yes)
CCQ: The new manager turned the company around.
Was the company doing well before? (No) Is it better now? (Yes)
notes: turn out + to be / that-clause / ravish ("Everything turned out well").
turn up (kelmoq) — ob'ektsiz; turn up the volume — ob'ektli.

O'quvchi so'raydi: Nega "Turn off it" xato? — Javob: ajraladigan phrasal verbda olmosh (it, them, me) fe'l va zarracha orasida turadi: turn it off. Ot bilan ikkala tartib ham to'g'ri: turn off the TV / turn the TV off.
O'quvchi so'raydi: "The frog turned to a prince" deyish mumkinmi? — Javob: yo'q, aylanmoq — turn into. turn to — boshqa ma'no: yordam so'rab murojaat qilmoq (She turned to her friend for help).
O'quvchi so'raydi: turn down va turn off farqi nima? — Javob: turn down — pasaytirmoq (qurilma ishlab turadi); turn off — butunlay o'chirmoq.
mistakes: She turned the job down it.
She turned the job down. / She turned it down.
It turned out to be true.
The frog turned to a prince.
The frog turned into a prince.
He turned on late for class.
He turned up late for class.

how: CORE 20 — hayvonlar va tabiat asoslari (species, habitat, predator, prey…); STRONG — tadqiqot va muhofaza (captivity, sanctuary, camera trap…); SUPER — Task 2 / Speaking kollokatsiyalari (protect endangered species, in the wild, a moral duty).
Misolda so'zning o'zi albatta bo'ladi, gap tabiiy va faktik to'g'ri; bugungi grammatika qolipi — ixtiyoriy, faqat tabiiy tushsa.
core: It turned out that the species was not extinct.
Tur yo'q bo'lib ketmagani ma'lum bo'ldi.
Forests are turning into farms, and habitats are disappearing.
O'rmonlar dalaga aylanmoqda va yashash muhitlari yo'qolmoqda.
Wolves are predators: they hunt deer and other animals.
Bo'rilar yirtqich: ular bug'u va boshqa hayvonlarni ovlaydi.
Mice are easy prey for owls.
Many birds migrate south in autumn.
Ko'p qushlar kuzda janubga uchib ketadi.
The national park is full of wildlife, from bears to eagles.
Milliy bog' yovvoyi hayvonlarga to'la — ayiqdan tortib burgutgacha.
Humans, monkeys and chimpanzees are all primates.
Odamlar, maymunlar va shimpanzelar — hammasi primatlar.
A chimpanzee turned a stick into a tool.
Chimpanzee behaviour turned out to be very similar to human behaviour.
Shimpanzelar xulqi inson xulqiga juda o'xshash bo'lib chiqdi.
Eagles build their nests high on cliffs.
Scientists at the research station watch the animals every day.
Tadqiqot stansiyasidagi olimlar hayvonlarni har kuni kuzatadi.
Some animals do not breed well in captivity.
Few baby turtles survive to become adults.
Toshbaqa bolalarining ozgina qismi voyaga yetguncha omon qoladi.
Poaching is a serious threat to elephants and rhinos.
Brakonerlik fillar va karkidonlar uchun jiddiy xavf.
Local people work with rangers to protect the forest.
Mahalliy aholi o'rmonni himoya qilish uchun qo'riqchilar bilan ishlaydi.
The old forest was turned into a national park to protect its wildlife.
Eski o'rmon yovvoyi hayvonlarini himoya qilish uchun milliy bog'ga aylantirildi.
Habitat loss is one of the biggest threats to wild animals.
Yashash muhitining yo'qolishi yovvoyi hayvonlar uchun eng katta xavflardan biri.
The tiger population has grown in some countries.
Animal rights groups say wild animals should not live in small cages.
Hayvonlar huquqlari tashkilotlari yovvoyi hayvonlar kichik qafaslarda yashamasligi kerak, deydi.
strong: Tool use is not only human: chimps and some birds use tools too.
Qurol ishlatish faqat insonga xos emas: shimpanzelar va ba'zi qushlar ham qurol ishlatadi.
Chimpanzees use grass stems to fish for termites.
Shimpanzelar termit ovlash uchun o't poyalaridan foydalanadi.
Field research means studying animals in the wild, not in a lab.
Dala tadqiqoti — hayvonlarni laboratoriyada emas, tabiatda o'rganish.
Her work turned ethology upside down.
Animals in captivity can turn aggressive.
Asirlikdagi hayvonlar tajovuzkor bo'lib qolishi mumkin.
The old zoo turned into a sanctuary for orphaned chimps.
Eski hayvonot bog'i yetim shimpanzelar panohgohiga aylandi.
In some areas, hunting for bushmeat is a serious threat to chimpanzees.
Ba'zi hududlarda go'sht uchun ov shimpanzelarga jiddiy xavf tug'diradi.
The illegal wildlife trade is a threat to parrots and tortoises.
Noqonuniy savdo to'tiqushlar va toshbaqalar uchun xavf.
Rangers patrol the park to stop poachers.
Qo'riqchilar brakonerlarni to'xtatish uchun bog'ni aylanib yuradi.
A camera trap took a photo of a snow leopard at night.
Fotokapkan tunda qor qoplonini suratga oldi.
Community-led projects turned villagers into protectors.
Captive breeding has saved some species from extinction.
Asirlikda ko'paytirish ba'zi turlarni qirilib ketishdan qutqardi.
The injured eagle was taken to a rescue centre.

class_ex.title: SPEAKING — Environment (og'zaki): Part 1, 2, 3
class_ex.instr: (12 daq, juftlik) 2 daq — Part 1: A 4 savolni so'raydi, B javob beradi (javob + sabab + misol), keyin almashadi; 1 daq — Kartochka A bo'yicha tayyorgarlik (faqat 5–6 kalit so'z); 2 daq — A gapiradi, B S-CHECK-4.0 ni to'ldiradi; 2 daq — B shu kartochkada gapiradi (box'dan 2+ ibora bilan); 2 daq — Part 3 juftlikda; 2 daq — ustoz NAMUNA A ni (L25, F bo'lim namunasi) o'qiydi — faqat shu darsdagi F baholashlari tugagandan keyin, o'quvchilar box'dagi iboralarni belgilaydi; 1 daq — ustoz feedback (S-4.0). FINAL SPEAKING (F bo'lim): 0–9 daqiqada, juftliklar ishlayotganda, ustoz o'quvchilarni navbat bilan yoniga chaqiradi — 1 daq tayyorgarlik (keyingi o'quvchi oldingisi gapirayotganda tayyorlanadi) -> 1–2 daq monolog (Kartochka A) -> 1 yakuniy savol; S-4.0 ballari ball varag'ining F ustuniga darhol yoziladi. Baholanadiganlar NAMUNA A ni eshitmasdan oldin baholanadi. Bir o'quvchiga ≈ 2.5–3 daq, shuning uchun 9 daqiqada odatda 3–4 o'quvchi ulguriladi (maqsad 4–5); ulgurmaganlar 24- yoki 25-darsda o'sha darsning kartasi bilan baholanadi. Baholanayotgan o'quvchining sherigi yonidagi juftlikka qo'shiladi (uchlik). ICQ: Necha daqiqa tayyorlanasiz? (1) B o'z navbatida nimadan foydalanadi? (Box'dagi kamida 2 ibora)
items: Part 1: Is your city clean?
Part 1: Do you recycle at home?
Part 1: Do you prefer spending time in parks or indoors?
Part 1: What do you do to save water or electricity?
KARTOCHKA A: Describe a place in nature that you like to visit. You should say: where it is; how often you go there; what you do there; and explain why this place is special to you.
Part 3: Who should do more to protect the environment — people or companies?
Part 3: Why are some animals endangered?
Part 3: What can schools do to teach children about nature?
box: I'd like to talk about …, which is about … from …
I usually go there with … in …, when …
The air feels … and it's very quiet, so …
What I like most is that …
It's home to a lot of wildlife, for example …
The trip turned out to be …
This place is special to me because …
answers: Part 1 namunalari (faqat ustoz uchun): 1) Mostly yes. The city centre is quite clean, because street cleaners work there every morning. However, some side streets turn into a mess after the weekend, when people leave rubbish next to the bins. 2) A little. We keep empty plastic bottles in a big bag, and a man from our mahalla buys them for recycling. I'd like my family to separate more of our rubbish, but there is only one bin in our yard. 3) I prefer parks, especially in spring. After a long day at my desk, I turn off my laptop and walk in the park near my house, because the fresh air helps me relax. In July, though, it's too hot, so I stay indoors. 4) I always turn off the lights when I leave a room, and I unplug my charger at night. In summer my family also turns off the air conditioner when nobody is at home, and our electricity bill has gone down.

NAMUNA A (Band 5.5–6, ~1.5–2 daqiqa, faqat ustoz uchun): Kartochka A — Final Speaking 23-dars kartasi; namuna yangi yozilmagan — L25, Final Test 'F. Speaking' bo'limidagi 'Namuna javob (23-dars kartasi, 158 so'z)'. Ustoz namunani faqat shu darsdagi F baholashlari tugagandan keyin (bosqichning 9–11-daqiqasida) ovoz chiqarib o'qiydi; undan oldin u o'quvchilarga ko'rsatilmaydi va o'qilmaydi. O'quvchilar tinglab box'dagi 1–5 va 8-iboralarni belgilaydi. 24/25-darsda baholanadiganlar boshqa kartada gapiradi, shuning uchun namunani eshitishi ularning bahosiga ta'sir qilmaydi.

Part 3 namunalari (faqat ustoz uchun): 1) I think companies should do more, because one big factory can pollute more than thousands of families. For example, if a factory cleans its waste water, the whole river benefits. Still, ordinary people matter too, because companies change when customers ask them to. 2) Mainly because of human activity. When forests and wetlands are turned into farms or roads, animals lose their habitat. Poaching is another threat; for instance, the snow leopard is still hunted for its fur. 3) Schools can take students outside instead of teaching only from textbooks. For example, a biology teacher could organise a trip to a nature reserve, so children see wildlife in the wild. Schools could also start an eco club that checks how much electricity the school uses.

Final Speaking (F bo'lim): baholangan o'quvchilarning (odatda 3–4, maqsad 4–5) FC/LR/GRA/P ballari ball varag'ining F ustuniga shu darsning o'zida yoziladi; yakuniy savol — 'Do you think young people spend enough time in nature?'. Ulgurmaganlar ro'yxatini yozib qo'ying — ular 24- yoki 25-darsda o'sha darsning kartasi bilan baholanadi.
Baholash: S-4.0 (jadval shu darsda); juftlikda — S-CHECK-4.0.
why: Bugungi grammatika Part 1/3 namunalarida: turn into a mess, turn off my laptop, turn off the lights, turns off the air conditioner, are turned into farms — TURN tabiiy joyda; box'da 'The trip turned out to be …'.
EW 23 so'zlari: wildlife, habitat, threat, poaching, wetland, nature reserve, in the wild, protect, human activity — Part 3 javoblari va box'da.
Box'dagi 1–5 va 8-iboralar L25 F bo'lim namunasida bor (o'quvchilar tinglab belgilaydi); 6–7-iboralar — bugungi lug'at va grammatika uchun qo'shimcha.
class_ex.note: S-CHECK-4.0 (sherik belgilaydi): 1) kartochkaning 4 bandi aytildimi; 2) 1.5 daqiqadan uzoq, uzun pauzasiz; 3) box'dan 2+ ibora; 4) bugungi grammatika (TURN) 1–2 marta; 5) Part 3 javobi fikr + sabab + misol. FINAL SPEAKING (F bo'lim): bosqichning 0–9-daqiqasida ustoz o'quvchilarni Kartochka A bo'yicha S-4.0 bilan baholaydi va F ustuniga yozadi (odatda 3–4, maqsad 4–5; ulgurmaganlar — 24/25-darsda o'sha darsning kartasi bilan); qolganlar juftlikda shu kartani mashq qiladi; NAMUNA A faqat baholashlardan keyin o'qiladi. class_ex.title: WRITING NORMATIV — Online shopping (yozma, 10 daqiqa)
class_ex.instr: (12 daq, yakka) 1 daq — ustoz savolni proyektorda ko'rsatadi va qoidani aytadi: kirish + 1 body, 110–140 so'z; daftar, telefon va namuna yopiq; taymer 10 daq shu daqiqadan boshlanadi. 9 daq — yakka yozish; vaqt tugaganda chiziq tortiladi. 2 daq — W-CHECK-4.0 bilan o'zini tekshiradi, so'z sonini oxirida yozadi; ish yig'iladi. ICQ: Nechta abzats yozasiz? (2 — kirish va 1 body) Daftar yoki namunaga qarash mumkinmi? (Yo'q)
items: Question: Online shopping is replacing traditional shopping. Is this a positive or negative development?
TASK: Write an introduction + ONE body paragraph (110–140 words) in 10 minutes. No notebook, no phone, no model.
Introduction: paraphrase the question + your clear position (2–3 sentences).
Body: ONE main reason for your position (a NEW idea — not the one from your Lesson 22 essay): Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link.
Use 1–2 TURN phrasal verbs (turn into, turn out to be, turn down) and 4+ Essential Words 22 words (customer, consumer demand, market, owner, supplier, profit …).
answers: Tahlil kaliti: savol turi — positive or negative development; kirishda bitta aniq pozitsiya (mostly positive yoki mostly negative) bo'lishi shart va body shu pozitsiyani qo'llashi kerak; normativda bitta body yetarli. 'Both positive and negative' deb pozitsiyasiz yozish — TR ko'pi bilan 2.

NAMUNA kirish + Body (faqat ustoz uchun, Band 5.5–6, 123 so'z): In many countries, including Uzbekistan, people now order goods from websites and apps rather than going to physical stores. In my view, this trend brings more benefits than problems.

The main reason is that online shopping has turned into a new source of jobs, especially for young people. When consumer demand moves online, companies need warehouse workers, couriers and staff who answer customer questions. For example, my cousin in Samarkand could not find work after college, but last year he started delivering parcels for an online market. The job turned out to be well paid, and now he is saving to become the owner of a small pick-up point. As a result, online shopping creates new opportunities rather than only closing old ones.

Namunadagi g'oya — onlayn savdo yaratayotgan yangi ish o'rinlari (ombor, kuryer, pick-up point); 22-dars inshosidagi qulaylik / narx g'oyasidan farqli. Kirish ham 22-dars MODEL kirishidan boshqa parafraz va tuzilmada (order goods from websites and apps / physical stores / more benefits than problems). O'quvchi 22-darsdagi kirish va body'sini yod olib qaytarmasligi uchun items'da 'NEW idea' talabi bor.
Baholash: W-4.0 (jadval shu darsda); NORM-4.0: 10–12 ball — 2 coin; 7–9 — bajarildi; ≤6 — uyda qayta yozadi. So'z soni 110 dan kam — TR ko'pi bilan 1.
why: Bugungi grammatika: has turned into a new source of jobs (aylanmoq), turned out to be well paid (bo'lib chiqdi) — 2 joy, tabiiy.
EW 22 so'zlari: consumer demand, customer, market (online market), owner — 4 ta; kollokatsiya: source of jobs, pick-up point, warehouse workers.
Bog'lovchilar: including, rather than, When, For example, but, As a result — CC uchun 4+ xil.
O'zbek hayotidan misol: Samarqanddagi kollej bitiruvchisi onlayn do'kon kuryeri bo'lib ishlaydi.

Izchillik va bog'lanish (CC)

Abzatslar aniq: kirish -> Body 1 -> Body 2 -> xulosa; har body: topic sentence -> izoh -> misol -> link; 4+ xil bog'lovchi to'g'ri (however, as a result, for example, on the other hand); ishora so'zlari (this, they, such) to'g'ri.
Abzatslar bor, mantiq tushunarli; 2–3 bog'lovchi, ba'zan mexanik (Firstly, Secondly…); 1–2 noaniq ishora.
Abzatsga bo'linmagan yoki body da topic sentence yo'q; bog'lovchilar 1–2 ta yoki noto'g'ri.
G'oyalar tartibsiz, bog'lanish yo'q.
Lug'at boyligi (LR)
Shu darsning Essential Words so'zlaridan 4+ ta va 2+ kollokatsiya to'g'ri; savol so'zlari parafraz qilingan; imlo xatosi 1–2 ta.
Mavzu so'zlari bor, lekin takror ko'p yoki 3–4 so'z noto'g'ri tanlangan; savol so'zlari ko'chirilgan; imlo xatolari ma'noga xalaqit bermaydi.
Oddiy, takroriy lug'at; so'z tanlash va imlo xatolari ma'noni qiyinlashtiradi.
Juda cheklangan lug'at, ma'no tushunarsiz.
Grammatika aniqligi va xilma-xilligi (GRA)
Sodda va qo'shma gaplar aralash (because, although, which, if); bugungi struktura 1–3 marta to'g'ri va tabiiy; gaplarning ko'pi xatosiz.
Qo'shma gap urinishlari bor; xatolar bor, lekin ma'no tushunarli; artikl/zamon xatolari takrorlanadi.
Asosan sodda gaplar; xatolar ko'p, ayrim gaplar tushunarsiz.
Gap tuzilishi deyarli yo'q.
Jami (12 ball) -> taxminiy band
11–12 ball ≈ Band 5.5–6
8–10 ball ≈ Band 5
5–7 ball ≈ Band 4–4.5
0–4 ball ≈ Band 3.5 va past
Qoidalar (ustoz uchun)
Vaqt: insho 40 daq (uyda, taymer), WRITING NORMATIV 10 daq; vaqt tugaganda chiziq tortiladi, chiziqdan keyingi qism baholanmaydi.
So'z sonini o'quvchi oxirida yozadi; ustoz 2 qatorni sanab tekshiradi; insho 180 so'zdan kam — TR ko'pi bilan 1.
Namuna yoki boshqa manbadan ko'chirilgani aniqlansa — 0 ball, sinfda boshqa savol bilan qayta yozadi.
Ustoz har ish chetiga TR/CC/LR/GRA ballarini va 1 ta eng muhim tuzatishni yozadi; umumiy 2–3 xato keyingi darsning 'Xatolar ustida ishlash' bosqichiga.

items: KARTOCHKA B: Describe something you do to protect the environment. You should say: what you do ; how often you do it ; when you started doing it ; and explain why it is important to you.
answers: NAMUNA B (Band 5.5–6, 157 so'z, ~1.5 daqiqa): I'd like to talk about something I do at home to protect the environment: I collect our kitchen waste and turn it into compost. Every day I put fruit and vegetable peelings into a special bucket instead of the rubbish bin, and twice a week I empty it into a wooden box in our garden. I started doing this about two years ago, after a biology project at school. Our teacher explained that food waste at rubbish dumps produces harmful gases, and that really surprised me. After a few months, the peelings turned into dark, rich soil, and now my grandfather uses it for his tomatoes. I also try to save electricity: I turn off my computer at night and turn down the heating when nobody is in the room. This is important to me because small habits like these reduce the threat to wildlife and their habitats. Besides, it makes me feel responsible for my home.
Baholash: S-4.0 (class_ex dagi jadval), NORM-4.0: 10–12 ball — 2 coin; 7–9 — bajarildi; ≤6 — qayta yozib yuboradi.

reading.title: Jane Goodall: from secretary to scientist
text: A. Jane Goodall was born in London in 1934. As a child, she loved animals and dreamed of living in Africa, but her family could not afford university, so she trained as a secretary. In 1957 a school friend invited her to Kenya. Jane worked as a waitress to pay for the trip, and she turned up in Kenya with very little money. There she met the scientist Louis Leakey, who gave her a job as his assistant.

B. In 1960 Leakey sent her to study chimpanzees at Gombe, in Tanzania. She had no degree, but Leakey believed this was an advantage: her mind was not shaped by old theories. At first the chimps ran away whenever she came near. Slowly, one older male, whom she named David Greybeard, began to trust her. One day she watched him pick a grass stem, pull off the leaves and push it into a termite mound. He had turned a plant into a tool. Until then, most scientists believed that only humans made tools. Leakey famously wrote to her: "Now we must redefine tool, redefine man, or accept chimpanzees as humans."

C. Not everyone was happy. Some scientists criticised her because she gave the chimps names instead of numbers and wrote about their personalities and feelings. However, Cambridge University accepted her as a PhD student although she had no first degree, and her results turned out to be correct. She also saw a darker side of chimp life: in the 1970s, one group fought another for four years. This showed that violence is not only a human problem.

D. In 1986 she went to a conference and learned how quickly forests were disappearing. It was the turning point of her life. She never went back to full-time research; instead, she turned into an activist. For many years she travelled around 300 days a year to give talks, and she started Roots & Shoots, a programme for young people in many countries.

E. Large crowds turned out to hear her speak, even when she was ninety. She died in 2025, aged 91, still on a speaking tour. She often told young people that everyone makes a difference every day, and that they should decide what kind of difference they want to make.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

listening.audios: Audio fayl yo'q — ustoz transcript'ni o'qiydi (Jony Academy skripti, 2 marta).
intro: You will hear a lecturer talking about how scientists study snow leopards.
1-tinglash: eslatmalarni to'ldiring; 2-tinglash: javoblarni tekshiring.
Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

tasks.title: Note completion — ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER
tasks.instr: Eslatmalarni to'ldiring (7 ta bo'shliq).
items: Number of cameras in the project: ___
Cameras are fixed to ___, not trees
Animals in the first week's photos: foxes and ___
Each leopard has its own pattern of ___
Number of different leopards: ___
Droppings contain ___, which shows if an animal is male or female
Some local shepherds now work as ___

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; monolog (IELTS Part 4 — ma'ruza) — ustoz o'qiydi, tuzatishlarda to'xtab, ovoz ohangini o'zgartiring.

Lecturer: Good morning, everyone. Today I'm going to talk about how scientists study animals that are very shy, such as the snow leopard. These cats live high in the mountains, and most people never see one.

Lecturer: The main method is the camera trap — a small camera that takes a photo when an animal walks past. In one project I worked on, we put out forty cameras — sorry, I mean fifty. Forty was the first plan.
Lecturer: You might think the cameras are fixed to trees, but at that height there are very few trees, so we fixed them to rocks.

Lecturer: We left the cameras for three months. At first we were disappointed: in the first week only foxes and some wild sheep — no, sorry, they were goats — turned up in the photos. But in the end, the results turned out to be much better.
Lecturer: How do we tell one leopard from another? Each cat has its own pattern — not of stripes, of course, that's tigers — of spots on its fur, a bit like a human fingerprint.
Lecturer: At first we counted fourteen leopards, but two of them had been photographed from both sides, so the real number was twelve.
Lecturer: Scientists also collect droppings, because they contain DNA. The DNA tells us whether an animal is male or female.
Lecturer: Finally, a project like this depends on local people. Shepherds tell us where they have seen tracks, and several of them now work as guides — well, as rangers, to be exact.

kahoot.q: Please turn ___ the TV when you leave the room.

kahoot.q: The music is too loud. Please turn it ___.

kahoot.q: The party started at 7, but he turned ___ at 10.
kahoot.explain: turn up — (kechikib, kutilmaganda) kelmoq.

kahoot.q: Everyone thought the story was false, but it turned out ___ true.
kahoot.explain: turn out TO BE — …bo'lib chiqmoq.

kahoot.q: In the fairy tale, the frog turned ___ a prince.
kahoot.explain: turn INTO — aylanmoq. 'turned to a prince' — xato.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: It turned out to be true.
kahoot.explain: Olmosh zarrachadan oldin: Turn it off.

kahoot.q: We had to turn ___ because of the storm and go home.
kahoot.explain: turn back — orqaga qaytmoq.

kahoot.q: The heating is too low. Can you turn it ___ a little?
kahoot.explain: turn up — (issiqlik, ovozni) oshirmoq; olmosh o'rtada: turn it up.

kahoot.q: Nobody expected it, but the quiet student turned ___ to be the best speaker in the class.
kahoot.explain: turn out to be — …bo'lib chiqmoq.

kahoot.q: In twenty years, the small village turned ___ a busy town.
kahoot.explain: turn into — aylanmoq (X turns into Y).

kahoot.q: The company was losing money, but the new manager turned it ___ in a year.
kahoot.explain: turn around — (vaziyatni) yaxshilamoq, o'nglamoq.

kahoot.q: A lion hunts zebras. The lion is a ___.
kahoot.explain: predator — yirtqich (ovlovchi); prey — o'lja (ovlanadigan hayvon).

kahoot.q: The natural home of an animal is its ___.
kahoot.explain: habitat — yashash muhiti.

kahoot.q: Killing animals illegally, for example for their skin, is ___.
kahoot.explain: poaching — brakonerlik (noqonuniy ov); poacher — brakoner.

kahoot.q: Habitat loss is a serious ___ to many wild animals.
kahoot.explain: threat — xavf, tahdid: a threat to wildlife (yovvoyi tabiat uchun xavf).

kahoot.q: Animals in zoos live in ___, not in the wild.
kahoot.explain: captivity — asirlik, qafasda saqlash.

kahoot.q: Every winter these birds ___ to warmer countries.
kahoot.explain: migrate — (fasl o'zgarganda) ko'chib o'tmoq.

kahoot.q: Chimpanzees use grass stems to catch termites. This is an example of tool ___.
kahoot.explain: tool use — qurol ishlatish (hayvonlarda).

kahoot.q: 'Breed' ma'nosi?
kahoot.explain: breed — ko'paymoq, nasl bermoq (captive breeding — asirlikda ko'paytirish).

intro: 7 asosiy fe'l: set off / out, set up, set in, set back, set aside, set down; set out to + V1 — maqsad; set off + ob'ekt — qo'zg'atmoq.
ZAXIRA (7-formula): set to, be set upon, be set against.
formulas: set off / set out (yo'l)
S + set off/out (for + joy)
We set off early in the morning.
Biz erta tongda yo'lga chiqdik.
set out to + V1
S + set out + to + V1
She set out to write a novel.
U roman yozishni maqsad qilib kirishdi.
set up
set up + tashkilot/narsa; set it up (olmosh o'rtada)
They set up a new business.
Ular yangi biznes ochishdi.
set in / set back
winter/rain/boredom + set in; set + X + back + (by + vaqt)
Winter has set in. / The storm set the project back by weeks.
Qish kirib keldi. / Bo'ron loyihani haftalarga kechiktirdi.
set aside / set down
set aside + pul/vaqt; set down + fikr
She set aside some money for her holiday. / She set her thoughts down on paper.
U ta'tili uchun pul ajratdi. / U fikrlarini qog'ozga tushirdi.
set off (qo'zg'atmoq)
set off + alarm / a reaction / a wave of …
The smoke set off the fire alarm.
Tutun yong'in signalini ishga tushirdi.
ZAXIRA: set to / set upon / be set against
set to + work; be set upon by …; be set against + ot/V-ing
He set to work immediately. / She was set against the idea.
U darhol ishga kirishdi. / U bu g'oyaga qat'iy qarshi edi.
presentation: CCQ: We set off at 6 a.m.
Did we start a journey? (Yes) Was it early? (Yes)
CCQ: She set out to write a novel.
Is she travelling? (No) Was writing a novel her aim? (Yes)
CCQ: They set up a new business.
Did the business exist before? (No) Who started it? (They did)
CCQ: Winter has set in.
Has winter started? (Yes) Will it continue? (Yes) Is it pleasant? (Usually not)
notes: O'quvchi so'raydi: "The lesson set in at 9" bo'ladimi? — Javob: yo'q. set in — noxush, davom etadigan holat (winter, rain, boredom). Dars: The lesson starts at 9.
O'quvchi so'raydi: set off va set out farqi bormi? — Javob: yo'lga chiqish ma'nosida deyarli bir xil; maqsad ma'nosi faqat set out to + V1 da.
O'quvchi so'raydi: Nega "set up it" emas? — Javob: olmosh fe'l va zarracha orasiga kiradi: set it up, set them aside.

KARTOCHKA A: Describe a tradition in your country that you are proud of. You should say: what the tradition is; when people follow it; who takes part in it; and explain why you are proud of it.
Part 3: Why is traditional food important for a nation?
Part 3: Why do many young people prefer fast food?
Part 3: Should schools teach students how to cook?
box: I'd like to talk about …, a tradition we follow every …
About ten days before the holiday, … sets aside …
Our neighbours set up … in one yard.
Everyone takes part: … , … and the younger generation …
In the morning, we set off with … and share it with …
I'm proud of this tradition because it shows real unity.
For me, it's a living part of our national identity.
I hope my own children will celebrate it in the same way.
answers: Part 1 namunalari (faqat ustoz uchun): 1) My favourite food is chuchvara — small dumplings in a hot soup. I like it most in winter, when the cold weather sets in and I need something warm and filling.
2) Mostly at home, because eating out every day is quite expensive and my mother cooks most evenings. But on Fridays my friends and I sometimes have samsa and green tea at a small cafe after classes.
3) Only a little. I can make a simple tomato and cucumber salad and boil potatoes. Last month I set out to learn mastava, and my grandmother is teaching me step by step.

4) Yes, quite a lot. As a child I ate whatever my parents cooked, but now I eat more fast food because I spend all day at school and courses. I'm trying to set aside time on Sundays to cook something healthier.

NAMUNA A (Band 5.5–6, 170 so'z, ~1.5–2 daqiqa): I'd like to talk about cooking sumalak, a tradition we follow every spring before Navruz, our biggest national holiday. Sumalak is a sweet, dark-brown dish made from young wheat, and it cooks for almost a whole night. About ten days before the holiday, my aunt sets aside a big bowl of wheat and keeps it wet until green shoots appear. On the evening before the celebration, our neighbours set up a huge pot in one yard and light a fire under it. Everyone takes part: grandmothers sing old songs, men bring firewood, and the younger generation stirs the pot in shifts so that it doesn't burn. In the morning, my cousins and I set off with full bowls and share the sumalak with every family in our street. I'm proud of this tradition because it shows real unity: nobody is too busy or too important to help. For me, it's a living part of our national identity, and I hope my own children will celebrate Navruz in the same way.

Part 3 namunalari: 1) Traditional food is part of a nation's history and national identity. Recipes are passed from parents to children, so they keep the memory of earlier generations alive. For example, dishes like sumalak or halim bring whole communities together on national holidays.

2) Mainly because it is quick and cheap, and young people are busy with studies and part-time jobs. Fast food chains also advertise a lot on social media, so burgers and pizza look modern and fun. As a result, many teenagers see traditional meals as something only for home.

3) Yes, I think schools should teach at least the basics. If students can cook simple, healthy meals, they will depend less on fast food when they live alone. For instance, a short cooking lesson once a week could also teach them about their national cuisine.

class_ex.instr: (12 daq, yakka) 2 daq — savol tahlili: savol turi, savolda nechta savol bor, sinfda qaysi qismini yozamiz. 8 daq — BITTA body paragraf, faqat sabablar ('Why is this happening?'), 100–120 so'z, qolip: Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link; oxirida so'z sonini yozing. 2 daq — sherik bilan almashib W-CHECK-4.0 bo'yicha tekshirasiz; ustoz 1 paragrafni W-4.0 bo'yicha ovoz chiqarib baholaydi. ICQ: Sinfda paragraf nima haqida? (Sabablar — nega yoshlar fast foodni afzal ko'radi) Necha so'z? (100–120)
box: Question: Fast food is becoming more popular than traditional food among young people. Why is this happening? Is this a positive or negative development?
Useful: There are several reasons why … / The main reason is … / In addition, … / For example, … / As a result, …
Ideas: convenience and busy days · price · global culture and advertising · cafes vs teahouses
items: Savol turi qanday? Savolda nechta savol bor va to'liq inshoda nechta body kerak?
Sinfda qaysi savolga javob beramiz: 'Why is this happening?' yoki 'positive or negative'?
Kalit so'zlarni qanday parafraz qilasiz (young people, more popular, traditional food)?
Bugungi grammatika qayerga mos keladi: set off, set aside, set up …?
Qaysi EW24 so'zlari bu mavzuga mos (kamida 2–3 ta)?
TASK: Write ONE body paragraph about the reasons (100–120 words): Topic sentence -> Explain -> Example -> Link.
answers: 1) Ikki qismli savol (reasons + positive/negative development): 2 ta savol -> to'liq inshoda 2 ta body. Body 1 — sabablar, Body 2 — ijobiy yoki salbiy (pozitsiya kirishda aytiladi va Body 2 da asoslanadi).
2) Sinfda faqat 'Why is this happening?' — sabablar paragrafi. Positive/negative — uyga QO'SHIMCHA (Body 2).
3) young people -> the younger generation / teenagers; more popular -> are choosing more often; traditional food -> national / home-cooked dishes.
4) set off early for school (vaqt yo'q), rarely set aside time to cook (sabab), cafes were set up near universities (misol).
5) EW24: the younger generation, global culture, celebration, national identity, balance tradition and modernity, take pride in.

NAMUNA paragraf — sabablar (faqat ustoz uchun, 117 so'z): There are several reasons why fast food is becoming more popular among the younger generation. The main reason is convenience. Many students set off early for school and courses and rarely set aside time to cook or to sit down for a family meal, so a quick burger seems like the easiest choice. In addition, global culture plays a big role. International chains advertise on social media, and eating there looks modern and fun. For example, in Tashkent, cafes near universities are full of students at lunchtime, while traditional teahouses attract mostly older customers. As a result, many young people now see traditional dishes, an important part of our national identity, as food only for family celebrations.
Namuna: 117 so'z (Topic sentence -> 2 sabab + izoh -> Toshkent misoli -> As a result). Bugungi struktura 2 marta: set off, set aside.
Baholash: W-4.0 (jadval shu darsda) + W-CHECK-4.0 (7-band: paragraf 100–120 so'z); NORM-4.0 — body paragraf: 10–12 — 1 coin; ≤6 — uyda qayta.
why: Bugungi grammatika: 'set off early for school' — set off + for + joy (yo'lga chiqmoq), ravish zarrachadan keyin; 'rarely set aside time to cook' — set aside + ob'ekt (vaqt ajratmoq).
EW24 so'zlari: the younger generation — yosh avlod (young people parafrazi); global culture — global madaniyat; celebrations — bayramlar; national identity — milliy o'zlik (CORE).
Bog'lovchilar: The main reason is, In addition, For example, while, As a result — W-CHECK 4-band uchun yetarli.
O'zbek misoli: Toshkentdagi universitetlar yonidagi kafelar va choyxonalar — aniq, hayotiy misol TR va CC uchun ball beradi.
class_ex.note: Jony Academy savoli (kitob SAMPLE ESSAYS uslubida); namuna paragraf Jony Academy original matni. Kuchsiz: 2 ta sabab + 1 misol, 80–100 so'z; Kuchli: + Body 2 rejasi (pozitsiya + 2 dalil). Positive or negative qismi — uyga QO'SHIMCHA (namuna homework answers da).

rows: Vazifaga javob (TR; Task 1 da TA)

Savolning BARCHA qismiga javob (sabab VA yechim; ikki fikr VA o'z fikri; ijobiy VA salbiy tomon); pozitsiya kirishda aniq va xulosagacha saqlanadi; har asosiy g'oya izoh va aniq misol bilan. Insho: kirish + 2 body + xulosa, 220–260 so'z; paragraf: talab qilingan so'z soni. Task 1: overview bor, asosiy raqamlar to'g'ri.
Savolga javob va pozitsiya bor, lekin bir qismi yuzaki yoki misol umumiy; insho 180–219 so'z yoki xulosa 1 gapdan iborat. Task 1: overview bor, ayrim raqamlar keraksiz.
Savolning faqat bir qismiga javob (masalan, faqat sabablar); pozitsiya noaniq yoki o'zgarib ketadi; g'oyalar takrorlanadi; insho 120–179 so'z. Task 1: overview yo'q.
Savolga javob yo'q, mavzudan tashqari, yodlangan boshqa matn yoki so'z soni talabning yarmidan kam.
Izchillik va bog'lanish (CC)

Abzatslar aniq: kirish -> Body 1 -> Body 2 -> xulosa; har body: topic sentence -> izoh -> misol -> link; 4+ xil bog'lovchi to'g'ri (however, as a result, for example, on the other hand); ishora so'zlari (this, they, such) to'g'ri.
Abzatslar bor, mantiq tushunarli; 2–3 bog'lovchi, ba'zan mexanik (Firstly, Secondly…); 1–2 noaniq ishora.
Abzatsga bo'linmagan yoki body da topic sentence yo'q; bog'lovchilar 1–2 ta yoki noto'g'ri.
G'oyalar tartibsiz, bog'lanish yo'q.
Lug'at boyligi (LR)
Shu darsning Essential Words so'zlaridan 4+ ta va 2+ kollokatsiya to'g'ri; savol so'zlari parafraz qilingan; imlo xatosi 1–2 ta.
Mavzu so'zlari bor, lekin takror ko'p yoki 3–4 so'z noto'g'ri tanlangan; savol so'zlari ko'chirilgan; imlo xatolari ma'noga xalaqit bermaydi.
Oddiy, takroriy lug'at; so'z tanlash va imlo xatolari ma'noni qiyinlashtiradi.
Juda cheklangan lug'at, ma'no tushunarsiz.
Grammatika aniqligi va xilma-xilligi (GRA)
Sodda va qo'shma gaplar aralash (because, although, which, if); bugungi struktura 1–3 marta to'g'ri va tabiiy; gaplarning ko'pi xatosiz.
Qo'shma gap urinishlari bor; xatolar bor, lekin ma'no tushunarli; artikl/zamon xatolari takrorlanadi.
Asosan sodda gaplar; xatolar ko'p, ayrim gaplar tushunarsiz.
Gap tuzilishi deyarli yo'q.
Jami (12 ball) -> taxminiy band
11–12 ball ≈ Band 5.5–6
8–10 ball ≈ Band 5
5–7 ball ≈ Band 4–4.5
0–4 ball ≈ Band 3.5 va past
Qoidalar (ustoz uchun)
Vaqt: insho 40 daq (uyda, taymer), WRITING NORMATIV 10 daq; vaqt tugaganda chiziq tortiladi, chiziqdan keyingi qism baholanmaydi.
So'z sonini o'quvchi oxirida yozadi; ustoz 2 qatorni sanab tekshiradi; insho 180 so'zdan kam — TR ko'pi bilan 1.
Namuna yoki boshqa manbadan ko'chirilgani aniqlansa — 0 ball, sinfda boshqa savol bilan qayta yozadi.
Ustoz har ish chetiga TR/CC/LR/GRA ballarini va 1 ta eng muhim tuzatishni yozadi; umumiy 2–3 xato keyingi darsning 'Xatolar ustida ishlash' bosqichiga.

homework.title: 4. SPEAKING NORMATIV — Food (og'zaki, ovozli): Kartochka B
homework.instr: MAJBURIY. 1 daqiqa tayyorgarlik (faqat 5–6 kalit so'z), keyin 1.5–2 daqiqa to'xtamasdan gapirib, ovozli yozuvni ilovaga yuboring. Matndan o'qimang. Bugungi strukturani (set up / set off / set aside / set out to …) 1–2 marta va EW24 so'zlaridan kamida 2 tasini ishlating. 1 marta qayta yozish mumkin.
items: KARTOCHKA B: Describe a traditional dish you would like to learn to cook. You should say: what the dish is ; who usually cooks it in your family ; what is in it ; and explain why you want to learn to cook it.
answers: NAMUNA B (Band 5.5–6, 156 so'z, faqat ustoz uchun): I'd like to talk about manti, a traditional dish that I'd really like to learn to cook. Manti are large steamed dumplings, and people usually eat them with yoghurt or a little vinegar. In my family, my grandmother cooks them, normally when all her grandchildren visit her at the weekend. The filling is chopped beef or lamb with a lot of onion, salt and black pepper, and in autumn she sometimes adds pumpkin. The hardest part is the dough, because it must be very thin but strong, so that the juice stays inside. I want to learn to cook manti for two reasons. First, I'd like to keep our family recipe alive, because my grandmother learned it from her own mother. Second, if I study abroad one day, I want to set up a small Navruz dinner for my friends, show them how we celebrate our national holiday and give them a taste of my homeland.
Bugungi struktura: set up a small Navruz dinner; EW24: celebrate, national holiday, homeland.
Baholash: S-4.0 (class_ex dagi jadval), NORM-4.0: 10–12 ball — 2 coin; 7–9 — bajarildi; ≤6 — qayta yozib yuboradi.

Mezon: 5 gap, mazmun aniq, misra ko'chirilmagan — 1 coin; STRONG 20 yozma — +2 coin.

homework.title: 7. QO'SHIMCHA — WRITING — Fast food and young people: Body 2 (positive or negative), 100–120 so'z (yozma)
homework.instr: Sinfdagi sabablar paragrafini W-CHECK-4.0 bo'yicha tuzating va ikkinchi body paragraf yozing: bu holat ijobiymi yoki salbiymi? Pozitsiya 1-gapda aniq, 2 dalil + O'zbekistondan 1 misol + xulosa gap. 100–120 so'z; bugungi struktura (SET phrasal verb) 1–2 marta; oxirida so'z sonini yozing.
items: Question: Fast food is becoming more popular than traditional food among young people. Why is this happening? Is this a positive or negative development?
Plan: Topic sentence (your position) -> Reason 1 + explain -> Reason 2 -> Example -> Link.
answers: NAMUNA Body 2 (Band 5.5–6, 106 so'z, Jony Academy original, faqat ustoz uchun): In my opinion, this trend is mostly a negative development. Firstly, fast food usually contains too much fat, salt and sugar, so eating it every day can cause health problems such as obesity at a young age. Secondly, when young people stop eating traditional meals, they also lose a part of their national identity, because family recipes connect generations. However, the situation is not hopeless. For instance, some young cooks in Uzbekistan have set up modern cafes that serve national dishes quickly and cheaply. Therefore, instead of simply copying global fast food, young people should balance tradition and modernity and take pride in their own cuisine.
Bugungi struktura: have set up modern cafes; EW24: national identity, balance tradition and modernity, take pride in.
Baholash: W-4.0 (class_ex dagi jadval), NORM-4.0: 10–12 ball — 1 coin; ≤6 — qayta yozadi.
homework.note: Namuna o'quvchiga baholangandan keyin ko'rsatiladi. Ijobiy pozitsiya ham qabul qilinadi, agar 2 dalil va misol bo'lsa.

reading.title: Abdulla Oripov — the village boy who wrote words for a nation
text: A. Abdulla Oripov was born in 1941 in Nekoz, a small village in the Kashkadarya region. He loved books from an early age, and as a teenager he set out to become a poet. After school he set off for Tashkent to study at the university. He graduated from the journalism faculty in 1963 and started work as an editor at a publishing house.

B. His first collection of poems appeared in the mid-1960s. At that time, many poets praised factories and five-year plans, but Oripov wrote about his mother, his village and what it meant to be Uzbek. In 1965 he wrote "O'zbegim" ("My Uzbek"), a poem about the long history of his people — its great scholars, its hard times and its hopes. Many readers learned it by heart.

C. Not everyone liked his work. Some officials did not like poems that seemed "too national", and not all of his writing could be published at that time. These problems set his career back for a while, but they did not stop him. He continued to write, and his readers stayed loyal to him.

D. After independence, the new country needed a national anthem. Oripov wrote the words, and the music was by the composer Mutal Burhanov. The anthem was adopted in 1992, and today it is sung at schools, official ceremonies and sports events across the country. Oripov later received the title Hero of Uzbekistan and led the Writers' Union, where he supported young writers.

E. One of his hardest projects was a translation. He set aside years of his life to translate the first part of Dante's "Divine Comedy" into Uzbek, so that Uzbek readers could enjoy a classic of world literature in their own language. Oripov's words are still sung, read and learned by heart today.
(Jony Academy tomonidan o'quv maqsadida yozilgan matn.)

listening.audios: Audio fayl yo'q — ustoz transcript'ni o'qiydi.
intro: You will hear a young woman phoning a volunteer centre about starting a club for children.
1-tinglash: formani to'ldiring; 2-tinglash: javoblarni tekshiring.
Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

tasks.title: Form completion — ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER
tasks.instr: Formani to'ldiring (8 ta bo'shliq).
items: Type of club: ___
Number of children: about ___
Start date: 1st ___
Meetings: every ___
Time: ___ a.m.
Room: ___
Volunteer card ready in: ___ days
Caller's surname: ___

transcript: USTOZ UCHUN: 2 marta o'qing; 1-rol — ustoz, 2-rol — kuchli o'quvchi (yoki ovozni o'zgartiring).
Officer: Good morning, Youth Volunteer Centre. How can I help you?
Caller: Hi. I'd like to set up a club for children at your centre. It's part of a school project.
Officer: Lovely. What kind of club?
Caller: I was thinking of a chess club — actually, no, a reading club. I think children need to read more.
Officer: A reading club, great. How many children are you expecting?
Caller: About twenty — sorry, fifteen. Our first group will be quite small.
Officer: When would you like to start?
Caller: On the 1st of September — oh no, that's too soon. The 1st of October. The meetings will be every Sunday — no, wait, Saturday is better. Families are busy on Sundays.
Officer: What time? The hall is free at ten.
Caller: Ten is a bit early for children at the weekend. Could we have eleven?
Officer: Yes, eleven is fine. We can set aside Room 4 for you — Room 2 is being painted.
Caller: Perfect.
Officer: You'll also need a volunteer card. It usually takes a week, but for school projects it's only three days. Can I take your name?
Caller: Malika Ergasheva. That's E-R-G-A-S-H-E-V-A.
Officer: Thank you, Malika. Good luck with the club!
